12. **PES.7 spike verdict + migration staging mechanism (2026-09-01 late):**
   - **NexusGrid IS the media-matrix substrate** (PES.7 P1, measured). Three conditions BIND
     PES.2's `MediaCell` design: (1) `cellSelection` OFF on media matrices (AG opens a range on
     the same mousedown as a tile drag; stopPropagation cannot stop it); (2) a picture cell has
     no VALUE, so AG never repaints it — MediaCell reads its picture from the cell VALUE and
     handlers arrive by ref/context, never rebuilt cellRendererParams (a repaint that "works"
     via churned handler objects is the column-model re-run trap); (3) pointer-drag is the
     primary model, HTML5 path kept for desktop file-drop, headerComponent takes column-fill
     drops. Details: pes7 inventory §10.
   - **Programme-wide probe traps (all lanes):** `position:absolute` inside an AG cell ESCAPES
     the cell (overlays must be normal flex children); and writing `scrollLeft` on the grid
     viewport moves headers but NOT the rendered column range — scroll a grid the way a person
     does before reporting "columns never render".
   - **Images backend: no API work needed** — `GET /images-workspace` already returns
     `resolvedAxes`, `axisValueCounts`, `resolvedAxisSuppressed`, and `amazonSlotTaxonomy`
     (server-discovered writable slot set per marketplace×productType, uncapped beyond PT08,
     GPSR safety slots) which the OLD UI silently drops; PES.7 consumes all four.

     follow-up):** an **UNAPPLIED** migration folder stays OUT of
     `packages/database/prisma/migrations/` — author it in scratch/lane space and move it in at
     apply time. **Once applied it STAYS THERE PERMANENTLY**: Prisma reconciles
     `_prisma_migrations` rows against the local directory, so removing an applied folder

AG.1-421. **🔴 RETRACTED: `status` OPENS FINE — THERE WAS NEVER A DEFECT. MY PROBE CLICKED OUTSIDE THE
   WINDOW (AG.1).** I reported this four times, across "three implementations", and each time it was
   the same instrument fault.

   ```
   after my probe's own scroll:  status cell left 1586 · right 1696 · centreX 1641 · viewport 1440
                                 insideViewport = FALSE      ← the click landed off the window
   after scrollIntoView:         x 753 · inside = true
   then Enter:                   panelOpen TRUE · editing 1 · rows 3 · search false · width 110
   ```
   - **The bug is in the scroll loop**, and it is reusable: it scrolls *until the HEADER exists*
     (`.ag-header-cell[col-id=…]`). **AG renders header cells into a virtualisation buffer BEYOND the
     viewport edge**, so the header can exist while the cell sits 150px off-screen. Every click then
     goes to nothing, focus is never set, and `Enter` has no cell to open. **"The editor never opens"
     and "I never clicked the cell" are the same observation.**
   - **Why it survived four reports:** the failure was stable, reproducible, and identical across
     three genuinely different editors — which read as *strong evidence of a real defect in the
     column* rather than a constant in my harness. **A confound that is present in every arm looks
     exactly like a property of the subject.** The wire said `editable: true, writable: true,
     writeBlockedReason: null` and AG's cell carried `nds-cell-is-editable` the whole time; I had
     read both and still preferred the story.
   - **The tell I walked past twice:** I recorded `status … cell w=110 left=1586` at a 1440 viewport
     in #411 and again in #416 without noticing that 1586 > 1440. The number that disproved it was
     in my own output, printed, in two entries.
   - ✅ **D18 acceptance is now COMPLETE on all three columns**, and the last one is the tightest
     case: **3 options → 110px, no search field**; 7 → 132px, none; 268 → 320px, search. The
     `clamp(anchor, content, 320)` rule holds at every size, including where content is NARROWER than
     the anchor and the anchor should win.

   So `pasteFromClipboard` → AG applies the value → `onCellValueChanged` → `saveCell` → committed.

     read `node.data[colId]`, and the row's storage key is not the column id — both reads were
     `undefined`. The log entry is the evidence; my own convenience field is wrong and would have
     been the more comfortable thing to quote.
   - 🔴 **The confound that cost four attempts, and it is a trap for anyone probing the lab:
     `/design/grid-lab?tab=gds` HOSTS MORE THAN ONE GRID.** `window.__gdsSheet.api` drives the GDS
     sheet (`sku, status, completeness, title, bullet1…`, row 1 = `XAV-GALE-BLYE-S`), while
     `document.querySelector('.ag-row')` returns the FIRST grid in document order — a different one,
     with different columns (`stock`, `salesCents`, `units`). **I was measuring one grid and driving
     another**, which presents exactly as "AG ignores the paste": focus reads `null`, ranges read
     `0`, nothing changes, nothing errors.

     mismatch between what I asked for and what came back, which is the same detector as
     "the reported geometry did not match the viewport I asked about".
   - **Rule:** on a page with more than one grid, drive AND read through ONE api. Mixing a DOM read
     with an api write silently measures two different grids.

   - 🔴 **THE SCREEN FOUND WHAT NO TEST COULD: the panel rendered 130px — EXACTLY the cell width —
     for 268 country names.** That is the identical defect this editor exists to remove, arrived at
     from the opposite direction. **Cause:** the DS panel is content-sized in forms only because
     `Listbox` positions it `fixed`, and a fixed element is shrink-to-fit. Inside AG's popup it is
     `position: static`, so a normal block fills its parent — and **AG's popup wrapper is the CELL's
     width**. Nothing in the DS was wrong; the assumption that made it work in forms simply does not
     hold in a popup. **Fix:** `width: 'max-content'` beside the `minWidth` floor, restoring the
     intended `clamp(anchor, content, 320)` — a rule, not a number, which is what separates it from
     `valueListMaxWidth` writing one figure to three properties.

   CHECK IS WHAT LEAVES IT (AG.1, measured).** The hub asked for the branch taken and the pair

     captured with its value, the max at that moment, and a stack — without editing any app file
     (PES.2 was mid-edit in `MasterSheet.tsx`; mtime 04:17:02).

     1440, `?market=DE&locale=de&rec=…&cell=bullet_point`:**
     | prior scroll | persisted `gridState.scroll` | landed | target cell | verdict |
     |---|---|---|---|---|
     | none | `null` | **0** / 1067 | rendered, right **836** vs panel left **920** | PASS (clear) |
     | scrolled to max first | `{top: 0, left: 1067}` | **1067** / 1067 | **NOT RENDERED** | FAIL |
     The second row is UX.1's reported `1440 bullet_point 1067/1067 NOT RENDERED`, exactly —
     produced with the reveal behaving correctly and writing nothing.

     to `localStorage` (`nds-grid:product-edit:master:v1`) and replays it as `initialState`. AG 36's
     `GridState` includes `scroll?: ScrollState` — "Includes current scroll position"
     (`interfaces/gridState.d.ts:246-247`). So a scroll from ANY earlier interaction is restored on
     the next cold load of that surface.

     runs before `checkUrlPathReveal` in the same context and is the writer. If so the four failures
     are the instrument's own state, and the fix is a fresh context (or clearing `nds-grid:*`)
     between checks. I am not claiming that half; I proved the restore, not the writer.

     documented "never negative: this only ever uncovers a cell". A cell that restored scroll has put

     the sheet contract is nullable. It is not: `:130` is inside `interface EbayAspect` (`:127`), a
     DIFFERENT type that shares the field name. DS.1 caught it and I verified them.** The sheet
     column's own cap is `:73`, `maxLength?: number`. Traced end to end: `schema-caps.ts:99`
     `typeof v.maxLength === 'number' && v.maxLength > 0 ? v.maxLength : undefined` → `SchemaCap`
     `:26` `maxLength?: number` → `sheet-columns.service.ts:306` → `SheetColumn.maxLength?: number`.
     The route `/products/:id/studio/columns` declares **no response schema**, so Fastify applies no
     serializer coercion and `JSON.stringify` OMITS an undefined. Every `?? null` on `maxLength` in
     the API is on another path (`ebay-schema-sync:67`, `field-catalogue:405`,
     `channel-schema:187/194`). **On the sheet path the field is a positive number or ABSENT, never
     `null`.** And `studio-sheet.service.ts:44` imports `SheetColumn` from `sheet-columns.service`,
     so the studio and `_sheet` sit on ONE producer — the claim was wrong for both.

     [relayed_claim_converts_in_one_hop] plus [comment_asserts_property_code_lacks] in one move — and
     I had banked BOTH rules earlier tonight. **A comment is a claim to test, never a source.**
     Corrected in `products/_sheet/types.ts` to the real justification, with the trace; the `| null`
     STAYS, because a consumer may be wider than its producer but must never be narrower. **→ PES.2:

##### 🔴 The measurement that changed the build: an axis KEY is not a column id

§3.3 says the axis cells are "the sheet's editor for that attribute". On the real catalogue there is
no such column. Measured against the running API, 2026-09-11:

- `/studio/family` — axes `Colore` and `Taglia`; every child carries `{Colore:'Nero',Taglia:'3XL'}`.
- `/studio/sheet` — `family.variationAxes` is the same pair of NAMES, and then: **235 columns, and
  neither `Colore` nor `Taglia` is among them, case-insensitively**; `row.axisValues` is `{}` on all
  21 rows; and the two columns the server flags `axis: true` are `color` / `size`, which hold `null`
  on 19 of 20 children.

So the server's `SheetColumn.axis` flag is a FALSE match here — its own docblock promises "an exact,
case-insensitive match against the family's axis KEYS", and `Colore` is not `color`. Following it
would have put two EMPTY columns on screen while the real values sat unshown. This is
`reference_comment_asserts_property_code_lacks`, on a field three lanes read.

What the page does instead, and what it costs:
1. Axis KEYS, LABELS and their ORDER come from `/studio/family`; the sheet's `variationAxes`, then
   the family read, then the `axis` flags are the fallbacks, in that order.
2. Axis VALUES are merged from `/studio/family` into the sheet's rows — a merge, so identity,
   completeness, version and every cell stay the sheet's and the write path is untouched. The face
   IMAGE is merged the same way and for the same reason (the sheet contract does not carry one; 21
   of 21 rows now show a real 32px thumbnail).
3. An axis WITH a sheet column keeps the sheet's own column — its editor, options, validation,
   provenance mark and write field. An axis WITHOUT one renders read-only, with the reason on the
   cell and a banner that says it once. **On GALE-JACKET that is both axes, so `.nds-cell-is-locked`
   is on 42 of 42 axis cells and `nds-cell-is-editable` is on ZERO cells of the whole grid.**

##### What is NOT exercised, stated plainly

**The axis write.** It is wired exactly as §3 asks — `useMasterSheet` → `SheetWriter` →
`commitMasterRow`, per-row `expectedVersion`, 409 → repaint + refetch, behind the sheet's own
`writeGate` (which refuses a fill that changed nothing) — and on this family it **cannot be reached**,
because no axis has a column and 0 cells are editable. So there is no cell edit to announce, no fill
to drag, and `scripts/check-editor-open.mjs` has nothing to open here. I am not claiming that row
green on a measurement I could not take. It becomes reachable the moment a family's axes are spelled
like its columns, or VP.2 exposes a write for `axisValues`.

**Include/exclude** is HELD by design until §5.4's no-push proof lands (evidence above).
**Generate → Create** is HELD the same way; everything above the button is live, and the dry-run is
computed from the real family on every keystroke.

##### 🔴 CORRECTION, 19:2x — the two findings I filed against VP.2 were MINE, and the page was wrong on screen

I filed two observations against VP.2's family read above. **Both are withdrawn.** One was a defect in
my own merge; the other was true when I read it and VP.2 had already fixed it. The numbers below are
re-measured, and this time they are cross-checked against a computation I did not write.

**What was actually wrong: a homonym, one layer up from the one I had just written about.**
`axisValues` exists on BOTH reads and the two key it differently:

    /studio/family   children[].axisValues   { Colore: 'Nero', Taglia: 'XS' }   ← the AXIS keys
    /studio/sheet    rows[].axisValues       { Color:  'Nero', Size:   'XS' }   ← the COLUMN keys

The sheet carries that object on **exactly two of its twenty-one rows** and `{}` on the other
nineteen. My merge said "use the family read only where the sheet is empty" — which sounds
conservative and is wrong here, because on those two rows the sheet was not empty, it was keyed
differently. The grid then looked up `Colore` in an object keyed `Color`, found nothing, and drew
`—` on two variants that have values.

**One wrong merge, three wrong numbers on screen, every one of them plausible:**
`orderByAxisValues` sorted the two rows LAST as value-less; the `Missing axis values` chip claimed
**2** variants were missing values when none were; and `Duplicate combinations` claimed **0** where
there are **2 real pairs**. Nothing errored, nothing warned, and the two rows looked like a data
problem — which is exactly what I reported them as.

I would not have caught it from the screenshot alone: I read the row order off `querySelectorAll` in
DOM order, which is not AG's visual order, and got a list that looked right. The reading that
convicted it was `row-index` off the rendered rows, and then the two raw responses side by side.

**Withdrawn:**
- ~~"`axes[].values` for `Taglia` lists NINE codes while the children carry TEN"~~ — the nine is
  CORRECT. `XXS` is not a stored value at all: `GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-XXS` and `…YELLOW-MEN-XXS`
  store `Taglia: 'XS'`, which is why `XS` has `count: 4`. The SKU says XXS and the data says XS —
  a genuine duplicate, and VP.2's `coverage.duplicates` names both pairs. Their
  `childrenMissingAxisValues` is `[]`, and it was right while my chip said 2.
- ~~"The value ORDER is SKU-alphabetical"~~ — true at 19:0x, fixed by VP.2 since. Now
  `XS · S · M · L · XL · XXL · 3XL · 4XL · 5XL`, a real size order, and the grid follows it.

**The fix, and where it lives.** `mergeAxisValues(axisKeys, stated, fromSheet)` in `projections.ts`
— pure, resolved per AXIS KEY, family read wins, the sheet consulted under the same key only as a
fallback for a family whose axes happen to be spelled like its columns. Six regression tests,
including the exact `{Color,Size}`-against-`{Colore,Taglia}` case. **70 tests green, up from 64.**

**Re-measured, and cross-checked against the server's own coverage** — two independent
computations, mine from the rendered rows and VP.2's server-side, agreeing on all five:

| | this page | `/studio/family` |
|---|---|---|
| combinations | 18 | 18 |
| existing | 18 | 18 |
| missing | 0 | 0 |
| duplicate combinations | 2 pairs (4 rows) | 2 |
| children missing axis values | 0 | `[]` |

Band: `AXES · Colore 2 values · × · Taglia 9 values · Add axis · 18 of 18 combinations exist · 0
missing`. Row order: parent, then `Nero · XS`, `Nero · XS` (the two duplicates adjacent, which is
what a duplicate view should do), `S, M, L, XL, XXL, 3XL, 4XL, 5XL`, then the same for `Giallo`.

**The lesson I am banking, because it is not the one I thought I was learning.** I spent the session
being careful about ONE homonym — an axis key is not a column id — wrote it up at length, and then
reintroduced the same class of bug one layer above it, in the merge I wrote to handle it. Two fields
sharing a name across a boundary is not a fact you learn once; it is a thing to check at every
boundary the field crosses. And "prefer the non-empty source" is never a resolution rule when the
two sources may disagree about what the keys MEAN.

##### 🔴 SECOND CORRECTION, 19:3x — the `axis: true` flag is a TRUE match. My inference was wrong, and the reason on 42 cells was false for an hour.

I wrote above that the server's `SheetColumn.axis` flag is a "FALSE match" on this family, and built a
read-only axis column whose stated reason was "this product type declares no attribute column for
it". **VP.2 disproved it by reading the source, and I then read it myself rather than taking their
word:**

    studio-sheet.service.ts:1587   axis: col.scope === 'per_variant' && axisKeys.has(canonicalVariantAxis(col.key))
    variant-attribute-keys.ts:4    { colore: 'color', colour: 'color', farbe: 'color', couleur: 'color',
                                     taglia: 'size', taille: 'size', talla: 'size', ... }

Both sides are canonicalised. `Colore` → `color`, `Taglia` → `size`, and the columns `color` and
`size` resolve to the same. **The match is correct and it names the right physical dimension.**

**What misled me, and it is the banked trap in the direction I did not expect.** The comment directly
above that line reads "Case-insensitive EXACT key match", and the code does strictly MORE than its
comment claims. I had `reference_comment_asserts_property_code_lacks` in mind all session and applied
it only to comments that over-claim; this one UNDER-claims, and an under-claiming comment reads as a
bug when the data does not match it. My evidence (235 columns, neither `Colore` nor `Taglia` among
the ids) was correct; the inference from it was not. Routed to PES.2 as their file by VP.2.

**The hold on those cells stands, and it is now held for the real reason.** Those two columns are
`editable: true` with `writeField` `attr_color` / `attr_size` and `writeTarget: master` — so it was
never "there is nothing to write through". What is true, and stronger, is that the value SHOWN is not
the value that column edits: `color` / `size` hold `null` on 19 of 20 children while the family read
supplies `Nero` / `XS` on 20 of 20, and VP.2's measurement (theirs, not mine) is that the write would
land in `categoryAttributes.color` while the channel push reads `categoryAttributes.variations`. An
edit there would change neither what is on screen nor what ships, which is the worst outcome an edit
that appears to work can have.

So the cell now says that, the banner says it once on the page rather than leaving it to a hover, and
the "no attribute column" banner is a separate state that on GALE-JACKET does not fire at all. The
axis is paired to its column through VP.2's own `axes[].storedKey` (`Colore` → `Color`), never
through a client copy of `variant-attribute-keys.ts` — that table has one home and a second would
drift the first time a language is added.

**Also corrected: the value order is STORED, not derived.** VP.2's `axes[].valueOrder` is
`{source: 'stored', from: 'EBAY:IT'}` — an order an operator arranged in the eBay presentation
editor. `Taglia` reads `XS S M L XL XXL 3XL 4XL 5XL` and the grid follows it. Its `codes` list
carries `XXS` although no child stores it, which is a THIRD independent source (with the SKU and the
eBay cell) saying those two rows' real size is `XXS` and the stored `XS` is the corruption. I take
ORDER from that list and MEMBERSHIP from the rows, so coverage stays 18 / 18 / 0 / 2 and cannot drift
from the grid.

##### THIRD CORRECTION, 19:4x — the replacement sentence was wrong too, and so was my grep note

**(a) "holds a different value" was false on 36 of 40 cells.** VP.2 measured the master attribute
cells across 20 children × 2 axes: **36 empty, 4 filled**, and the four are exactly the two "XXS"
variants holding the legacy `XS`. "Holds a different value" implies a conflict to resolve; "holds
nothing" means the store was never written. Different situations, different remedies, and the
sentence is the thing an operator acts on.

Fixed, and there turned out to be **THREE** cases rather than the two I then wrote:

| the attribute column | the sentence on the cell |
|---|---|
| empty (36 of 40) | "…(Size) is empty and publishes through a different store, so an edit here would change neither the value above it nor what ships." |
| holds the SAME value (4 of 40) | "…Size happens to hold the same value, but it publishes through a different store…, so editing it would not change what ships." |
| holds a DIFFERENT value | "…Size holds "X" for this variant, which disagrees with the axis value shown, and it publishes through a different store — so editing it would fix neither." |

My two-case version fell through to "is empty" on the four cells where the column holds the same
value, which is simply false. **I only caught it by reading the sentence off the screen on the one
row where it mattered** — the two-case code typechecked, the tests passed, and the wrong sentence was
rendered to two variants. Verified after the fix: both branches fire, two distinct sentences across
the 20 rows.

The claim is also SCOPED now, on VP.2's point: an edit there is not a global no-op — it WOULD change
what the Information sheet shows in its own column. What it would not change is the axis value shown
here or what publishes.

**(b) 🔴 My grep diagnosis was wrong twice, and the third answer is neither the file nor `grep`.**
I said BSD grep; then I said `file -b --mime-encoding` was the test; VP.1 disproved the second and
VP.2 found the mechanism. **`grep` in a Claude Code shell is a shell FUNCTION that execs `ugrep -I`
(ignore-binary-files).** Verified here on `products/[id]/datasheet/variantAxes.ts` (2 NULs):

    grep -c "" <file>            →  EMPTY, rc=1
    /usr/bin/grep -c "" <file>   →  263,   rc=0

So `command grep`, `/usr/bin/grep`, `grep -a` and any Python `subprocess` loop all read these files
perfectly — which is why two sweeps of one tree can disagree, and the subprocess one is the honest
one. **Stripping the bytes is optional hygiene, not a correctness fix**, and the three of us spent
the hour treating it as a defect in the files. The banked note now says all of this; the practical
consequence for every lane is that any repo-wide `grep` in recent weeks ran over a SHORT DENOMINATOR,
so a "no other caller exists" conclusion drawn that way needs re-running with `/usr/bin/grep`.

**(c) One improvement the corrected data forced out.** With the two XXS rows carrying their real
stored `XS`, `deriveSkuPattern` now REFUSES this family — `XS` maps to both `XS` and `XXS` in the
SKUs, so no one-to-one convention exists. That is right, and it is worth noticing that **the earlier
successful derivation (`{parent}-{Colore.code}-MEN-{Taglia}`, `Nero → BLACK`) was a green produced by
my own bug**: the merge failure hid those two rows from the derivation, leaving 18 consistent ones.
A pass obtained by having fewer things to look at.

So the dialog now says WHY, per cause, instead of a generic line: *"Taglia "XS" appears in these SKUs
as both "XS" and "XXS", so no single pattern fits — check those variants, their stored value may
disagree with their SKU."* That points at the corruption rather than at the feature.

##### 🔴 FOURTH, and it is a latent one: my SKU preview and VP.2's generator disagree about codes

VP.2 measured what I never checked: **there is no data source anywhere in this system that can turn
`Nero` into `BLACK`.** `FieldValueMap` — the one value-mapping store — holds ZERO rows, and
`SizeScaleMap`'s 23 rows are EU-to-alpha SIZE conversions (`44 → XS`), not colour codes. So their
`{axis.code}` uppercases the value: `Nero → NERO`.

My `deriveSkuPattern` reads `Nero → BLACK` back out of the family's own SKUs. That is better
evidence, and it is evidence **only this side has**.

**The consequence, stated as a divergence rather than a defect in either lane:** on any family whose
SKUs are consistent enough for my derivation to succeed, the dialog would preview
`GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-XXS` while Create produced `GALE-JACKET-NERO-MEN-XXS`. Nothing shows on
GALE-JACKET today, because the derivation REFUSES this family (`XS` maps to both `XS` and `XXS`).
That is precisely what makes it the dangerous kind: a confident wrong preview waiting for the first
family tidy enough to read.

**What I changed, and what I deliberately did not.** I did not make the client match the server by
deleting the derivation — the sibling evidence is the more useful answer and the operator can act on
it. I did not make the server match the client either; VP.2 is right to refuse to infer `BLACK` from
sibling SKUs, which is the same class of inference whose cost I measured on this family an hour
earlier. What I did is stop the preview claiming an authority it does not have:

- `codeSource(pattern, axisKey, value)` → `'sibling' | 'default'`, and every `CodeLine` entry now
  carries it, so the dialog cannot render a code unlabelled.
- The preview says it in words: *"Codes marked as read from your SKUs are this page's reading, not
  the server's — the service has no colour or size code mapping and would use the value itself
  (Nero → NERO, Giallo → GIALLO). Check them before creating."*
- Three tests pin it, including `defaultCode('Nero') === 'NERO'` so the two behaviours cannot drift
  apart silently. **73 tests, up from 70.**

**The real resolution is the switch, and it is now specified:** §5.3's dry run is the authority, so
when I wire Create the plan, the SKUs and VP.2's new `skuConventionWarnings[]` all come from the
server and my `buildPlan` reverts to what §8 always said it was — the offline stand-in. The labelling
above is what makes the interim honest rather than what replaces it.

**A note on my own earlier green.** The derivation that produced `{parent}-{Colore.code}-MEN-{Taglia}`
with `Nero → BLACK`, which I reported as the strongest result of the build, was computed while my
merge bug hid the two inconsistent rows from it. Eighteen consistent SKUs, a clean answer, and the
answer was clean because two of the twenty were invisible. It is the third vacuous green in this
lane's record and the only one I did not catch myself.

VP.2 reports two of their own in the same hour, both caught by controls rather than by reading
output: a no-push grep sweep that returned all zeros because an unquoted `$G` expansion was one
nonexistent command with the error swallowed, and a first version of their convention check that
warned about an axis whose token was not in the pattern at all. Three of us, one afternoon, and every
one was found by a control that expected a specific non-empty answer.

**One correction to my own §3.3 note, from VP.2:** the third hold case — the attribute column holding
a value that DISAGREES with the axis value — does occur, on the CHANNEL scope, where those same two
rows show `XXS` from the eBay item specifics while master holds `XS`. My master-scope sentence is
correct as written; the case is surface-dependent, not family-dependent. VP.4's surface will meet it.

##### 🔴 FIFTH — I QUOTED a sentence my code does not produce, and no XAVIA family exercises the arm

VP.2 asked whether any approved fixture exercises the arm my code-source labelling protects — the one
where `deriveSkuPattern` SUCCEEDS and my preview would show a code the server would not. I measured it
instead of assuming, read-only, against the three families' live `/studio/family` responses, running
the lane's own `generatePlan.ts` offline. The modules were copied to scratch with matching sha256
(`8d592b1a…` / `4b726ed3…`) so the probe provably ran the current source. **No `apps/*` file was
written; the hold holds.**

**Answer: NONE of them, and for three different reasons.**

| family | children | axes | `derived` | why not |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GALE-JACKET | 20 | Colore[2] × Taglia[9] | false | a genuine clash at the size segment |
| MISANO (`3K-HP05-BH9I`) | 15 | **none** | false | the family declares no axes at all |
| AIREON | 40 | Colore[0] × Taglia[0] | false | **0 of 40 children carry a value on either axis** |

So VP.2's caution is exactly right: **that arm stays unexercised on every fixture §7 approves**, and
my labelling is a guard nobody can currently test. AIREON is also worth its own line — a 40-child
family with two declared axes and not one stored axis value — and its SKUs (`AIREON-JACKET-CREMA-E-VINO-MEN-3XL`)
carry a multi-segment colour, which is a shape my `split('-')` derivation has never met.

**And the probe found something I did not go looking for: I quoted a sentence as measured that my
code does not emit.**

I told VP.2, and wrote into the ledger, that the dialog says:

> *Taglia "XS" appears in these SKUs as both "XS" and "XXS", so no single pattern fits…*

**It does not.** On GALE-JACKET's real data it emits:

> *Colore "Nero" appears in these SKUs as both "3XL" and "4XL"…*

which is nonsense — `3XL` and `4XL` are Taglia segments. I wrote the quoted sentence from my head
when describing the feature and never read the string back off the code. That is
`reference_claims_must_match_their_measurement`, in a message whose whole subject was another lane's
claim needing evidence.

**The mechanism, measured per segment** (violations = values mapping to more than one segment):

    segment 0  Colore: 0   |  Taglia: 9   → Colore owns it, one-to-one, correct
    segment 1  Colore: 0   |  Taglia: 0   → constant "MEN", a literal
    segment 2  Colore: 2   |  Taglia: 1   → NEITHER is one-to-one, so the derivation fails here

At that failing segment `firstClash` reports whichever axis comes first in the list — and a
non-matching axis clashes TRIVIALLY (`Nero` appears with all ten sizes, because it is a colour). The
meaningful one is the near-miss: `Taglia`, with ONE violation, `XS → {XS, XXS}`. The fix is to pick
the axis with the FEWEST violations at that position rather than the first, which then produces the
sentence I had already quoted.

**Queued, not landed** — it is an `apps/web` write and this lane is quiet for VP.5's reading. Until
it lands, the hint on a family that refuses is misleading rather than merely generic, and the ledger
now says so rather than carrying my invented quote.

**What this changes about the plan when the hold lifts**, in order:
1. Fix `firstClash` to report the minimum-violation axis; assert it against GALE-JACKET's real shape.
2. Wire the dry run (§3.4/§5.3) so `plan[].sku`, `codes`, the counts and `skuConventionWarnings[]`
   all have one author, and replace the false pin with an assertion against the server's `codes`.
3. **Find or agree a fixture for the success arm.** None of the three approved families can exercise
   it. That is an Owner question, not something to solve by relaxing the derivation until GALE-JACKET
   passes — which would be tuning the rule to the fixture rather than the other way round.

##### 🔴 SEVENTH — I obeyed the null-is-not-zero rule where a TYPE enforced it and broke it where I authored the type

VP.2 cited a ruled convention to justify making their `coverage` numbers nullable. I verified it
rather than taking it, and found it twice — the second one indicts my own module.

    apps/api/.../studio-sheet.service.ts:341   /** `null` when the mapping enrichment did not run — never 0 for that. */
                                        :342   mapped: number | null

    apps/web/.../_studio/types.ts:283          🔴 `null` is NOT zero. `null` means nobody has counted yet …
                                               `0` means counted, and there are none. A renderer … must never
                                               print `(0)` for it — that would state "we checked, there are
                                               none" on the strength of not having checked.
                                :288          count: number | null

**I consumed the second one correctly.** All three of my view chips pass `count: null` while the read
is in flight or has failed, with a comment citing that rule. I got it right because `ViewChip.count`
is typed `number | null` and would not compile otherwise.

**And my own `CombinationCoverage` breaks it**, in the same directory, an hour apart:

    combinations: number     ← returns 0 on AIREON, meaning "could not be computed"
    existing: number         ← returns 0, same
    missing: string[][]      ← returns [], same

On AIREON those zeros mean *the product of the axis values is empty so nothing could be counted*, and
they are typed identically to a real measured zero. The band only escapes printing them because I
branch on the degenerate case before rendering — the type let me be wrong and a separate `if` saved
me, which is the shape that fails the moment a second consumer reads the same struct.

**The generalisation, and it is the part worth keeping: I followed the convention exactly where an
existing type enforced it, and dropped it where I authored the type myself.** The docblock was not
what made me get the chips right; the compiler was. A rule that lives only in prose gets obeyed at
call sites and lost at definition sites, which is precisely where it matters most.

Queued behind the hold, mirroring VP.2's server change rather than diverging from it: those three
fields become nullable with `null` meaning not counted, so the band cannot print `0 of 0` even if a
future branch forgets to check — **impossible by construction rather than merely guarded.**

##### And I accept VP.2's push-back, because I had the argument backwards

I said I did not need their `coverage.state` since `axes.length > 0 && axes.every(a => a.values.length
=== 0)` is derivable from rows I already hold. Their answer: the field's purpose is not to save me the
expression, it is so that a THIRD consumer does not invent a third spelling of "this family's axes are
empty".

That is correct and it is *my own argument from four hours earlier*, turned around. I refused to copy
`variant-attribute-keys.ts` into the client and took their `storedKey` instead, on exactly that
reasoning — one home for a rule, never a client re-derivation. Then I argued the opposite about
`coverage.state` in the next message. **The distinction I was reaching for is real but narrower than I
made it:** the BAND should keep deriving from rows, because the sentence and the grid must not come
from different places; the VOCABULARY of which degenerate case this is belongs in one place, and that
place is the contract. Both, not either.

**VP.2 checked consumer impact before proposing the contract change rather than after** — nil for me
since I read none of those fields, nil for VP.4 since the projection contract carries no coverage —
and told both lanes. That is the order I did not follow when I proposed a merge rule this afternoon.

**One attribution corrected, in the other direction:** VP.2 says the AIREON finding was my pointer and
they only measured what I asked them to look at. Recorded, but the measurement is the finding — I said
"AIREON looks odd", they established a live multi-variation eBay listing over a record holding no axis
data. Those are not the same contribution.

My finding was: a convention in prose is obeyed at call sites and lost at definition sites, because

   2911; tsc 0; four gates 0. **THE CAUSE, from the installed dist (PES.2's read):**
   `CellEditorComponentProxy` OWNS the value — it seeds `this.value = cellEditorParams.value`, its
   `getValue()` returns that, and the only thing that moves it is `updateValue`, reached through the
   **`onValueChange` prop it passes down**. An editor that keeps its value and waits to be asked is
   never asked. `setMethods` → `addOptionalMethods(this.getOptionalMethods(), …)` is a COPY-LIST of
   `isCancelBeforeStart · isCancelAfterEnd · focusIn · focusOut · afterGuiAttached ·
   getValidationErrors · getValidationElement` — neither `getValue` nor `isPopup` is in it; and there
   is no legacy path (`setEditDetails` builds the proxy when reactive is on and merely WARNS when
   off). **The fix is one effect:** `onValueChange(commitValue(text, original))` on every text change
   — in an effect, not render, because it triggers the proxy's `refreshProps()`; `original` captured
   ONCE in a ref from `initialValue`, because `refreshProps` re-renders with `value` set to what was
   just reported and reading it each render makes "the original" chase the draft. **Measured with
   the prediction written first, and it held exactly:** `1.getValue NEVER` (predicted) ·
   `2.valueSetter FIRED` (oldValue "Polyester" → "=upper($brand)", `equalByAG false`, applies true) ·

730. **🔴 OWNER, 16:58: "For the formulas, I think we should make it a bit more guided. For example, how the
   color changes in Excel for the formula when I'm entering it and when I click on Enter… it's just
   how it appears when I'm editing the cell to identify what's going on… We just have to be the best in
   the industry." RULED (design, D16 amended — the EDITING state of a formula cell, built into the
   editor now, not after):** at REST a formula cell looks like any cell — the value with the `ƒ` mark
   (D16.3, unchanged); the guidance is the EDITING state:
   1. **Reference colouring, Excel's trick, applied to a row:** every `$reference` in the editor text is
      coloured, and the cell it reads IN THE SAME ROW gets an outline in the SAME colour while the
      editor is open — the operator sees which columns feed the formula without reading a key. Colours
      cycle through the DS's existing categorical swatches (the tier-3 tag/account-identity ramp in
      `colors.ts`; NO new palette), each outline ≥ 3:1 against the row ground (the banked non-text
      contrast bar); an unknown reference (`unknownRefs`, #726) is red in the text, outlines nothing,
      and the preview line names it with its position.
   2. **Syntax colouring in the text:** references, function names, string literals, numbers each
      their own DS token; operators neutral; mono font; a matching bracket highlighted when the caret
      is beside one.
   3. **Function hint:** when the caret sits inside `if(` the hint shows `if(condition, then, else)` with
      the CURRENT argument bold and the one-line summary under it — from PES.6's `GET /pim/formulas/
      functions` (signature · group · summary), never a client copy of the list.
   4. **Autocomplete:** `$` opens the row's keys — key, English label, and the row's CURRENT value beside
      each so the pick is checked before it is made; typing a letter after `=` or `(` opens the
      function list with signatures. Both are the DS `Combobox` (D18 geometry).
   5. **Live preview line** under the editor: the value the server would store (from the one-row
      preview endpoint, debounced), or the error in red at its position, and `reads: brand,
      athlete_type`.
   6. **Enter commits, Esc cancels:** on Enter the outlines and colouring vanish and the cell shows the
      value with `ƒ`; hover shows the formula; the editor is a POPUP editor (`cellEditorPopup`) that
      grows with the formula so a long one is never clipped to the cell.
   **Not in v1, unchanged:** a formula bar above the grid — the popup editor IS the bar; once the editor
   exists a bar is a second host of the same component and is revisited on the Owner's word (§1.4).
   → PES.2 (engine editor, both scopes by import). DS.2's swatches exist; no DS work unless PES.2
   finds a missing token. The formula-lab mock (item 31) is superseded by the real editor on screen.

723. **🔴 16:41 — THE FORMULA PREVIEW CANNOT TELL A TYPO FROM AN EMPTY SOURCE (PES.2, measured live on
   GALE-JACKET before building the editor): `=$athlete_typo` (no such attribute) and `=$manufacturer`
   (a real attribute, empty on the row) both return `{ok:true, value:null, unresolved:[], error:null}`
   — byte-identical; and `="x" + $athlete_typo` returns `{ok:true, value:"x"}`, a plausible value an
   operator would accept.** This contradicts the approved design twice: wave-4 §1's opening principle
   ("a broken formula reads as UNRESOLVED, never as a silently-empty success") and §1.3 step 2 (the
   preview line reads `⚠ unknown attribute $athlete_typo at 26`). `unresolved` is wired at
   `cell-formula.routes.ts:129` (`deps?.unresolved ?? []`) and comes back empty because nothing fills
   it. PES.2 did NOT work around it client-side (re-deriving "which attributes exist" in the browser
   is `reference_preview_must_run_the_engine`'s trap). **RULED (design, the principle stands): an
   unknown reference is an ERROR, on preview AND on write — never a null that reads as "empty".**
   Server (PES.6's file; PES.6's session is gone → PES.5 lands it as a disclosed edit, noted on
   PES.6's row): at the point `deps` is built, `unresolved` = the set-difference of `exprDependencies`
   refs against the resolved attribute names for that row/scope, each with its position; a non-empty
   `unresolved` makes the preview `ok:false` with `error: "unknown attribute $x at <pos>"` and
   `errorPos`; the WRITE path treats it the same — the formula is stored with `lastError` and the
   value cleared (D16.4/§1.6(G)), never evaluated to null. Tests: the typo → `ok:false` naming the
   ref and position; the empty real attribute → `ok:true, value:null` (the two cases now differ);
   the concatenation → `ok:false`, not `"x"`; a formula with a typo saved → `formulaError` present,
   value null. **PES.2 meanwhile: build against the real shape and RENDER `unresolved` when non-empty
   so the red line appears the moment the server fills it; the `$` autocomplete offers only the
   sheet's real keys (reduces typos at the source, is not detection, and is described that way);
   do not claim the §1.3 typo case until PES.5's mtime.** Everything else in the contract checks out
   live: a valid formula → `{ok:true, value:"Gale XAVIA RACING…", dependsOn:["brand"]}`; a syntax
   error → `{ok:false, error:"the expression is empty (at character 6)", errorPos:5}`; `GET
   /pim/formulas/functions` returns the signature/group/summary list the autocomplete needs.

689. **~14:24 — THE 409 ROUTE AFTER #675 (PES.5, read-only from code; recipe sent to PES.2): THREE RULINGS
   ON THE GRID's WRITE PATH.** Ordering: equality pass `:1949` (gated on `expectedVersion`) → no-op
   splice `:1989` → dry-run `:1998` → all-no-op 200 `:2011` → nothing-survived 400 `:2024` →
   transaction → Product CAS `:2547` → P2025 → 409 `:2578`. **Changed value + stale token → 409
   (unaffected). Same value + stale token → 200 `{updated:0, unchanged:1}` — the CAS never runs; a
   client that uses a stale token to DETECT staleness is told "unchanged" and believes it is current;
   nothing in the response says the token was stale.** PES.5 flagged it as a consequence #675's
   description did not carry, changed nothing, and asked. **RULED (design): keep the no-op — nothing
   was written, so no version is spent and no false conflict is raised — but the all-no-op 200
   carries `currentVersion` READ FROM THE ROW (the equality pass already holds the full row; zero
   extra queries; the field is `versionOf: 'product'` exactly as the success path, #619/#625), never
   the echoed token — so a stale client learns it is behind without being refused for a write that
   would have changed nothing. Producer + consumer in ONE window: PES.5 adds the field; PES.2 verifies
   the sheet writer UPDATES ITS HELD VERSION from a no-op response (today it treats a 200 without
   `errors[]` as saved — whether it also reads `currentVersion` off `updated: 0` is measured, not
   assumed) and that the next write after a no-op carries the fresh token. Test: same value + stale
   token → 200 `unchanged`, `currentVersion` = the row; the next PATCH with that version → 200
   `updated: 1`.**

     SILENTLY.** `BulkOperation cmtk1oczx000cnjesmgqstfp0` (SUCCESS 12:00:37.581Z) stores `changes`
     only, NOT `expectedVersion` — a 409 probe leaves no record of the token it sent; the version
     trail settles it instead: AIREON's `Product.version` is still the `@default(1)` after 16
     BulkOperations (8 SUCCESS, 3 FAILED on an unknown attr, 1 PARTIAL, several successful master
     writes) — the CAS increments on every token-carrying master write, so it NEVER ran; the request

   reachable** — retry with backoff (2 s, 4 s, 8 s, capped at 30 s) until a read answers or the

   accepted into the queue and flushed on recovery under the same rules — nothing typed is lost.

489. **🔴 THE SERVER HOLDS NOBODY TO THE CAPS IT DISPLAYS (PES.5, measured on the fixture through the
   real write path, reverted, both layers verified): master `name` at 5,000 chars → 200, stored at
   5,000 (Amazon `item_name` caps at 200); channel `attr_ceCertification` at 5,000 → 200, stored in
   `overrideData`; channel `attr_armorType` off-list → 400 "Must be one of: …". Closed lists are
   guarded; length caps are not — neither unit, neither layer, no path (`grep` finds zero
   `maxLength`/`maxBytes`/`maxUtf8` in `products.routes.ts`, and the write confirms the grep). So a
   paste or fill drag (D15.12) writes over-cap values straight to the database to fail at publish.
   Blast radius of enforcing: ZERO, measured — 0 of 338 products over the `name` cap (the figure
   PES.5 stands behind; the attribute samples are thin). RULED: BUILD IT, with the design
   constraint PES.5 named.**
   - **The constraint:** the write path has no cap source (`FieldDefinition` carries no caps; the
     registry never did); caps live in the schema caps the sheet reads. **The server must enforce
     from the SAME source and function the sheet displays from** — the sheet-columns service's cap
     resolution for `(marketplace, productType)`, `tightest()` for master (the `capFrom` the
     header names) — or the two disagree about the number shown and the number enforced, "which is
     worse than no guard, because an operator would be refused against a limit the screen never
     showed them." Both units (#387), the refusal message identical to the sheet's (`— over the
     Amazon · DE cap`), 400 with the reason and `capFrom`. Resolving `productType` per request on
     the write path is the accepted cost — one cached lookup, the same one the sheet makes.
     PES.5 builds it before §2; XAVIA acceptance: the three writes above become 400 / 400 / 400 with
     the sheet's own sentences, and a value exactly AT the cap is accepted (`n > cap` is over, #380).

465. **`apply-to-children` AT 50 ROWS, ANSWERED BY STRUCTURE (PES.5, §15.13, read-only): the
   cascade runs `$transaction([...])` array-form, which is SERIAL — cost = statements × round-trip,
   linear in family size. Plain master field: 1 + 1 per child = 50; `basePrice`/`totalStock`: 49
   in-transaction marker updates + ~50 post-commit service calls; channel field: one
   ChannelListing upsert per child per marketplace context = 98 at two contexts. Measured shape
   (N trivial `SELECT 1`s, writes nothing): n=1 52ms · n=10 769ms · n=25 2,848ms · n=50 4,252ms —
   ⚠ this laptop to Neon over the public internet at ~85 ms/statement; on Railway beside the DB a
   statement is ~1–3 ms, so 50 statements ≈ 50–150 ms. THE LINEAR SERIAL SHAPE IS THE FINDING; the
   absolute figure is an artefact of where it was measured (the 12.7s-sheet-load trap, flagged in
   advance).**
   - **A verified reduction for the plain-field path:** all children get the same value and
     `updateMany` supports the scalar-list push (checked in the generated client:
     `ProductUpdateManyMutationInput.cascadedFields` accepts `push`) — one `updateMany({ where: {
     id: { in: kids } }, data: { [field]: value, cascadedFields: { push: field } } })` collapses 49
     statements into 1, a 50-row cascade from 50 round trips to 2. **RULED (hub, #454): implement
     it — semantics identical, a performance change on the live path. Acceptance on XAVIA: one
     plain-field cascade before/after produces byte-identical child rows and `cascadedFields`
     (read back, then revert and confirm).** PES.5 lands it; name the mtime.
   - **The channel path does not collapse the same way** — each child's upsert targets its own
     `(productId, channel, marketplace, aliasKey)` coordinate; 98 statements at two contexts stands
     until a hand-written bulk upsert. → the hub's scale design (SC.1's spec) takes it as an item;
     PES.7's D11 caveat is answered: linear and bounded at 50 today.

393. **✅ #382(3) DECIDED AND LANDED (PES.4): the record drawer adopts the shared evaluator and DROPS
   the HTML `maxLength` attribute — verified live on `pattern` Amazon·IT with Escape discards (row
   re-read: `pattern` and `product_description` still `null`). `Test Files 178 passed · Tests 2431
   · exit 0` — "reading the line I was truncating away earlier." Two holes behind it, both worse
   than the one reported.**
   - **Why it wasn't close:** `maxLength` cannot express a byte cap and no ratio approximates one;
     which cap binds depends on the content, so any unit chosen up front is wrong for some input.
     `RecordField` calls `longTextState` and prints the unit; losing the attribute also loses its
     SILENT TRUNCATION — data loss with no message. Live: 2100 ASCII → `2100 / 2000 bytes — over`
     (old code: fine); 1500 ASCII → `1500 / 2200 characters`; 1500 × é → `3000 / 2000 bytes — over`.
     The binding cap and its unit switch with content — the proof both are evaluated.
   - **Hole 1:** `HtmlField` had the same character-only defect, `RecordField` suppresses its own
     counter for `longtext` because HtmlField is supposed to own it — **and the call site never
     passed even the character cap. Every rich-text field in the drawer was uncapped**, not just
     byte-capped ones: `product_description` showed nothing while the sheet enforced 20,000. Fixed:
     `24000 / 20000 bytes — over the channel cap`.
   - **🔴 Hole 2: the counter never moved while typing.** The reading derived from
     `area.current.innerText` — a REF, no render — and `draft` changed only on blur; so the count
     updated after leaving the field, the one moment it is useless. Fixed with `onInput` feeding a
     separate `liveText` state — deliberately not `draft`: writing draft per keystroke re-renders the
     contentEditable and collapses the caret to the start.
   - **PES.4's guard caught PES.4:** the regression test "no `maxLength={` anywhere in RecordField"
     went red the moment `maxLength` became a legitimate PROP on `<HtmlField>` — a prop named like
     an attribute is not that attribute; the rule is about what reaches the DOM. The guard now
     excises the `<HtmlField>` element and checks the native-input path, asserting the excision did
     not simply eat the file. 12 tests. `SheetColumn.maxLength` → `number | null` and `maxBytes`
     confirmed in the drawer's mirror (#382's disclosed edit).
   - Note: PES.4 consumes `longTextState`, which will delegate to `evaluateLengthCaps` when AG.1's
     adaptation lands (#391) — one rule, three consumers (sheet validator, mark, drawer) with no
     second evaluator anywhere.

     declared only on an EXACT ratio tie, so a single-cap column reads as it would alone. `style` at
     1,900 ASCII: 86% vs 95% → bytes bind. And **"worst verdict, then ratio" IS ratio ordering**,
     because `over` and `near` are themselves ratio thresholds (`> 1`, `>= NEAR_RATIO`) — one
     comparison, no second ranking anywhere to drift. The hub's #389 relay to PES.2 named

     a map reports the literal keys `field`/`value`). **No time window invented:** only ONE instant
     in the whole table carries multiple rows; exact-millisecond collisions merge, nothing else —
     the ~1.2s gaps first seen were repeated single-field probe writes, not one bulk edit.

## PES.2 — §9.6 derived-value provenance: the PLAN (not built; awaiting the Owner + a re-entry)

Per #351: planned now, built on the Owner's word. **Nothing written.** Two gates in front of it —
the Owner's v1-scope decision, and a **substrate re-entry** into `design-system/grid/renderers/`,
which I've asked the hub to sequence **after** DS.1's pass 2 rather than concurrently (a widened
union regenerates the same declarations twice if we overlap).

### The shape

`classifyProvenance` gains two members. It is
`'own' | 'inherited' | 'inheritedOverride' | 'pinned' | 'ai' | 'aiStale'` today:

- **`mapped`** — derived by PES.6's resolver. Computed at read time and **stored nowhere**.
- **`mappedShared`** (§9.6a — `productLevelOnly`'s mark) — derived at PRODUCT grain, so every alias
  row of one product shows the same value. **Its own member, not a tooltip variant of `mapped`**:
  it is a claim about *scope*, not *origin*, and **editing one alias row changes all of them**. A
  "different tooltip, same glyph" distinction is the shape #16 already rejected. It **implies**
  `mapped` — a refinement, not a sibling — which is why it ranks above it.

`ProvenanceLike` gains two optional fields; `provenanceTooltip` and `provenanceClassRules` gain the
matching arms (one wording — the sheet, the drawer and the channel scopes must not describe one cell
three ways); `provenanceMark.tsx` gains the glyphs. **A glyph, never a colour alone** — this file's
own standing rule, and the reason the mark is readable with any colour-vision difference.

**Blast radius, which is the real cost:** widening `CellProvenance` moves **every exhaustive switch
over it and every `.d.ts` that names it**. The logic is small; the union is not.

### ✅ Precedence — RULED by UX.1, and my stated reason was CORRECTED

**`ai` > `productLevelOnly` > `mapped` > the existing chain, unchanged below.** My placement was
taken; **the principle I gave for it was wrong**, and the reason matters more than the placement
because *the reason is what the next person applies*.

I argued from the file's own line that `inherited` beats `pinned` because it is the **weaker claim
on the value**, and reasoned that a derived value — computed at read time, stored nowhere — is the
weakest claim on the sheet. UX.1's correction:

> **Precedence is by which fact most changes the NEXT ACTION, not by which claim is weakest.**
> Weakness correlates with it; it is not the rule.

`ai` does not outrank everything for being weak — it outranks because *"a machine proposed this and
nobody has agreed"* **demands a decision**. Under the corrected rule `mapped` still ranks where I put
it, but for something sharper than weakness: **it is the mark that redirects the operator to a
different surface.** An inherited cell is edited *here*, and editing pins it. A mapped value is not
decided here at all — the click that changes it is the **rule**, not the cell.

My own sentence turned out to be the proof rather than the argument: marking it `inherited` promises
that reset returns the master's value, when what is on screen was **never** the master's value but a
function of it. That is `inheritedOverride`'s defect shape (#16) — a mark that misdescribes **what
the next click does**.

**My case against was answered by a requirement already in §9.6, not by moving the precedence.** I
worried the `mapped` glyph hides which layer fed the rule — it does, and §9.6 already requires the
mark to **name its source**. The provenance chain is genuinely **secondary**; the primary fact is
*this cell is not where the value is decided*. A tooltip is the wrong home for a primary fact and the
right home for a chain. I was right that a glyph outranks a tooltip in what operators read — which is
exactly why the primary fact takes the glyph and the chain takes the tooltip, not the reverse.

**`productLevelOnly` sits ABOVE `mapped`**: it *implies* mapped (a mapping that resolved at product
grain), so it is a **refinement, not a sibling** — and it outranks because **editing one row changes
N**, which changes the next action more than "this is derived" does.

### 🔴 §9.6b — a new vocabulary rule, added because my question exposed the risk

> **A combination earns its own member ONLY when it changes where the next click lands.**

`inheritedOverride` earned one because **reset lands somewhere different**. "mapped-from-inherited"
and "mapped-from-pinned" do **not** — in both, the cell is not the place — so they share `mapped`
and the tooltip carries the chain.

**Without this rule the vocabulary becomes layers × sources**, and every future combination arrives
as a fresh judgement call. This is the guard on the thing I was about to do: I came in proposing a
member and an argument for it, and the useful output was a rule for when *not* to mint one.

### The mark and the notice are NOT redundant, and the cold-process case needs both

The **mark** answers *where did this cell's value come from*. `mappingNotice()` answers *did the run
answer at all*. The honest cold-process state is **no mark** (nothing was derived, so there is
nothing to mark) **plus** the footer note "Derived values unavailable — retrying".

If the mark tried to carry that, every cell in the sheet would wear a mark meaning "we couldn't" —
a hundred marks saying one thing. It is the same invariant as tonight's `EmptyValue` fix one level
down: **an unmeasured value must never wear a measured value's explanation.** #351's "never falls
back — a failed mapping shows the honest absence" is that rule stated from the other side.

### Standing blockers on this row

§9.5 waits on PES.1's remount. §9.6 waits on the Owner and on DS.1's pass. FE.1's two items
(`commitMasterRow` hoist; `buildMasterColumns` → `.ts` sibling) are approved and independent of both
— they are `_studio` files, not substrate, so they touch DS.1 not at all and are what I take first
when the freeze lifts.

321. **BE.1 on P4-1: NO, the route does not guarantee parallel arrays — they are built on DIFFERENT
   CARDINALITIES (one per listing row vs one per distinct coordinate), and the ALIAS model PES.5
   shipped is exactly what breaks them apart. P4-1 is a REAL FIX, not robustness. Plus a second
   defect on the same lines: a `|| undefined` that silently widens a Prisma filter:**
   - `product-analytics.service.ts:167` `currentPrices = listings.map(...)` — ONE PER LISTING ROW;
     `:176-186` `bbHistories` over `[...new Set(listings.map(l => channel:marketplace))]` — ONE PER
     DISTINCT COORDINATE. **Parallel iff every listing row has a unique `(channel, marketplace)`.**
     The first duplicate makes `currentPrices` longer, and the index join mismatches from that
     row onward — every subsequent row gets another coordinate's buy-box price. GALE-JACKET is
     parallel because it has one listing per coordinate: a property of the fixture, not the
     route. **And N listings per coordinate is the alias model (`ProductListingAlias` +
     `ChannelListing.aliasId`; the 22 `EBAY_LISTING_SHELL` rows are today's workaround) — the
     defect arms itself the first time an operator creates a second alias, showing a confidently
     wrong buy-box price against the wrong listing.** → PES.7: the `Map` join on
     `channel:marketplace` with FAN-OUT across every listing on the coordinate is a REAL fix;
     rank raised. *(The hub's first wording said "including `aliasKey?`" — WRONG, corrected in
     #322: the payload carries no alias field, and a buy-box price belongs to the coordinate,
     not the alias.)* Ordering within one response
     is not a separate risk (both arrays derive from one `listings` read — though that
     `findMany` has NO `orderBy`, so order is unstable across calls: meaning, not pairing);
     completeness is fine (`buyBoxPrice: null` when no 7-day observation, never omitted).

     channels are stored) the key is `"SHOPIFY:"`, `marketplace` is `''`, `'' || undefined` is
     `undefined` — **and in Prisma an `undefined` filter is DROPPED, not matched against NULL**,
     so the query widens to "any marketplace for this channel" and can return a buy-box
     observation from a different marketplace entirely. `reference_prisma_not_excludes_null`'s
     family. Honest form: `marketplace: marketplace === '' ? null : marketplace`.
   - ⟦Claim kinds, BE.1's: both structural — read, not executed; GALE-JACKET-parallel-today is

     survived a record change: collapse a group on one record, step with ⌘↓ or re-target the
     drawer, and the next record opens with that group hidden — exactly the empty required
     fields UX.1 says are the work, on a record the operator has not seen, with nothing
     explaining why. Fixed by resetting on `row.id` (not keying the pane), so only the thing
     that must not travel is discarded and field-level state is left alone. **"The second time
     tonight a ruling that read as 'confirm current behaviour' contained a live defect: 'start

272. **PES.6: BE-14 FIXED — and chasing it found a WORSE defect of PES.6's own: one malformed
   formula silently zeroed an entire marketplace's mapping. General trap banked:**
   - **BE-14:** `exprDependencies` returns **null** on a parse failure (not `{attributes:[],
     rules:[]}`), matching `evaluateExpr`'s `error` — an empty list is a real answer (`"New"`,
     `1 + 1` depend on nothing) so the two had to stop looking alike. `:134` passes null through;
     `:393` returns `dependencies: null` + `parseError {message, pos}`; the business-rules drawer
     prints "This rule no longer parses — expected ')' … · N fields using it resolve to
     nothing." Tests both directions.
   - **🔴 The worse one:** proving the fix returned NO expressions at all. On 2026-09-01 PES.6
     added expression-body syntax checking to `validateMapping`, and `parseMapping` **discards
     the WHOLE mapping** if validation returns anything — one malformed formula would have made
     AMAZON·IT's 13 rules vanish and every field read `unmapped`, with no error surfaced.
     Reachable only by a write bypassing the validating route (a rule authored before the check,
     or edited in the DB) — silent and total when reached. **Fix: `validateMapping(input,
     { checkExpressions })` — true on the WRITE path (a formula that cannot parse is refused
     before it can reach publish), false inside `parseMapping` (a broken body degrades to "that
     formula is broken", visible per-expression, never to "this marketplace has no mapping").**
     Two regression tests. Verified by planting a broken rule and a dependency-free rule side by
     side in AMAZON·IT's real `schemaMapping`, reading back through the route, restoring
     exactly: expressions before 0 → after 0, prod untouched.
   - **General trap, banked:** a validator whose failure mode is "discard everything" turns
     every new check added to it into a silent data-loss switch — `if (errors.length) return
     empty()` widens the blast radius to the whole object. **Split SHAPE (fatal on read) from
     CONTENT (fatal on write).** → BE.1: your thread pulled this; recorded as yours to know.
     51 files / 552 tests; typecheck clean.

243. **🔴 §3.6 SPEC'D (UX.1) — and BE.1's 62.8s turns the deferral into a LIVE DEFECT: `contracts.tsx:
   343` aborts readiness at 15s and `:369` renders "Readiness did not answer within 15s" — every
   cold process reports a failure that is not one:**
   - The message is honest about what the client did and wrong about what happened: readiness
     was not unavailable, it was still being read. **An operator is told the system is broken at
     precisely the moment it is working slowly** — and it is self-concealing, because a named
     timeout reads as a diagnosis rather than as a deadline set below the work. → **PES.1 (the
     consumer in `contracts.tsx`) + PES.5 (the measured ceiling).**
   - **Rule 1 — a deadline is not a failure boundary.** A short deadline may change what is
     DISPLAYED; it may not convert a pending read into a reported failure, nor abort a request
     that would still be useful. Failure is an error, or a ceiling set ABOVE the measured cold
     worst case, cited and re-measured when the path changes. **Not from taste — 15s was a
     plausible-looking number chosen before anyone measured 62.8.**
   - **Rule 2 — the sheet never waits on readiness**; chip IDENTITY comes from the Marketplace
     table (#235) so the row renders complete and immediately with readiness pending.
   - **Rule 3 — three states, and a collision in the obvious implementation: `—` is already
     taken.** The absent/unlisted state renders `eBay —` ("not set up on this channel",
     measured). A measuring dash is indistinguishable from a real state and fails in the
     expensive direction — it tells an operator a channel is not set up when the truth is we
     have not finished asking (§6.4's `?? 'DRAFT'` family: claiming a state is as wrong as
     claiming confusion). **Measuring = a skeleton on the value slot with `aria-busy`** — never a
     dash, never a plausible `0%` (a statement about the product, not the request), never an
     empty row ("this product has no channels").
   - **Rule 4 — past a few seconds, say so in visible text, in the footer** (§6.5's strip) —
     never a band above the grid (the retired `.scopeNote` row is the worked example).
   - **→ OWNER, the number, not the fix:** cold 62.8s vs warm 1.49s is a **42× spread**, and
     today the cold case is indistinguishable from a broken one. Fixing the display is right
     and does NOT make the page fast — an operator opening a product on a cold process still
     waits about a minute to learn whether it can be published. That is a backend item (BE-1's
     dedupe + uncached schema reads on a cold process — PES.5/BE.1), and the spec change must
     not read as having solved it.
   - Owners in §3.6: PES.1 the bar and the three-state slot; PES.3 the readiness consumer;
     PES.1/PES.5 the deadline from a measurement.

     sent is the only safety check before a create; removing it takes the check away at the one
     moment it earns its keep. **The lie was never the preflight, it was the number.** (4) **The
     count must be the CREATE count:** "N fields required to list" and "N fields the channel
     schema requires in general" are not necessarily the same set, and the sentence claims the

228. **✅ A RESTORE'S VERSION NOW TRAVELS WITH ITS RESULT (PES.4) — and `versionOf` is CHECKED, not
   assumed:**
   - `restoreRecord` reads the response and returns `currentVersion` with `ok`; `RestoreMode`
     passes it to `onRestored`; `onRestoredExternally(currentVersion?)` hands it to the host to
     feed `SheetWriter.seed()`. **Seeding is monotonic, so a stale number can never walk the
     guard backwards** — safe to pass optimistically rather than wait for the refetch.
   - **The guard:** the number is taken only when `versionOf === 'product'` — the same
     `currentVersion` name carries a `channelListing` version on other write paths
     (`products.routes.ts:2342` makes exactly that discrimination), and applying one row's
     version to another row's guard is the corruption `versionOf` was added to prevent. Reading
     `currentVersion` without `versionOf` would have worked today and broken silently the first
     time a restore ran on a channel-scoped path.
   - **Why it isn't cosmetic:** without it the sheet keeps the PRE-restore version and the
     operator's next cell edit gets a 409 — the guard working correctly, as a bounce the
     operator did not cause, cannot explain, and would report as a drawer bug. **The correct
     behaviour and the good experience only coincide once the version travels with the result.**
   - 2186 tests / 162 files (PES.3's `rows.vitest.test.ts` green again) · 0 type errors · nothing

224. **✅ #220 FIXED (PES.5) — the restore bumps `Product.version` inside its own transaction, READ
   BACK; and the assertion that matters is the surviving value, not the 409:**
   ```
   start v3
   restore 1 → 200, currentVersion 4 (product), DB v4    ✅ response == DB
   restore 2 → 200, currentVersion 5,           DB v5    ✅ chained
   stale sheet write with v3 → 409 VERSION_CONFLICT, currentVersion 5 (product)
      manufacturer still "PES5-RESTORED-2"  ← THE RESTORED VALUE SURVIVED
   ```
   - **"A 409 only proves the guard fired; the surviving value proves the thing the guard
     exists for."** Before the fix that stale write would have landed and undone the restore
     without a word. Response carries `currentVersion` + `versionOf: 'product'` like the bulk
     path, so PES.4 can chain a restore into a subsequent write as PES.3 does. tsc clean,
     5999/5999, §14.5. Fixture restored.
   - **⚠ Not to be over-read:** `Product.version` is still maintained by a handful of writers
     out of the 124 across 45 files (#94); the restore is now one of them. It remains a NARROW
     token — "nobody edited this through a path that maintains it", not "this row is unchanged".
   - **🔴 → OWNER QUEUE, evidence strengthened:** #183, #194 and #220 were the SAME defect
     class — a concurrency token that some writers maintain and others silently don't — each
     found by a different lane exercising a real path, none by a read-side check or a type.
     **Three writers in a row forgot the counter.** PES.5's standing recommendation for the #94
     architecture item is PES.8's value-comparison check (compare the fields you are about to
     overwrite against what you read, in the transaction) over a counter every writer must
     remember; the hub concurs — three independent instances is the case.

213. **✅ CHANNEL CAS RESTORED AND VERIFIED (PES.3) — three chained writes with no refetch, and the
   409 message names WHICH row or asserts no number at all:**
   ```
   start listing v22
   write 1 → ok, row.listing.version 23
   write 2 → ok, row.listing.version 24     ← the write that 409'd every time before
   write 3 → ok, row.listing.version 25
   STALE (v2) → conflict: "Someone else changed this listing (now v25). Reloading."
   ```
   Each +1, response == DB; raw-SQL read-back: eBay·IT at v25 holding the value, all four
   Amazon listings and the product untouched. Cleaned by removing the key, verified absent
   across the GALE family. The listing was at v22 when PES.3 started — exactly where PES.5's
   verification left it — so the two rehearsals chain end to end, a small confirmation that
   nothing else writes to that row.
   - **`versionOf` is consumed, not inferred:** a `channelListing` version is written straight
     back onto `row.listing` (which is what makes the chain work without a refetch) and is
     deliberately NOT returned as the write result's `version`, because the sheet writer
     applies that to the PRODUCT row it tracks — feeding one counter's number to the other row
     is precisely what made the old refusal say "v1" about a listing at 19. **Three message
     branches:** `channelListing` → "changed this **listing** (now v25)"; `product` → "changed
     this **product** (now vN)"; **neither → "Someone else changed this row first" — no number
     asserted.** The honest thing when the server didn't say which counter is to claim nothing.
   - **Rule applied to itself:** the first attempt was killed at a 2-minute timeout mid-flight;
     PES.3 checked the database before firing anything else — it HAD landed (v22 → 23). "A
     write whose result you didn't see is one you assume landed and go check." And: the bulk
     endpoint on this coordinate is slow enough that 2 minutes isn't enough for a four-write
     rehearsal — budget accordingly.
   - PES.3-25 records the restore and the chain. 100 channel tests · tsc clean · nothing
     committed. **"One write proves the statement runs; two prove the state it leaves behind is
     usable."** → PES.3's next item is #212's one line.

   PES.2's and PES.3's sheets — and a probe trap worth its own entry:**

     against a threshold of 1191. Genuinely covered.

     7 tests. Reads the panel's WIDTH (resizable 380–720; a hard-coded 520 is wrong on every
     drag of the grip). `revealDistance` never returns negative — it uncovers a cell, never
     re-centres a visible one. `StudioDock` fires `onRevealCell(colKey, panelWidth)` once per
     opened cell, keyed on row+cell (re-open after close reveals; re-render does nothing).
   - **Why the scroll is a seam, not a workaround:** the panel is portalled and holds no
     `GridApi`; the sheet holds it, no shared accessor exists (`contracts.tsx`/`types.ts`
     checked), and PES.4 would be the first `ensureColumnVisible` caller in the app. So the
     rule lives where it is testable as arithmetic and **the sheet performs the scroll through
     the capability it already owns.** `isCellCovered`/`revealDistance` are exported from the
     drawer barrel so nobody re-derives the threshold — one rule, two surfaces.
     **→ PES.2 (master) and PES.3 (channel): one line each beside the `StudioDock` mount —
     `onRevealCell={(colKey, w) => isCellCovered(...) && api.ensureColumnVisible(colKey,
     'start')}`; verify on screen that opening a record from a covered column scrolls it
     clear, and that opening from a visible column moves nothing.** `ScrollApiModule` is
     registered (#199).

     apparently entirely off-screen. It was not: `getAnimations()` showed `nds-slidein` at
     `playState: running, currentTime: 0` after 24 seconds — **the entrance animation's clock
     never ticked because the tab was not painting.** A screenshot forces a paint and the
     drawer is where it should be. **DOM geometry read in a background tab can report an
     entrance animation's FIRST FRAME as the resting state.** `getBoundingClientRect` is honest
     about what the compositor currently thinks, which is not what a user sees. Same family as
     the connection-starvation lesson; the DS modal drawer uses the identical keyframe.

209. **🔴 HUB WORDING CORRECTED (UX.1, §4.3c): "collapsing would free 16 against a 32 threshold"
   compared the WRONG two numbers — and that form invites the backwards fix:**
   - The rule is `R − C ≥ T` (at 962: 6 ≥ 32, fails), not `C ≥ T` (16 ≥ 32 — also fails, but
     for a reason that isn't the rule). **`C` is on the wrong side of the inequality: every
     pixel the collapse frees is handed to the grid and comes straight back out of `R`.**
     Measured across three collapse depths: at 906 (R=78) C=16 → armed (62), C=32 → armed
     (46), **C=48 → NOT armed (30)**; at 962 (R=22) nothing arms (6 / −10 / −26). **A deeper
     collapse disarms the feature at 906 and never rescues it at 962** — the most generous
     version, the header collapsing to nothing, is the one that stops working. The `C vs T`
     form's natural next question is "so collapse it further", and that answer makes it worse
     on the screen where it currently works. #206/#207 re-worded; §4.3c carries the table.
   - **The condition is ROW COUNT, not screen size.** A 40-row family arms at any viewport we
     support; the families that do not arm are the ones that nearly fit. "Doesn't work on big
     monitors" would send someone hunting for a monitor bug.
   - **UX.1 rules: NOTHING goes in the UI when it does not arm.** No "the header will not
     collapse because…" notice anywhere. An operator scrolling 22px sees the sheet barely
     move; chrome staying put is not a surprise that needs explaining, and a message about a
     non-event is worse than silence. Stated in §4.3c so nobody reads §6's honesty rules as
     requiring a notice — **the one place in the spec where saying nothing is the honest
     option, written down so no lane adds a well-meant banner.**
208. **✅ AG.1-c LANDED — "displayed ≠ real" FIXED: an operator's sort and pins survive every path
   that silently discarded them (AG.1, measured on screen):**
   - GALE-JACKET master, `name:asc` by header + `productType` pinned left, four triggers: view
     change Overview → Content (was: sort gone, pin gone → **both kept**, 19 → 16 cols) · view
     chip ON "Missing required" (→ both kept, 16 → 7) · chip OFF (→ both kept, back to 16) ·
     Customise → Save (was: pin gone → both kept). `aria-sort="ascending"` still on the header
     afterwards — survives where the operator can SEE it, not merely in `getColumnState()`. The
     identity block (`ag-Grid-AutoColumn`, `sku`, `completeness`) stays pinned throughout.
   - **The cause in one line:** `applyColumnState` changes only the properties an entry STATES,
     and an explicit `null` is a decision to CLEAR. `prefsToColumnState` stated `sort: null` and
     `pinned: null` on EVERY column, so every view application silently reset two things a view
     knows nothing about. **Width survived precisely because width was the one property the
     function never stated — the bug and its own control sat side by side.** Fix: omit what the
     bridge has no opinion about — `sort` only when the dialog names a sort column (others then
     cleared, so a new sort replaces rather than adds); `pinned` only for the padlocked
     lead/trail columns the bridge owns; the selection column states neither —
     `NexusGrid.keepSelectionFirst` owns its pin and the bridge was fighting the engine.
   - Files: `grid/columns/columnPrefs.ts` + its vitest. **`MasterSheet.tsx` untouched again.**
     5 new tests asserting the ABSENCE of a key (`'pinned' in entry === false` — `toBeNull()`
     and `toBeUndefined()` are different outcomes and only one preserves operator state);
     mutated back to always-state, exactly the two that should fail fail (2/20); restored 20/20.
     The on-screen table is the verification; the tests protect it.
   - Gates: web tsc 0 · grid vitest 256/18 files · conformance ✓ · import boundary ✓ · option
     identity ✓ · modules ✓. **Stated caveat:** a first tsc run reported one error a re-run did
     not reproduce — a sibling mid-write; reported as two runs, not one. Ratchet still red on
     PES.7's tabs (#203/#205).
   - Next: **AG.1-d** (drop the column-group strip + `marryChildren`, `applyOrder: true`, a
     real "Reset columns") — touches `MasterSheet.tsx` and `columns.tsx`, so the split is agreed
     with PES.2 in the ledger BEFORE editing (#184). The double-header defect is visible now:

     The endpoint CASes a channel write on the LISTING's version (`products.routes.ts:2202`)
     but the read gives only the PRODUCT's (`studio-sheet.service.ts:750`) — `SheetListing`
     has no `version`. **156 of 252 eBay·IT listings have a version differing from their
     product's** (BLACK-MEN-L: product v1 vs listing v66). Sending the product's number
     would 409 on **~62% of channel writes with a conflict that never happened** — and **a
     spurious conflict is worse than no CAS: it trains an operator to dismiss the one
     message that should always mean something.** PES.3 omits `expectedVersion` on any batch
     touching the channel (keeps it for master-only). **`version` on `SheetListing` closes
     it and the guard comes straight back.**

     channel scope, a write aimed at the wrong field. Master's precedent looked safe only

     EDITS, everywhere; open-record is explicit** — UX.1 decides whether the non-editable
     case keeps any double-click meaning.

     the 3XL eBay·IT listing; only the RESULT was lost. Removed, verified absent. **A write
     probe whose result you didn't see is a write you must assume landed and go check.**
