179. **✅ `dryRun` FIXED (#176 closed) — one-way by construction, proven by mutation with the
   gate LIVE (PES.7):**
   - **The guard is `isDryRunEnv() || callerRequestedRehearsal` — one-way by construction:**
     `true` forces a rehearsal; `false`/`undefined` defer to the gate; **a caller can never
     CAUSE a submission the gate would have prevented.** `AmazonBatchSubmission` gains
     `dryRun?: boolean` (optional, so the two `bulk-action.service.ts` callers with no
     per-call opinion are untouched); `...(dryRun ? {} : {})` becomes `dryRun,`. **The audit
     now records `result.dryRun` — what HAPPENED — with `requestedDryRun` kept as a
     separate field**, since those entries previously recorded intent while looking exactly
     like a record of outcome.
   - **Beyond the brief, on the record:** the no-SKU early return echoed the caller's
     request; that path never calls Amazon, so it now reports `dryRun: true` — echoing the
     wish there would claim a live submission on a path that cannot make one.
   - **The invariant is written in WITH ITS HISTORY:** with the gate closed the caller-flag
     half never changes an outcome and reads as dead code beside `isDryRunEnv()` — "which is
     exactly how it was lost the first time." The comment names that and the consequence of
     deleting either half.
   - **Proven by mutation, all three caught:** guard reduced to `isDryRunEnv()` alone → the
     "honours an explicit dryRun:true" test fails; forward deleted → source assertion fails;
     original empty spread restored → both fail. **The behavioural tests run with the gate
     LIVE, because that is the only configuration where the flag is load-bearing — a test
     with the gate closed passes whether or not the fix exists.** `amazon-sp-api` mocked to
     throw on construction so a regression fails loudly instead of reaching Amazon; one test
     asserts the live path IS entered when nothing requests a rehearsal, so the dry-run
     branch cannot quietly swallow everything and make the others vacuous.
   - **🔴 BANKED: tsc CANNOT catch the forward's removal.** `dryRun` is optional, so deleting
     `dryRun,` compiles cleanly (verified: exit 0 with it gone). **That is why SOURCE
     assertions sit beside the behavioural tests, and it is the mechanism by which the
     original bug survived review.**
   - **A trap walked into and fixed:** both source assertions failed on first run because
     **the fix's own explanatory comment QUOTES the bad pattern** — the "must not contain
     `...(x ? {} : {})`" assertion matched the explanation, and the `})` inside the quote
     truncated the extracted call. Now strips comments first. Same class as the DS guard
     that greps comments: **writing a good explanatory comment is enough to break a source
     guard.**

     re-measured after at the standing baseline (65/81/2 PUBLISHED/24). No publish fired.

176. **🔴🔴 `dryRun` IS NEVER FORWARDED — a latent safety defect that fires the moment the
   publish gate opens (PES.7; P5 COMPLETE):**
   - **The defect, structural:** in `submitAmazonImageFeed`, `...(dryRun ? {} : {})` — **an
     empty object in BOTH branches** — and `AmazonBatchSubmission` has no `dryRun` field, so
     the "override" the comment describes does not exist. Submission is decided SOLELY by
     `getAmazonPublishMode() !== 'live'`. **With the mode `live`, a request carrying
     `dryRun: true` submits a REAL feed — and the audit records `dryRun: true`.** Latent
     today because all three channels are gated; **it bites the instant the gate opens.**
   - **→ OWNER, top of the queue, gating the gate:** the publish flag must NOT be flipped to
     live until this is fixed. **→ PES.7 AUTHORIZED to fix** under the unclaimed-territory
     pattern (they found it, they hold the context, the service is unclaimed), with #154's
     conditions: forward the flag so `dryRun: true` NEVER submits regardless of mode; log
     what HAPPENED, not what was asked; provable no-op today (gate closed — nothing changes
     until it opens); re-verify at the moment of the change; disclose the file; write the
     invariant into the code with a note explaining why it must not be "simplified".
   - **PES.7 had shipped the same lie:** `PublishPanel` computed the outcome as
     `res.data?.dryRun || dryRun || plan.rehearsalOnly` — **the request flag wins that OR**,
     so with the gate live it would have submitted a real feed and then reported "nothing
     was submitted to Amazon". Fixed both halves: outcome from the server's answer alone
     with `undefined` as its own state ("the server did not say"); the checkbox no longer
     offers a choice the endpoint can't honour — disabled, reflecting the gate, reason in
     visible text.
   - **A retraction that follows:** "38 starts, all `dryRun: false`" had been read as "these
     were real Amazon submissions". **The audit records what was ASKED FOR; whether a feed
     was submitted depended on the publish mode at the time, which the audit does not
     record.** Struck.
   - **TWO LESSONS, banked:** (1) **an API accepting, defaulting, returning and logging a
     safety parameter is not evidence it honours it — follow it to the call that would ACT
     on it.** Four of the five places `dryRun` appeared were honest; the fifth was the only
     one that mattered. (2) **Never OR a safety outcome with local intent — the local value
     wins the OR precisely when the server disagrees.**
   - **The planner (D1's mandatory piece) is built:** leads with DESTINATIONS, not targets,
     taken from `options.channels` — **11 Amazon markets, not the 5 inferred from the audit
     log** (the DB's own answer beating a sample inference, again). Selecting Amazon
     IT+DE+ES + eBay IT renders *"4 targets, but only 2 destinations — some of them
     overwrite each other"*, names Country-Specific Upload and A+ Content as the two
     mechanisms that would give per-country images, and says neither is automated here.
     Button reads "Rehearse 4 targets" from the server's gate. **Not pressed** — the
     sequential-fire path is typechecked and unexercised, stated as such.
   - 318 tests / 20 files, both tsc 0, 15 guards green. **P5 COMPLETE.** Next: P6/P7
     ancillary → §5 parity audit.

171. **⚙ CHANNEL-WRITE DESIGN RULED (PES.5's four choices, #58/#169) — the layer already
   exists; only the write side is missing:**
   - **The good news, measured:** `ChannelListing.overrideData` (JSONB, "PIM A.1 channel-level
     master attribute overrides") is ALREADY resolved by `resolveAttributes` as
     `channelOverride` — above master/variant, below the explicit *Override columns
     (attribute-resolver.ts:258). Cascade, provenance and the sheet's `layer`/`pinned`
     rendering work the moment something writes it. **`overrideData` is `{}` on ALL 977 rows;
     exactly ONE writer exists in the whole API.** A pure write-side gap.
   - **RULED 1 — `target: 'master' | 'channel'` per change, defaulting to `'master'`.**
     Not the prefix map (`ebay_attr_material` explodes the namespace and makes the client
     mangle names). Defaults to today's behaviour so no caller changes; **the write contract
     becomes the mirror of the read contract** — PES.3 echoes back the `writeTarget` the
     sheet read gave it instead of deriving a name. The six prefixed fields keep working.
   - **RULED 2 — `marketplaceContexts[].aliasKey`, optional, `''` = primary, and a MISSING
     aliasKey is NEVER defaulted to primary.** The studio edits one scope at a time; R.1's
     fan-out semantics stay intact; the silent-wrong-listing failure both lanes avoided on
     the read side (#142) is refused on the write side too.
   - **RULED 3 — channel writes CAS on the LISTING's own `version`** (NN.1, schema:1643) and
     return it, same 409 semantics. The alternative (CAS on `Product.version`) is simpler

     pre-restart log (~5 hours of wall clock between first and last logged entry). Neon's
     `-pooler` endpoint is the host named. `[sidebar/counts] failed` ×30, `premature close`

     + `pricingRule=FIXED` — the combination for which `computeListingPrice` returns exactly
     the master price — yet only 63 have `price = basePrice`. 155 DIVERGE.** The zeros are

151. **🔴 "A CAUSE IS NOT A VERDICT" — 399 writes that NEVER REACHED THE CHANNEL were being
   called fine (PES.5, self-caught):**
   - **All 399 `throttled` rows are `isDead=true`, retryCount 3/3, `nextRetryAt=null`** —
     they **exhausted their retries WHILE being throttled. They will never run again. The
     write never reached the channel.** The classifier was saying *"deferred by our own
     throttle — it will retry without you"*, `actionable: false`, **which is false for every
     one of them.** On PES.3's pane, 33 of the 36 rows being toned quiet are **writes that
     silently never happened** — "telling an operator that 399 writes which never occurred
     are fine is the exact failure class this classifier exists to remove, one level down."
   - **Corrected model — `actionable` depends on whether the row can still PROGRESS, not on
     cause alone**, plus a new `reasonWillRetry`: throttled+runnable → not actionable
     ("will retry without you", genuinely true) · **throttled+DEAD → ACTIONABLE** ("gave up
     while throttled; never reached the channel") · internal+DEAD → ACTIONABLE ·
     **gated+DEAD → still not actionable but now says "enabling the flag will not resend
     this row"** — *the difference between paused and lost* · rejected → actionable either
     way. **Actionable: 1,780 → 2,185.** eBay·IT's "3 need you" → **36**, "the opposite of
     the reassurance currently on screen — I'd rather hand them that number than let the
     quieter one stand."
   - **Safe-by-default API:** calling `deriveFailureReason` WITHOUT the `isDead` option
     keeps the old retry-optimistic reading, so **a caller that doesn't know deadness cannot
     silently receive the dead verdict.**
   - **🔴 THE LESSON, banked: A CAUSE IS NOT A VERDICT.** `throttled` correctly describes
     WHY a write stalled; it took the row's STATE to know whether anyone still needs to
     care. **And validating the classifier against its own distribution proved nothing here
     — "the distribution was right and the interpretation was wrong."** (2,553 rows, clean
     split, gated:368 matching exactly — all true, all silent about this.) **An argument for
     shipping a classifier to a REAL SURFACE early: only a consumer rendering it on screen
     revealed it.**
   - **Credit recorded as PES.5 asked:** PES.3's *"grouping without weighting is only half
     the honesty"* is what made this findable — 36 undifferentiated rows and nobody looks at
     the 33.
   - Mutation-checked using #144's own applied-assertion habit: dropping the dead override
     fails 3 tests, **and the patch was asserted to have landed** rather than trusted.

142. **🟢 SKU + ALIAS ON QUEUE ROWS (PES.5, §13.1) — the alias was SERVER-knowable, and the
   THREE-STATE answer is the point:**
   - **SKU on every row**, verified 200/200 on a full page across 21 distinct products —
     exactly PES.3's cause-group case.

     alias, but a row linked to a `channelListingId` reaches one via
     `ChannelListing.aliasKey`. **Measured on the GALE family: 396 of 441 rows (90%)
     resolve**; the other 45 are product-only and genuinely cannot.
   - **🔴 THE THREE STATES, distinct ON PURPOSE:** `aliasKey ""` + `aliasResolved true` =
     known to be the PRIMARY listing · `aliasId "<id>"` + resolved = known to be that alias
     · `aliasKey null` + `aliasResolved false` = **UNKNOWN, and not "primary"**.
     **`""` (known primary) and `null` (unknown) are different answers, and collapsing them
     is exactly the bug PES.3 sidestepped by shipping scope-only jumping.** PES.3 can now
     jump precisely for 90% and stay scope-only for the rest, **without either lane
     guessing.** (Same family as the readiness `pct: null` rule — an honest vocabulary
     needs a value for "unknown" that is not a plausible-looking real value.)
   - **⚠ DELIBERATE BOUNDARY, ratified:** the server returns **COMPONENTS** (productId, sku,
     aliasId, aliasKey, aliasResolved), **NOT a composed sheet row id** — "the sheet owns
     its `alias:productId` format; encoding that server-side would couple us and break
     quietly the moment they change it." The server resolves the one piece only it can
     know; the sheet composes. → PES.3's call if they'd rather have the composed id, taken
     knowingly rather than assumed.
   - Cost: **two BATCHED reads per page** (listings, then products), never per row — a
     200-row page would otherwise be 400 queries. 812ms for 200 rows.
   - **→ APPROVED, small and it serves honesty: a derived REASON from errorCode so the 368
     gated-refusal rows are distinguishable from genuine failures.** They currently sit in
     `dead` alongside real rejections, and **"refused because publishing is switched off"
     reads very differently from "Amazon rejected this"** — a console that conflates them
     misreports the health of the channel. PES.5 to add, PES.3 to render.

     act on — **with the opposite sign: falsely clean rather than falsely blocked, which is
     the worse direction.**

118. **⚙ REGISTRY GAPS RULED — preflight→run payload APPROVED; parameter ORDER fixed
   (2026-09-01 ~20:05; both found by WRITING verbs against the type, not reading it):**
   - **(1) APPROVED, → PES.2 to land: `ActionImpact.payload?: unknown` + `run(rows,
     impact?)`.** Without it, pull-from-channel must fetch the channel TWICE — and the
     second call is the one that gets throttled (the old ChannelListingTab wrapped exactly
     this call in rate-limit retry) — and worse, it opens a **TOCTOU the confirmation
     cannot cover: the operator approves snapshot A and `run` applies snapshot B.** A
     confirm describing data that is not what lands is precisely the dishonesty the whole
     shape exists to prevent. The registry stays ignorant of the payload's meaning; only
     the producing lane reads it. Optional both sides — no existing verb changes.
   - **(2) RULED, no type change: the ORDER is COLLECT → PREFLIGHT → CONFIRM → RUN.** A
     parameterised verb (broadcast: "which sibling coordinates?") owns its picker in the
     lane, runs it FIRST, then folds the choice into the impact it returns — so the

     unchanged". **A CAS that SUCCEEDS can still overwrite a sync job's write.**

     makes it look reliable is worse than the honest narrow semantics, because the next
     consumer would trust it further." **→ OWNER/ARCHITECTURE QUEUE:** make it real (bump
     via Prisma extension covering all writers, with the bulk-path cost weighed) or accept
     the narrow semantics and rename the field. The 124/45 measurement rides the item.
   - **Consumers warned (also named in the code comment now):** PES.2's SheetWriter
     autosave (its 409 protection guards against other EDITOR writes only), the
     products-catalog inline grid (~:1213), and PES.8's AI draft-apply (can win its CAS and

     row's obligations make an empty slot a problem, and a cell renderer cannot see them.
     PES.7's matrix-level count is the better home by design, not accident.

     "a warn on a cell with no picture is deliberately unreachable", asserting the behaviour
     and explaining it, so the next person finds an answer instead of an hour of renderer
     debugging. The same test pins the easily-conflated REACHABLE neighbour: `refused` on an
     src-less cell (a failed upload must never read as an untouched slot). And where the
     change goes if a future surface needs per-tile required-and-empty is written down: the
     precedence, never the caller.

Active here: none"* + `availableChannels: []` — but `/api/marketplaces` says **AMAZON IS active on PL**; the message asserts a fact about marketplace CONFIG while reporting one about listing PRESENCE (`present` filters to coordinates carrying listings). An operator starting on PL — the D9 "List on…" path — is sent to check a connection that is fine. · ⚠ **BE-15 DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED (symptom stands, cause was wrong — PES.5 told directly before acting).** I filed it as `present`-vs-configuration confusion; **it is not** — the channel path passes `includeEmptyChannels: true` (`studio-sheet.service.ts:630`) so `present` is undefined, and PL's Amazon row IS active (all 19 marketplace rows are). **Real cause: `coordinatesFor:393`'s `only` narrowing runs BEFORE the throw, and `:639` builds `availableChannels` from the already-narrowed list** — so it is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION every time the error fires, and "Active here: none" can never be true. PL has Amazon; correct answer is `['AMAZON']`. **This is a side-effect of PES.5's BE-1 fix** — the `only` narrowing is right and also narrowed what the error message reads from; the throw was fixed, the message is the half left behind. My PRESCRIPTION survives (derive `availableChannels` un-narrowed). Also: I nearly handed PES.5 an 8-row call-site sweep table built with a crude 6-line grep window — it mislabelled `studio-sheet.service.ts:619` as un-narrowed when the full call passes both options; verified BEFORE sending, not after. · **CLOSED by PES.5 (#295) — BOTH my hypotheses wrong, AND my replacement claim too.** The Amazon·IT "variance" is the mapping enrichment's 8s budget timing out while its Redis queue connects (cold 25.9s, warm-1 18.4s, then 6.0/2.4/1.7s once connected); it decays and whichever scope loads first pays it. My four "identical warm requests" were a decay curve sampled in the other direction — not contention, not a serial await. **And "DE/ES are FASTER than IT" is ALSO wrong as a causal claim** (DE was measured on an already-warm queue): market is not the variable in EITHER direction. Two retractions on one number in opposite directions before an in-request instrument found it. **Outside-the-request timing could not have answered this** — it localises cost to a route, never tells you what the route waits on. Consequence is BE-4's class: the derived column renders SILENTLY EMPTY while the budget times out (→ PES.2). Coordinate count 5 confirmed correct vs PES.5's 2. · **+BE-16** (my BE-15 tail question → PES.5 measured it → I corroborated via a DIFFERENT path): the presence-filtered column build hides a channel the rest of the studio shows. `/studio/columns` master scope — IT 102 cols `[Amazon·IT, eBay·IT]` · **DE 96 cols `[Amazon·DE]` only, eBay·DE INVISIBLE** · PL 30 cols, zero coordinates — while `/readiness?market=DE` (which passes `includeEmptyChannels`) DOES return eBay·DE as a chip. **The scope bar offers a channel the column build cannot see**, and enrichment reads the blind one (`generate.service.ts:241`). ⚠ I did NOT verify PES.5's "DE has real listings" — `present` is a PLATFORM-WIDE groupBy, so eBay·DE's absence may be correct for a presence view; the surface DISAGREEMENT is measured, the populated-market characterisation is theirs. **§3 item 11 rewritten to keep BOTH halves** on PES.5's fair objection: the restore DOCTRINE is sound (coordinate guard, undo-in-transaction, allow-list excluding `version`, forced DRAFT) and the code was dead from one field name in a string array no type could check — what is retracted is the EVIDENCE CLASS, not the verdict. "Reviewed favourably, never run" is the right lesson about my METHOD and the wrong verdict on that CODE. · **BE-16 SEVERITY CORRECTED DOWN 🟠→🟡** — PES.5 counted listings after I declined to absorb their "market with real listings" phrase: `AMAZON:DE 214 / ES 123 / FR 115 / IT 273 / EBAY:IT 252`. **EBAY:IT is the ONLY populated eBay coordinate platform-wide**, so `present` excluding eBay·DE is CORRECT for a presence view — nothing populated is hidden and the implied severity does not exist. **What survives is the better half:** `/readiness` offers eBay·DE as a scope chip while the column build behind that scope cannot see it — a defect however many listings exist, and PES.8's lead. **+ PES.5's sharpest consequence:** the same filter is why master is 147 cols on IT and 142 elsewhere — IT isn't special, it's where the eBay listings are, so **the extra cap appears the moment anyone creates a first eBay·DE listing: a constraint that tightens under an operator who did nothing.** A presence-derived schema changes when someone else sells something.

## UX.1 — layout v2 spec DELIVERED, and a correction to a number I put in this file

**`docs/2026-09-01-layout-v2-spec.md`** — measured on the running studio (GALE-JACKET, local web
:3000 → local API :8091), every claim tagged ⟦measured⟧ or ⟦derived⟧ with the model stated.

**🔴 CORRECTION to my own first report, which the hub recorded above.** I told the hub "chrome
above the sheet is 297px, sheet = 60.2%" and "8 default columns totalling 1149 of 1660px — 511px
of unused width". The 297 is right. **The other two are wrong, and both are the same mistake: I
measured the loading skeleton.**
- **60.2% counts the AG header as sheet.** The AG header is 87px (column-group strip 30 + header
  row 28 + floating filters 29). What an operator calls the sheet — rows of data — is
  **458 of 906px = 50.6%.** The Owner's "almost 60%" was generous.
- **There is no unused width.** Loaded, the master `Overview` view is **2749px** of columns in a
  1660px viewport — 1089px of horizontal scroll, and 1537px at 1280. The sheet is not short of
  columns; it is short of *screen*.
Lanes that took the 511px figure from me (DS.1 said it reframed their spacing work): it is
withdrawn. Same family as the inherited-number trap — I introduced one, so I am retiring it by
name.

**The four numbers the spec is built on** (all ⟦measured⟧, master scope, GALE-JACKET):
1. **Rows are 50.6% of the viewport at 1728×906.** Band stack: AppTopBar 56 · header 48 · scope 44
   · tabs 34 · family bar 49 · toolbar 65 · AG header 87 · **rows 458** · footer 40 · gutter 24.
   The three bands nobody had counted (family bar, toolbar, AG header) are **201px**.
2. **"Barely a few columns" = four.** At 1728 with the drawer docked, the columns FULLY visible are
   select · tree · SKU · Master% · Markenname · Name · Product Type — and Status is clipped. Of the
   **seven fields Amazon requires for OUTERWEAR, one is on screen.** At 1280 drawer-closed: also
   one of seven. **The columns you can see are the ones already filled; the work is off-screen.**
3. **The channel scope's default view is 15664px wide** — 11.4 screens at 1372px. Ruling #173's
   default-view rule reached master and never reached the channel scopes. → PES.3/PES.2.
4. **The channel toolbar is 102px tall for FOUR controls** (Warnings pill, listing count, Preflight,
   + Add listing alias) spread over three rows, with 1077px of horizontal emptiness on row 1. One
   40px row holds all four. 62px, free.

**What v2 wins: +164px of rows at every viewport height** (the saving is vertical, so it is
width-independent). 458 → 622 at 906 (50.6% → 68.7%); 369 → 533 at 817; 452 → 616 at a derived
1440×900.

**Three rulings other lanes should read before they build:**
- **The slide-over is NON-MODAL** (§5). Four reasons, and the fourth decides it: at
  `--nds-z-rail` the drawer sits BELOW `--nds-z-overlay` (1400), so `ActionConfirm` lands on top
  **by construction** — `reference_drawer_confirm_overlay` cannot recur, no new token is needed,
  and DS.1 is not made a prerequisite for a layout change. Choosing modal would have required
  solving the z-race first. Consequences (no backdrop, no focus trap, `aria-modal` absent) follow
  from the one choice rather than being separate decisions. **Esc is owned by the innermost
  focused thing** — drawer if focus is in it, cell editor if a cell is editing (Esc reverts, per
  `SHEET_GRID_OPTIONS`). PES.4: also §5.4 — on open, scroll the grid so the originating cell is
  not underneath the 520px panel.
- **Collapse arming, as an invariant** (§4.2): collapse is armed iff `R − C ≥ T` **where `R` is
  measured against EXPANDED geometry**. The arming test must never be recomputed from collapsed
  geometry — that is the loop, in one sentence. And a result worth knowing: **at v2's own
  proportions a 21-row family at 906px with 28px rows has R = 22 and never collapses at all**
  (the height saving removes the range the trigger depends on). That is the rule working, not a
  defect. Also: **do not animate the height** — `GridSheet` re-measures through a ResizeObserver on
  `document.body`, so a 200ms height animation makes AG re-virtualise every frame. Animate the
  header's contents, snap the height.
- **🔴 PES.1's #172 constraint "one compact row overflows at 1440" does NOT bind the real
  components.** Measured intrinsic widths: label 50 + 6 chips 561 + 5 tabs 450 + market/locale 192
  + gaps 32 = **1285, and the container at 1440 is 1374.** It fits with 89px spare. PES.1's
  1520–1550 came from a mock of **9 channel×market chips**; the studio has 6 channel chips and a
  separate market switcher. The constraint is true of what was mocked and not of what exists — so
  the spec carries the real breakpoint instead: **it overflows at 1280 (1285 > 1214)**, and Tier B
  fixes that with icon-only inactive tabs (1109 ≤ 1214). **Channel×market chips are refused**: nine
  need a ~1983px viewport, and the real cross-product is 6 channels × 4 markets = **24**, not 9.

**Three things went to the Owner as questions rather than assumptions** (§12): the AppTopBar is the
only lever that reaches their stated 90–95% (83–85% without it, 89–91% with it dropped on this
route, costing ⌘K and notifications); the thumbnail's price (32px thumb on a 36px row = 17 rows;
/products/next's 56px on 85px = **7 rows**, which would undo everything the height budget just
won); and chips staying channel-only.

**And the Owner's warnings strip, located and diagnosed** (§6): `button.nds-pill.warning`
"Warnings (42)" at x1144 y214 on the channel scope, `⚠ Missing required (42)` in the same slot on
master. Contrast is fine (8.05:1, computed) — the styling is not the problem. **It is a filter
wearing a warning's clothes**: clicking it narrows the sheet, yet it carries a ⚠, a warning tint
and a permanent count in the corner the eye reaches first when scanning column headers. It looks
urgent, is never urgent, never goes away — and it occupies the slot a real warning would need. The
spec splits them: counts-of-work become **views** (neutral, counted, in the view control);
provenance warnings go **inline in the footer** beside the save state, where `adapted read` and
`N refused` already live — one honesty surface, not two; refusals stay **on the cell**; and
**nothing may be dismissable into silence** (a count may collapse, it may not be ✕'d).

### UX.1 — spec AMENDED after the DS.1 + AG.1 audits (same session, later)

Four changes, one of which changes what the Owner is told. Full text in the spec.

- **🔴 Owner complaint (5) is a BROKEN CONTROL, not a polish item.** AG.1 traced the sheet's select
  editor: the DS `Listbox` portals to `document.body` and autofocuses its search box, AG sees focus
  leave the cell, fires `cellEditingStopped` and unmounts the editor with the panel inside it —
  **2ms, open to gone.** The operator gets a trigger that cannot be opened. Consequence for my §7:
  it **passed my horizontal-scroll invariant for the wrong reason** — it cannot widen the document
  because it is destroyed before it can. My own sweep would have recorded it compliant
  ([[reference_a_scanner_passing_for_the_wrong_reason]]). The Owner's *other* dropdown complaint
  (opens right, widens the page) is now down to **one** unexamined surface, the floating-filter
  popups — DS.1 cleared the DS combo, the Publish menu and AG's column menu at 1440; AG.1 cleared
  the select.
- **🔴 I specified a call that throws.** §5.4 was written against `ensureColumnVisible`;
  **`ScrollApiModule` is not registered** in `design-system/grid/modules.ts`. I wrote it from AG's
  API surface rather than this repo's registration. PES.4 is marked BLOCKED on §5.4 in §11 so
  nobody builds against it. Loud cousin of [[reference_ag_module_silent_omission]] — and the same
  gap will bite the `Missing required (42)` chip the moment its stated job (take me *to* those
  cells) becomes real.
- **§9.2's ordering rule was unimplementable and now carries three preconditions (§9.2a).**
  `marryChildren: true` makes AG discard a whole declared ordering (warning #39), which is why
  `applyPreset` passes `applyOrder: false` — a view's column order is thrown away silently today.
  Preconditions: drop the married groups · `applyOrder: true` · decide whose order wins on reload
  (`useGridState` persists AG's entire `getState()` to localStorage on every `stateUpdated`, so a
  single historic column drag outlives every view change). Adopted: rule wins on fresh load,
  explicit operator reorder wins until reset, **"Reset columns" becomes a real menu item** — not
  offered today because `columnDialog` passes only `customise` and AG's own Reset was removed
  without replacement.
- **The column-group strip is CONFIRMED dropped, on AG.1's reasons rather than mine.** Mine was a
  preference; theirs is a defect — the strip **draws its header twice** once an operator pins a
  column (measured), against a code comment asserting the very condition pinning falsifies. Budget
  settled at 56px.

Also folded from DS.1: 40px stays a literal because **the DS has no control-height scale at all**
(`var(--nds-toolbar-h)` would resolve to nothing and silently collapse the bar — token added only
*after* the Owner ratifies §2.1); the 32px thumb needs nothing new (`compact.thumb` is 32), and the
36px row is a **new ROW KIND, not a fourth tier** (`rowMedia` is 52 because it stacks photo · title
· sub-line). **DS.1 also stopped me quoting "52px costs 10 rows" to the Owner** — neither they nor
PES.2 has refused the ask, and costing a refusal nobody made puts a number in the Owner's head that
is nobody's position. Worth generalising: a conditional cost is still an assertion about someone
else's unstated position.

### UX.1 — #182 folded in; the spec is APPROVED and every number re-derived

The AppTopBar removal changes every figure in the budget, so §2, §4.3, §8.2, §10's five mockups and
§12 were re-derived rather than annotated. Arithmetic re-checked end to end after the edit.

**The new budget (AppTopBar dropped, 36px rows):**
| | today | v2 at rest | v2 collapsed |
|---|---|---|---|
| rows @1728×906 | 458 (50.6%) | **678 (74.8%)** | **694 (76.6%)** |
| sheet @1728×906 | 700 (77.3%) | **810 (89.4%)** | **826 (91.2%)** |
| rows @1440×817 | 369 (45.2%) | **589 (72.1%)** | 605 (74.1%) |
| channel rows @1440×817 | 424 (51.9%) | **616 (75.4%)** | — |
**+220px of rows at every viewport height** (was +164 before the AppTopBar came out); **18.8 rows
visible at 906 with a 32px thumbnail**, against 16.4 today at 28px with none.

**🔴 The finding that came out of re-deriving, and it matters to PES.1 and PES.2 both: the Owner's
two answers depend on each other.** At 28px rows the v2 budget leaves the grid **zero scroll
range** (`S` = 644 vs a 678px viewport) — so the collapsing header could never fire, on any family,
at 906px. The 36px row ratified for the thumbnail is what restores the range (`S` = 812, `R` = 134,
armed). **Anyone who "optimises" the row back to 28px silently kills the collapsing header**, and
the failure would look like a collapse bug rather than a density change. §4.3 states it.

**§5.5 — the gesture map (hub item 182b), generalised past §7.3's local case.** AG.1 measured the
collision as the NORMAL case (95 of 100 columns editable) and PES.3 found their own double-click
handler opening an editor on the WRONG cell after the drawer's reflow. Ruled: **double-click EDITS,
everywhere; a record opens only from an explicit affordance** (identity-cell control, `open-record`
verb, Enter on the identity cell). And the gap the hub asked me to close: today typing **replaces**
(destructive), F2 edits (undiscoverable) and Enter navigates — **there is no discoverable
non-destructive way to start editing.** So: **Enter on a focused editable cell starts editing with
the value preserved**; Enter while editing still commits and moves down; Enter on the identity cell
(`sku.editable === false`, measured) opens the record, safe because that cell has no other meaning
for Enter; vertical movement goes to ↓↑. Requires `enterNavigatesVertically: false` (AG.1) **and a
new footer hint string** (PES.2) — the current one advertises `Enter ↓` and becomes false the moment
this lands ([[reference_docs_describe_deleted_code]] in the one place an operator actually reads).
Note for PES.3/PES.4: **their wrong-cell bug is fixed twice over** — the slide-over removes the
reflow, this ruling removes the second handler; either alone would have hidden the other.

**§7.3 — the anchoring clause (hub item 182b).** DS.1's framing, adopted: *an invariant that a live
complaint satisfies is an incomplete invariant.* My `scrollWidth === clientWidth` rule held on every
popup two lanes could open — and AG's `agLargeTextCellEditor` still floats detached over the
drawer's gallery with `scrollWidth` steady at 1440. §7 now demotes "never widens the page" to
necessary-but-not-sufficient and adds: **a popup must stay anchored to the element that opened it,
and close or reposition when its anchor moves, is occluded, or scrolls away.** DS1-8's guard must
assert the OUTCOME, never portal parentage — parentage would fail AG's correctly-clamping column
menu (§7.2) and pass this one. Banked to shared memory as the general form: a green sweep against an
incomplete invariant is worse than no sweep, because it retires the suspects.

**Still blocked, not open:** §5.4 waits on AG.1 registering `ScrollApiModule` (PES.4 must not build
against a throwing call); `var(--nds-toolbar-h)` must not be written until DS.1 mints it.


## DS.1 rulings & hand-offs (nexus-commerce-e2) — read before touching DS tokens or styles

**These are decisions, not status.** I had been answering them in messages; the hub kept re-asking because
a decision announced only in a message is not recorded. That is my own "a finding filed is not a finding
landed" inverted, so they live here now.

1. **`--nds-z-*` RULED (#232): AG's popups take `--nds-z-popover` (1450), the DS popover layer.**
   Scale: `sticky 5 · actionbar 20 · rail 50 · overlay 1400 · drawer 1410 · popover 1450 · toast 1600 ·
   tooltip 1700`. AG renders its column menu at **5** (`--nds-z-sticky`) — **below the rail (50)**. That
   is not a rival convention, it is an accident that has not bitten only because AG's menus are short and
   bottom-anchored. A column menu, a rich-select list and a filter popup ARE popovers.
   🔴 **TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN RULING, both mine, both verified since (#244):**
   (a) I told AG.1 to **pin the value through the Theming API. That route does not exist** — AG 36.1's
   theming types contain **zero** z-index params (`grep -rniE zindex .../dist/types/src/theming/` → no
   hits). AG.1 pinned `.ag-popup-child` in `grid/theme/grid.css` instead, unscoped because it portals to
   `body`, which is the only available mechanism. **I asserted a mechanism without checking it, in the
   same message where I had properly verified `popupShadow` by grepping AG's types** — I applied the
   discipline to one claim and not to the one beside it.
   (b) I stated the consequence as "above a slide-over drawer (1410)". **The slide-over is not at 1410.**
   `.nds-drawer-dock` computes `var(--nds-z-rail)` = **50** (#182's design: non-modal, below
   `--nds-z-overlay` 1400 so `ActionConfirm` lands on top by construction). 1410 is `--nds-z-drawer`,
   used by the MODAL `.nds-drawer` at `components.css:429` — a different surface. Verified both myself
   rather than taking the correction. The conclusion survives: popovers at 1450 above a non-modal panel
   is correct, and no new token is needed. To be proven, not asserted, on
   UX.1's `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs` popover harness (3 popovers x 3 widths).
   ✅ **RESOLVED (#240): `--nds-z-topbar: 60` minted** (both apps, generators run, fork-drift green) and
   adopted at `app/_shared/app-topbar.css:50` — **unclaimed file, disclosed edit**. Verified on screen:
   `HEADER.nds-topbar` computes `z-index: 60`, not `auto`, so the token resolves in that scope; rail 50;
   bar above rail. No pixel moved.
   🔴 **I mis-framed this when I filed it.** I called it "a layer nobody named"; in fact
   `app-topbar.css:47` already carried the reason — *the rail hover-expands to 344px and must slide UNDER
   the bar* — so **the 60 was reasoned and correct and only the NAME was missing**. That is why placing it
   on an existing step would have been wrong: 50 would have tied it with `--nds-z-rail` and broken a
   documented invariant. **A literal encoding a decision is not the same defect as a literal encoding an
   accident** (AG's 5 was the latter). Read the comment before ruling on the number.

2. **DS.2's `styles/components.css:818` line CONFIRMED (#231) — it stays, no revert.** DS.2 restored the
   Listbox panel's min-width floor as a class on the panel; the fix is half a class in `Listbox.tsx`
   (theirs) and half a rule in the stylesheet (mine under #222). **Splitting an atomic two-line fix
   across a lane boundary would have left a class with no rule or a rule with no class** — a boundary
   applied that way is being applied wrongly. Their measurement is decisive
   (`pop.matches('.nds-listbox .nds-combo-pop') === false`, `minWidth: 0px`, while the rule sat loaded
   and plausible in `document.styleSheets`), and they swept for the same shape rather than fixing the one
   instance. **Standing disclosure: DS.2 may edit `design-system/styles/**` with a note.** I would rather
   have their fix and a disclosure than a clean boundary and a broken component.

3. **`--nds-gutter-content: 16px` MINTED (#222)** — `css-vars.ts` in BOTH apps, both generators run,
   `tokens:check` in sync, fork-drift green. **It changes no pixel today and that is the point**: the
   four content-left edges DS.2 first measured are already down to two (PES.1 and PES.2 each fixed their
   half) and every surviving band agrees on 16px. The token NAMES that agreement so the next band does
   not pick 14 the way `.nds-grid-footstrip` did. A named ROLE, not an `--nds-space-N` step — the space
   scale is 1px-granular and is used **once in 429 spacing declarations** across the DS's own
   stylesheets, so a step token demonstrably does not get adopted (DS.2's census).
   Residuals, both deliberate and neither a gutter mismatch: the **1px** between frame bands (82) and
   sheet bands (83) is `.nds-gridcard`'s border — UX.1's §2 card question, and if the border goes they
   align for free; the **128px** right padding on the status bar is `--nds-fab-reserve-inline` keeping
   text out from under the Ask-AI button.

4. **`GridSheetNote` BUILT and handed to PES.2 (#230)** — `design-system/grid/toolbars/GridSheetNote.tsx`
   + `grid.css` rules, exported from the toolbars barrel. Two kinds; **the kind owns the glyph and tone,
   never the bar** (§6.3). **No `onDismiss` prop exists, and its absence is the design** — "never
   dismissable into silence" was a convention every caller could forget; an absent prop is one the type
   system refuses. The DS `Banner` was checked first and is page-scale (18px icon, title, description,
   action, dismiss) against a 40px strip.

5. **`.d.ts` freeze pass: the count is 42, not the 36 I first reported** — it grew as lanes edited
   components. DS.2's `Menu.d.ts` regen is verified out of the list (I checked the count, not the
   reasoning). The rest stays mine at the freeze.

## PES.5 notes for other lanes (read `docs/pes5-phase0-backend.md`)
- **PES.2 / PES.3:** API contracts are in §3 — `/api/products/:id/studio/{columns,sheet,history}` + `/api/products/:id/readiness`
  + alias CRUD. `StudioCellValue` carries `layer` / `pinned` / `follows` / `writeField` / `writeTarget`,
  so the grid never re-derives where a cell writes. Not implemented yet — do not code against it until approved.
- **PES.3:** the primary listing is returned as an `AliasGroup` with `id: null`, so aliases are ONE
  uniform list with no special case. There is deliberately **no** family-total quantity field —
  quantity is per alias and must never be summed.
- **PES.3:** 22 `EBAY_LISTING_SHELL` products in prod are the existing alias workaround (§0 F2).
- **PES.4:** per-cell history today records *when* + the *new* value only; *who* and *previous value*
  are not written (§0 F3). The contract carries `coverageSince` for the honest empty state. Do not
  design the history panel around a full old→new diff until decision 2 in §8 is approved.
- **PES.1:** your `GET /api/products/:id/readiness?market=` shape is ADOPTED VERBATIM, including `pct: null`
  + `note` when it cannot be computed. One call for every chip. ⚠ Your `ready|warn|blocked|absent` scope
  states and the shipped row-level `ReadinessState` (`ready|missing|errors|live|unlisted`) are different
  vocabularies — see §3.3; neither lane should map one onto the other locally.

## PES.6 notice — additive edits inside PES.5-owned resolver files (read before merging)

Layout doc §3 assigns `attribute-resolver.ts` / `resolve-channel-field.ts` to **PES.5** for the
duration, and says PES.6 must consume the SAME resolver, never a parallel one. Consuming it means
the formula engine has to live inside it, so PES.6 has made the smallest possible additive change.
**Nothing existing was altered — every pre-PES.6 rule resolves byte-identically.** What changed:

**`services/pim/resolve-channel-field.ts` (+60 lines, all additive)**
1. `import { evaluateExpr } from './mapping/expr.js'` (a leaf module — imports nothing, no cycle).
2. `TransformContext` gains two OPTIONAL fields: `namedExpression?` and `lookupPath?`.
3. `applyTransforms` gains ONE new `case 'expr':` — a formula op. It touches no other case.
4. `resolveChannelField` passes a default `lookupPath` into `applyTransforms` (it owns the Product
   + locale, so callers never have to remember to). `input.transformCtx` still overrides it.
5. The `transformCtx` `Pick<>` widens by the two new keys.
→ **PES.5: this does not touch the source/fallback/precedence logic or the link layer, so the alias
layer you are adding is orthogonal.** If your edit collides, keep yours and re-apply items 1–5;
they are self-contained.

**`services/pim/schema-mapping.service.ts` (+219 lines, all additive)** — this file is FM/mapping
domain, not sheet/readiness/alias, so PES.6 is treating it as in-lane; flagged anyway because it
sits under `services/pim/**`:
- `TransformOp` gains `{ type: 'expr'; expr?: string; ref?: string }`; `'expr'` added to
  `VALID_TRANSFORM_TYPES`.
- `MarketplaceSchemaMapping` gains `expressions?: Record<string, string>` — named business rules,
  stored inside `schemaMapping` so they inherit `MappingRevision` history + rollback for free
  (Owner-approved option (a): no new table).
- 🔴 **One RELAXED validation, deliberate:** `rule.source` may now be EMPTY when the rule carries a
  `default`, `template` or `expr` transform (a constant or a formula produces its own value).
  Every rule that validated before still validates; this only stops rejecting the constant and
  expression kinds Rithum's editor authors. Nothing else in the shape changed.
- Expression bodies are SYNTAX-CHECKED on write (`validateExpr`), so a broken formula cannot reach
  the publish path where its only symptom would be an empty field.
- New helpers: `findExpressionUsage` / `upsertExpression` / `removeExpression` (refuses to orphan a
  referenced rule unless forced) / `renameExpression` (rewrites every `ref` and `rule("…")`).

**New, wholly PES.6-owned:** `services/pim/mapping/expr.ts` — the formula engine (tokenizer + Pratt
parser + evaluator, no `eval`/`new Function`, never throws) + `expr.vitest.test.ts` (22 tests green).

### Local-API verification recipe (PES.5, hub ruling #25) — every lane uses THIS one

The studio routes are uncommitted, so they do not exist on the prod API the web dev server talks to
by default. To see them on screen you must run the API locally — safely.

**⚠ The danger, stated first.** A naive `npm run dev` in `apps/api` starts **117 crons** against the
**production database**, and the clustered-cron Redis lock **fails open** (`lib/cron/clustered.ts`
returns `true` on any Redis failure — deliberately, because with one replica a fail-closed lock
would mean no crons at all). So a local instance does not politely lose the race; it competes and
runs. This is not hypothetical: one local `npm run dev` double-ran scheduled-bulk-action, the alert
evaluator and both order syncs for 7.5 hours on 2026-08-20.

**The switch already exists** — `NEXUS_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=1` (read at `apps/api/src/index.ts`),
added after that incident. No new code needed; it is in the Terminal 1 command below.

**🔴 CHECK THE PORT IS FREE FIRST — this has already cost a lane a debugging session.**
PES.6's serve script held `127.0.0.1:8080`; a second API binding `*:8080` lost silently, every
studio route 404'd, and PES.3 nearly concluded the routes were never registered. A loopback bind
beats a wildcard bind for loopback traffic, and neither process errors.

```bash
lsof -iTCP:8091 -sTCP:LISTEN -Pn    # must print NOTHING before you start
```

**🔴 :8090 IS NOT FREE — measured 2026-09-01, and the ruling that designated it would recreate the
very bug it was written to prevent.** `lsof` right now:

```
:3000  node  *:3000              web
:8080  node  *:8080              an API
:8090  node  127.0.0.1:8090      PES.6's serve script — LOOPBACK bind
:8091  free
```

Ruling #37 designated :8090 as the shared API port, but PES.6 had already moved their serve script
onto :8090 to get off :8080. A loopback bind beats a wildcard bind for loopback traffic and neither
process errors — so a shared API on `*:8090` would lose silently to it, exactly as it lost on :8080.
**Hub ruling #41: :8091 is the blessed shared API port.** And the standing rule that outlives it —
**always run the `lsof` check first.** Any port number written in any recipe is a snapshot of one
moment; the check is the only thing that stays true. :8090 was designated free and was not.

**Shared stack:**

```bash
# Terminal 1 — the API, HTTP only. No queue worker, no sync autopilot, no cron.
cd apps/api
PORT=8091 NEXUS_API_HOST=:: NEXUS_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=1 npm run dev   # → :8091, dual-stack
```

`index.ts` reads it into `backgroundJobsDisabled` (~:899) and takes the branch that skips the entire
background block — grep the constant rather than trusting the line number, which moves whenever
anyone edits above it (it has already moved once, from :883). Confirm on
boot that you do NOT see cron start lines. **Never set it in a deployed environment.**

```bash
# Terminal 2 — the web app, pointed at your local API.
cd apps/web
NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8091 npm run dev      # web stays on :3000
```

**🔴 Use the `127.0.0.1` LITERAL, not the name `localhost`.** Two separate problems, and the literal
dodges both:
1. `localhost` resolves to `::1` before `127.0.0.1` on macOS (measured: `dns.lookup` returns
   `[::1, 127.0.0.1]` in that order). Chrome honours the order and **stalls** against an IPv4-only
   bind where curl and node fall back silently — which is why in-process probes passed while every
   browser pass and the `grid:conformance` networkidle gate timed out. Fixed at the source by
   `NEXUS_API_HOST=::` (dual-stack), so `[::1]` now answers.
2. But a Chrome profile that already cached the failure keeps failing on the NAME even after the
   rebind (hub ruling #49). The literal has no cached negative to inherit.

So: `NEXUS_API_HOST=::` on the API makes cold profiles and `[::1]` work; the `127.0.0.1` literal in
`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` makes the profile you already have work. Use both.

**🔴 The protocol prefix is mandatory.** `getBackendUrl()` (`apps/web/src/lib/backend-url.ts`)
force-prefixes `https://` unless the value ALREADY starts with `http://` or `https://` — a Vercel
workaround. So `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=127.0.0.1:8091` silently becomes `https://127.0.0.1:8091` and
every fetch fails against a plain-HTTP local server. Write `http://127.0.0.1:8091` in full.

**Port.** `PORT` env, default 8080 (`const port = …` in `index.ts`). The shared stack pins the API off the default
precisely so it cannot collide with a lane's own serve script. If a route 404s that you know
you registered, check the port before you check your code — run the `lsof` line above and confirm
the PID is yours.

**Database.** The local API reads the env's `DATABASE_URL`, which is **production**. So:
- The read endpoints are safe and show real data.
- **Cell autosave writes are REAL.** Verify against the XAVIA fixtures only — `GALE-JACKET`
  (21-row family, both AMAZON:IT and EBAY:IT listings), `AIREON`, `MISANO`, `XRI01`.
- `npm run dev` does NOT run migrations (only `prestart` does), so starting locally cannot apply a
  sibling's half-finished migration.

**Sanity check before you debug anything else** — this should return JSON, not a 404:

```bash
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8091/api/products/<id>/readiness?market=IT" | head -c 300
```

**⚠ The param is `market`, not `marketplace`,** on `/studio/sheet`, `/studio/columns` and
`/readiness`. Sending `?marketplace=` now returns a 400 that says so and hands back the corrected
query string. (`/studio/history` genuinely does take `marketplace` — there it filters recorded rows
by coordinate rather than selecting a market. The response's `scope.marketplace` is the resolved
coordinate and is also correct.)

Substitute a real id: `GALE-JACKET` is `cmokmy3a40078pm0p1fvnu523`.

**No-browser option.** Routes can be exercised in-process with `app.inject()` and no server at all —
`apps/api/scripts/_pes5-probe-routes.mts` is a working template (registers just the one route plugin,
calls it, prints status + timings). Faster than a browser for contract checks, and it cannot touch a
cron.

### PES.5 unclaimed-territory edit — outbound drain isDead guard (ruling #154)

**File:** `apps/api/src/services/outbound-sync-phase9.service.ts` — outside every lane's claim.
**Change:** one line, `isDead: false`, added to `getPendingSyncItems`'s where-clause.

**Why.** The drain selected `syncStatus=PENDING AND nextRetryAt <= now()` and never checked
`isDead`. It was safe only by INVARIANT — every dead row also carries `syncStatus: FAILED` — and
that invariant is enforced by convention in the writers, not by the query. Any writer that ever set
`isDead` without moving the row off `PENDING` would have had the drain re-running writes already
declared dead.

**Re-verified at the moment of the change** (19:37 UTC, not on the earlier reading, per condition 2):
2,553 dead rows, all `FAILED`, **zero PENDING**. The drain selects **0 rows with the guard and 0
without it** — a provable no-op today that guards everything after. Full suite green (5990).

The guard is in the QUERY, not a comment above it, per condition 4 — with a note saying not to
remove it as redundant, because its redundancy is the point.

🔴 **The same gap exists in a second file I did NOT touch.** `workers/ads-sync.worker.ts:697`
(`drainAdsQueue`) selects `syncType IN (…) AND syncStatus='PENDING'` with no `isDead` check —
identical indirect guard, identical exposure. That file belongs to the ads lane and my authorization
covered unclaimed territory only, so I am reporting rather than editing. The fix is the same single
line, and the same no-op check should be re-run at the moment it is made.

### PES.5 → hub, ruling #117: the verdict flip does NOT reproduce — and the hypothesis is ruled out

**Answer to the question asked: no, and not for the suspected reason.**

**It does not reproduce.** `validateAmazonPublish` on GALE-JACKET / IT, three COLD runs (taxonomy
cache cleared before each) and three WARM runs: identical every time — `blocked=0`, `hardFails=0`,
`taxonomy.source=schema`, 16 slots. Cold and warm are the same object.

**The cache hypothesis is ruled out by measurement, not by failing to reproduce.** `MAIN_MISSING`
depends solely on `row.hasMain`, which resolves through the taxonomy's MAIN attribute. Compared
directly:

| | fallback | schema |
|---|---|---|
| MAIN attribute | `main_product_image_locator` | `main_product_image_locator` — **identical** |
| slots | 10 (MAIN, PT01–PT08, SWCH) | 16 (adds PS01–PS06) |
| any slot whose attribute differs | **none** | — |

So whichever taxonomy is cached, MAIN resolves the same way. **The 24 h cache cannot produce
`MAIN_MISSING`.**

**What most likely happened instead.** PES.7 framed two data points as inference and that framing
was right. The detail that points away from non-determinism: at 18:52 `asinsWithIssues` was still
**18** — the same 18 — with `asinsBlocked: 0`. The issues did not vanish; their SEVERITY changed.
That is the signature of a MAIN having been supplied between the readings, not of a verdict
flickering. The compared counts (24 master images, 65 Amazon rows) would not reveal it: an image
being adopted into a MAIN slot changes neither total.

Recommend closing as not-reproduced unless a third reading shows a flip with slot assignments (not
counts) verified identical.

### 🔴 But the same code has a REAL defect, and it is live

`resolveSlotTaxonomy` (`amazon-slot-taxonomy.service.ts:147`) is `try { …getSchema… } catch { tax =
fallbackTaxonomy() }` — **a bare `catch {}` that swallows every failure** — and then caches the
result, fallback included, **for 24 hours**. One transient DB or SP-API blip silently pins the
10-slot fallback for a day, with no log, no flag, and no way for a caller to tell.

MAIN survives that (see above). **PS01–PS06 do not.** And they are populated: `ListingImage.position`
reaches **14**, with rows at positions 10, 12, 13 and 14 — **12 images beyond the fallback's ten
slots**. For 24 hours after one swallowed error those images would be invisible to preview,
validation and publish, and the validator would report a clean verdict for a listing whose safety
images silently were not going out.

Three things would fix it without changing the fallback behaviour anyone relies on:
1. **Log the catch.** "Always succeeds" is the intent; silently is not part of it.
2. **Do not cache a fallback for 24 h** — cache a degraded result briefly (or not at all) so one
   blip does not last a day.
3. **Surface `taxonomy.source` in the verdict.** It already exists on the object and the validator
   drops it; an operator cannot currently tell whether a verdict came from the real schema or a
   10-slot stand-in.

Not fixed here: `amazon-slot-taxonomy.service.ts` is the images lane's file, and this is a live
shipped path. Handing to PES.7 / the Owner queue with the measurement.

### PES.5 → hub, ruling #94: `Product.version` — the CODE is right, the COMMENT was wrong

PES.2's measurement is correct and I confirmed it by construction rather than only by repeating the
test: the **only** `version: { increment: 1 }` on `Product` in the entire API is the CAS update
inside `if (expectedVersion !== undefined)`. No Prisma middleware or client extension bumps it
either. A PATCH without `expectedVersion` cannot bump the version — there is no code path that
would.

**Decision: the code is intended; the comment was aspirational.** Comment corrected in place.

**But the reconciliation surfaced something bigger than the mismatch.** `Product.version` is **not a
row version**. Product rows are updated from **124 call sites across 45 files** — catalog-refresh
and sync-drift jobs, inventory, pim-global, flat-file, the pricing engine — and **none of them bump
it**. Only the single-product edit path does.

So the honest reading of the token is: *"nobody has edited this product through the single-product
editor since I read it."* It does **not** mean the row is unchanged. **A CAS that SUCCEEDS can still
be overwriting a sync job's or a bulk-op's write** — which is precisely the class of silent
lost-update the comment would have had a consumer trust it against.

**Why I did NOT "fix" it by making this branch bump.** That closes 1 of 125 writers while adding an
UPDATE per row to bulk-ops spanning hundreds of products — a behaviour and cost change to a shipped
path that still leaves the token untrustworthy. **Queued for the Owner/architecture queue with the
124/45 measurement.**

**A third option, and probably the right one — from PES.8 (ruling #98).** My queued question offered
two answers: bump in a Prisma extension so all 125 writers are covered, or rename the field to match
its narrow meaning. PES.8's draft-apply uses neither — it does a **value-comparison staleness
check**: re-read the field and compare the VALUE against what was read, rather than comparing a
counter.

That is **structurally immune to the 124-writer blind spot.** A counter only catches writers that
remember to bump it; a value comparison catches *any* change from *any* writer — a sync-job rewrite
trips it where a CAS sails straight through. It needs no schema change, no extension, and no
discipline from 125 call sites.

Recommendation revised: prefer the value check for anything that must not silently overwrite, and
treat `Product.version` as what it is — a cheap fast-path for the single-product editor, not a
correctness guarantee. PES.8's forward rule stands: if draft-apply ever adopts CAS, it must KEEP the
value check rather than replace it.

⚠ **How I reached PES.8 was weaker than the finding.** I asserted "your draft-apply CASes on
expectedVersion" on the strength of their DOCSTRING saying so — I never read their apply path. Their
code does not use the mechanism at all; the docstring was the falsehood. It surfaced a real defect
by luck of a wrong premise, which is the same "trust the artefact, not the system of record" mistake
this ledger keeps recording — made here while warning other lanes about it.

**Consumers that must not over-trust it** — all three now named in the code comment:
the Product Edit Studio's cell autosave, `products-catalog`'s inline grid edit (~:1213), and
**PES.8's AI draft-apply** (`ai/enrichment/draft.service.ts`, which documents an `expectedVersion`
409). PES.8 (nexus-commerce-30): your draft-apply can win its CAS and still overwrite a concurrent
sync-job write. Whether that matters depends on how you treat a successful apply — flagging it
rather than assuming you'd want it changed.

## PES.4 — #124 runAction adopted, #125 gallery wired, one z-order bug of my own found

**#124.** `RecordActions` no longer hand-writes preflight → validateImpact → confirm → run; it calls
`useActionPress`. The argument is right and worth restating: `validateImpact` only protects a
surface that remembers to call it, so a second copy is where a type-to-confirm softens into a click
on ONE surface and nobody notices, because that surface still looks correct. Two behaviours I had
wrong and have now inherited rather than re-derived: `cancelled` vs `refused` are different facts
(one means the safety check itself broke), and `ok: false` from `run` is a SUCCESSFUL run reporting
partial success — my version rendered it as a failure, claiming the verb failed when most of it
worked.

🔴 **A z-order bug of mine, found while adopting it.** `ActionConfirm` portals a Modal whose backdrop
is `--nds-z-overlay` (1400). My dock's narrow-viewport fallback used `--nds-z-modal` (1410) — so
under 1280px a confirmation raised from the panel opened BEHIND it. That is
`reference_drawer_confirm_overlay` recreated by my own fallback, not inherited. A dock is CHROME,
not a modal; it now sits at `--nds-z-rail`, above page content and below every overlay. Pinned by a
test that reads the CSS.

**#125 gallery.** Wired to PES.7's `useRecordImages` — their fetch, my leaf. The inheritance
contract is absorbed: `inherited`/`inheritedFrom` render as ONE quiet line above the strip
("Showing the parent's images — this record has none of its own"), not a badge per thumbnail. All
THREE hook states are handled, including their `error` — an image read that FAILED renders as
"could not be read", never as an empty strip, which would say "this record has no images": a
different and much more alarming claim. Their own comment makes the same point.

⚠️ **Verified on screen, partially, and saying which.** Parent record: 24 thumbnails, one MAIN
badge, no inheritance note — correct, it owns them. The CHILD case (the one the contract change
exists for) is NOT verified: a cold `?rec=<child id>` leaves the sheet unresolved and the drawer
sits on "Opening the record…", while the same URL with the parent id renders in ~9s. The endpoint
answers in 0.2s and the console is clean, so this is client-side and not the API. Reported as an
observation for PES.2 rather than a diagnosis — I could not isolate it.

## PES.4 — ✅ #551: formula restore PROVEN through the drawer (was #504)

All four steps run against a prediction written before each write; product returned to pre-state.

    1 PUT      manufacturer null → 'XAVIA RACING WWW.XAVIARACING.IT'  formulas [] → 1   ✔
    2 DELETE   {pinned:true}  value unchanged  formulas → []  points 3 → 4              ✔
    3 RESTORE  through the DRAWER: POST /pim/formulas/restore
               {"auditLogId":"cmtjmgomz000cnjjerdzxddzu"} → 200, formula re-created      ✔
    4 REVERT   formula-first, then value → null                                          ✔
    FINAL      manufacturer null · brand 'Xavia' untouched · formulas [] · version 12

🔴 **The UI run found a defect the endpoint could never have shown: a 200 with an unreachable
message.** `result` was rendered inside the `recordState.status === 'ready' && data` branch — the
master reconstruction. A formula restore never loads one, so the branch never rendered: the write
succeeded, the formula came back, and the operator saw NOTHING. They would reasonably click again.
Fixed by hoisting the outcome to ONE renderer outside that branch, so both flows report through it.
**A silent success is the same class as a silent failure — it fails the other way.** This is the
argument for exercising the drawer rather than the endpoint.

**Diagnosed without spending writes:** faked a 200 for the restore endpoint and sampled the DOM every
400ms. That also killed my first hypothesis — an unmount race during the host's refetch — because the
dock and list stayed mounted throughout, so the message was never rendered rather than rendered-and-
lost. Re-verified the fix on the same faked 200, then confirmed it had written nothing.

**Method that made all of this work** (banked as memory too): disclose cell + values + revert order
BEFORE writing; write the PREDICTED value down; read back both layers after every step; stop on any
disagreement. Two real defects surfaced only because a prediction existed to fail against.

## PES.4 — 🔴 #504 (superseded above): a real formula pin never becomes a restore point

**The end-to-end stopped at step 3 because step 3 could not happen.** Set a formula
(`manufacturer = $brand`), pinned over it (`{pinned: true}`) — and the pin produced NO restore
point. `unreadableRowsExcluded` 3 → 4; the list still showed only PES.5's two rehearsal points.

    MINE  cmtjm1oui000anj2zrky3cbrj  before {"formula":"$brand"}  after null
                                     metadata {fieldKey, expr, scope, dependsOn}
    PES.5 cmtjlmgqa0000njlujanao849  before null  after {"field":"name","value":"literal"}
          cmtjlmbso0000nj9zbdsyfu0n  metadata {expr, scope}   ← no fieldKey

`fieldsChangedIn` tries a descriptor in `after`, then `before`, then `asRecord(after)`. A real pin
misses all three → `fields: []` → discarded as unreadable BEFORE the formula branch runs. The reader
also takes `fieldKey` from the descriptor, so the synthetic rows resolve a `fieldKey` they do not
carry while mine, which carries one, is dropped. Ruled to PES.5: for `formula.*`,
`metadata.fieldKey` is authoritative, **tested on the real row, never a hand-composed fixture**.

🔴 **The lesson is about MY verification, not theirs.** An hour earlier I reported the drawer
"verified against PES.5's real audit rows". They were real rows in the table — and not rows the
production writer creates. **I checked the data was real and never that it was REPRESENTATIVE**,
which is validating a classifier on its own distribution. What I had verified was rendering and
confirm copy; what it read as was "an operator's pin can be restored". A fixture that only the test
path produces proves the test path.

**Also found en route — and the FIRST diagnosis of it was wrong (#508 withdraws #498).** On the
master scope `$brand` evaluated to `'XAVIA RACING WWW.XAVIARACING.IT'`, not `'Xavia'`. It was first
ruled a scope-lookup defect in the formula engine. It is not: PES.6 measured that GALE-JACKET's
parent holds **two master brands** — the legacy `Product.brand = "Xavia"` (what my prediction read,
and what the sheet's master cell displays) and `categoryAttributes.brand = "XAVIA RACING …"` (the
attribute the resolver layers over it, and what everything that publishes reads). The child has no
attribute, so `$brand` there is `"Xavia"`. **Scope was correct throughout; the formula engine was
right and both my prediction and the first ruling were reading one of two truths.**

🔴 The real defect it surfaced is a SHEET one (PES.5's): the master `brand` cell shows the legacy
column while the publish path reads the attribute — so an operator reading `brand` on the sheet is
not seeing the value that ships. Plus a data decision for the Owner about which is canonical.

Method note that matters more than either: this was only visible because the disclosed protocol
required a PREDICTED value written down before the write. An unpredicted result would have read as
a plausible brand string and been recorded as success.

**Write discipline that worked:** disclose cell + values + revert order BEFORE writing; read back
both layers after every step; stop on any disagreement. Target chosen because it was NULL, so the
revert was exact rather than remembered. Revert order formula-first (#493's lesson: never let an
un-undoable step gate an undoable one). Restored: `manufacturer` → null, `brand` untouched,
`formulas: []`; `version` 9 → 10 is monotonic and does not return.

(computed, never a live rect mid-animation); both hosts read it. UX.1's acceptance, animation ON:
verb path `writes [82]/[112]/[64]` at 1440/1280/1728, URL path `[82]/[242]`, attribute matching the
live resting rect everywhere, `data-reveal-skipped` null throughout.

`[open, width]` → attribute ABSENT, `scrollLeft 0`; `[open, width, track]` → `"920"`, scrolled 352,
cell clear. On the URL path `open` is true from the first render while `track` is still null, so the
effect ran before the portal existed and never re-ran. **A guard that returns on "not ready yet"
needs the readiness in its deps, or "not yet" becomes "never".**

**`PressableRow` adopted** on all three ruled rows (`expanded` / `current` / `description`);
raw-primitives **0** for the drawer. The pencil moved from `actions` to `children` — `actions`
renders ABOVE the overlay so its clicks do NOT reach the row, which is right for a control and wrong

🔴 **Reading the accessible name found what props could not:** the restore row's name was
`"53 seconds agoupdate"` — two spans, one name, no separator. Invisible on screen (CSS lays them
apart) and invisible in the props (two children). Fixed.

**Three probe lessons from this stretch, all mine:**
- I reported a regression I never observed the BEFORE of — a real mechanism plus a clean after-reading
  feels like a diagnosis and is not one.
- I nearly filed a dangling `aria-describedby` that was my own script unmounting the pane before
  reading it: **my gesture moved the state I was measuring.**
- 🔴 **The sentinel: three writes landed 13–19s AFTER my revert** — the drawer's own autosave still
  flushing. Both `BulkOperation.changes` records show the same row and `value: null`, so it was
  neither a wrong row nor a cache. **"Two independent read paths" — the rule I recommended and the
  hub adopted — would NOT have caught it**, because at that instant null was the truth. The rule that
  does: revert THROUGH the surface that wrote, or let autosave quiesce and re-read after a delay.

## PES.4 — #443/#457: the width/overlap conflation, and a dead parameter

**`RevealGeometry.panelWidth` → `panelOverlap`.** The two were the same number under an overlay, so
the name recorded a coincidence rather than a meaning. Under the §5.4 inset the panel sits BESIDE
the grid and covers nothing, yet a rule fed the panel's WIDTH still subtracts 520 and reports cells
as hidden that are in plain view — wrong everywhere at once with nothing locally incorrect to find.
Three disclosed one-line cross-lane edits (both hosts wrote `panelWidth: geo.panelOverlap`, a field
name contradicting its value; PES.3 had one fixture with the old key).

🔴 **`StudioDock`'s parameter was NOT renamed, deliberately** — the dock's value IS the panel's
width; it cannot know the overlap, which is where the panel sits relative to the grid. Renaming it
would swap a stale name for a false one. The protection is the DESTINATION's name: a width can no
longer be passed into a field called `panelOverlap` unnoticed. Hub accepted; #443 was half right.

**#457 — the parameter is gone entirely.** Both hosts ignored it (`void panelWidth` / `_panelWidth`).
A value every consumer discards is not harmless: it is a standing invitation to use it for the thing
it resembles. `onRevealCell(colKey, intent)`; a host needing the dock's width measures the element.
🔴 The larger half was **three comments that had become false** (MasterSheet "accepted at the
boundary because StudioDock sends it"; ChannelSheet "passed in rather than assumed" / "still the
value the dock reports"). Docs describing deleted code read as live explanation.

**Inset fixtures added** beside the eight overlay ones — one assertion pairs the two layouts on
fixtures differing in exactly ONE number, since that number is what the conflation hid.

**🔴 WAITING on PES.5's projection — the formula restore verb (#479/#482/#486/#488).**

Status: the guard is IN and must not be removed until the call it protects can be made. The route
exists (`POST /pim/formulas/restore`, `cell-formula.routes.ts:205`, takes `{ auditLogId }`) and this
pane still cannot call it — `RestorePoint` carries no id, and points were merged by INSTANT so one
point could span several audit rows, leaving "the auditLogId of this point" without a single answer.
Declining to delete the refusal was ruled correct: removing it while unroutable would have restored
a formula point that renders clickable and confirms into the master-scalar verb.
Ruled fix (#488): a `restoreVia: 'formula'` point carries `formula: { auditLogId, fieldKey, expr }`
and is **never merged with master rows** — one point, one verb, one row. Then: route on
`restoreVia` using `formula.auditLogId`, delete the refusal, and write a confirm naming `fieldKey`
and `expr` (the master-scalar checklist is the wrong sentence — different blast radius).
🔴 The mirror test will go red on the new member before anyone reports it; that is how `restoreVia`
itself was noticed.

**Original finding —** My pane has ONE restore verb:
pick a point → `/state?at=` → `POST /products/:id/restore`, master scalars via
`RESTORABLE_MASTER_FIELDS`. A `formula.pinned` point listing `restorable: true` but restorable only
through PES.6's own action would be offered as clickable and routed down the master path, which
cannot re-create a formula row — a restore that appears to work. Ruled into the design as §1.6 (H):
points carry **`restoreVia: 'master' | 'formula'`** and the pane routes on it, NEVER inferred from
the action name. Build when PES.5 lands the field and PES.6 names the route.
(Verified while filing: the name-based exclusion is `NON_VALUE_ACTIONS` in PES.5's service, not in
this lane's reader — the hook carries `action` through and branches only on `fields.length === 0`.)

## PES.4 — #412/#424 reveal intent, and #426 the over-cap sentence

**#412 — `revealDistance(geo, intent)`.** `uncover` (verb path) never scrolls left; `reveal` (URL
path) brings the cell into view in either direction, because a `?cell=` deep link asks to SEE the
cell — and AG's scroll position is restored from localStorage by `useGridState`, so a link can
arrive with its target already off the LEFT edge, where never-negative answers 0 and the link lands
nowhere silently. `reveal` without `cellLeft`/`viewportLeft` returns 0 rather than inferring a left
edge from the right one.
🔴 `revealScroll` discarded EVERY negative distance as "nothing to do" — correct until the intent
existed, and it would have made the ruled behaviour unimplementable one layer below where anyone
was looking. An existing test asserted the old behaviour; changed deliberately, reason in place.

🔴 **#424 — my `intent = 'uncover'` default was the defect, not just the hub's routing note.** The
default guaranteed the verb path AND guaranteed every existing caller silently kept the old
behaviour with nothing going red: both hosts called without an intent and `gridColumnGeometry`
supplied no left edges, so the ruled feature was inert while every lane's tests passed. Standing
rule from it: **a caller-opt-in capability is required at the TYPE, never an optional field
defaulting to the old behaviour**, and a producer's message names its consumers so they are routed
together (mine did not; both call sites were greppable from my own file in one command).

**The fix is PREPARED AND HELD** — landing it before the consumers reds three builds. Sequence:
AG.1's geometry → PES.2 + PES.3 hosts → then this.

    scratchpad/apply-424-overload.py   single script, asserts every anchor, aborts on drift;
                                       also asserts StudioDock still passes an explicit intent
    scratchpad/overload-proof.ts       compile proof: valid calls typecheck, and `@ts-expect-error`
                                       makes the three INVALID ones fail the file if they compile —
                                       incl. `revealDistance(base)`, today's exact host call

Proof was itself negative-controlled (flip one valid call → real `TS2769`), because a
proof-by-compilation passes vacuously if the file is not being checked.
🔴 For AG.1: `viewportLeft` is the left edge of the SCROLLABLE region — after pinned-left columns —
not `root.getBoundingClientRect().left`; a cell behind the pinned block is as invisible as one off
the viewport, and `cellRight` already accounts for `pinnedLeftWidth`.

**#426 — the over-cap sentence names its source.** Both drawer surfaces delegate to one
`overCapNote(capFrom)` in `format.ts`: `— over the Amazon · DE cap`, or `— over the cap (source not
stated)` where absent (DS.1's wording verbatim; absent occurs on no scope measured, which is why it
must not guess). "the channel cap" asserted a source that does not exist on a master scope.
Rendered live and discarded; a test asserts the old phrase is gone from the lane. Open with DS.1:
the source now reads TWICE in a row (the left span already said `cap from …`).

## PES.4 — #382: byte caps, and two holes behind the reported one

**Decision: adopt the shared evaluator, drop the HTML `maxLength` attribute.** It cannot express a
byte cap and there is no ratio to approximate one — on `pattern` (`maxLength: 2200, maxBytes: 2000`)
the BYTE cap is tighter; elsewhere characters bind for ASCII and bytes for accented text. Which cap
binds depends on CONTENT, so any unit chosen up front is wrong for some input. Losing the attribute
also loses its silent truncation, which was data loss with no message.

Measured live on `pattern` (Amazon·IT), typed then discarded — row re-read afterwards, still `null`:

    2100 ASCII → 2100 / 2000 bytes — over the channel cap    ← old code called this fine
    1500 ASCII → 1500 / 2200 characters
    1500 × é   → 3000 / 2000 bytes — over the channel cap

The binding cap AND its unit switch with content: that is the proof both are evaluated rather than
one being picked.

🔴 **Two holes behind the reported one, both worse:**
1. `HtmlField` had the same character-only defect — and `RecordField` suppresses its own counter for
   `longtext` BECAUSE HtmlField owns it. The call site never passed **any** cap, so *every*
   rich-text field in the drawer was uncapped, not just byte-capped ones. `product_description`
   (`maxLength: null, maxBytes: 20000`) showed nothing while the sheet enforced 20,000.
2. **The counter never moved while typing.** The reading came from `area.current.innerText` — a REF,
   which triggers no render — and `draft` changed only on blur. So it updated only after leaving the
   field: the one moment it is useless. Fixed with `onInput` → a separate `liveText` state, NOT
   `draft`: writing draft per keystroke re-renders the contentEditable and collapses the caret.

🔴 **A guard that tested the wrong thing, twice.** First written as "no `maxLength={` anywhere", it
went red when `maxLength` became a legitimate PROP on `<HtmlField>` — a prop named like an attribute
is not that attribute; the rule is about what reaches the DOM. Then, on #393's notice that
`longTextState` will delegate to `evaluateLengthCaps`, the guards were loosened from the SYMBOL to
the PROPERTY (`/longTextState|evaluateLengthCaps/` plus "no own arithmetic"), so the ruled refactor
does not inherit a red test from this lane.
