## PES.4 — #366: restore points, and a guard that went quiet

**A contract test stopped checking anything — and the reason I first gave was WRONG.**

PES.5's #364 extraction changed `products.routes.ts` from `const ALLOWED: Set<string> = new Set([…])`
to `const ALLOWED = RESTORABLE_MASTER_FIELDS`, so my extractor threw at module scope.

🔴 I reported that vitest "counts a collect failure as skipped". **It does not.** Reproduced with a
throwing probe file: `FAIL <file>`, `Test Files 1 failed | 177 passed (178)`, **exit code 1**. PES.2
was right and I was wrong.

What actually hid it was my own instrumentation: a collect failure contributes **zero tests**, so the
`Tests` line stays perfectly clean (`2406 passed`, no failures, no skips) and the failure appears
ONLY in the `Test Files` line and the exit code. I was reading results with `| tail -4`, which cuts
off `Test Files` — it is the fifth line from the end — and I never checked `$?` because the output
looked clean. I then joined that to an unrelated `12 skipped` from another lane and built a story.
🔴 The real trap is **`tail -4` on a vitest run hides the only line that reports a collect failure**;
same class as the AbortError finding — the probe was lying, not the subject.

Fixed three ways, and the third is the one worth copying:
1. Repointed at `restorable-fields.ts`, the single source now.
2. Every failure path RETURNS a reason; nothing throws at module scope — including `readFileSync`
   itself, which was still a collect-time throw on a renamed file until it was wrapped.
3. Added an assertion that the ROUTE still filters against that shared module. Without it the
   mirror can be pinned to a file the route no longer honours and still pass.
Proved by renaming the source: **2 failed**, not "no tests".

**Restore points replace the free `datetime-local`.** `GET /products/:id/restore-points`, read
through `useStudioRead`. `min`/`max` went with the input deliberately: bounding an arbitrary
instant improves a control that should not exist, since "what did this look like at 14:32" always
answers with the last recorded change. The list IS the history.
- `restorable: false` rows are SHOWN, disabled, reason **in text on the row** — never a `title`, as
  a disabled control takes no hover on touch and no keyboard focus.
- 🔴 GALE-JACKET has 11 restorable points and ZERO unrestorable, so the real data never exercises
  the disabled path; verified with an injected page rather than trusting a vacuous `every()` over
  an empty array. All three zero-point coverage sentences render distinctly.
- `RESTORABLE_FIELDS` (the hand mirror) STAYS: a point's `restorableFields` is that moment's
  restorable subset, not the global allow-list, so substituting it would wrongly block fields that
  are restorable but were not changed at that instant.

**Not mine, routed to PES.5:** `cell-history.service.ts:86` reads only `after?.field`, so the ~320
map-shaped rows (`{"de.description": …}`, ai-draft) are silently skipped. The drawer parses no audit
rows — it renders what `/studio/history` returns — so this is a server fix. But it surfaces here as
a lie: with rows skipped, "No recorded change to X since <date>" is false. `RestorePointsResult`
already carries `coverage.unreadableRowsExcluded`; the ask is the same block on `/studio/history`.

## PES.4 — VERIFIED on Amazon·IT (#342, §14.2, P3-4)

**#342.1 — the compare reads had ALWAYS failed.** The query sent `marketplace=`; the route reads
`market=` (`product-studio.routes.ts:116`). Every read 400'd — and `readScope` mapped 400 → `null`
as "no listing on this coordinate", so a contract bug rendered as a confident, wrong, plausible
sentence for every target, always. 🔴 The tolerance was the worse half: fixing the param alone
would have left the next mismatch just as silent. Now only **204** means no listing; a 400 carries
the server's own message. Proven: 10 reads, all `market=`, all 200, master via the drawer-scope
fallback (PES.3's master target has no marketplace of its own).

**#342.2** — "this record" matched by COORDINATE (kind + channel + marketplace + aliasId), no
`?? targets[0]` fallback. Was marking Amazon·BE on Amazon·IT. Verified: one marker, "Amazon · IT".

**`useCompare` stall test PASSES** (13 stalled discarded / 13 fresh / 0 stale), negative control
2 stale / 0 fresh, restored byte-identical. 🔴 **The control found a defect the passing test could
not**: `readScope` absorbed its own AbortError into a per-target failure. Harmless for superseded
requests, but the **30s deadline aborts the same controller and is not superseded** — so a timeout
would have resolved `run` SUCCESSFULLY with every target blaming the marketplace for our own
deadline, and the honest "given up on, not answered" sentence was unreachable. Aborts now rethrow.

**§14.2 / P3-4 verified.** No `?cell=`: 7 groups, 0 expanded, 0 fields mounted. `?cell=map_policy`
(last of 61): only Attributes opens, `scrollTop 8779/8827`, field fully in view.
🔴 **The landing check asked the wrong element.** `.nds-drawer-b` is `scrollHeight === clientHeight`
inside the dock; the real scroller is the pane below it (9,468px in a 641px window). It now walks up
for the first genuinely scrollable ancestor and requires FULL visibility — an overlap test passes on
a field one pixel over the fold, which no one can read.

**Still open:** Restore's "moments that hold changes" list — no endpoint exposes record-level change
instants (`/state` gives counts, `/studio/history` needs a fieldKey). `max` is bounded to now; `min`
deliberately unset rather than guessed.

**#290/#300/#317 — watched, not inferred.** Stall test: patch `fetch`, stall the first

switches the pane, so B's button leaves the DOM if you go A → B directly).

## PES.4 — parity 8.4 (Recover → time-travel): READ and WRITE both measured (#216)

**(1) The reconstruction READ — verified, with one honest limit.** The ask was three fields; GALE-JACKET
has ONE. Measured: 83 audit rows, two fields ever touched (`manufacturer`, `name`), and only
`manufacturer` carries any `before`. So the read was tested across FOUR points in time on that field
instead — 3 reconstructable, all three matching the audit trail exactly, including a recorded `null`
(the empty-vs-unrecorded distinction working end to end). The fourth point has no later `before` and
correctly returns current with no coverage entry.

⚠️ My first attempt at this PASSED 4/4 and was worthless — the extractor used the wrong response key,
so the timeline was empty, every expectation was `None`, and the ticks were vacuous. Same
false-positive shape this lane has been guarding against all session, written by me. Redone with an
assertion that refuses to report a pass on an empty timeline.

**(2) The restore WRITE — round-tripped on the XAVIA fixture.** Value taken from the reconstruction
rather than invented: `POST /restore` at 15:42:30 → `manufacturer` `null` → `'PES2 GUARD PROBE'`,
read back from the API (landed), then reverted to `null` and confirmed server-side. Both writes
produced `AuditLog` rows with `source: 'restore'` carrying correct `before`/`after` — so the
pre-restore capture works and the drawer's confirm promise ("the values being replaced are recorded
first, so this restore appears in each field's history and can itself be undone") is now VERIFIED
rather than asserted.

🔴 **And a finding: `/restore` never bumps `Product.version`.** Measured — version stayed 9 across
two restores that both changed the data. The handler READS version for its CAS check
(products.routes.ts, `expectedVersion !== product.version → 409`) but its
`prisma.product.update({ where: { id }, data })` does not include it, while the bulk PATCH explicitly
CAS-bumps inside its transaction. Consequence, read from that code rather than separately
demonstrated: a sheet holding the pre-restore version still believes it is current, so its next cell
write passes the guard and silently overwrites the restored values with no 409. The optimistic
concurrency that protects every cell edit does not protect against a restore. → PES.5.

## PES.4 — 4.9 registry mirror BUILT + 4.10 VERIFIED ON SCREEN (and it found a PES.5 bug)

**4.9 verb mirror.** `RecordActions.tsx` adapts `GridAction` from `design-system/grid/actions/registry`
— the drawer declares NO verb of its own (#110). It honours four registry rules a hand-rolled button
would get wrong: disabled verbs are KEPT with their reason; a preflight always resolves before the
operator is asked; `consequences[]` render itemised, never counted; and 🔴 `validateImpact` problems
REFUSE the verb. That last one needed `DrawerConfirm` to grow real `type-to-confirm` support first —
silently downgrading a typed confirm to a click is how a five-listing delete becomes one-click, so
refusing had to be possible before it could be chosen. Imported from the registry MODULE, not the
grid barrel: the barrel re-exports `NexusGrid.tsx`, which drags JSX into a node test environment and
the whole grid into the drawer's bundle.

**4.10 verified on screen at XAVIA GALE-JACKET · IT — and the first real payload found two bugs.**
- **Mine, fixed:** the pane derived its diff by COMPARING VALUES, using the sheet row as "current".
  The sheet is keyed by sheet column (`item_name`), the reconstruction by product column
  (`bulletPoints`) — different keyspaces, so every field read as emptied. Measured: **28 rows**, most
  of them internal columns (`createdAt`, `categoryAttributes`, `amazonAsin`) plus false
  "(empty) → value" diffs. Now it filters on the SERVER's `coverage` (sparse on purpose — 3 of 93
  fields) and fetches the current record in the same keyspace. 28 → 3.
- 🔴 **PES.5's, reported not patched:** `/products/:id/state` reconstructs into fields called
  `field` and `value`. The rollback loop spreads `AuditLog.before`'s KEYS as product fields
  (products.routes.ts:709), but the bulk PATCH writes `before: {field, value}` — so it sets
  `state.field = 'brand'` instead of `state.brand = …`. The `after` branch eight lines below
  handles the same shape correctly. **Consequence: time-travel rolls back NOTHING written by the
  bulk PATCH, which is every studio edit and now every restore** — it returns current values graded
  `unchanged`. The pane is honest about it (both junk keys render "not a restorable field") and they
  vanish when the loop is fixed.

## PES.4 — 4.10 restore BUILT (#114/#115); 4.9 state display BUILT, verb waits on PES.3

**4.10 — time-travel restore, as a MODE inside the History pane** (Owner: no fifth pane). Timestamp
→ `GET /state?at=` → only the fields that DIFFER, each graded, ticked individually, behind an
acknowledged confirm. `uncertain` fields are EXCLUDED (Owner) and listed with the reason rather
than omitted, so an operator sees what cannot be recovered instead of wondering why the list is
short. Server `warnings[]` render verbatim. `expectedVersion` → 409 → "reload and try again".

🔴 **The confirm says what THIS mechanism does, not what §12's does.** They are different
mechanisms and conflating them would be the expensive error here: §12 listing restore writes a
`ChannelListing`, sets `isPublished=false`, carries `undoSnapshotId`, and leaves the marketplace
serving old content. §12.1 master restore rewrites the master record's scalars through the ordinary
`AuditLog` trail and makes **no channel call at all** — verified in the handler (one
`product.update`, an audit write, an event; no `masterContentService`, no publish). So the confirm
promises exactly three true things: the replaced values are recorded first (so the restore is itself
undoable and shows up in each field's history), it writes master so every inheriting channel is
affected, and nothing is published by it.

**4.9 — `offerActive` and `isPublished` render as TWO facts** (#115.2), because they are: a paused
OFFER is a live listing with its buy box suppressed; not-pushed is a marketplace still serving what
it last received. A listing can be paused-and-pushed or selling-and-unpushed. Collapsing them into
one "active?" row would misreport both. `offerActive` absent → "not reported", never assumed true.
The pause VERB still waits on PES.3's registry entry shape (#112.1) — not built drawer-only.

**Pinned:** `restorable.vitest.test.ts` asserts `RESTORABLE_FIELDS` against the route's own ALLOWED
set in BOTH directions — a field missing here is silently never offered; a field extra here is
offered, sent, and dropped by the server's filter with no error, so the pane would report a restore
of N and N-1 would happen. Proved by deleting a field from the route, watching it go red, and
restoring the API file (md5-verified identical — it is PES.5's file, mid-edit, so exactness matters).

### From BE.1 (nexus-commerce-89, backend review) → PES.5 (nexus-commerce-1f) — THREE WRITE REHEARSALS, per hub ruling #233

BE.1 makes **no database writes**. These three findings need a write to prove; each is written as an exact
rehearsal for PES.5 to run on GALE-JACKET/XAVIA. Full detail in `docs/2026-09-02-backend-simplicity-review.md`.
Chaining method is **#213's** (three writes with no refetch between them — the second and third are where a
computed version diverges from the stored one).

**R1 — BE-2: the version read-back's `.catch(() => null)`** (`routes/products.routes.ts:2460-2464`, `:2604-2605`).
The comment claims *"Reading the stored value cannot drift from it whatever the statements do."* A failed read
collapses to the same `undefined` that means "master write", so the response falls back to the computed
`expectedVersion + 1` and labels it `versionOf: 'product'` for a channelListing write — the field whose comment
(`:2341`) says it exists *"so a client cannot apply it to the wrong one"*.
1. Read `ChannelListing.version` → `v`. 2. `PATCH /api/products/bulk`, channel-target change, `expectedVersion: v`.
3. Assert response `currentVersion` **equals a fresh read** of that row and `versionOf === 'channelListing'`.
4. Chain writes 2 and 3 with no refetch (#213). 5. Revert, confirm server-side.
6. **The half that matters:** stub `findUnique` to reject, repeat — assert the response **omits** `currentVersion`
and `versionOf` rather than computing one. Today it returns `expectedVersion+1` / `'product'`.

**R2 — BE-3b: a channel-scoped `attr_*` write with no marketplace context is dropped silently.** The empty-context
guard (`:1362-1380`) is gated on `isCh`, which is `hasOwnProperty(CHANNEL_FIELD_MAP, f)` — a closed 6-key set
(`amazon_title`, `amazon_description`, `ebay_title`, `ebay_description`, `amazon_variationTheme`,
`ebay_variationTheme`; **0 keys begin `attr_`**). `isCategoryAttrField` is `f.startsWith('attr_')`. The two are
**disjoint**, so an `attr_*` change with `target:'channel'` never meets the guard, reaches `validated`, then hits
the fan-out at `:1968-1980` where `for (const ctx of effectiveContexts)` executes **zero times** — nothing built,
**nothing pushed to `errors[]`**, and the change still counted by `updated`.
Composed with FE.1's client measurement (`useChannelSheet.ts:281` refuses on `errors[]` first, `:291` only checks
`updated === 0`): `errors` is empty and `updated >= 1`, so **the cell paints `saved` for a write that reached no
table.** Also `:2529-2532` writes an audit row with `layer:'channel'` and `channel: null`.
Rehearsal: `PATCH /api/products/bulk` on XAVIA with `changes: [{ id, field: 'attr_<x>', target: 'channel', value }]`
and **`marketplaceContexts` omitted**. Assert: response `updated`, `errors`; then read the row back and assert the
value did NOT change. Expected today: `updated: 1`, `errors: []`, value unchanged — a silent drop. Revert if anything
did land. ⚠ **BE.1 has NOT observed this** — it is read from the two predicates and the control flow. If it does not
reproduce, the finding is wrong and I would rather hear that than have it stand.

**R3 — BE-3: `updated` counts `validated.length`** (`:2591`). Four post-write error sites (`:2070`, `:2375`, `:2412`,
`:2452`) push to `errors[]` without decrementing it, unlike the pre-write refusals which correctly
`validated.splice()` (`:1731`, `:1790`). Rehearsal: a batch of 3 where one forces a post-write failure; assert
`updated` equals the number actually written, not the number validated.

**Acceptance test for BE-1** (ruling #233 makes BE.1's probe the acceptance test, no write needed): after the fix,
`GET /studio/columns?market=IT` with `&channel=AMAZON` / `&channel=EBAY` / `&channel=SHOPIFY` / none must return
**four DIFFERENT** `columns` hashes (today all four are `sha256 9310b84a3442a9c2`, 102 columns), and the eBay
scope's capped columns must carry `capFrom: 'eBay · IT'` or none — never `'Amazon · IT'` (today 36 of 36 do).
Third call site to check in the same change: `master-schema.service.ts:145` (`channels: ['AMAZON']`).

## Cross-lane DS requests (owning lane implements)
### From PES.2 (family surface, D2) → PES.3 (action registry, wave 1) — contract asks
Ruling #110 says my family verbs are registry entries from day one. Good — my proposal already puts
them on the row menu and selection bar, so the placement agrees. Five things the contract must carry
or family verbs will not fit, each from a real property of these endpoints (all verified live):

1. **Three scopes, not one.** `reparent`/`promote`/`delete` act on ONE row; `unlink`/`attach`/bulk
   delete act on a SELECTION; `add variation`/`demote parent` act on the FAMILY. A registry that
   assumes row-or-selection cannot express the third. Ask: `scope: 'row' | 'selection' | 'context'`.
2. **Availability is role-dependent and must EXPLAIN itself.** Promote is standalone-only, demote is
   parent-only, unlink is child-only. So not `enabled: boolean` but
   `available(rows) => true | { hidden: true } | { disabled: true, reason: string }` — a disabled
   verb that cannot say why is the trap `reference_disabled_control_cannot_explain` names.
3. 🔴 **An async PREFLIGHT step, separate from `run`.** This is the one most likely to be missing
   from a channel-shaped design and it is the one protecting live data. `DELETE
   /api/products/:parentId/children/:childId` is a HARD delete (`prisma.product.delete`) and channel
   listings cascade with it — no server-side guard at all. Measured on a real GALE-JACKET child:
   **5 ACTIVE listings** across Amazon DE/ES/IT + eBay. The confirm can only be honest if it fetches
   `GET /api/products/:id/listings` BEFORE asking. Ask: `preflight?(rows) => Promise<Impact>`.
4. **Confirm severity comes FROM the preflight, not from a static flag.** Deleting a variation with
   no listings deserves a plain confirm; deleting one with five live listings deserves a typed-SKU
   confirm. Same verb, different weight, decided by what the preflight found.
5. **A completion signal that invalidates ROWS, not cells.** Family ops change which rows exist, so
   the sheet must refetch — unlike a cell write, which repaints one cell. Ask: `run` resolves with
   `{ rowsChanged: true }` or similar.

Two hidden consequences the registry should let a verb surface, because the endpoints do them
SILENTLY: `POST /pim/reparent` clears the OLD parent's `isParent` if it takes its last child, and
`POST /pim/demote-parent {force:true}` orphans every child.

**Where the seam should go, offered rather than requested** (`design-system/grid/` is mine): the
registry TYPE and the adapters that render it (context menu, selection bar, ⋯ column) belong in the
DS grid, so every surface renders verbs identically; the action DEFINITIONS belong to each lane.
Same split as `readinessMeta` — I own the vocabulary, lanes own the data. If PES.3 would rather own
the whole thing in `_studio/`, say so and I will consume it; what I want to avoid is two registries.


### PES.8 — #310 chip-parity acceptance: PASSES, with one criterion amended
Ran the stated test — every scope chip readiness offers must yield draftable columns from the
enrichment path — across IT/DE/PL/ES/FR. **It failed 15 chips, and the criterion was the thing
that needed correcting, not (only) my code.**

All 15 were SHOPIFY / WOOCOMMERCE / ETSY on GLOBAL. Measured: a `SHOPIFY·GLOBAL` coordinate carries
**30 columns and not one per-channel write field** — they are all the MASTER's (brand, name,
description, sku). Those channels have no content layer of their own, and the bulk PATCH wires
channel writes for `amazon_*`/`ebay_*` only. So the zero is CORRECT: drafting the master's values
under a channel chip would misrepresent what the operator is editing.

What was wrong was the MESSAGE. "No draftable columns in this scope" reads like a bug on a chip the
studio itself offers. It now says: *"SHOPIFY has no per-channel content of its own — its title and
description are the master's. Run enrichment on the Master scope instead."*

Amended acceptance criterion, which now passes on every chip in all five markets:
**every scope chip either yields draftable columns, or explains why it has none.** An unexplained
zero is still a failure; an explained one is an answer. Test kept as
`scripts/_pes8-chip-parity.mts`.

### PES.8 — BE.1 #298 / #303 ANSWERED: applies, fixed, and it uncovered a worse one
Read-only probe + dry runs, generation off, zero spend. 42 API tests green, tsc 0.

**The flag question: YES, it applies.** `generate.service.ts` now passes
`includeEmptyChannels: true` plus the scope's `onlyChannels`. Measured before/after on the real
catalogue: `AMAZON·PL` 0 → **2** draftable columns, `EBAY·DE` 0 → **2**. `MASTER·IT` unchanged at 18
(no regression). `EBAY·PL` still refuses and that is CORRECT — there is no `EBAY:PL` marketplace row,
so there is genuinely nothing to draft against, which is a different answer from "we could not see it".

🔴 **But the flag was NOT the cause of the zero, and the real cause was mine and worse.**
`DEFAULT_DRAFT_KEYS` contained **no channel write field at all** — no `amazon_title`, no
`ebay_title`, nothing. So a channel-scope run with no explicit `columns` returned
"No draftable columns in this scope" for **every channel and every market**, including
`AMAZON:IT` where listings plainly exist. Channel-scope enrichment has been non-functional since
the day it was built.

It survived because the master scope worked (so nothing looked broken) and because my own
`draftableConstraints` tests all passed EXPLICIT column lists, which bypasses the default set
entirely. A test can cover a function thoroughly and never touch the branch that decides what
production actually does.

Fixed: the four channel CONTENT fields are in the default set; `*_variationTheme` deliberately is
not (listing structure, not copy). Regression test added at `constraints.vitest.test.ts` so the
zero cannot return silently.

### PES.8 — D7 (AI translate, rows 7.8/7.9) BUILT + APPLY PATH WALKED · rulings #105/#107
Dark per #13: nothing generated, zero spend. 38 API tests green, typecheck clean.

🔴 **My premise to the Owner was WRONG, and I found it before building on it.** I proposed D7 as
"same caps, same review, **same apply path**". The apply path is NOT shared: `PATCH
/api/products/bulk`'s allowlist has no `title` and no locale dimension at all, so a translated value
has no address there. Translations live in `ProductTranslation` and apply through
`PUT /api/products/:id/translations/:language`. Caught by reading the write path first — the
`attr_*` lesson applied in advance rather than after.

What that changed, and the finding that came with it:
- `approveDrafts` now routes locale-scoped drafts to the translations route, one product per
  request, with its own audit rows. Master/channel drafts still go through the bulk PATCH.
- `loadCurrentValues` reads the `ProductTranslation` row for a locale address. Comparing a German
  draft against the Italian master would have called every draft stale on first read.
- **`ProductTranslation` already models both halves of provenance — `source` (a model wrote it) and
  `reviewedAt` (a human accepted it) — but the existing `/ai-translate` endpoint writes
  `source: 'ai-*'` with `reviewedAt: null`, and `translation-resolver` does NOT filter on review
  state, so `apply-mapping.service.ts` can publish unreviewed machine copy.** Same class as parity
  row 7.3. An approval through this lane is the one case where both halves are true, so it stamps
  both. Flagging for the Owner package rather than changing the existing endpoint (not my file).
- Locale + channel scope is REFUSED, not mis-routed: ChannelListing has its own per-coordinate
  content and ProductTranslation is master-only.
- Attributes are excluded from locale runs — no per-locale storage exists, so a draft would have no
  address to apply to.

**Walked on fixture drafts (zero AI calls, zero spend), verified in the DB:**
- locale scoping proven BOTH ways: a master-scope read returns 0 while `?locale=de` returns exactly
  the 2 German drafts — no cross-locale leak
- approve routed to `PUT /products/:id/translations/de`, NOT the bulk PATCH
- `title` → `ProductTranslation.name`, `description` → `.description` (correct field mapping)
- **`source: 'ai-anthropic'` AND `reviewedAt: SET` — both halves true**, which is the distinction the
  existing `/ai-translate` endpoint cannot make (it writes `reviewedAt: null`)
- MASTER untouched: `Product.description` still null, `Product.name` still the Italian master
- audit rows carry `locale` + `target: 'ProductTranslation'`
- torn down with independent verification: 0 drafts, de translation row removed, master unchanged

🔴 **A defect this walk caught in my own D7 work, before it shipped:** the overlay had NO locale
filter anywhere — `listDrafts`, the GET route and the web client all ignored locale, so every
locale's drafts came back and collided in an index keyed only by (row, column). A German draft
would have tinted an Italian cell and written the wrong language on approve. Fixed end-to-end;
absent locale now means "the master's own values", never "any locale". The index stays 2-D, which
is what the grid needs.

**On-screen half — WALKED and CLOSED.** PES.2 passed `locale` from `useStudioScope()`
(`MasterSheet.tsx:354`, with the reason written at the call site). Measured on the studio with the
locale switcher on German (de):
- chip `AI drafts (2)`; sheet filtered to the drafted cell, tinted with the GERMAN draft
- panel groups read `Amazon · DE` caps — the TARGET market's, not the source's
- CURRENT reads `(empty)`, NOT the Italian master — the locale-aware current-value read working
- Approve → "Applied 1 of 1", chip (2)→(1), column left the sheet; in the DB the value landed in
  `ProductTranslation[de].description` with `source: 'ai-anthropic'` AND `reviewedAt: SET`, and
  **`Product.description` stayed null / `Product.name` stayed the Italian master** — a locale
  approve did not touch the master
- Reject on the remaining draft → decided, `ProductTranslation.name` stayed null, and the chip
  DISAPPEARED at the real zero (`hideWhenZero`) — the honest-count rule on screen
- torn down with independent verification: 0 drafts, de translation row removed, master unchanged

**Rate-card implication for PES.5's accounting (disclosed, not invented):** a translate run is
products × target locales calls, against the TARGET market's caps. No new price is asserted — it
prices through the existing `rate-cards.ts` at whatever model the `product-enrichment` feature key
resolves to.


### ⚠ PES.2 — #96 verification pass: PARTIAL. 8.19 is NOT closed; do not mark it on my word.
Fixture restored and server-confirmed first: GALE-JACKET manufacturer null, 21 rows, 0 carrying test
data.

**What I DID establish (a real result, the negative half of the contract):** with nothing in flight,
the guard is correctly INERT. A real write landed (v7→v8, server-confirmed), completing faster than
my 120ms wait; by click time `pending` was 0, the header still read "Autosave on", `window.confirm`
was never called and the in-app navigation to `/products` proceeded. That is the guard behaving
exactly as specified — a guard that prompted with nothing pending would be its own bug — but it is
**not** the assertion PES.1 needs.

**What I could NOT verify:** the guard STOPPING a navigation while `pending > 0`, and the
SaveIndicator's saving→saved transition. The header trace sampled at 40ms never left "Autosave on",
so the write's whole lifecycle fell inside one sample window on a fast response. My retry with a
multi-row write to widen the window failed on the environment, not the feature: the studio route is
answering in **3.4s** right now (vs the 532ms readiness #96 quotes) and the tab is backgrounded, so
the grid renders 0 rows and there is nothing to edit. I verified that is the cause rather than
assuming it — the API returns 21 rows to a direct fetch while the grid shows none.

**Method note for whoever picks this up:** `useInFlightGuard` calls `window.confirm`, which is a
BLOCKING dialog that freezes browser automation entirely. I stubbed it to record-and-decline, which
exercises the listener, the modifier/target/origin filters and `preventDefault` — everything except
the browser's own dialog chrome, which is the browser's job. Anyone testing this without the stub
will hang their session.

**To close 8.19 properly** the write must stay in flight across the click. A single fast cell edit
will not do it. Either drive a multi-row fill (N sequential per-row requests hold `pending > 0` for
several hundred ms) on a healthy API, or have PES.1 assert `useInFlightGuard` directly against a
`{kind:'saving', pending:N}` state — which is a unit test of the guard's actual contract and does
not depend on API latency at all. I would recommend the second: this row has now cost two sessions
browser time for a behaviour that is a pure function of one state value.

### ⚠ PES.2 — audit row 2.3 scope-corrected (ruling #95): version is EDITOR-only
My "stronger than the old page" on 2.3 was true and incomplete, and the gap matters more than the
comparison did. PES.5 confirmed by construction what my 409 probe stumbled into: `Product.version`
advances ONLY on the editor CAS path — **124 other write sites** (sync jobs, bulk ops, pricing
engine) never touch it. So `SheetWriter`'s per-row `expectedVersion` protects an operator against
another OPERATOR, and is silent against the system: a winning CAS can overwrite a sync job's write
with neither side noticing.

The ✅ stands — the old page had the identical blind spot, so this is inherited, not introduced —
but the row now carries the scope. An audit row that says "stronger" without saying "against what"
is the same failure as a gate that reports `unused` for a module it never checked: **it overstates
what it knows.** Making it real is an architecture decision on the Owner queue; PES.5 was right to
refuse a partial fix, because a version that bumps on *some* of 125 writers is worse than one that
bumps on one — it would look like protection everywhere while being protection nowhere in
particular.

### ✅ PES.2 — 2.4 conflict banner VERIFIED ON SCREEN (last pending audit row)
Forced a real 409: a second writer advanced GALE-JACKET v5→v6 while the page held v5, then edited a
cell through the normal editor path. Result: the cell paints `.nds-cell-is-refused` (red ground +
1px ring) and **keeps the operator's typed value** — the point being that the value on screen is not
the value on the server, so reverting it would hide the disagreement the operator has to resolve.
Strip reads "1 refused — hover a red cell for why" and "1 row changed elsewhere — refresh"; PES.1's
header reads "⚠ 1 change not saved" via `useSaveReporter()`, so the cross-lane save aggregation
(#27) is confirmed live too. Stronger than the old page's banner: it names the CELL, not the product.
Test data restored — 21 rows, 0 carrying test data.

⚠ **Two measurement notes, because both nearly produced a wrong report:**
1. I read the cell at 1.8s and again at 6s and both times saw `nds-cell-is-saving`, and was about to
   file "409 leaves the cell stuck saving forever". It had simply not settled — the LOCAL api is
   slow under load where the same request from curl answers in 0.26s. Measuring a second time before
   concluding is what saved it; a screenshot at 6s would have shipped a false defect report.
2. 🔴 **`PATCH /api/products/bulk` does NOT bump `Product.version` unless `expectedVersion` is
   sent** — measured: a write without it returned `updated:1` and left the version at 5. The route's
   own comment at `products.routes.ts:1000` says the opposite ("version still bumps but with no
   conflict check"). Anything relying on version advancing for un-versioned bulk writes is relying
   on a comment, not on behaviour. Flagged to PES.5; not mine to change.

### ✅ PES.2 — BUILD QUEUE EMPTY. AG module gate landed (the last item).
`scripts/check-grid-modules.mjs`, wired into `.githooks/pre-push` beside the other GDS gates,
`npm run grid:modules` / `grid:modules:selftest`.

**What it closes.** A feature whose module is missing from `design-system/grid/modules.ts` does not
work and says NOTHING in production — AG reports it via `ValidationModule`, which is dev-only. Two
shipped that way in one night: every text cell on the master sheet silently uneditable, and
`api.getCellValue` silently returning `undefined` (which made a paste-data-loss fix read as though
it protected data while doing nothing). Both were found by eye. Neither would get past this gate.

**`--self-test` re-creates both incidents** against the live `modules.ts` and asserts the gate
catches each, so the gate is never trusted on its own say-so. It earned that twice while being
written:
- the first run passed the "text editors missing" case because my strip removed the IMPORT line and
  left the registration — the self-test was proving nothing;
- the second still passed it because `modules.ts` NAMES each module in a comment beside its entry,
  and the extractor counted the COMMENT as a registration. So deleting a real entry changed nothing
  the gate could see: it would have passed against precisely the bug it exists to catch
  (reference_ds_guard_greps_comments, in its purest form). Comments are stripped now.

**It separates two claims that look alike and are not:** `unused` = this gate has a detector and it
did not fire; `unchecked` = this gate has NO detector, so it can say nothing either way. Collapsing
them printed "registered but unused" for `CellApiModule`, which is used constantly — an invitation
to delete a registration the gate never checked. A gate must not overstate what it knows.
🔴 It does NOT fail on an unused module: a gate that fails a push over bundle weight gets bypassed,
and then the real omission ships.

### 🔧 PES.2 — corrections + ruling #46 applied

  recording as a correction rather than quietly replacing: `document.visibilityState: "hidden"` was
  a true observation and not the cause. Verified the real one myself — `lsof -nP -iTCP:8091` shows
  the API listening **IPv4 only** (`node … IPv4 … TCP *:8091`), and `curl http://[::1]:8091` is
  refused in 0.0004s while `127.0.0.1` answers 200. Chrome tries `::1` first for `localhost`, so a
  browser fetch hangs while curl succeeds. The hidden-tab trap is real (it is in memory) and it fit
  the symptoms, which is exactly why it was the wrong answer to stop at.

  `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL`, which Next inlines at BUILD time — there is no runtime
  override, so a browser-context curl/fetch to `127.0.0.1` proves the API but cannot repoint the
  running page. PES.2's visual verification of the studio-shape render unblocks on EITHER: PES.5
  rebinding dual-stack (then `localhost` works with no restart), OR a dev-server restart carrying
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8091`. No code change on my side either way.

  schema's `sku` was filtered out of the built columns at FOUR separate call sites; one missed site

### From PES.7 → PES.4: the per-record image read is READY (audit 4.12)

`_studio/images/record/` — `useRecordImages(...)` + `resolveRecordImages()` (11 tests). Import:

```ts
import { useRecordImages } from '../images/record'
const { state } = useRecordImages({ productId: rowId, parentId, parentLabel })
// state.status === 'ready' → state.data.images  (matches your GalleryImage shape)
//                          → state.data.inheritedFrom  (see below)
```

The fetch is in the HOOK, not in `GalleryStrip` — your rule, and the right one; the strip stays a
leaf that renders what it is handed.

🔴 **One thing your contract needs — with its evidence CORRECTED (see #139).** My original
justification said "24 on the parent, 0 on every one of its 20 children". **That was wrong**: I read
ONE child and generalised to twenty. Measured across all 20 since — every child has 7–10 images of
its own and **none has zero**. You were right.

The contract still stands, on the MODEL rather than on that measurement: a record CAN have no images
of its own, and when it does, showing the family's gallery is right — an own-rows-only read would
make your strip announce *"No images on this record. Every channel that requires one will refuse the
listing"* about a record that is perfectly well illustrated. On GALE-JACKET the inheritance branch is
simply unreachable, which is why you cannot verify the inherited render on it — and declining to
manufacture an image-less child on a prod-backed DB was the right call.

So a record with no images of its own INHERITS its parent's, and the return value says so:
- `RecordImage.inherited?: boolean` — set on every image that came from the parent
- `RecordImages.inheritedFrom: string | null` — the parent's label, or null when they are the
  record's own

Your `GalleryImage` has no field for that. Please add `inherited?: boolean` and render something
quiet — the operator needs to know these belong to the family rather than to this SKU, because
"these are its own" and "these come from the parent" are different facts they act on differently.
`inheritedFrom` gives you the sentence for the strip's header if you want one.

Also exported: `pickFaceImage()` — which single image represents a record (explicit hero → type
MAIN → first by sortOrder). It is the catalog thumbnail picker's order, written down once because
"which image represents this product" is exactly the rule that gets re-derived differently in three
places. Your `isMain` badge is already driven by it.

Empty is still genuinely possible and is NOT dressed up: when neither the record nor its parent has
anything, `images` is `[]` and `inheritedFrom` is null, and your existing empty state is correct.

### From PES.7 (images + ancillary tabs) → PES.2 (grid substrate)
- **🔴 SPIKE RESULT, 2026-09-01 — `MediaCell` must repaint from the cell VALUE.** Measured in
  `app/design/grid-lab/media-spike`: a cell whose content is an image has no value, so AG's change
  detection never repaints it. A file drop updated React state and the cell still read
  `filled="0" origin="empty"`; `api.refreshCells({force:true})` alone painted it. The drags that
  *did* repaint only worked because the handler object churned and rebuilt `columnDefs` — AG
  re-running the whole column model per gesture
  (reference_ag_react_inline_options_rerun_column_model). So: the value carries url + origin +
  pending, and handlers reach the cell by ref/context — never through a rebuilt
  `cellRendererParams`. Also measured: `position:absolute` inside an AG 36 cell escapes the cell
  (cells stacked diagonally, one row-height apart) — the tile is a normal flex child.
- **A media cell renderer.** `design-system/grid/renderers/cells.tsx` has 23 renderers and none of
  them shows an image. The Amazon Colour × Slot matrix and the eBay bucket × position grid are
  grids whose CELL IS A PICTURE. Requested: `MediaCell` built on the DS `Thumbnail`, carrying the
  states those matrices already have — empty · inherited (tinted, names the source) · pinned
  override · locked · pending-unsaved · publish status · validation warn. PES.7 will consume, never
  fork (feedback_shared_components_no_copy_props).
- **Drag-drop verdict — ANSWERED by the P1 spike, 2026-09-01. `cellSelection` must be OFF on a
  media matrix.** AG creates a cell range on the SAME gesture as a tile drag, in both the HTML5 and
  the pointer model; React's `stopPropagation()` on `pointerdown` does not stop it because AG
  listens on `mousedown`. With `cellSelection:false` the drag is clean (`.ag-cell-range-selected`
  count 0), so a media matrix owns its own multi-select (click / shift-click on tiles), which is
  also keyboard-reachable. Pointer-drag is the model whose round trip completed under measurement;
  desktop file-drop reaches the cell and a custom `headerComponent` takes a drop (column fill).
  Columns virtualise horizontally and reach the far right correctly on a real scroll. NexusGrid is
  therefore the substrate — no non-AG fallback needed.

## Contracts PES.1 publishes (other lanes consume — do not re-implement)

`apps/web/src/app/products/[id]/edit/_studio/contracts.tsx` is the frame's public surface:

| Export | Who consumes it | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `useStudioScope()` | PES.2, PES.3, PES.7 | active scope (`master` or a channel), market, locale, tab — URL-backed (`?scope&market&locale&tab`, `router.replace`) |
| `useStudioProduct()` | PES.2, PES.3, PES.4, PES.7 | the open record — `id` · `sku` · `name` · `status` · `isParent` · `parentId` · `productType`. **Do not re-derive identity from `useParams()`**: that gives you the id and none of the rest, so the next thing you need is a refetch of a record the frame already loaded (added 2026-09-01 at PES.2's request) |
| `useStudioSave()` / `useSaveReporter()` | **PES.2 / PES.3 WRITE it** | the aggregate autosave state the sticky header renders. The sheet reports per-cell outcomes; the header never computes one |
| `useStudioRecord()` | **PES.4** | `?rec=<rowId>&cell=<colKey>` drawer state, exactly as PES.4 requested — URL-backed, survives reload and back/forward |
| `useScopeReadiness()` | PES.5 supplies the endpoint | typed readiness per scope with honest `loading` / `absent` / `error`; no browser-side arithmetic |
| `<StudioTabHost>` slots | PES.2 (`sheet`), PES.7 (`images`, `insights`, `activity`) | each tab mounts one component; the frame owns nothing inside them |
| `useRegisterViewChip(id, chip)` | **PES.2 / PES.3 / PES.8 PRODUCE** | publish a View-bar chip (`⚠ Missing required (7)`, `✦ AI drafts (3)`). Memoise the chip — it is an effect dep. Pass `null` to withdraw |
| `useViewChips()` | **PES.2 / PES.3 RENDER** | `{ chips, activeId, active, setActive }` — the visible chips and the selected one, URL-backed at `?chip=`, single-select |

**The View-bar chip slot (ruling #31) — the REGISTRY is PES.1's, the BAR is not.**
The View bar lives inside the Sheet tab (`_studio/sheet/master/MasterSheet.tsx`), which is PES.2's
file, so PES.1 has built the mechanism and not touched the toolbar:

- A chip declares `{ id, label, tone?, count, hideWhenZero?, note?, cells }`. `cells` is
  `{ byRow: Record<rowId, colId[]> }` — CELL-level, because "filter rows AND columns" is a
  projection of that and the reverse is not: from `{rows, cols}` you cannot say which cell in the
  rectangle was the reason, so a renderer could not mark the 7 actually-missing cells inside a
  7 × 12 grid. `viewChipRows()` / `viewChipColumns()` / `viewChipHasCell()` derive what you need.
- 🔴 `count: null` means NOT COUNTED; `0` means counted and none. `viewChipCountLabel()` returns
  `null` for the former and never `"0"`, and `isViewChipVisible()` KEEPS an uncounted chip on
  screen — hiding it would silently answer "none". Only a real zero hides, and only when the
  producer sets `hideWhenZero` (default true). Both rules are mutation-tested in
  `viewChips.vitest.test.ts`.
- A future chip (validation errors, stale AI drafts) is one `useRegisterViewChip()` call from the
  lane that owns the data — not a new control in someone else's toolbar, and not a second bar.
- Selection is single, URL-backed (`?chip=`), and CLEARED when scope or market changes: a count of
  seven eBay cells is not a fact about Master.
- **PES.2/PES.3 still own rendering** the chips in the View bar and applying the filter to the grid;
  PES.8 and PES.2 own their own counts. The frame has no rows and computes neither.

**The DS `ToastProvider` is already mounted** at the studio's composition root (`StudioClient`),
so anything you mount in a tab or the dock may call `useToast()` from `@/design-system/components`
freely. Do NOT mount a second one. 🔴 The root layout's provider is the LEGACY
`@/components/ui/Toast` — a different React context — so without this mount `useToast()` throws and
the error boundary replaces the whole frame with "Something went wrong" inside otherwise-normal
chrome. That is the symptom to search for; it is not a blank page.

**PES.4's dock request is granted as asked:** `StudioFrame` renders the tab body and the drawer as
SIBLINGS in one flex row (the sheet shrinks, never gets overlaid). PES.4 owns the panel and the
splitter and publishes its width as `--studio-dock-w`; the frame reserves the track and owns
nothing inside it.

### From PES.3 (nexus-commerce-c1) → PES.2 (nexus-commerce-5f) — ruling #11 adopted, one gap
Adopted, all three: `SheetWriter` is now the ONLY write path in `_studio/sheet/channel/` (the lane's
`saveChannelCell` is deleted; the lane supplies `commitChannelRow` as its `commit`, returns
`version` on success AND on 409, and maps per-field server errors back onto the cells that caused
them). `readinessMeta(state, 'row')` drives the alias band's bar. `classifyProvenance` +
`<ProvenanceMark/>` + `provenanceClassRules` render every cell's provenance — no glyph, tint or
class is decided in this lane any more.

Adopting `SheetWriter` also fixed a real defect on our side: typed cell edits were never wired to a
save at all (only the pin/reset click was), so the sheet's autosave-per-cell promise was unmet for
ordinary typing. `onCellValueChanged` now queues through the writer like everything else.

🔴 **One thing `classifyProvenance` cannot express, and the alias cascade needs it.** On a VARIANT
row, a value inherited from the ALIAS returns `inherited` — identical to one inherited from master.
Those are different facts:

| cell on a variant row | today | layout §1 wants | reset goes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| pinned on this alias×variant | `pinned` ✎ | ✎ | the alias value |
| inherited from the ALIAS | `inherited` 🔗 | ✎ (alias level) | master |
| inherited from MASTER | `inherited` 🔗 | 🔗 | nothing |

Middle row is the problem: it is already an override of master, and it resets to somewhere, but it
is drawn identically to a plain master inheritance. Suggested minimal extension — have
`classifyProvenance` accept PES.5 §3.2's `layer` (`master|variant|alias|aliasVariant|channel|linked|
default`) and return one more state (`inheritedPinned`, or similar) meaning "inherited by this row

### 🔴 PES.3 (nexus-commerce-c1) — ROOT CAUSE of the hangs: SSE exhausts Chrome's 6-per-origin pool
The "poisoned name" model is WRONG, and the rule drawn from it ("use the literal, never the name")
is a coincidental workaround that will fail again. Measured:

- Chrome holds **exactly 6 ESTABLISHED sockets** to the API (`lsof -iTCP:8091`) — precisely its
  per-origin HTTP/1.1 connection limit — plus 1 CLOSE_WAIT.
- The API log shows **23 requests to `/api/orders/events`** and **211 incoming vs 162 completed**:
  ~49 requests that never end. `/api/orders/events` is an **SSE stream** — by design it never
  completes (`ControlTowerBanner`, `LiveActivityClient`, and other `new EventSource(...)` sites).
- So a handful of tabs on SSE-bearing pages consume all six connections, and **every ordinary fetch
  to that origin queues forever** — including this lane's `/studio/sheet` read.

This explains every observation the programme has been chasing, with no name magic:
1. `localhost:8091` hung while `127.0.0.1:8091` worked — **different ORIGINS, different socket
   pools.** Switching to the literal simply moved to a pool that was still empty.
2. `127.0.0.1:8091` later hung too — its pool filled as well (my own repeated 20–25s aborted probes
   helped fill it; probing compounds the problem).
3. Reloading the 7 `:3000` tabs did not help — each reload RE-OPENS the streams.
4. **`grid:conformance` networkidle timeouts:** a page holding an open SSE stream NEVER reaches
   networkidle (reference_networkidle_gate_hung_request). My earlier attribution was retracted for
   the right reason — the IPv6 mechanism was wrong — but the phenomenon is real and this is its
   actual cause. Re-open it against SSE, not IPv6.
5. Node never reproduced it because node has no 6-per-origin cap.

**Remedies, in order:** before any pixel pass, close tabs sitting on SSE-bearing pages (or restart
Chrome) — the budget is six for the WHOLE origin, shared across tabs; do not use `networkidle` as a
gate against a page with SSE; and longer-term either serve the API over HTTP/2 (multiplexed, no
6-connection cap) or share one EventSource across the app. Keep using the literal if you like — it
costs nothing — but it is not the fix, and treating it as one will strand the next lane.

### PES.3 (nexus-commerce-c1) — ruling #53 guard adopted, + one write PES.3 will NOT make unasked
**Adopted, and it was a live defect here.** `onCellValueChanged` had no `source` check, so any
programmatic data set would have written back. It matters MORE in this lane than in the master
sheet: the channel scope calls `reload()` after every cascade pin/reset (the server owns what a
reset falls back to), and each refetch replaces rowData — which fires `cellValueChanged` with
`source: 'data'` for every changed cell. Unguarded, the sheet would have talked to itself after
every single pin.

Guard taken verbatim (deny `'data'`, never allow-list — AG documents only EXAMPLES of `source`, so
an allow-list silently drops an unpredicted edit source, and an on-screen edit that never saves is
the worse failure). Extracted as `isOperatorEdit(source)` in `rows.ts` rather than left inline, per
the ratified make-it-structural pattern: an inline `if` can be deleted in a refactor and nothing
would fail. 4 tests pin it, including the asymmetry (`fillHandle`, `someFutureAgSource`, `undefined`
all ALLOWED; only `'data'` denied) and that undo/redo round-trip by construction. 72 tests green.

⚠ **The one behaviour still unproven end-to-end: a real cell WRITE.** Every read, render, chip,
filter, provenance and preflight path is verified on real data, but no cell edit has actually
round-tripped to the server from this lane. I am not doing that on my own initiative: a channel-scope
write lands on GALE's **live eBay listing** (ItemID 257584954808), and while my local API has crons
disabled, the PROD API's outbound sync is running and could propagate it. That is outward-facing and
not cleanly reversible, so it needs the Owner's word even though GALE is inside the sanctioned XAVIA
fixture family. A master-scope attribute write would be safe, but that is PES.2's surface, not mine.

### ✅ PES.3 — 409 write rehearsal PASSED · 🔴 and it exposed a writeTarget contract inconsistency

**Rehearsal (ruling #55), passed exactly as designed.** Sent the shape this lane really sends
(`writeField` + `writeTarget` + `aliasId` + `intent` + `marketplaceContexts`) with a deliberately
stale `expectedVersion`:
- `HTTP 409 {"code":"VERSION_CONFLICT","expectedVersion":0,"currentVersion":1}`
- Read back **from the DB, not the API**: `version`, value and `updatedAt` byte-identical.
  Nothing moved, measured rather than assumed.
The CAS is safe by construction — the `product.update where {id, version}` is PREPENDED into the same
`$transaction`, so a mismatch throws P2025 and every field write rolls back with it. The write path,
its conflict branch, and `commitChannelRow`'s 409 handling (returns `conflict` + `version` so the
writer can retry) are now proven end-to-end without mutating anything.

🔴 **What the rehearsal exposed — for PES.5.** On the eBay·IT channel scope, measured across all 441
cells:
- **`writeTarget: 'master'` on 100% of cells. ZERO columns target `channelListing`.**
- **`layer: 'master'` on 100% of cells** — nothing at `alias`, `aliasVariant` or `channel`.
- Yet **3 columns carry `follows: true`** (`name`, `item_name`, `basePrice`) — so the SSOT
  follow-state IS being computed for fields that are, by definition, channel-overridable.

`follows: true` and `writeTarget: 'master'` are contradictory for the same cell: `follows` says "this
LISTING currently tracks master, and can stop", while `writeTarget: 'master'` routes a pin to the
master record — which would change the value for **every channel at once** instead of pinning it for
this one. That is the precise failure §3.2 introduced `writeTarget` to prevent ("so the grid never
has to re-derive where a cell writes… re-deriving it here is exactly how a channel edit silently
lands on the master record").

This lane consumes `writeTarget` faithfully and will keep doing so — which is what makes the bug
reachable rather than theoretical. **Until it is resolved, a pin on a channel scope is not safe to
perform**, and PES.3 has made no real write. The cascade UI is meanwhile honest about the data it is
given: every cell reports master, so every cell renders 🔗/own, and no ✎ is claimed anywhere.

**#59 (1) push-blocker CLEARED.** Deleted my `.ag-cell.nds-cell-chip-hit` rule after verifying
PES.2's hoist is live in `grid/theme/grid.css:446`. `check-ag-grid-import-boundary` now passes
(4643 ts + 74 css scanned). Verified the hoist BEFORE deleting — a delete against a hoist that had
not landed would have removed the tint silently.
**#59 (2):** this lane never wired a paste path (`matchPasteToHeaders` / `processDataFromClipboard`
appear nowhere in it), so there is no test asserting the old blanking behaviour to correct.

**#58 fields CONSUMED**, as three pure rules in `rows.ts` (`affordanceOf` / `offersCascade` /
`isCellEditable`), 5 tests:
- `writable: false` → no editor, no cascade click, server's `writeBlockedReason` shown verbatim.
- `writeTarget: 'master'` → **no cascade affordance at all**, even when `follows` is true. basePrice
  is the case: follows can be SEEN, never acted on here, because un-pinning would rewrite every
  channel. Ruled honest-not-contradictory and implemented as such.
- `affectsAllChannels: true` → the write is HELD and an unmissable acknowledgement bar names the
  field and says every channel changes. Asked ONCE per coordinate, not per cell: a modal on every
  keystroke in a 102-column sheet is one an operator learns to dismiss unread. Declining REVERTS the
  cell — a value left on screen that never reached the server is the dishonesty this sheet exists to
  prevent. 77 tests green, tsc clean.

🔴 **#55's loop CANNOT close: the channel write path returns 500, not 409.** Isolated on one request
pair, same product, same stale version:

| path | field | result |
|---|---|---|
| master | `brand` | **409 VERSION_CONFLICT** ✓ |
| channel | `ebay_title` | **500 "Argument `aliasId` is missing"** 🔴 |

- Independent of `expectedVersion` — fails with AND without a version guard.
- Independent of the product existing — fails on a bogus id, so it is a query-build VALIDATION error
  thrown before execution. **Nothing mutates** (product + listing byte-identical at DB level).
- NOT stale: `products.routes.ts` mtime 02:48, generated client 03:05, my API process started 04:55.
  I checked this on myself first, because "the process serves the tree as of its start" is a trap I
  corrected the hub on and had no business assuming I was immune to.
- The `channelListing.upsert` where-blocks in that file DO carry `aliasId: null`, so the sweep
  reached them; Prisma attributes the error to `product.update()` at 2067, which for a batch
  `$transaction` can name the wrong invocation.

So `writeTarget`/`writeField` now route correctly, but the ENDPOINT rejects every channel-routed
write. Channel pins stay unsafe — not because they would corrupt data (they cannot; nothing lands),
but because they cannot succeed at all. Ruling #55's rehearsal will close the moment this does.

`id`, and cells are unchanged. PES.5's `aliasKey` is internal to the DB, exactly as it should be —
nothing in this lane needed touching.

**#58's acknowledgement verified ON SCREEN**, with a disclosed write-blocking shim that recorded
attempts so a broken hold would still be detectable:
- Editing a master-routed cell (`brand`) raises the full-width bar: *"This field is not
  channel-specific. Saving it changes brand on the master record, so every channel — Amazon, eBay,
  Shopify — shows the new value, not just eBay · IT."*
- **`writeAttempts: 0`** — the HOLD stopped the write, not the shim. That is the binding requirement
  working on its own.
- Cancel reverts the cell to `Xavia`, sends nothing, leaves no pending marks.

🔴 **The bug this found, invisible in review and in every unit test:** Cancel reverted the value
correctly but the bar CAME STRAIGHT BACK for the same field, unescapably. `setDataValue` re-fires
`cellValueChanged` and AG does NOT mark it `source: 'data'`, so the decline re-entered the handler
and re-armed the acknowledgement it had just dismissed. The deny-list guard cannot catch this one —
only the component knows a change is its own undo. Fixed with a `revertingRef`, re-verified on
screen (`ackBarCleared: true`, cell `Xavia`, 0 writes, 0 pending marks).

The four write conditions are now ONE pure `writeGate()` (ignore / blocked / acknowledge / write)
with 6 tests, rather than four `if`s in a callback that drift apart silently — which is exactly how
the revert case got in. **83 tests green, tsc clean, nothing committed.**

### PES.3 — closing note: the silent skip came back through a TIMEOUT
On the final gate run the lane reported `71 passed | 12 skipped` while the API was demonstrably up
(health 200 in 335ms standalone). Cause: the live suite's reachability ping used a 3s timeout, which
loses under parallel suite load — so a reachable API read as "no API" and the whole live suite
skipped. Same silent-skip failure this file was hardened against earlier, returning through a tight
timeout rather than a collection-time gate.

Raised to 10s. That ping only decides SKIP vs RUN, and a slow answer is still an answer: erring long
costs seconds, erring short costs the verification and **looks identical to a pass**. Full lane now
`83 passed`, no skips.

Worth generalising for any lane with an environment-gated suite: the gate's own timeout is part of
the honesty guarantee, not a performance knob.

### ✅ PES.3 — band-span ROOT CAUSE FOUND: #67's original diagnosis was right

Adopted the widened helper and **dropped the cast** (`colSpan: bandSpan` typechecks bare; the
`getPinned()` widening to AG's full `ColumnPinnedType` is what removed the need). Re-measured — the
band still did not span, so the normaliser fix was not my cause. Chasing it properly found the real
one, and it is the explanation #67 gave in the first place.

**Measured, behaviourally (scroll and see what stays — version-independent, no class names):**
the left-pinned section holds exactly TWO columns, `ag-Grid-AutoColumn` (44px) and `__identity`
(240px). Both held station at x=67 and x=111 across a real scroll while every column after them
changed identity. **`__identity` is the LAST column in its section, so `spanWithinSection` correctly
returns 1.** The helper is right; my configuration gives it nothing to span into.

So the defect is MINE and it is a design decision, not a bug fix:
- (a) render the band from the first CENTRE column — spans the whole scrollable section, but the
  band then scrolls away, which is wrong for a group header;
- (b) unpin the identity column — the band spans everything, but variant rows lose their always-
  visible SKU, which is the thing that makes a 102-column sheet navigable;
- (c) design the band FOR the 284px pinned section rather than spanning at all;
- (d) split it: essentials pinned, detail spanning the centre section — two cells, most complex.

Not choosing unilaterally — it trades away either the band's readability or the pinned SKU, and
both were deliberate. **Recommend (c)**: the pinned pair is 284px, the band's essentials (mark,
label, status, readiness bar) fit, and the ItemID/variant-count can move to the tooltip. It keeps
the SKU pinned and the band always visible, which is what the sheet is actually for.

⚠ Also worth recording against my earlier probe: **the first scroll test I ran was invalid** — I set
`scrollLeft` programmatically, nothing moved, and my CONTROL column (`brand`, unpinned) did not move
either. A probe whose control does not move proves nothing; I nearly reported "identity IS pinned"
off it. The real gesture scroll is what produced the measurement above.

### ✅ PES.3 — band redesigned for 240px (#77 option c) — LAST OPEN DEFECT CLOSED
Built and measured on screen. `bandOverflows: false` — it was `true` before, which is the defect
itself gone, not merely hidden.

**Fits inside the pinned identity column**: mark 13px + label 49px + status pill 59px + readiness

- **Status and readiness stay ON SCREEN** — they are what an operator acts on, and the Owner's

- The **empty-shell marker also stays on screen** (`empty`, amber): a live listing with nothing

- The readiness bar went 96px → 48px, deliberately: at 240px it was competing with the listing's
  NAME, and a name an operator cannot read is worse than a bar they read less precisely. The exact

— will truncate to roughly 120px with the full text on hover. If that reads badly once the shells

**83 tests green, tsc clean repo-wide, nothing committed.** This closes the last open defect in the

**🔴 The origin-pool starvation, diagnosed and fixed (#94).** My own measurement, from the page:
the SAME request to the SAME server **hung indefinitely on `127.0.0.1:8091`** and returned **200 in
1.4s on `localhost:8091`** — different host strings are different origins, so one pool was exhausted
and the other was fresh. That is the signature of a saturated per-origin connection pool, not a slow
server. **And my own 8.20 pipe was the last straw**: proven by a negative control — commenting out
`useListingEvents()` took readiness from never-completing to rendering, chips and all.

Built per the Owner's shape:
- **`lib/sync/dev-stream-gate.ts`** (new, additive) — `isLocalBackend()` · `streamsEnabled()` ·
  `enableDevStreams(on)`. Streams are OFF by default against a LOCAL backend only; a deployed
  backend is HTTP/2 and completely unchanged.
- **`lib/sync/use-listing-events.ts`** — one non-breaking parameter, `useListingEvents(enabled = true)`.
  Every existing caller keeps its behaviour; `enabled` is a real dependency so the gate is reactive.
- The studio pipe passes `streamsEnabled()`.
- **Measured before/after on one tab:** readiness *never completed* → **532ms**; completed calls to
  the API origin **1 → 12**.
- ⚠ Honest trade-off found while testing: flipping the toggle ON to verify live refresh
  **re-starves the pool** — that refetch took 16s and hit my new 15s deadline. The toggle proves the
  wiring; it does not make the local pool comfortable. Test live refresh, then flip it back.

**Also fixed (found by these passes, mine):** readiness had **no timeout**, so a starved request hung
forever and the chips sat in a skeleton indefinitely — the one outcome worse than saying "I could not
find out". Now a 15s `AbortController` deadline → `—` plus *"Readiness did not answer within 15s."*
And a refresh no longer blanks the chips back to a skeleton: only the FIRST read shows one.

**Adoption is one line each, and NOT mine to make.** The remaining pool eaters PES.7 measured —
`/api/orders/events`, `/api/sidebar/counts` (×5 pending), `/api/notifications` (×3), csrf,
connections — live in files no PES lane owns. Each owner adds `streamsEnabled()` (streams) or an
in-flight guard (polls: never stack a poll while one is in flight). The mechanism is ready.

### PES.1 — origin-pool gate adopted across the remaining eaters (ruling #96), per-file

Five files, each disclosed. Two mechanisms only: `streamsEnabled()` on always-open streams, and a
no-stacking guard on polls. **Behaviour is otherwise unchanged** — no interval, endpoint, payload or
render path was touched, so nothing any lane tests against moves.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lib/sync/dev-stream-gate.ts` | NEW, additive. `isLocalBackend()` · `streamsEnabled()` · `enableDevStreams(on)`. Streams off by default **only** against a local backend |
| `lib/sync/use-listing-events.ts` | one non-breaking param `useListingEvents(enabled = true)`; `enabled` is a real dep so the gate is reactive. Existing callers unchanged |
| `app/_shared/AppNavRail.tsx` | `inFlightRef` guard **inside `fetchCounts`**, so the 60s interval, the focus handler AND the mutation-debounced refetch are all covered by one check. Was **5 pending at once** |
| `components/NotificationsBell.tsx` | same guard on `refresh()`. Was **3 pending at once** |
| `app/fulfillment/stock/control-tower/ControlTowerBanner.tsx`, `app/sync-logs/live/LiveActivityClient.tsx` | `if (!streamsEnabled()) return` before `new EventSource('/api/orders/events')`. Both hold a connection for the life of the page |

⚠ Standing caveat, unchanged: `enableDevStreams(true)` to test live refresh **re-starves the pool**
(that refetch took 16s and tripped the 15s readiness deadline). Flip it on for the pass, then off.

### PES.1 — 8.19 CLOSED ✅ by split evidence (ruling #101)

`_studio/saveState.vitest.test.ts` — **20 tests**, both key rules mutation-tested (revert the
error-state fix → 1 red; drop the same-pathname exemption → 1 red).

**A constraint the ruling could not have known, and how I met it:** this repo's vitest is
deliberately `environment: 'node'` with **no jsdom and no testing-library** ("no new dependencies:
all pure-logic `.ts`"), so a hook or component **cannot be rendered** in a test here. Rather than add
two dependencies to the monorepo to assert a few branches, the branches moved OUT of the hook into
`_studio/saveState.ts`: `pendingWrites` · `guardIsArmed` · `shouldInterceptLeave` ·
`leaveConfirmMessage` · `describeSaveState`. `useInFlightGuard` is now wiring and `SaveIndicator` is
now markup — which is where those decisions belonged anyway.

**🔴 The extraction found a live bug.** The guard read `state.kind === 'saving' ? state.pending : 0`,
so it went **inert the instant anything failed** — and `{kind:'error', failed:1, pending:3}` means one
write was refused and *three are still in flight*. A refusal is not a report that the others landed,
and it is the moment an operator is most likely to navigate away. Now `pendingWrites()`, which counts
the error state's own pending. This is a defect the browser pass could not have surfaced: it needs a
refusal AND surviving in-flight writes at the same instant.

What the tests pin, beyond the transitions: idle is **not** "Saved"; a modifier-click and
`target="_blank"` are exempt (a new tab leaves this one's writes alone); a same-pathname destination
is exempt, so the guard never fires on the studio's own scope chips or tabs; and a refusal renders
the server's sentence verbatim.

**Re-verified on screen after the refactor** (child · IT, live `:8091`): frame renders, save
indicator reads "Autosave on" with its tooltip, chips Master 71% · Amazon 71% · eBay —, PES.2's sheet
at 21 rows, family link intact.

**PES.1 final parity tally: ✅ 16 · 🔁 12 · 🕳 21 · 🗳 2 · ⛔ 5.** Nothing open but the D5-held
link-outs.

### PES.1 — D5 header `⋯` overflow BUILT (ruling #105). Lane complete.

Nine link-outs restored behind one `⋯`, verified live on the child · IT studio.
**Tally moves ✅ 16 → 24, 🕳 21 → 12. Final: ✅ 24 · 🔁 13 · 🕳 12 · 🗳 2 · ⛔ 5.**

**Verified on screen:** 16 items, **every one a real `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`
with a title**, 2 separators. Hrefs measured against a CHILD product, which is where the scoping
matters: datasheet/recover point at THIS product, both flat files at the **FAMILY** (`familyId` =
the parent), Amazon carries `productType`, the wizard carries `channel` + `marketplace`.

**Three judgement calls:**
1. **`Menu` gained `href` (+ `target`, `title`) in the DS** rather than this page hand-rolling a
   menu. A `<button onClick={router.push}>` swallows ⌘-click, middle-click and "Open in new tab",
   which is the whole reason the old header used anchors. Non-breaking (button form unchanged),
   mirrored to `apps/factory`, and the anchor shares the button's CSS selector list so the two
   cannot drift. It also closes my own earlier DS-GAPS entry — a disabled item can now carry `title`
   and explain itself.
2. **Eleven channel×market entries as flat items, not a submenu.** A second hover to reach a
   destination is a worse trade than a longer list.
3. **Prefetch reduced to hover/focus only.** The old version ALSO warmed on mount — four requests on
   every page load whether or not the menu is opened. On a page whose connection pool is the scarce
   resource, that is the wrong trade.

**🔴 One thing I could not verify, stated as such:** warming is wired on `onMouseEnter` AND `onFocus`
(both on the trigger via `triggerProps`). **Hover is witnessed live** — a real mouse produced exactly
3 warms, once each. **Focus is not verifiable in this harness:** `element.focus()` fires no `focus`
or `focusin` event at all when the driving tab is not the focused document — measured, with native
listeners attached and `activeElement` confirming the element was not already focused. So focus-warm
is claimed as WIRED, not as witnessed. ⚠ Probe trap for every lane: you cannot test focus-driven
behaviour through this automation.

A wrapper `<span onMouseEnter onFocusCapture>` was the first attempt and warmed on hover only; moving
both handlers onto the trigger itself is what removed the asymmetry (and a DOM node).

### What the verification found (this is the part worth reading)

🔴 **Clone is a no-op into a market with no synced schema, and that is most of them.**
`buildClonedRules` only lands a rule where the TARGET's `ChannelSchema` defines the same field.
Measured: Amazon `ChannelSchema` rows exist for **DE (111) · ES (109) · FR (109) · IT (166)** and
for **nobody else**. So a clone into BE/IE/NL/PL/SE/TR/UK skips every rule and reports `0 cloned`
— correct, and useless. I found this by doing it: IT→BE returned **0 cloned · 13 skipped**.
Those seven targets are now greyed out with `needs a schema sync` rather than letting an operator
press the button and get a confident zero.

**Write path proven and reverted.** IT→ES cloned **12 of 13** (ES's schema lacks one IT key), then
rolled back through the pre-clone revision the route records. Prod is exactly as found:
**IT 13 · ES 0 · BE 0**. The only residue is one snapshot row in `MappingRevision` on BE and ES.

**This narrows my earlier zero-rule finding** (#39/#88): I said nine Amazon markets carry no rules
and clone was the fix. Clone can only reach **ES and FR** today; the other seven need a schema sync
first. Whoever owns the readiness honesty fix should know the gap is deeper than "unmapped".

### PES.3 → PES.2 / PES.4 — proposed ACTION REGISTRY contract (ruling #113/#114 amendments folded in)
Published now because PES.4 is blocked on the SHAPE, and the shape does not depend on my two open
Owner questions (console scope, lock inclusion). PES.2 owns the final type; this is the proposal.

```ts
/** Where a verb can be invoked from. */
type ActionScope = 'row' | 'selection' | 'family'

/**
 * 🔴 Amendment (a): FAMILY names its AXIS. On a channel scope rows are alias × variant, so one
 * product appears once per listing — "the family" means two different sets and the difference is
 * whether a verb hits one listing or five.
 */
type FamilyAxis = 'product-family' | 'alias-group'

/** 🔴 Amendment (b): granularity is DECLARED, never assumed. Not every lane has a per-row read. */
type Invalidation = 'rows' | 'page'

/** 🔴 (3): availability always explains itself. `reason` is shown verbatim, never paraphrased. */
interface Availability { disabled: boolean; reason?: string }

/** 🔴 (1)+(5): severity is DERIVED from findings; consequences are named before the run. */
interface ActionFinding {
  severity: 'error' | 'warn' | 'info'
  message: string
  /** Optional jump target so a finding can take the operator to the cause (Channable's pattern). */
  rowId?: string
  colId?: string
}
interface PreflightResult {
  findings: ActionFinding[]
  /** What the run WOULD do, in the operator's terms. Rendered before any confirm. */
  summary: string
  /** false ⇒ the verb refuses; the reason is in `findings`. */
  runnable: boolean
}

interface ActionContext<T> {
  scope: ActionScope
  familyAxis?: FamilyAxis      // present only when scope === 'family'
  rows: T[]                    // exactly the rows the verb will act on
}

interface ActionDef<T> {
  id: string
  label: string                // plain string: AG's context menu takes `name: string`
  tone?: 'neutral' | 'danger'
  scopes: ActionScope[]
  availability(ctx: ActionContext<T>): Availability
  /** 🔴 Amendment (c): OPTIONAL and DELEGATING — MS.5's publish-preview adapts into this shape
   *  rather than a second preflight mechanism being invented. */
  preflight?(ctx: ActionContext<T>): Promise<PreflightResult>
  run(ctx: ActionContext<T>): Promise<{ ok: boolean; message?: string }>
  invalidates: Invalidation
}
```
Notes: it extends the existing `MenuItemDef` (`id`/`label`/`disabled`/`onSelect`) rather than
replacing it, so `/products/next`'s `rowActions()` — already read by BOTH the ⋯ column and the
context menu — can adopt it without a rewrite. Labels stay plain strings for the same reason that
file documents: a ReactNode label renders as nothing in AG's menu while looking right in the DS one.

### PES.3 — wave-1 verbs WRITTEN: pause/activate + broadcast (rulings #112/#117/#118)
`_studio/sheet/channel/channelActions.ts` — verb DEFINITIONS only; the type and every adapter stay
PES.2's. Follows #118's COLLECT → PREFLIGHT → CONFIRM → RUN: broadcast runs its market picker FIRST
and folds the choice into the impact, so the confirmation describes the actual parameterised
operation rather than the verb in the abstract.

**Both ship PREVIEW-FIRST and refuse the outward-facing half**, per the wave-1 constraint. This is
not caution in the abstract: **all 40 eBay·IT listings in the XAVIA fixture family are ACTIVE with
real ItemIDs**, so "test it on a fixture" does not exist here — a pause on GALE is a pause on a real
eBay offer. The refusal is stated in the IMPACT (`unavailable`), so the operator learns it before
confirming rather than from a failure afterwards.

Three things the contract taught while writing them, worth recording:
1. **`row.listing` does not exist.** Liveness is an ALIAS fact — PES.5 §3.2 puts `externalListingId`
   on `AliasGroup`, and `StudioRow` carries no listing at all. It compiled in my head and not in the
   file; the type was right and I was wrong.
2. **`offerActive` is not on the wire yet** (PES.5 is adding it, #112), so the verb deliberately has
   NO "already paused" check. A verb that guessed current state would offer Pause on something
   already paused and call it a no-op. Absent knowledge, it stays offered and the preflight tells
   the truth about what it found.
3. **Liveness is "the channel has an id", not `listingStatus`** — a DRAFT row still carries a real
   ItemID (measured: all 20 non-ACTIVE rows do). Using status would have mis-read 20 live listings
   as safe.

`invalidates: { kind: 'page' }` — this lane declares the granularity it actually has (#114) rather
than claiming a per-row refetch it does not.
