### PES.2 (nexus-commerce-5f) — F1 verified, F2 BUILT: the four reversible family verbs

**F1 (family bar) — closed, seen on screen.** Renders `Parent · 20 variations · Colore × Taglia`
above the sheet. Two things the screen changed after the diff read fine:

- `"Demoting orphans 20 variations"` parses as a NOUN on first read — "demoting orphans" — which
  is the opposite of a warning. Now `"Demoting would orphan 20 variations"`.
- That warning sat permanently in the bar, warning about a consequence of a button nobody can
  press. It now rides the Demote control's own tooltip, where it is the context an operator needs
  at the moment they consider it.

**F2 — attach / unlink / reparent / promote, declared as `GridAction`s.** Reversible by another
verb in the same set, which is exactly why delete and demote are F3 and behind a server preflight.

#### Substrate added (all lanes inherit it — `design-system/grid/actions/`)

| file | what it owns |
|---|---|
| `runAction.ts` | the SEQUENCE: preflight → validate → confirm → run, nine rules, 13 tests, **7/7 mutations killed** |
| `ActionConfirm.tsx` | the ASKING: consequences itemised, side effects kept separate, typed phrase must match |
| `useActionPress.tsx` | the React glue: busy, outcome wording, where the dialog mounts |

Extracted rather than written per surface because PES.4's `RecordActions` already implements this
sequence for the drawer, and a family bar re-typing it is a second place for "refuse a malformed
impact" to be got wrong — the failure being that a `type-to-confirm` softens to a click on exactly
one surface. **PES.4: `RecordActions` can now drop its inline sequence and call `runAction`; the
behaviour is identical and it is exported from the grid barrel.** Not changed by me — your file.

#### 🔴 Finding 1 — the family verbs do NOT share one permission

`permissions-manifest.ts:383` gates `/api/pim` with `pim.manage`; **line 353 gates `/api/amazon`
with `channels.sync`** — and unlink is the one family verb served from `/api/amazon`
(`POST /api/amazon/pim/unlink-child`; there is no PIM-namespaced unlink, so a plausible-looking
`/api/pim/unlink` 404s at the moment an operator presses it).

So an operator can hold three of these four and not the fourth, in either direction, and nothing
about "unlink this variation" hints at a channel-sync capability. Without asking up front, Unlink
looks identical to its neighbours and fails at press-time with a bare "Access denied" — a missing
permission indistinguishable from a bug. Permission is therefore an INPUT to `familyActions`, and
the refusal names the permission so it can be asked for.

**Binding on any lane wiring a verb that crosses namespaces: check the manifest prefix, not the
verb's subject matter.**

#### 🔴 Finding 2 — a disabled control told the Owner a confident lie, and the screen caught it

The tooltip read *"Unlinking needs the "channels.sync" permission, which this account does not
have"*. Measured: `/api/auth/me` against the deployed API answers `isOwner: true`. The claim was
false about a real person's permissions.

Cause, measured rather than reasoned: **this machine's web app talks to a local API on
`127.0.0.1:8091`** (an earlier port sweep of 3000/3001/4000/8080 missed it, and I had wrongly
concluded the page was hitting prod). The browser holds no session cookie for that origin, so the
app's own `/api/auth/me` returns **401**, `AuthProvider` sits at `status: 'anon'` with an empty
permission set, and every `has()` is false.

A `can()` that is merely false in that state is indistinguishable from a real denial. Fixed by
making the three auth states three different sentences — checking / not signed in / genuinely
lacking it. **This affects every permission-gated control in the app under local dev, not just
mine:** they are all currently disabled or hidden locally for a reason no surface states.

#### What is NOT verified, and why

The four verbs are wired, typed, tested (24 lane tests, **9/9 mutations killed**) and refuse
correctly on screen — but **no round trip has been run**. Two reasons, both honest blockers:

1. The local API session is `anon` (above), so every verb is disabled for the operator.
2. The local API on :8091 is not a safe sandbox — per `reference_local_handler_writes_prod_db` it
   writes the production database, so "run it locally" is not a way around the standing rule that
   autosave writes are REAL.

A round-trip probe script against the deployed API was blocked by the sandbox classifier, correctly
— it wrote to prod. I did not work around it.

**Two claims are therefore still SOURCE-READ, not MEASURED**, and both are stated to operators in
the unlink confirmation. They are read out of the handler, not inferred from the endpoint's name:

- `unlink-child` passes `variantAttributes: undefined` to `updateMany`, which in Prisma means
  "leave this column alone" — so the axis values SURVIVE a detach. This is what makes unlink
  reversible by re-attaching, and it is the opposite of what the handler reads like it intends.
- `unlink-child` has no `isParent` logic at all, so unlinking the last child leaves a **childless
  parent** behind. `/pim/reparent` explicitly demotes an emptied parent; unlink does not.

Both are marked in `familyOps.ts` and will be measured the moment a verb can actually be pressed.

#### Also worth knowing

- `POST /pim/attach-to-parent` is **partially successful by design** — one transaction per child,
  answering `{ attached, errors[] }`. "It worked" is not an answer it can give, so the result never
  claims it; a partial attach reports `ok: false` with the server's own words.
- `/pim/reparent` **demotes the old parent** when it takes its last child. The verb's name does not
  say so, so the confirmation does.
- `StudioRow.listing` is singular and `null` on the master scope, so a per-row count of live
  listings is not knowable there. The unlink confirmation states the unconditional fact ("channel
  listings are not changed") rather than a number it cannot measure.

### PES.3 — #123 permission check DONE, and the answer is counterintuitive
Checked the manifest rather than inferring. **Both wave-1 verbs need `products.edit`, NOT a channels
permission.** `PATCH /api/products/:id/offer-availability` and `PATCH /api/products/bulk` are caught
by the ordered prefix rule `RW(productsView, productsEdit, pfx('/api/products'))` at
`permissions-manifest.ts:412`, while `/api/marketplaces` needs `channels.sync` (line 357). The route
decides, not the subject matter — exactly #123. Guessing "channel verb ⇒ channel permission" would
have named the wrong permission in every refusal, which is worse than naming none.

Exported as `CHANNEL_VERB_PERMISSION` and named verbatim in refusals. The three-state rule is
implemented as `permissionRefusal(state)` with FOUR outcomes — `checking` / `no-session` / `granted`
/ `denied` — and the local-dev case says *"Local dev holds no session for the API origin, so this is
not a permission problem"*, because a developer reading a missing cookie as a permission defect is
the exact confusion #123 exists to prevent. 4 tests pin it, including that `no-session` and `denied`
never render as the same sentence.

`NexusGrid.tsx` and cannot transform in a node-env test. Fixed to the registry's own module path.
Second time tonight for me, after I banked the lesson and passed it to other lanes; it is an easy
one to re-make because the barrel import is what every React file correctly uses.

### PES.2 (nexus-commerce-5f) — F3 BUILT: delete variation + demote parent, behind a real preflight

Both Owner-approved. Neither is reversible by anything in the F2 set, which is why only these two
carry a server preflight rather than a warning written in advance.

#### 🔴 Finding 3 — a THIRD permission, and a path whose own docstring is wrong

| verb | path the router actually serves | permission |
|---|---|---|
| delete variation | `DELETE /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children/:childId` | `products.edit` |
| demote parent | `POST /api/pim/demote-parent` | `pim.manage` |
| the preflight read | `GET /api/products/:id/all-listings` | `products.view` |

`catalog.routes.ts` documents the delete as `DELETE /api/products/:parentId/children/:childId`, and
`index.ts` registers `catalogRoutes` at prefix `/api/catalog`. **The documented path 404s.** That is
now the third path in this lane whose handler comment disagrees with its router, so every path in
`familyOps.ts` was read from `register(..., { prefix })` rather than from the comment above the
handler. Recommend other lanes do the same.

So the family verbs span **three** permissions, not one — `pim.manage`, `channels.sync`,
`products.edit` — plus `products.view` for the preflight to be able to look at all.

#### 🔴 Finding 4 — the obvious definition of "live" would have called 20 live listings safe

`DELETE .../children/:childId` is a HARD delete; ChannelListings cascade by FK with no server-side
guard. So the confirmation is the only thing between an operator and a live marketplace listing,
and it is only as good as its idea of "live".

The obvious idea is `listingStatus === 'ACTIVE'`. **PES.3 already measured that it is wrong** — a
family where all 20 non-ACTIVE eBay rows still carried a real ItemID. Keyed on status, this delete
would have described 20 live listings as safe to destroy and asked for one click.

`listingRisk.ts` therefore keys on **`externalListingId`** (Amazon ASIN / eBay ItemID) and reports
status only as context. An unpublished row holding an ItemID is still an eBay listing a delete
takes down.

This is also why the preflight reads `/products/:id/all-listings` and **not** the more obvious
`/products/:id/listings` — the latter selects a whitelist that omits `externalListingId`, so a
confirm built on it could only ask about the field that lies.

#### How the two verbs ask

- **Delete** — severity from fact: nothing listed → plain confirm; a live id → `type-to-confirm`
  with **the real SKU** as the phrase (never "DELETE", which trains an operator to type five
  letters without reading). ONE ROW AT A TIME, deliberately: a typed phrase must name exactly what
  is destroyed, and one SKU authorising six deletions is a weaker gate than the one approved.
- **Demote** — childless → plain confirm (promote reverses it). With children → `type-to-confirm`
  on the parent SKU, naming every child, and saying the thing the operator actually wants to know:
  the variations are **not** deleted, they survive as standalone products. `force` travels in the
  approved payload and is never re-derived at run time.
- A preflight that could not LOOK sets `unavailable`; `runAction` refuses the verb rather than
  falling back to a gentler question. **Verified on screen**, not just in tests.

#### Rules collapsed rather than duplicated

`familyVerbAvailability` used to answer for all four F2 verbs. Once `familyActions` declared them,
each had TWO sources for "may this run, and why not" — the exact drift the registry exists to
prevent. It is now trimmed to `add-variation` alone (F4, no registry definition yet), with a test
that **fails if a registry verb's rules are ever added back**.

#### The confirmation is now inspectable by every lane

Added GDS lab scenario **`#action-confirm`** (`/design/grid-lab?tab=gds`) rendering the three shapes
that actually occur: plain confirm, typed confirm with live ids, and a malformed impact. A
confirmation nobody can look at is a confirmation nobody has checked.

**Looking at it found three defects that all the tests passed:**
1. `consequences` and `findings` printed the SAME listings twice, under two headings.
2. An **enabled** confirm button still read "Type the name to confirm" — telling the operator to do
   what they had just done.
3. The itemised lists had no bullet markers (the app reset strips them), so five live listings read
   as one paragraph nobody counts.

All three fixed and re-verified on screen. The refusal path was verified too: *"Delete variation was
refused: level is type-to-confirm but no confirmPhrase was given — refuse rather than downgrade to a
click"*, with no dialog opened.

**Green:** 1863 tests, repo `tsc` 0, **13/13 F3 mutations killed**, grid:conformance ✓ (12 probes),
AG module gate ✓, ds-conformance ✓, css-shadow-ratchet ✓, fork-drift ✓, ag-import-boundary ✓.
Nothing committed. `check-ds-dts-fresh` still red from other lanes; none of the stale declarations
are mine.

**Unchanged from my last filing:** no family verb has been round-tripped, because the local session
is `anon` against :8091 and that API writes the production database. F3's verbs are destructive, so

### PES.3 — Errors & Sync console: CORE BUILT (#127 approved) + two cross-lane asks
`_studio/channel-ops/syncQueue.ts` — the grouping core, pure and tested (12 tests). Built first
because grouping IS the feature: 2,553 rows sorted by date is a list; grouped by cause it is a
handful of problems, and the operator's next action differs completely between "one incident that
retried itself 2,000 times" and "2,000 independent failures". The tests guard BOTH directions —
collapsing the same failure carrying different ids into one cause, AND refusing to collapse two
genuinely different failures, because a tidy console hiding a real second problem is the worse bug.

`groupByCause` returns row count AND distinct-SKU count deliberately: 2,000 rows over 3 SKUs is one
product retrying into the ground; 2,000 rows over 2,000 SKUs is a channel-wide outage. Row count
alone cannot tell those apart and they need opposite responses.

**### From PES.3 → PES.5 — the console needs one read**
No product-scoped sync-queue read exists (the `outboundSyncQueue.findMany` calls live in
advertising/control-tower routes, none per product × coordinate). Requesting:
`GET /api/products/:id/sync-queue?channel=&market=&filter=dead|retrying|stuck` returning rows shaped

### PES.2 → ruling #127: the `?rec=` hang is the KEY, not the value — and not the drawer

Handed to me as "a cold load of `?rec=<CHILD id>` leaves the sheet unresolved". Five reproductions
on a **warm** dev server:

| URL | result |
|---|---|
| no `?rec=` | sheet renders 21 rows, family bar fine |
| `?rec=<CHILD id>` | sheet 0 rows + "Loading the family…" + "Opening the record…" |
| `?rec=<PARENT id>` | **identical hang** |
| `?rec=THIS-ID-DOES-NOT-EXIST` | **identical hang** |
| `?rec=<CHILD id>&tab=images` | Images tab stuck at "Loading images…" |

Three corrections to the report as filed:

1. **The child/parent distinction is not real.** The ~9s parent render was the same hang losing a
   race. Nothing is special about child records; that search is a dead end.
2. **It is not record resolution.** A `rec` value matching no product anywhere hangs identically,
   so nothing is ever resolved — the hang precedes any id mattering.
3. **It is neither the drawer nor this lane.** The Images tab renders no sheet, no family bar and no
   drawer, and `?rec=` stalls it too. That places it in the studio FRAME's handling of the `rec`
   URL key (`_studio/contracts.tsx`), not in PES.4's drawer and not in PES.2's sheet.

PES.4's instinct that it is client-side is right: on a warm load `studio/sheet` returns **200
twice**, `readiness` 200 twice, `pim/family` 200 twice, the child's `images` 200 — and the UI still
shows 0 rows. Console clean.

#### A wrong turn of mine, recorded so nobody builds on it

I first read a COLD-load network log — every studio read repeating ~7× in lockstep with
`auth/csrf`, `sidebar/counts`, `connections`, ~10 `orders/events` SSE streams, and a wall of pending
requests — and concluded connection-pool exhaustion on `127.0.0.1:8091` (the HTTP/1.1 six-connection
cap). **Wrong as the cause.** Idle measurement shows zero requests, so it is a cold-load storm that
settles rather than a live loop; and the warm load hangs with everything returning 200. Two
observations agreeing is not the same as being right when both sample the same transient.

The storm is real and separate, and worth someone's attention: it fires the whole app's reads ~7×
per cold load, and early on `/api/products?page=1&limit=100…` and `/api/products/:id/readiness`
return **503** — the local API shedding load under it.

Also observed, not diagnosed: one `studio/sheet` request went to `http://localhost:8091` while every
other request went to `http://127.0.0.1:8091`. Different origins → different connection pools and
different cookie jars. Every sheet caller I can find uses `getBackendUrl()`, so I cannot explain it
and did not guess.

#### Item 2 — repo tsc

Clear: `apps/web` 0, `apps/api` 0, 0 in `familyActions.vitest.test.ts`. PES.3 caught a real
transient — they ran during the window where I had added `actions` to `FamilyBarProps` before
`MasterSheet` passed it, and used `useAuth` before importing it. Both are in the browser console log
timestamped 19:26–19:27 and both were fixed within minutes.

#### One thing fixed in my own code while here

`famActions`' `useMemo` depended on `has`, which `AuthProvider` rebuilds every render — so the memo
never cached and both memo'd bars re-rendered for nothing. It now depends on the three permission
ANSWERS, which are stable, rather than on the function, which is not.

#### On PES.4's z-order fix

Right call. Worth folding into the ruling that `ActionConfirm` inherits the DS `Modal`'s layer
(`--nds-z-overlay`, 1400) while a token literally named `--nds-z-modal` sits at **1410** — so any
surface reaching for the "modal" token covers the confirmation. The naming is the trap, not their
dock. I own the confirm, not `Modal`.

### ✅ PES.3 — #129 wiring DONE, and the field-drift scan found TWO more than the three named
`StudioDock` is mounted on the channel scope with `rowActions={channelActions(...)}`, so PES.4's
adapter has a surface AND verbs for the first time. `onWrite` deliberately returns
`{state: 'refused'}` — this scope's writes go through the sheet's cascade + `SheetWriter`, and a
second write path in the drawer would be two ways to change one cell.

**The scan was worth more than the three fields.** Measured the live payload against the local type
rather than reading either. Beyond `basePrice` / `listing` / `completeness`:

4. 🔴 **`AliasReadiness.percent` is `number | null`; mine said `number`.** The server sends null when
   a coordinate declares NO required fields — "nothing to be ready against" — and its own comment
   says 0 (alarming) and 100 (falsely reassuring) are both inventions. My `clampPct` turned null
   into **0**, so the band drew an empty red bar reading "0% ready" on a listing with nothing to
   measure. Fixed: null survives, the bar renders as an empty track, the figure reads `—`.
   ⚠ **A test of mine was asserting the 0.** It was protecting the bug, not the behaviour — the same
   shape as PES.2's paste test asserting the blanking. Rewritten to assert null, with a note saying
   why the old assertion existed.
5. 🔴 **`ChannelReadiness.issues` was optional; the server always sends it.** This is what actually
   blocked the dock — `SheetRow` requires it, so `ChannelSheetRow` did not satisfy the constraint.
   An optional mirror of a required field is not a harmless loosening: every consumer writes `?? []`
   and a genuinely absent array then reads as "no issues".

Both were invisible to the tests because the tests were written against the same wrong mirror. 87
tests green in the lane, 478+ across the studio, repo tsc clean.

### PES.1 — ruling #132: the `?rec=` "hang" is NOT a hang, and not a frame bug

**Measured, one page load, `?rec=DOES-NOT-EXIST` on the parent:**

| t | sheet rows | completed API calls |
|---|---|---|
| 5s | 0 | 8 |
| **15s** | **21** | 14 |
| 30s | 21 | 15 |

**It renders. It is SLOW, not stalled** — and 15s is long enough that five reproductions all look like a hang. PES.2's five cases are real and their reasoning was sound; the conclusion is what the clock
disproves.

**Cause, with a negative control:**
- WITHOUT `?rec=` → dock has **0** children, sheet renders 21 rows, an origin probe returns **ok in
  2464ms**, 5 completed calls.
- WITH `?rec=` (any value) → PES.4's drawer mounts (**520px**, dock has 1 child), and the same probe
  **HUNGs >6s** on `127.0.0.1:8091` while `localhost:8091` answers in 1600ms.

So the key's PRESENCE mounts the drawer; the drawer adds ~5 fetches; **StrictMode doubles every
fetch** (`studio/sheet` ×2, `pim/family` ×2, `saved-views` ×2, `readiness` ×2 — all visible in the
completed list); ~15 requests queue against a **6-connection** pool on a slow local API. ≈15s to
drain. The value never matters because any value mounts the drawer — which is exactly the symmetry
PES.2 found and correctly could not explain from record resolution.

🔴 **Why the pool hypothesis was retracted, and why the retraction was wrong.** "Idle at zero
requests" is *precisely* what starvation looks like: a **pending** request never appears in
`performance.getEntriesByType('resource')`, and no new ones start because the pool is full. I made
the same misreading earlier tonight — it is in
`reference_local_dev_hits_prod_api` for exactly this reason. The reliable test is the two-host probe
(`127.0.0.1` vs `localhost` are different origins, so different pools).

**Nothing to fix in `_studio/contracts.tsx`.** The `rec` handling is correct: read the key, publish
it, and let PES.4's drawer mount. The cost is the drawer's request count against a dev-only pool
limit, on a local API where each call takes ~1–2s.

### Adjacent item 2 — the `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` split: DISPROVED, not guessed
**Every one of 18 app API requests on a studio load goes to `http://127.0.0.1:8091`. Zero go to
`localhost`.** `getBackendUrl()` is the only base builder and returns one baked value, so the app
*cannot* split origins. The single `localhost` `studio/sheet` was therefore not the app's — almost
certainly a devtools console probe, which appears in the Network tab indistinguishable from an app
request. I ran several such probes myself tonight for exactly this diagnosis.

### DS z-order (PES.4's finding) — the naming is inverted against its users
- `--nds-z-modal: 1410` has **exactly one consumer, `.nds-drawer`** (web AND factory).
- Modals have **no z of their own**: `.nds-modal` sits inside `.nds-backdrop`, which is
  `--nds-z-overlay: 1400`.
- `--nds-z-drawer` is **an unused name**.

So a token called *modal* is the DRAWER's layer, sitting above the layer modals actually occupy —
which is how a confirmation ended up behind a drawer. **Recommended: rename `--nds-z-modal` →
`--nds-z-drawer`** (accurate, name is free, values unchanged ⇒ **zero visual change**), which removes
the trap at its source. ⚠ Separately and NOT the same question: whether a confirmation should
out-rank a drawer at all is a real stacking decision affecting every modal+drawer pair app-wide —
that one wants the Owner, not a rename. `tokens.css` is generated from `tokens/css-vars.ts`, so the
rename is a source edit + regenerate + factory mirror. **Not done — proposed.**

### PES.1 — `--nds-z-modal` → `--nds-z-drawer` DONE (ruling #136)

Renamed at source in BOTH apps (`tokens/css-vars.ts`), regenerated `tokens.css` +
`tokens-global.css`, and moved the single consumer in each `components.css` together — web and
factory in one step, so the two copies never disagreed even momentarily.

**Zero visual change, verified on screen rather than asserted:** a real `.nds-drawer` element still
computes to **1410**, `--nds-z-overlay` is still **1400**, and `--nds-z-modal` no longer resolves.
Sheet renders 21 rows, drawer docks, frame intact.

Also corrected a now-stale explanatory comment in `components.css` that told the reader "NOT
`--nds-z-modal`" — a token that no longer exists. It now names the new one and notes that the
comment IS the bug the old name caused.

⚠ **Not changed, queued for the Owner:** whether a confirmation should out-rank a drawer at all.
That is a stacking decision across every modal+drawer pair app-wide, and a different question from
what the layer is called.

### PES.2 — F4 BUILT (add variation), #133 fixed, and #136 accepted against my own retraction

#### F4 — add variation, COLLECT → PREFLIGHT → CONFIRM → RUN

`POST /api/catalog/products/:parentId/children`, `products.edit` — the same `/api/catalog` prefix
trap as delete. The form is the COLLECT step, `addVariation.ts` is the pure rule set, the verb is a
registry entry like the other five. **The last hardcoded placeholder is gone from the family bar**;
all six verbs now arrive through `actionsFor` in declaration order.

Four things read out of the handler:

- 🔴 **Its comment says it lower-cases axis keys "for consistency with how the read path reads
  them". It does not** — it only trims (`String(k).trim()`). So the dialog builds one field per
  `family.self.variationAxes` entry rather than offering free text: a free-text box would let one
  variation be `Colore` and the next `colore`, silently splitting the family into two axes that look
  identical on screen. Another comment claiming a mechanism the code has not got.
- 🔴 **A new variation is created `status: "ACTIVE"` carrying the parent's `syncChannels`** — live
  from the moment it exists, not a draft. Nothing in the verb's name says so, so the confirmation
  does.
- The server validates exactly two things: `sku`/`name` present, and SKU globally unique (409
  `DUPLICATE_SKU`). The client now names the **sibling** a duplicate clashes with, instead of
  relaying a bare "already exists" about a SKU the operator can see on screen.
- A missing axis value **warns and does not block**. A family with an unset axis is a state this
  catalogue already contains; blocking would invent a rule the server has not got.

`copyFromProductId` is offered as "start from an existing variation" — it clones a sibling's channel
listings with the axis-specific SP-API fields stripped.

**7/7 mutations killed**, after one genuine survivor: the errors-before-warnings test used a draft
whose natural push order was already sorted, so it passed with the sort removed. A test describing
the implementation instead of protecting the operator — the second time that exact shape has bitten
this lane (the paste test that asserted the empty strings was the first).

#### Ruling #133 — the disabled confirm button, fixed

PES.4's finding, and better than the three I found looking at the same dialog. The disabled danger
button rendered white on `rgb(163,33,26)` at `opacity: 0.5` — **2.60:1, vs 7.53:1 enabled** — while
carrying the words "Type the name to confirm". WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive controls and that is
normally right; it is void when the disabled control holds the only instruction on screen. The
affordance was inverted: 2.6:1 exactly while it was needed, 7.5:1 once it was not.

Fixed — the button says "Confirm" in both states, and the instruction beside the input is **no
longer `nds-cell-muted`** either, because dimming the one remaining instruction is the same mistake
one step less obvious. Generalised into DS-GAPS beside its two siblings (`Input ::placeholder` at
2.04:1, `Listbox .ph` at 3.10:1): **an instruction may never live only on a disabled control**, with
a suggested lint — a `disabled` control whose label contains an imperative.

#### Ruling #136 — my retraction was wrong, and why

I withdrew the pool-exhaustion hypothesis on the strength of "idle measures zero requests". That is
**exactly what starvation looks like**: a pending request emits no resource entry and starts no
successors, so a starved page and an idle page produce byte-identical evidence. Zero requests cannot
discriminate between them in either direction — I read the absence of data as data.

The reliable test is the **two-host probe** (`127.0.0.1` and `localhost` are different origins and
therefore different pools; measured 127.0.0.1 hung >6s while localhost answered in 1600ms), because
it forces a positive signal instead of asking silence to testify. And it is not a hang at all: ~15s,
from ~15 requests draining a 6-connection pool at 1–2s each, with StrictMode doubling every one.

Also corrected: the odd `studio/sheet` to `localhost:8091` was a **devtools console probe**, not app
traffic — `getBackendUrl()` bakes one value so the app cannot split origins. I had made console
fetches on that tab earlier and should have accounted for my own probes before reporting it.

The key-not-value isolation and the five reproductions stand; the clock is what none of us measured.

**Green:** 1894 tests, `tsc` 0 both apps, grid:conformance ✓ (12 probes), eight guards ✓
(ds-conformance, css-shadow-ratchet, fork-drift, grid-modules, ag-import-boundary, ds-gaps-append,
silent-disabled, button-vocabulary). Nothing committed.

**Still not round-tripped.** Local session is `anon` against :8091, so `add-variation` is disabled
with an honest permission reason and its form is unreachable in this environment — correct
behaviour, and it leaves F4's dialog the one piece of this lane never seen on screen.

### PES.3 — Errors & Sync console SHIPPED, #135 closed (2026-09-01, late)

*Numbering: `#N` is hub-issued; this lane's own findings are prefixed `PES.3-N` so the two
namespaces cannot collide (hub housekeeping note, 2026-09-01). References to `#110`, `#129`, `#130`,
`#131`, `#135` below are hub rulings.*

**On screen, real GALE eBay·IT data, shim-free** (`localhost:3011` → local API on 8092):
`36 queued writes across 2 causes · 24 products`, filters reading **Dead (36) · Retrying (0) ·
Stuck (0) · All (40)**, two expandable cause groups, verbatim messages per row, the coverage note
and the dormant-sources footer. **`Stuck (0)` renders empty** — "Nothing stuck for this product on
eBay." — with the coverage sentence directly beneath it, which is #130 and #131 satisfied in the one
state that could have been faked.

#### PES.3-1 — `errorCode` is the OUTCOME, not the cause; grouping by it would have been a lie

My own rule ("prefer the channel's error CODE, it is stable vocabulary") was wrong, and measurement
killed it before it shipped. Across every coded row in `OutboundSyncQueue`:

```
MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED   2,490 rows — 308 distinct messages
WRITE_GATE_DENIED      2,198 rows — 300 distinct messages   ← together 97% of all coded rows
EBAY_VALIDATION           30 rows —  29 distinct messages
```

Grouping by code renders the console as **two buckets named after the queue giving up**. Underneath
`MAX_RETRIES_EXCEEDED` alone sit four unrelated problems: an eBay `get offers` 404 (1,708), our own
circuit breaker (377), and **`NEXUS_ENABLE_AMAZON_PUBLISH=false` (356) + `NEXUS_ENABLE_EBAY_PUBLISH
=false` (12) — a flag deliberately switched off, not a failure at all**. A console reporting 2,490
broken writes when 368 are a switch someone turned on purpose is worse than no console. Same under
`WRITE_GATE_DENIED`: `entity_bounds` and `campaign_allowlist` are different intended refusals.

Fix: `OUTCOME_CODES` fall THROUGH to the normalised message; the code is still rendered beside the
group, never as its name. Channel rejection codes (`EBAY_VALIDATION`, `EBAY_LISTING_ENDED`) are
causes and are used as-is.

**Generalisable:** a status field that names your own lifecycle is not a diagnosis. Check the ratio
of distinct messages per code before grouping by the code — 308:1 is the number that says "this is
a bucket, not a cause".

#### PES.3-2 — `\b\d+\b` skipped every number glued to a unit, and only real data showed it

The normaliser's digit rule was written `\b\d+\b`. `Retry in 427s.` keeps its 427 — `7`→`s` is not a
word boundary — so the real GALE queue grouped into **33 causes for 36 rows, one per retry timer**:
precisely the "thousands of separate failures" illusion, manufactured by the code written to prevent
it. Nine unit tests passed throughout; the fixtures all had numbers followed by spaces. Dropping the
trailing `\b`: **33 → 2**. Table-wide, 4,817 rows with messages → **21 causes**.

Second miss in the same function: cuids contain letters past `f`, so `[0-9a-f]{8,}` never matched
one — four `campaign_allowlist` groups differing only by a campaign id. A `[a-z0-9]{20,}` rule
collapses them to one (1,143 rows). Both are regression-tested against strings copied from the DB.

**Generalisable:** a normaliser can only be validated against the corpus it will normalise. Test
fixtures are written by the same person who wrote the regex and share its blind spots.

#### PES.3-3 — #135 closed: the drawer opens on double-click, and the verb hides where it is circular

`onRowDoubleClicked` → `record.open(row.rowId)`, mirroring `MasterSheet.tsx:852` exactly. Verified on
screen: double-clicking GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-3XL opened PES.4's drawer on
`?rec=primary:cmokmy0jf0003pm0ppnu1b2yy` with Record/History/Compare/Listings, provenance chips and
the "Writes to the master record" cascade sentence. The gesture does **not** also enter cell edit.

Also declared `open-record` in `channelActions` for discoverability — and then measured where verbs
actually render. **The registry has exactly ONE adapter today: `RecordActions`, inside the drawer**
(`RecordDrawer.tsx:478`). AG's row context menu is still stock Cut/Copy/Export; no ⋯ column exists.
So "one definition, four surfaces" is currently one surface, and an "Open record" verb would render
only in the place where it does nothing. It now takes `openRecordId` and returns `HIDDEN` on the
record already open — hidden, not disabled, because a verb offered on the thing it would open is
meaningless rather than unavailable. It appears the moment a row-menu or ⋯ adapter lands.

**→ PES.4 / PES.2:** the row-menu and ⋯-column adapters are the missing half of #110. A ⋯ column is
grid chrome and belongs to the engine, not to my sheet, so I have not hand-rolled one.

#### PES.3-4 — a hardcoded `permission: 'no-session'` would have shipped every gated verb dead

`ChannelSheet` passed `permission: 'no-session'` as a literal, from the measured local-dev fact. It
compiles, it reads as honest, and on prod — where there **is** a session — every gated verb would
have been permanently disabled behind a message saying the user isn't signed in. Now derived from
`useAuth()`, whose `'loading' | 'authed' | 'anon'` maps one-to-one onto the four states I had
already declared: `checking` / `no-session` / `granted` | `denied` by `has('products.edit')`.

**Generalisable:** a measured constant is still a constant. The measurement justifies the *shape* of
the answer, never the answer itself — cf. `reference_fleet_stale_constant_class`.

#### PES.3-5 — Next blocks its own dev resources from `127.0.0.1`, and the page renders without hydrating

Two hours of the console appearing "stuck on loading" were not my effect. Serving the dev server
over `http://127.0.0.1:3011` produces:

```
⚠ Blocked cross-origin request to Next.js dev resource /_next/webpack-hmr from "127.0.0.1".
```

…and the page **server-renders perfectly while never hydrating**: correct markup, correct initial
state, zero console errors, no effects, no interactivity. Every symptom points at your own component
(a stuck `loading` flag, a `cancelled` closure, a fetch that never settles) and none of them is real.
The tell is that the *initial* render state is the one on screen and `read_console_messages` finds
**no** logs from an effect you just instrumented — not an error, an absence.

`http://localhost:3011` is the same server and hydrates fine. Note this is the second time in this
programme that `127.0.0.1` vs `localhost` — different origins, different sockets, different rules —
has cost a session hours (cf. #136's two-host probe). **Use `localhost` for the dev web server.**

Related, for anyone pointing a second dev server at a local API: `ALLOWED_WEB_ORIGINS` contains only
`http://localhost:3000`, so any other port needs `NEXUS_WEB_ORIGINS` on the API. I ran a second API
on 8092 with it set rather than restarting 8091, which other lanes may be using.

#### Open, not mine to close

- **The queue row still carries no SKU.** With 21 products in one cause group and `Open sheet` not
  yet row-precise, an operator cannot tell which product a failed write belongs to. Re-asking PES.5.
- **Jump-to-row is scope-only** (`setTab('sheet')`), labelled "Open sheet" for what it does. Precise
  jump needs a productId → rowId resolution (a sheet row id is `alias:productId`, and the queue row
  carries no alias); guessing `primary:` is right today and silently wrong when ② exists.
- **All 36 dead rows on this coordinate share one `externalListingId`** (257584954808) across 21
  products — consistent with one multi-variation eBay listing, but it makes the column useless for
  triage. Flagging as a data observation, not acting on it.

**Green:** 517 studio tests, `tsc` clean, guards ✓ (p3-token-sweep, ds-conformance, link-targets,
ag-grid-import-boundary, grid-chrome, grid-option-identity, grid-modules, grid-kit-ratchet).
Nothing committed.

#### PES.3-6 — the gate banner: the most useful sentence this pane can say, and it had to be measured first

An operator looking at 36 dead writes reaches for Retry. While the coordinate's publish mode is
`gated`, that retry is refused by **the same helper that failed them**: `outbound-sync.service.ts`
line 1209 calls `getEbayPublishMode()` — the identical function the sheet's preflight reports — and
on `'gated'` fails the write with the message that appears verbatim on 368 queue rows. One helper,
both paths, one line apart.

That check is the whole point. Written from the flag's *name* it would have been a plausible guess
delivered in the same voice as a fact; written from the two call sites it is a claim I can defend.
The console now renders, above the groups and whether or not there are rows:

> eBay publishing is switched off on the server (mode: gated). Re-running these writes would be
> refused by the same gate that failed them — the queue already holds 368 rows that are exactly
> that. **The flag, not the retry, is what has to change.**

Mode comes from `GET /api/listings/publish-readiness` (a GET, no ids, all three channels), never
from env in the browser. `modeForChannel()` returns **null** for a channel that response does not
describe (WooCommerce, Etsy) — `'live'` would be the most dangerous possible default. `dry-run` and
`sandbox` get their own sentences: a cleared queue under dry-run would not mean the channel was
updated. If the readiness read fails the console still works and simply says nothing about the gate.

This is also why I did **not** ship a Retry verb yet. A permanently-disabled button whose only
content is this sentence would put the explanation on a disabled control
(`reference_disabled_control_cannot_explain`); the banner carries it instead, and Retry arrives when
there is a send path worth pressing.

#### PES.3-7 — `--nds-warning-bg` does not exist, and CSS said nothing

The banner shipped as a bare outline on a transparent ground for one screenshot. `background:
var(--nds-warning-bg)` — no such token — resolves to `rgba(0,0,0,0)` with no error, no warning, and
no guard hit. The DS's warning surface is `--nds-warning-soft` (`primitives.css:287` pairs it with
`--nds-warning-text` on `.nds-tag.warning`). Fixed and **measured on the element's own computed
background rather than an assumed page colour**: `#fff6e8` under `#6d3f10` = **8.27:1**.

The tell was reading the computed style, not the screenshot — at a glance a faint outline looks like
a deliberately quiet banner. Sibling of `reference_undefined_css_class_is_silent`, one level down:
an undefined *token* is as silent as an undefined class, and `var()` has no strict mode.

#### PES.3-8 — components, not a composed row id (answering PES.5 via hub #142)

**Keep the components.** PES.5's instinct is right and I'd rather they not take the coupling: the
row-id format is `${aliasKey ?? 'primary'}:${productId}`, it lives in this lane's `studioRowId()`,
and it has already changed once this programme. If the server composed it, a future change here
would silently emit ids that resolve to nothing — and the symptom is a jump that does nothing, which
reads as a UI bug forever rather than as a contract drift anyone would look for. Components fail
loudly at the type level; a stale composed string fails silently at runtime.

Their three-state answer is exactly right, particularly `aliasKey null` + `aliasResolved false` as
its own state rather than a defaulted "primary" — that distinction is what makes precise jumping
safe for the 396 and honestly scope-only for the 45.

**On the derived gated-refusal reason: yes, and it matters more than it sounds.** Those 368 rows
sit in `dead` beside genuine rejections today, and "refused because publishing is switched off"
needs to read differently from "eBay rejected this" — one is a switch, the other is a problem. When
it lands I'll group them separately and suppress the gate banner's duplicate accounting.

### PES.2 — ruling #141: the row-menu and ⋯-column adapters, and a rule the screen disproved

**Both adapters shipped** in `design-system/grid/actions/menuAdapters.tsx`, exported from the barrel,
and **wired live onto the master sheet's grid** — right-click a row and the family verbs are there,
above AG's own items, separated by a rule. Verified on screen.

- `actionMenuItems(opts)` → the `⋯` column's items, for `actionsColumn({ items })`
- `actionContextMenu(opts)` → AG's `getContextMenuItems`

Both are thin on purpose: they map, `actionsFor` filters, `runAction` runs. `/products/next`'s
`rowActions()` is the precedent; this generalises it with the list coming from the registry.

#### 🔴 The finding: my scope rule was consistent, tested, mutation-proof, and wrong

Both adapters first filtered on `ROW` alone. That is defensible on paper — and it rendered **an
empty menu** on the only grid in the programme, because every family verb is `selection` (unlink,
reparent, delete) or `context` (attach, promote, demote, add variation). **Not one is `row`.**

It passed 11 tests. It survived nothing — 9/9 mutations killed, including one that specifically
asserted SELECTION verbs must NOT reach a row menu. The tests, the mutations and the type system all
agreed with each other and all encoded the same wrong assumption. **The screen was the only thing
that disagreed**, and only because I right-clicked a row and saw stock Cut/Copy/Export.

The rule that is actually right: **a right-clicked row is a selection of one.** "Unlink this
variation" is the same verb whether reached from the bulk bar with one row ticked or from the row's
own menu; a registry that made those different would be two answers to one question. `context` stays
excluded — the container is not a row, and that half of the original rule was correct.

**This is the third time this session that a green, mutation-tested unit was wrong in a way only
looking could reveal** (after the paste test that asserted the empty strings, and the sort test whose
input was already sorted). Mutation testing proves a test protects the behaviour you wrote down. It
cannot tell you that you wrote down the wrong behaviour.

#### A second on-screen fix: a menu that stopped being a menu

With reasons appended to the labels, the right-click menu measured **~900px wide** — three permission
sentences inline turned a context menu into a paragraph laid over the grid. AG's `MenuItemDef` has a
`tooltip?: string` slot (menuItem.d.ts:23), so the reason moved there and the menu is a normal ~260px.
The DS `MenuItemDef` has no tooltip slot, so the ⋯ menu keeps the reason appended — the two surfaces
differ in WHERE the reason renders and in nothing else, which a test now pins.

#### Also, from #141's warning about baked constants

Audited: nothing in this lane bakes a measured auth state. `authStatus` traces to `useAuth().status`
and `can` to `has`. But it **was** optional with an `'authed'` default, which is the same trap one
step quieter — a caller who simply forgot would get *"which this account does not have"*, a confident
claim about a real person's permissions, defaulted rather than measured. It is now **required**: it
cannot be forgotten, and there is no safe value to guess.

One more thing caught before it shipped: `rowPress.confirmElement` was initially unmounted. A verb
run from the context menu would have awaited an `ask()` whose dialog never rendered — the promise
never settles, the menu just closes, and nothing happens with no error anywhere. **Every surface that
runs a verb must mount its own confirm.** Worth stating in the ruling, because it fails silently.

**Green:** 1931 tests (149 files), `tsc` 0 both apps, grid:conformance ✓, seven guards ✓, adapters
9/9 mutations killed. Nothing committed.

#### Scope note on #141 — three surfaces on this sheet, not four

Checked after the ruling, because "one definition, four surfaces" should not be truer of the claim
than of the screen:

- **Mounted on the master sheet:** the family bar (context verbs), the selection bar (selection
  verbs), and now AG's right-click menu. `SHEET_GRID_OPTIONS` defines no `getContextMenuItems`, so
  the sheet's own grid options were not overridden by adding it — checked, not assumed.
- **Built, tested and exported but mounted on NO grid:** `actionMenuItems` — the `⋯`-column adapter.

That is deliberate rather than unfinished. A `⋯` column costs a permanently pinned ~60px in a sheet
whose whole problem is 102 columns competing for width, and it would buy nothing here: the same
verbs already reach the operator through the selection bar (tick a row and they are on screen,
labelled, with reasons) and through right-click. `/products/next` mounts one because it is a browse
grid where the row is the unit of work; on an edit sheet the CELL is, and a column of menus beside
every row is chrome charging rent.

The adapter exists for the lanes whose grids are row-shaped — it is `actionsColumn({ items:
actionMenuItems({ actions, onSelect }) })`, and it is under test so the first lane to mount it is not
the one debugging it.

#### PES.3-9 — the adapters adopted: three surfaces, one definition, verified on screen

`ChannelSheet` now mounts PES.2's `actionMenuItems` (⋯ column) and `actionContextMenu` (right-click)
alongside the drawer's `RecordActions`, all reading one `channelActions(...)` list, hoisted out of
the JSX so it is not a fresh identity re-running the column model each render.

Verified on the real GALE eBay·IT sheet: right-click offers **Open record · Pause offer on eBay·IT ·
Activate offer on eBay·IT · Broadcast to other markets…** above AG's Cut/Copy/Export; the ⋯ column
shows the same four; and clicking Open record from the ⋯ menu ran `press → runAction → run` and
opened the drawer on `?rec=primary:cmokmy0kl0006pm0p9auaundx`, the row whose ⋯ was clicked. The band
row correctly has **no ⋯** — `isRecord` excludes it, so a group header offers no verbs at all.

**#145's warning does not apply to `open-record`, and the code says so.** `menuAdapters.tsx:58`
unions **both** scopes — `[...actionsFor(actions, ROW, [row]), ...actionsFor(actions, SELECTION,
[row])]` — and their own test asserts `['open', 'delete', 'promote', 'unlink']` where the first
three are ROW-scoped. A ROW verb renders. `ROW` is also the semantically correct scope here: "open
record" on twelve selected rows is not a thing. Kept as declared, verified rather than assumed.

**Inherited, not rediscovered (#145 point 1):** the sheet mounts its own `confirmElement`. Both
`pause-offer` and `broadcast-to-listings` carry preflights, so without it a verb would await an
`ask()` whose dialog never renders — promise never settles, menu closes, nothing happens, no error
anywhere.

#### PES.3-10 — `actionsColumn` defaults to UNPINNED, which on a 100-column sheet means absent

The ⋯ column shipped invisible for one screenshot. `actionsColumn` defaults `pinned = false`
(`presets.ts:157`), and this scope renders ~100 channel field columns, so the column existed and sat
permanently past the right edge of a horizontally scrolling grid. Measured before believing it: the
rendered `col-id` set contained no `actions` and `.ag-pinned-right-cols-container` was empty — a
column that is present in the model and unreachable in the viewport.

**Generalisable:** a default that is fine on a 12-column grid is a bug on a 100-column one. Check a
preset's defaults against the width of the grid you are putting it in, not against the preset's
example.

#### PES.3-11 — I nearly reported a working tooltip as missing

First probe: `.ag-menu-option` carries no `title` attribute, so I wrote down that the three disabled
verbs give the operator no reason — `reference_disabled_control_cannot_explain`, apparently live.

Wrong. AG builds the tooltip **lazily into its own `.ag-tooltip` element on hover**, not as a `title`
attribute. Dispatching a real hover and waiting 2.5s produced it in full: *"Not signed in to the API
— this needs products.edit. Local dev holds no session for the API origin, so this is not a
permission problem."* The reason is there and it is the three-state one.

The first reading was a probe measuring the wrong thing and finding nothing — which is exactly what
a real absence looks like (`reference_browser_probe_lies`, `reference_quiet_measurement_is_not_a_
negative_result`). Caught only because "PES.2 says they moved the reason to `tooltip`" and "the
tooltip is not in the DOM" is a contradiction worth one more probe rather than a bug report.

**Measured for PES.2:** the DS ⋯ menu, which appends the reason to the label rather than using a
tooltip slot, renders **1059px wide — 61% of a 1728px viewport** on this sheet. #145 already names
this as the known trade-off; recording the number since it is now visible on a second grid.

#### PES.3-12 — the undefined-token guard, written and mutation-tested

`scripts/check-css-token-definitions.mjs` (hub-routed, #143). Every `var(--nds-…)` **without a
fallback** must name a token defined somewhere in the repo; definitions are collected repo-wide
including `setProperty('--nds-x', …)`, so a runtime-defined token is never called missing.

**It found 5 real ones on its first run, zero false positives** — each hand-checked against the
token files before being believed. Three were fixable by me: `--nds-font-mono` (×3, my own CSS —
the DS defines **no** mono token at all, it inlines the stack at `primitives.css:680`), now written
`var(--nds-font-mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace)` so it picks the token up the
day the DS defines one. **→ DS: a mono family token is a genuine gap.** The other three are other
lanes' and untouched: `--nds-surface-2` (6 refs, apps/factory), `--nds-text-1` (3, marketing/ads),
`--nds-primary-subtle` (1, apps/factory).

**Two self-caught defects in the guard itself, both of the class the guard exists to avoid:**

1. **It reported the wrong line numbers.** Block comments were replaced with a single space, which
   collapses a multi-line comment and shifts every line after it. Caught by opening one reported
   site and finding unrelated code. A guard that names a confidently specific wrong line is worse
   than one that names none — the reader stops trusting the tool. Now replaced newline-for-newline.
2. **It reported a test's negative assertion.** `recordActions.vitest.test.ts` asserts
   `not.toContain('z-index: var(--nds-z-modal)')` — a token name whose whole purpose is to be
   absent. Test files are no longer scanned for references.

**Mutation-tested four ways, and the file restored byte-identical afterwards:** a real reference to
a non-existent token is reported and `--check` exits 1 · the *same* token inside a block comment is
NOT reported (comment stripping actually works — the file that motivated this guard now carries a
comment naming `--nds-warning-bg`) · `var(--x, fallback)` is not reported · baseline `--check`
already exits 1.

**🔴 Not wired into pre-push.** It is red on landing because of the three pre-existing references
above, and a gate that lands red either blocks every lane or gets bypassed on day one. It runs
clean the moment those are fixed or given fallbacks — that is a decision for whoever owns those two
files, not something I will silently ratchet around.

### PES.2 — ruling #146: both substrate fixes, and a stale `.d.ts` that made me build the worse one

#### 1. `actionsColumn` now defaults to `pinned: true`

PES.3's framing is right and the change is the default, not the docs. Unpinned only sets
`lockPosition: 'right'` — the column is last in the ORDER and scrolls off the end, which is
invisible on a ~100-column sheet. The asymmetry is one-sided: on a narrow grid pinning changes
nothing an operator can perceive (there is no horizontal scroll to be frozen against); on a wide one
it is the difference between a working control and an absent one. **A default should be wrong in the
cheap direction, and this one was wrong in the expensive direction.**

Blast radius measured before changing it, not after: three consumers. `/products/next` (the Owner's
benchmark) relied on the old default — **checked on screen, its grid fits the viewport with no
horizontal scroll, so pinning is a visual no-op there**; Edit + `⋯` render exactly as before.
`ChannelSheet` already passed `pinned: true` explicitly with a comment about this very trap. The lab
has one of each. `pinned: false` stays available.

#### 2. 🔴 The DS menu HAS a tooltip slot. A stale `.d.ts` hid it, and I built the worse UI.

`components/Menu.tsx` has carried `title?: string` — commented *"Tooltip — also the only way a
DISABLED item can explain why"* — the whole time. `components/Menu.d.ts` **omits it**. I read the
declaration, concluded the DS had no tooltip slot, and appended reasons to labels instead: ~900px
wide here, 1059px (61% of the viewport) on PES.3's channel sheet.

Both adapters now put the reason in a tooltip — AG's `tooltip`, the DS's `title` — and both labels
stay clean. Pinned by a test that compares the two surfaces field by field.

**The general point is worth more than the fix.** `check-ds-dts-fresh` has been red all session from
other lanes' uncommitted component work, and I filed it as a push-blocker for someone else to
coordinate. It is not only a hygiene problem: **a stale declaration does not merely fail to describe
a component, it makes the next lane build a worse one.** Two lanes then measured the consequence as
a UI defect without either of us suspecting the declaration. That raises its priority.

#### ⚠ Open question handed back rather than assumed

`title` on a **disabled** `<button>` is not reliably rendered — browsers suppress pointer events on
disabled controls, and my on-screen probe (a real disabled button with a `title`, hovered) produced
no visible tooltip, though native tooltips also screenshot unreliably so the probe is **inconclusive
either way**. I have used the DS's designated slot rather than working around it, but the DS comment
asserts something I could not confirm. If it does not render, every disabled menu entry is silent —
the exact trap the slot exists to prevent — and the fix is a real DS tooltip (`InfoTip`) rather than
the native attribute. **Not mine to decide: `components/Menu.tsx` is a DS component, not grid
substrate.**

**Green:** 1937 tests (149 files), `tsc` 0, grid:conformance ✓ (12 probes), five guards ✓.

#### PES.3-13 — PES.5's alias + reason fields consumed, and they reframe what the console was saying

Wired `sku`, `aliasId`/`aliasKey`/`aliasResolved`, `reason`/`reasonSummary`/`reasonActionable`.
`jumpTargetOf()` composes the sheet row id **here** (`${aliasKey || 'primary'}:${productId}`), which
is the whole reason PES.5 returns components, and returns **null** when `aliasResolved` is false
rather than guessing `primary` — a jump to the wrong row is worse than no jump, because the operator
believes it.

**The reason field changed the headline, and it should have.** Measured on the real coordinate:
of 36 dead writes, **33 are `throttled` — our own circuit breaker, "it will retry without you" —
and only 3 are `rejected`**. The console was presenting 36 problems where there are 3. That is the
illusion this console exists to dispel, repeating itself one level up: I had collapsed 2,553 rows
into 2 causes and then rendered both causes with identical weight. Now the summary reads
**"36 queued writes across 2 causes · 21 products · 3 need you"**, the throttled group is toned
quiet and the rejected group red, and each row names its SKU. Verified on screen: the three
actionable rows are GALE-JACKET-YELLOW-MEN-XXS, GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-XXS and GALE-JACKET, all one
eBay `get offers 404`.

#### PES.3-14 — two URL writers in one tick lose one key (→ PES.1)

`setTab('sheet')` followed by `record.open(rowId)` in one handler **silently drops the tab change**.
Both `push` (`contracts.tsx:604`) and `pushHistory` (`:620`) build their next URL from the same
`search` snapshot captured at render, so two calls in one tick each patch the *pre-jump* query
string and the second overwrites the first. Measured on screen: the URL took
`rec=primary:cmokmy0mm000bpm0pm7k7eke4` and lost `tab=sheet`, leaving the operator on the console
with a drawer that has nothing to render it (the drawer is mounted by the sheet).

I have **not** worked around it by composing the URL in my own file — that would duplicate exactly
what I argued PES.5 should not duplicate. The jump is tab-only until the frame can do it in one
navigation, and **the control says "Open sheet" rather than "Go to row"**: `jumpTargetOf` is correct
and tested and the `title` names the row it would land on, but nothing may claim a precision the
navigation cannot deliver. **→ PES.1: one navigation that sets tab and record together.**

#### PES.3-15 — 🔴 I started a second API with invented disable flags and it ran prod crons

Full account in `reference_local_api_duplicates_prod_crons`. I started an API on :8092 with
`NEXUS_DISABLE_JOBS=1 NEXUS_DISABLE_CRONS=1 DISABLE_CRONS=1`. **None of the three exist** — the only
switch is `NEXUS_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=1`. So it came up running every cron and the autopilot
worker against the production database, silently: an unread env var throws nothing and logs nothing.
PES.0 spotted it from outside and told me; I verified by grep and by the *absence* of the
`background jobs DISABLED` boot line, then stopped it.

**Measured damage:** 9 duplicate `(jobName, minute)` pairs, all within 19:12:58–19:19:5xZ —
`scheduled-bulk-action` ×7 minutes, `scheduled-export` ×1, `scheduled-import` ×1. Every other job
ran exactly 1/min (advisory lock held). **Nothing executed:** 0 bulk actions ran, and there are 0
enabled `ScheduledBulkAction` rows with a `nextRunAt` at all; 0 imports, 0 exports; all `CronRun`
rows SUCCESS. Lucky rather than safe, exactly like 2026-08-20.

**The aggravating fact: the correct invocation was already running in the same session** — :8091 has
`NEXUS_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_JOBS=1` set correctly, which is why no duplicates appear before 19:13Z. I
typed plausible names from memory instead of copying a command that was demonstrably working, and
the flag is documented in the memory file I did not re-read. Both my processes are now stopped.

**Generalisable, and it is the same class as PES.3-7's `var(--nope)`:** an invented name for a
switch fails loudly at no layer — CSS, env, feature flags. Prove the mechanism READ it (a log line,
a grep of the source), never that you passed it. And the check is an ABSENCE, so it must be looked
for on purpose.

**Green:** 526 studio tests, tsc clean, `next build` exit 0, guards ✓ (p3-token-sweep,
ds-conformance, link-targets, ag-grid-import-boundary, grid-chrome, grid-option-identity,
grid-modules, grid-kit-ratchet, css-token-definitions on my own files). Nothing committed.

#### PES.3-16 — 🔴 correcting my own "6 ACTIVE eBay listings at 0/0": it is 13, and the cause I assumed is wrong

Asked by the hub for the measurement behind a number I had put on the record, I re-derived it rather
than restating it. **It does not reproduce as 6.**

**Basis — a set scan over all 252 eBay `ChannelListing` rows, zero and NULL kept apart:**

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE quantity = 0)  AS qty_measured_zero,   -- 117
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE quantity IS NULL) AS qty_null,          -- 0
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE price = 0)     AS price_measured_zero,  -- 14
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE price IS NULL) AS price_null,           -- 0
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE quantity = 0 AND price = 0) AS both     -- 13
FROM "ChannelListing" WHERE channel='EBAY' AND "listingStatus"='ACTIVE';   -- 222 ACTIVE
```

**13 with both at a measured zero, 14 with a zero price.** No NULLs anywhere in either column, so
every zero here is a stored zero and not a null read as one.

**🔴 "ACTIVE" is OUR column, not eBay's.** 222 ACTIVE (222 with an ItemID) and 30 DRAFT (25 with an
ItemID) — the DRAFT rows carrying real ItemIDs are the same evidence that made me refuse a live
pin→reset witness earlier. So this says our record marks them active; **what eBay currently shows is
not knowable from here**, and 12 of the 13 have not been touched since 2026-07-28.

**A hypothesis I formed and then killed.** All 13 are `followMasterPrice = true` with
`masterPrice IS NULL`, which looked like a clean explanation: the zero is a materialised value from
a master that has no price. Then I checked the base rate — **222 of 222 ACTIVE rows have exactly
that configuration**, while 208 of them carry a non-zero price. So the follow-master setup does not
distinguish the 14 at all, and the explanation is wrong. Testing the base rate is the whole reason
this is a correction rather than a second wrong claim.

**The sharpest row is not one of the 13.** `WATERPROOF-OVERJACKET-BLACK-MEN`, ItemID 257608449467:
**quantity 10, price 0.00** — the one with stock to sell. The 13 at 0/0 cannot transact; this one
could. If it is what the Owner acts on, it should be this row first.

**Still open, and I am not going to guess it:** with `followMasterPrice = true`, whether the stored
`price` is even the value the outbound path would send is unresolved — reading
`outbound-sync.service.ts`'s price derivation would settle it, and a single eBay `GetItem` would
settle what eBay actually shows. Neither is done, so nothing above claims a live shopfront price.

### PES.1 — two URL writers in one tick: FIXED generically (ruling #149)

PES.3's diagnosis was exact. Both writers built the next URL from the `search` snapshot captured at
RENDER, so two writes in a tick each patched the pre-jump query string and the second won.

**Fixed by COALESCING, not by a combined setter.** A `openRecordInTab()` would have fixed the one
pair somebody hit; ordering can't fix it at all (both reads are stale from the same snapshot). Now
every call merges its patch into a pending set and ONE microtask later a single navigation applies
all of them to the freshest URL. **Every present and future pair is correct by construction, and no
caller changes** — PES.3 just calls `setTab('sheet')` then `record.open(row)` and both land. Their
control can become "Go to row" with no other change, as they planned.
`replace` vs `push` is the union: if any write in the tick was a history write, the batch is one.

**Verified end-to-end, and mutation-tested.** Clicking a scope chip and a tab in the SAME tick:
`?market=IT&scope=EBAY&tab=activity` — both keys, market preserved, both controls active. Reverting
the writers to the snapshot form reproduces the defect exactly (**`scope` lost, `tab` won**), so the
test genuinely fails when the fix is absent.

**The audit found a second instance, as predicted.** `contracts.tsx` had ONE more direct
`router.replace` — the last-used-market restore — which was therefore the one write that could never
be coalesced. Moved below the writers and routed through `push`. There is now exactly one write path
(the flush) plus `router.back()` in `closeRecord`, which is a history pop and legitimately different.

🔴 **And the fix shipped with a bug of its own, caught on screen before reporting.** The queue's
`alive` ref was set to `false` in the effect cleanup but never back to `true` on mount. Under
StrictMode's mount → cleanup → mount, it latched off and **silently disabled every URL write in
dev** — the frame rendered perfectly, chips and tabs responded, and nothing reached the URL. Fixed
by setting it true in the effect body. A flag only ever cleared by a cleanup is a StrictMode trap.

1941 tests · 7/7 guards · tsc clean · nothing committed.

#### PES.3-17 — 🔴 my pane told an operator "3 need you" when the answer was 36

PES.5's corrected classifier (hub #151) exposed a defect on my side, and it is the exact failure this
lane exists to prevent: **a false reassurance rendered confidently.**

**Verified before changing anything.** Every circuit-open row in the database: **377 rows, all
`isDead=true`, all `retryCount 3/3`, all `syncStatus='FAILED'`** — they exhausted their retries
*while being throttled*, so the write never reached the channel and never will. One correction to the
hub's account: **`nextRetryAt` is NOT null, it is populated on all 377.** The conclusion is unchanged,
but a dead row carrying a future retry timestamp reads as *scheduled* to anyone checking that column,
which is worse than null. (My basis is the `circuit open` message — 377 — against their classifier's
399; narrower filter, not a contradiction.)

**The defect was mine and it was in the tone rule, not the copy.** I toned a group by its **cause**:
`throttled` was styled quiet because throttling is normally self-healing. But a throttled row that
died mid-defer is a lost write wearing a reassuring label. `groupIsQuiet()` now returns true only
when **every** row in the group is non-actionable, consuming the server's verdict rather than testing
the reason string. The group header also renders the server's **`reasonSummary` verbatim** — "Gave up
while throttled — this write never reached the channel and will not retry" — because any shorter
label I write for it is the same compression that hid the problem.

Real data through the real code path (`:8091`, 2026-09-01):

```
HEADER: 36 queued writes across 2 causes · 21 products      ← no "3 need you"
actionable: 36 of 36
  [NEEDS YOU] throttled · will not retry — 33 writes / 21 products
  [NEEDS YOU] rejected  · will not retry —  3 writes /  3 products
```

**The lesson, and it is one level past PES.3-13's.** Grouping without weighting is half the honesty —
and weighting by the wrong field is worse than not weighting at all, because it is confident. A cause
describes why a write stalled; only the row's STATE says whether anyone still needs to care. **A
cause is not a verdict**, and the fix was to stop deciding tone from a label I recognised.

#### PES.3-18 — the precise jump restored (PES.1's coalescing, hub #152)

Verified on disk before relying on it: `contracts.tsx:636` merges every patch in a tick and flushes
once via `queueMicrotask`, later keys winning. So `setTab('sheet')` + `record.open(rowId)` both land.
The control is now **"Go to row"** when the alias resolved and **"Open sheet"** for the ~10% where it
did not — two labels, each true, rather than one that overpromises on exactly the rows an operator
would most resent being misled about.

**✅ Both verified on screen** (`localhost:3000`, which the hub had already repointed at the local
API — my premise that it pointed at prod was stale, and the hub was right to make me measure it from
the page rather than accept it: `{"http://127.0.0.1:8091": 11}`, zero Railway).

PES.3-17 on screen: header "36 queued writes across 2 causes · 21 products", **no "3 need you"**,
both groups red (`throttled · will not retry`, `rejected · will not retry`), and each carrying the
server's verdict verbatim. PES.3-18 on screen: all three actionable rows read **"Go to row"** with

### PES.2 — a defect of mine, found while re-verifying after the server restart

Re-verified the #141 right-click menu in the clean post-restart environment. The page hung first, and
checking *why* rather than assuming found something I had introduced.

**Not the cause. 🔴 AND THE LABEL I PUT ON IT WAS WRONG — see the retraction below.** The page
showed `studio/sheet` and `pim/family` **pending** with `readiness` **503**, while the same
endpoints answered **200** from `curl`. Applying #136's positive-signal test was right and is what
ruled my code out; calling the result "pool starvation" was pattern-matching.

**The real defect, mine:** `useActionPress` returned a **fresh object literal on every render**, and
`MasterSheet` depended on the whole object in the `useMemo` that builds `getContextMenuItems`. So
the memo recomputed every render, and an unstable `getContextMenuItems` re-runs AG's entire column
model each time — the exact trap my own comment two lines above cites
(`reference_ag_react_inline_options_rerun_column_model`).

Fixed at **both** ends, because either alone leaves the trap set:
- The host now depends on `rowPress.press` (a stable `useCallback`), not the object.
- **The hook now returns a memoised object.** That is the more important half: a hook whose result
  cannot be used as a dependency makes every consumer's memo a lie, and it would have punished each
  lane that wired it up *correctly*. PES.3 and PES.4 both consume `useActionPress`.

Verified after the fix: the sheet loads and the right-click menu renders its three verbs at normal
width in a clean environment.

**Green:** 1941 tests (149 files), `tsc` 0, grid:conformance ✓ (12 probes), four guards ✓.

### PES.2 — RETRACTION: "pool starvation" was pattern-matching, and one of my numbers was a filter artifact

Hub ruling #153 challenged the label; PES.3 sharpened it. Both were right.

🔴 **"Only three requests fired" was an artifact of my own network filter.** I read with
`urlPattern: "8091/api/p"` and reported the count as a total. SSE streams, notifications, sidebar,
connections and auth all fail that pattern. The real figure at the stall is **8–12 pending
simultaneously**. The count objection was correct for a better reason than either side knew: my
count was measuring my filter, not the page. Same class as
`reference_inference_from_your_own_scaffolding` — committed while arguing about measurement
discipline.

PES.3's point is the decisive half: **a 503 is the server answering, and a starved client never gets
a status at all.** That alone rules out pool exhaustion for the readiness call.

#### What was then measured — discriminating, without establishing a cause

| test | result | rules out |
|---|---|---|
| 6 parallel `curl`s during the stall | all **200 in 0.82–1.30s** | API down, API serialising |
| fresh tab, same URL | same stall | tab-local React state |
| closed the stuck tab, reloaded | still 8 pending | "one wedged tab holds the origin" |
| pending set contents | `auth/csrf`, `notifications`, `sidebar/counts` | anything in this lane's code |

⚠ **Correcting one of those tests as it is filed:** Chrome's socket pool is **per-origin, shared
across tabs**, so "open a new tab" was never a clean-pool test. It rules out tab-local state; it does
NOT rule out the origin's connection pool. Recorded weaker than it first appeared.

The hub's own wedged-EventSource-across-restart hypothesis is refuted by rows 2 and 3.

**No fourth label offered.** What the evidence supports is narrow: the API answers curl fine and
concurrently at the moment the browser cannot get answers on the same host; it is not tab-local, not
the old tab, and not cleared by a restart or a fresh tab. PES.3's clean run minutes earlier makes it
intermittent or state-dependent somewhere neither of us has measured. Handed to PES.1 with the
evidence rather than a diagnosis — and the one piece nobody has read yet is **what the API logs when
it emits the 503**.

**The lesson, which is the same one twice tonight in this area:** matching a known failure is not a
diagnosis until it has been discriminated against the alternatives the same evidence allows. I wrote
that rule down after the first time and then broke it, because the second symptom looked like the
first.

### PES.1 — starvation ROOT CAUSE found and fixed: a third stream the sweep missed (rulings #153–#160)

**It was "a third consumer", not "the gate isn't applying".**
`components/dashboard/CompetitiveAlertWatcher.tsx` opens `/api/orders/events` and lives in the
root layout's **`overlays`** slot — which `AppShell`'s `noRail` branch **does** render, so it mounts
on the studio (and on every other route). My #99 adoption sweep gated `ControlTowerBanner` and
`LiveActivityClient` and missed it, because I grepped the two files a narrower search had already
surfaced instead of enumerating every `new EventSource` site and asking which ones render here.

**Before → after, same tab, same stack, one page load apart:**

| | 8 concurrent probes to the app origin | sheet rows | completed API calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | **ALL 8 PENDING after 10s** | 0 | 3 |
| after | **219 · 219 · 242 · 250 · 251 · 272 · 298 · 303 ms** | **21** | 19 |

Also gated `GlobalAccountHealthBanner` and `GlobalDlqBanner` — same class, same slot family
(`banners`, so full-chrome routes rather than the studio).

**What this explains:** why `?rec=` mattered (the drawer's extra requests push an already-loaded pool
over), why it was intermittent (pure timing overlap — PES.3's clean run is the same code), and why a
fresh tab didn't help (the socket pool is per ORIGIN, shared across tabs).

**Measurements that stand, and one of my own claims that does not:**
- The per-origin limit here is exactly **6**, measured: 8 requests on an uncontended origin tier
  **6 then 2** (50ms ×6, 100ms ×2).
- During a stall the same server answered `localhost` in **410ms** while `127.0.0.1` hung — so the
  API was never down or serialising.
- All four heavy endpoints return in **170–1056ms** on an uncontended origin.
- 🔴 **I was wrong to claim "no EventSource is open" from an empty resource-entry list.** A stream
  that never completes leaves no entry, exactly like a pending fetch — the same trap I had already
  banked. The static enumeration is what found it; the resource list could not have.

**Still unexplained, and NOT this bug: PES.2's 503.** A starved client never receives a status code,
so a 503 is the server making a decision — as PES.3 argued. That reason exists in an API log nobody
has read, and it remains the last untouched evidence. I have no access to the hub-owned API's logs.

**Not swept:** ~19 other `EventSource` sites on routes the studio never loads (orders, dashboard,
ads, sync-logs, bulk-operations) plus four `lib/sync/use-*-events` hooks. Each is one line —
`if (!streamsEnabled()) return` — for whoever owns them. I gated global chrome only, because that is
what mounts everywhere.

1963 tests · 7/7 guards · nothing committed.

#### PES.3-19 — the price question settled, and the 13 turn out to be a corner of something bigger

Took the read the hub offered (read-only; no lane file touched).

**Settled:** the eBay push sends `payload.price` from the queue row
(`outbound-sync.service.ts:1473/1496` → `buildEbayOfferUpdate(offer, payload.price, currency)`),
never `ChannelListing.price` read at push time. `master-price.service.ts:266` writes that payload
from the *same* computed value it writes to the column, so the two agree at cascade time — but the
column records the last cascade, it is not the source of the send. **"Our row says 0.00" does not
establish that we ever told eBay zero.**

**The 14 are two different problems, which one number hid:**
- **10** also have `Product.basePrice = 0.00`: the listing faithfully mirrors a product with no
  price. The gap is upstream, in the product record.
- **4** have a real basePrice their listing has not taken up — AIREON (159.00), AIRMESH-JACKET
  (109.99), **WATERPROOF-OVERJACKET-BLACK-MEN (19.99, quantity 10)**, normal-knee-slider (21.99).

**The larger measurement.** All 222 ACTIVE eBay listings are `followMasterPrice = true` +
`pricingRule = FIXED` — the combination for which `computeListingPrice` returns exactly the master
price. **Only 63 have `price = basePrice`; 155 diverge.** The zeros are the visible corner of that.

**🔴 I am not calling the 155 a defect, and that restraint is the finding's method.** At least twelve
services write `ChannelListing`, several pricing-related (`repricing-engine`, `pricing-outbound`,
`bulk-action`, `promotion-scheduler`, `amazon-market-offer`). A repricer legitimately moving a price
off the master produces this exact signature. My tidy explanation was "no cascade ever ran for
these"; I could not establish it, so it is not shipped — the same base-rate discipline that killed
the `followMasterPrice`/null-master story one entry earlier.

**The question that has to be answered first, and it is not mine:** is `followMasterPrice = true` an
**ongoing invariant** or only **cascade behaviour**? The field name implies the first; the contract of
`computeListingPrice` — called on a master update, returning what the price should *become* — implies
the second. Under the first reading 155 rows are wrong; under the second most are fine. Nobody should
act on either number until that is settled.
