### PES.2 — the 503 was never real, and my lane re-verified in the first healthy environment

**Ruling #162's correction, accepted.** I reported `503` four times and it went four rulings without
anyone checking it, me included. The API log — hub-owned, and the last untouched evidence, which I
had myself named as the thing nobody had read — shows **zero 503s** and **88 × HTTP 500**
(`[sidebar/counts] failed` ×30, `premature close` ×24, `Connection terminated due to connection
timeout` ×16).

🔴 **The generalisable part: a browser network panel's `statusCode` is not the server's status.** The
reading tool surfaced a status the server never sent — plausibly synthesised from a connection that
died mid-flight, which fits the 24 `premature close` entries exactly. The argument built on it
survives untouched (a **500** is equally the server answering, and a starved client receives no
status at all, so ruling out pure client-side starvation was still right) — but the number was
wrong, and it was wrong in the one direction I could have checked cheaply at any point. **Never
assert a specific 5xx from a browser network panel. Read the server log; it is the only place the
status actually exists.**

That is the third instrument failure of this session, all the same shape: a filtered request count
quoted as a total, a native tooltip that screenshots unreliably reported as inconclusive (correctly),
and now a synthesised status quoted as fact. The lesson is not "measure more" — it is **know what
your instrument is actually reporting**.

**Root cause, for the record (PES.1's):** `CompetitiveAlertWatcher` opens `/api/orders/events` from
the root layout's `overlays` slot, so it renders on every route including the studio; #99's sweep
gated the two files a grep surfaced rather than enumerating every EventSource site. Measured 8
concurrent probes pending after 10s and 0 sheet rows before; 219–303ms and 21 rows after, same tab,
one page load apart.

🔴 **RETRACTED (ruling #164) — "one root cause, two pools" is wrong, and I amplified it.** The
Prisma errors are not pool timeouts. Grepped text: **"Can't reach database server at
`ep-purple-river-…-pooler…neon.tech` — Please make sure your database server is running"**, 45 times
across 18 entries. `Connection terminated due to connection timeout` sits in the same window and is
consistent with the same thing: **Neon was unreachable.** So the API's 500s were a
database-reachability window, NOT its Prisma pool being starved by SSE streams. The two symptoms
were **coincident, not causal**. PES.1's browser fix stands entirely on its own before/after
measurement (8 probes pending vs 219–303ms); it did not cause the server errors.

**My part in this is worth naming.** The hub proposed the unification and I wrote it into this file
as fact within minutes — because it vindicated the instinct I had already retracted, and a
correction that hands your hypothesis back is the one you check least. I applied more scepticism to
the corrections that cost me something than to the one that returned something. That is the same
failure as the 503: **a claim passed hand to hand, everyone reasoning correctly on top of it, nobody
re-measuring the thing itself.** One grep settled it, and I did not run it.

#### Re-verified on the fixed stack — the first healthy environment of this lane

Every on-screen check in this lane was made under the degraded condition, so all of it was re-run:

- Studio loads: **21 rows**, family bar reads `Parent · 20 variations · Colore × Taglia`, scope
  percentages fill immediately.
- Right-click a child row: **Unlink from parent · Move to another parent… · Delete variation…** above
  AG's own items, separated by a rule, at normal menu width, each disabled with its reason in a
  tooltip.

All prior verification stands. **Green:** 1963 tests (150 files), web tsc 0, api tsc 0,
grid:conformance ✓, guards ✓. Nothing committed.

🔴 **CORRECTION to my own §22 claim, on my own second reading.** The job list shipped saying
**"37 with no recorded outcome"**. The outcome was recorded — on the same rows, in
`resultSummary.perSku`, a field §22 never read. All 37 carry Amazon's per-SKU processing report.
Corrected in `publish/jobs.ts` and on screen; nobody had to catch this for me, which is the only
part of it I would repeat.

**The measurement** (complete sets, not samples — all 78 job rows, all 71 `imagePublish*` audit
entries, 83 entries total for the product on one unpaginated page):

- **The status column is close to inverted.** 37 Amazon rows say `IN_PROGRESS` while carrying a
  finish time *and* a 666-line receipt; 6 say `DONE` while carrying neither. **43 of 78 rows
  contradict themselves** — now a number on the surface that expands into the rows it names.
- **The two logs cannot be joined, and it is structural, not a data accident.** Amazon writes a
  start (with `jobId` + `feedId`) and *never* an outcome — `amazon-images.routes.ts` has no
  `imagePublishCompleted` call at all, and its own comment says the terminal status would come
  "from `pollAndUpdateFeedJob` **if/when we wire that**". eBay writes outcomes with real error text,
  never a start, and its 24 outcome rows carry **no job reference**. The surface therefore shows two
  unmerged lists and says why once — pairing them on a timestamp would attribute outcomes to named
  jobs on a guess.
- **The Amazon half IS joinable and now visibly is:** the audit start's `feedId` is the job row's
  `vendorEntityId`, so both lists show a reference column and the same feed id appears in both, a
  second apart.

⚠ **The 666/666-accepted receipt is evidence of completion, NOT proof of success** — checked before
being believed, because it is exactly the falsely-clean shape of §19. `accepted` is
`errors.length === 0`, and the service deliberately treats an *absent* processing report as zero
issues. The distinguishing field (`resultSummary.processingReport`) is not exposed by the API. So
the surface says "Ended · 18 SKUs, none rejected" with a note that this is evidence it finished
rather than proof it published, and keeps "Ended, no report" as a separate, differently-labelled
state. Positive confirmation lives on the listing rows' own `publishStatus` in the matrix.

   job rows. Two call sites in `channel-image-publish.routes.ts`.

**→ Hub, ruling #156 (hook object literals): swept and fixed in this lane.** All six hooks returned

## PES.2 — ruling #169 piece 1: the curated default view, proposed from measurement

Lane reopened for Layout v2. This is the list for the hub to put to the Owner. **Measured across 120
rows / 5 families** (GALE-JACKET, AIREON, 1J-EYE5-Y0TW, REGAL-JACKET, WATERPROOF-OVERJACKET) on the
live studio contract, not chosen by taste.

### What the measurement found, which reframes the complaint

| fact | number |
|---|---|
| columns offered on the master scope | 102–147 depending on product type |
| columns carrying data on **more than one family** | **7** |
| columns never populated in **any** of the 5 families | **134 of 155** |

The Owner said "I barely see a few columns". The deeper problem is the opposite of what it sounds
like: **there were never a hundred useful columns to see.** ~90 of them are blank on every row, so
the sheet was spending its width on emptiness and squeezing the seven that carry the product.

Populated: `name` `sku` `status` `basePrice` `totalStock` 120/120 · `productType` 104/120 ·
`brand` 84/120. Everything else is per-product-type attributes.

### 🔴 Why the default cannot be a fixed key list

The required set is **per product type**, and measured `required.total` per row is `7` (78 rows),
`6` (26 rows), `0` (16 rows). `fabric_type` is required for OUTERWEAR and meaningless on a knee
slider. A fixed list would be wrong for most of the catalogue in one direction or the other.

**So the default view is a RULE, and the ~12–15 is its typical output, not its definition:**

1. **Identity — always.** Thumbnail + SKU (the pinned identity cell), `name`, `status`, readiness
   chip. *Earns it:* 100% populated; the row's handle and its verdict.
2. **Commerce spine — always.** `basePrice`, `totalStock`, `brand`, `productType`. *Earns it:*
   100/100/70/87% populated, and `productType` decides which schema applies to everything else — a
   readiness warn on 16 rows is about this field being wrong.
3. **Every field REQUIRED for this row's product type — filled or not.** *Earns it:* this is an
   editor, not a report. An empty required cell is the work; hiding it is hiding the job. Measured,
   this adds ≤7 columns.
4. **Any field with a readiness issue on a row in view.** Measured: `dsa_responsible_party_address`
   and `gpsr_safety_attestation`, 104/120 each — **GPSR, and the message says the listing can be
   suppressed on EU marketplaces.** A field that can get a listing suppressed belongs on screen by
   default.

Typical output on GALE-JACKET: **14 columns.** On a product whose type has no schema (16 rows
measured) it degrades to the 8 in rules 1–2, which is correct — there is nothing else to show.

### What this buys, stated so the Owner can reject it precisely

- The most common single row state in the sample is "`product_description` and `bullet_point` are
  missing" — 104/120 rows. Under the current default those two are somewhere among 102 columns.
  Under this rule they are on screen, always, because they are required and absent.
- The other ~90 stay reachable through the DS Customize dialog and saved views. Nothing is removed.

**Not built yet — this is the proposal.** I did not want to implement a column set the Owner has not
seen, and the rule is the part worth agreeing before code.

### PES.7 — P5 COMPLETE, and a latent safety defect (2026-09-01 ~23:20)

🔴 **`dryRun` is accepted, logged, returned — and never forwarded.** Found wiring the planner's fire
path. In `submitAmazonImageFeed`:

```ts
...(dryRun ? {} : {}),  // ← empty object in BOTH branches
```

and `AmazonBatchSubmission` has no `dryRun` field, so the "override" that comment describes does not
exist. Submission is decided **solely** by `getAmazonPublishMode() !== 'live'`. **Structural claim** —
that spread is the only path the flag could take.

| publish mode | request | what happens | audit records |
|---|---|---|---|
| not `live` | anything | dry run — safe | the request's flag |
| **`live`** | **`dryRun: true`** | **a real feed is submitted** | **`dryRun: true`** |

All three channels read `"mode":"gated"` today, so it is **latent, not firing**. → Owner/service
owner: either forward the flag or drop it from the contract; and the audit log should record what
happened, not what was asked.

**I had shipped the same lie.** My `PublishPanel` offered "Dry run — build and check the feed without
submitting it" and reported `res.data?.dryRun || dryRun || plan.rehearsalOnly` — **the request flag
wins that OR**, so with the gate live it would have submitted a real feed and said "nothing was
submitted to Amazon". Fixed: the outcome now comes from the server's answer alone (`undefined` is its
own state — "the server did not say"), and the checkbox is disabled, reflecting the gate, with the
reason in visible text. Verified on screen: `checked/disabled/readOnly` all true.

**→ This retracts one of my own inferences:** I read "38 audit starts, all `dryRun: false`" as "these
were real Amazon submissions". The audit records what was *asked for*; whether a feed was submitted
depended on the publish mode at the time, which the audit does not record.

**The planner** (D1's mandatory cross-market preview) leads with **destinations, not targets**, and
takes its list from `options.channels` — which declares **11 Amazon markets**, not the 5 I assumed
from the audit log. Selecting Amazon IT+DE+ES and eBay IT renders: *"4 targets, but only 2
destinations — some of them overwrite each other"*, then *"DE, ES, IT all write the same set of
pictures on AMAZON … whichever finishes last is what Amazon keeps"*, then the mechanism note naming
Country-Specific Upload and A+ Content as the two paths that would give per-country images and
saying neither is automated here. Button reads "Rehearse 4 targets" from the server's gate.
**Not pressed** — no publish was fired, so the sequential-fire path is built and typechecked but
unexercised, and that is stated rather than implied.

Banked in permanent memory as a class: **an API accepting, defaulting, returning and logging a
safety parameter is not evidence it honours it** — and never OR a safety outcome with local intent,
because the local value wins precisely when the server disagrees.

**Green:** 318 tests / 20 files, web tsc 0, api tsc 0, 15 guards 0. **P5 complete.** Nothing committed.
Next: P6/P7 ancillary tabs, then the §5 parity audit.

`defaultViewColumns()` implements ruling #173's four rules; `flaggedColumnKeys()` feeds rule 4 from
the rows in view. 10 tests. The old "landing view is 5–8 columns" assertion is superseded and now
bounds the rule at 8–20 — moved up rather than deleted, because a default that grows without limit
is the hundred-column sheet coming back by another route.

**Verified against the LIVE contract** (not a fixture — two fixture assumptions of mine were wrong
first, see below). Run over the real 102 columns the rule returns **16**:
`name status color size basePrice totalStock brand productType product_description item_name
country_of_origin bullet_point supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation fabric_type
gpsr_safety_attestation dsa_responsible_party_address` — all four rules firing.

🔴 **On screen the grid renders 9 of those 16.** Missing: `color` `size` `basePrice` `totalStock`
`fabric_type` and both flagged keys. Localised, by elimination rather than assumption:

| candidate | ruled out by |
|---|---|
| the rule itself | returns all 16 against the live contract |
| stale saved column state | cleared `nds-grid:product-edit:master:v1`; identical result |
| server saved views overriding the rules | `/api/saved-views?surface=product-edit:master` returns **0** |
| `schemaColumns` filtering them out | it is all columns minus `sku`; all 7 are present in it |
| AG column virtualisation (off-screen) | scrolled the full 3069px width; still 13 unique col-ids |

So the defect is in applying a view's column list to the grid, downstream of `masterViews`. Not
fixed here — it needs the prefs-bridge/landing path, and I would rather hand over a located defect
than a rushed fix.

**Two fixture errors of mine, recorded because the pattern is now three-for-three tonight.** The
unit fixture first omitted `scope: 'per_variant'` (axes silently dropped), then used ENGLISH labels
`Color`/`Size` — at which point `size` failed to match `Taglia` and it read like a defect in
`isAxisColumn`. **Measured against the live contract, the matcher is fine: the labels ship localised
as `Colore`/`Taglia`.** I nearly filed a false defect against working code, from my own scaffolding
again — the same class as the filtered request count and the browser-reported 503.

### Piece 2 — the thumbnail identity cell: wired, deliberately not lit

`ProductCell` now renders the shared `IdentityCell` (grid/renderers/cells.tsx) with the thumbnail —
not a lookalike, since the products page's geometry is measured into that component.

🔴 **Gated on the row actually having an image, because the contract supplies none.** Measured: no
`imageUrl` on any row, no image column among the 102. An ungated thumbnail would put a grey
placeholder on all 21 rows — a column of nothing, which is the exact complaint that reopened this
lane. **Needs PES.5 to add `imageUrl` + `photoCount` to the studio row**, derived with the server's
existing `pickFaceImage` (`product-read-cache.service.ts:42` — isPrimary → MAIN → lowest sortOrder),
which is the same rule PES.7's client `pickFaceImage` uses in the drawer. Same rule both ends means
the grid thumbnail and the drawer's main image cannot disagree. It lights up per row with no further
change here.

**Green:** 2093 tests (157 files), web tsc 0, module gate ✓. Nothing committed. Geometry held for UX.1.

**PES.7 — `dryRun` FIXED (2026-09-01 ~23:30, authorised by ruling #176).** Three files, disclosed:
`services/channel-batch/amazon-batch-feed.service.ts` (adds `dryRun?: boolean`; guard becomes
`isDryRunEnv() || callerRequestedRehearsal` — **one-way**, so a caller can never cause a submission
the gate would have prevented; left optional so the two `bulk-action.service.ts` callers are
untouched), `services/images/amazon-image-feed.service.ts` (`...(dryRun ? {} : {})` → `dryRun,`; the
no-SKU early return now reports `dryRun: true` because that path never calls Amazon), and
`routes/images/amazon-images.routes.ts` (audit records `result.dryRun` = what happened, keeping
`requestedDryRun` separately).

**The invariant is written into the code with its history**, per #176: with the gate closed the
caller-flag half never changes an outcome and reads as redundant — which is exactly how it was lost
before.

**Proven by mutation, not by passing.** Three mutations run and all caught: guard reduced to
`if (isDryRunEnv())`; forward deleted; original empty-spread restored. The behavioural tests run with
the gate **LIVE** (the only configuration where the flag is load-bearing), `amazon-sp-api` is mocked
to throw on construction so a regression cannot reach Amazon from a test run, and one test asserts
the live path *is* entered without a rehearsal request so the others cannot become vacuous.
⚠ **tsc cannot catch the forward's removal** (the field is optional — verified exit 0 with it gone),
hence the source assertions.

Both source assertions failed first time: the fix's own comment quotes the bad pattern, so the
"must not contain" check matched the explanation and the `})` inside it truncated the slice. Now
strips comments first — same class as [[reference_ds_guard_greps_comments]].

**No-op verified at the moment of change:** all three channels `"mode":"gated"`. Prod re-measured
after: 65 Amazon / 81 listing / 2 IT rows still PUBLISHED / 24 master images — baseline. No publish
fired. **Green:** api 5500 tests / 411 files, api tsc 0, web 318 tests, web tsc 0, 15 guards 0.
Nothing committed.

#### PES.3-20 — §14 consumed: channel writes land on the listing, proven at the database

`commitChannelRow` now sends the §14 contract: `changes[].target` **echoed from `writeVerb`**,
`marketplaceContexts[].aliasKey` from the alias group, and the legacy `writeTarget`/`aliasId` keys
(which the endpoint never read) removed.

**Verified by a real write, read back in raw SQL — never through the sheet's own read**, per §14's
own rehearsal rule. Before: eBay·IT listing v14, `overrideData {}`; product v1. After
`country_of_origin → 'IT'`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| **eBay·IT** listing | v14, `{}` | **v15, `{"country_of_origin": "IT"}`** |
| Amazon DE/ES/FR/IT | v61/40/57/87, `{}` | **unchanged, `{}`** |
| `Product` (master) | v1, `country_of_origin` null, updated 08-31 16:45 | **all three unchanged** |

The write landed on exactly the listing the cell belongs to, bumped that listing's version, and did
not leak to master or to a sibling coordinate. Cleaned up afterwards by removing the KEY — verified
**absent**, not set to null.

**Three rules now regression-tested** (`channelWrite.vitest.test.ts`), each of which fails silently:
1. `target` is echoed, never derived. The six column-backed fields have `writeTarget:
   'channelListing'` but `writeVerb: 'master'` — deriving one from the other sends both routes.
2. `aliasKey` is `''` for primary, **never `'primary'`**. `aliasKeyOf` returns `'primary'` and exists
   only to build a sheet row id; sending it would miss the upsert's `ON CONFLICT` target and INSERT
   a second listing. Added `wireAliasKey()` so the two can't be confused again.
3. `expectedVersion` is **dropped when any cell in the batch writes to the channel** — see below.

#### PES.3-21 — 🔴 the CAS gap: the read contract cannot supply the version the write contract checks

The endpoint CASes a channel write on the **listing's** version (`products.routes.ts:2202`), but the
read contract only ever returns the **product's** (`studio-sheet.service.ts:750`) and `SheetListing`
carries no `version` field at all. Measured on eBay·IT: **156 of 252 listings have a version that
differs from their product's** — GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-L is product v1 against listing v66, and the
row I wrote was product v1 against listing v14.

So sending the product's number would 409 on ~62% of channel writes with a conflict that never
happened. A spurious conflict is worse than no CAS: it teaches an operator to dismiss the one
message that should always mean something. `expectedVersion` is therefore omitted whenever the batch
touches the channel, and kept for master-only batches — the case the CAS was built for. **→ PES.5:
`version` on `SheetListing` closes this; the guard comes back the day it lands.**

#### PES.3-22 — my own #135 gesture was actively harmful, found by using it

Double-clicking a cell did **two things at once**: AG opened the cell editor *and* my
`onRowDoubleClicked` opened the record drawer — whose mounting re-flows a horizontally scrolled grid,
so the editor that had just opened now belonged to a **different cell and a different row** than the
one double-clicked. On a channel scope that is a write aimed at the wrong field.

Fixed: the drawer opens on double-click only when the cell is **not editable**. A double-click on an
editable cell means edit; the ⋯ menu's `Open record` remains the unambiguous path, so losing the
gesture on the editable columns costs nothing. Unit tests and the master precedent are unaffected —
master's grid does not scroll horizontally the same way, which is why the precedent looked safe.

#### PES.3-23 — 🔴 a tool error is not proof the action didn't happen

While diagnosing, I fired a `PATCH` from the page's console and the tool returned *"Inspected target
navigated or closed"*. I read that as "the probe did not run". **It ran.** The read-back later found
`{"item_name": "PES3-PROBE"}` on the GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-3XL eBay·IT listing — the request had been
sent and had succeeded before the tab navigated; only the *result* was lost.

Removed, verified absent. But the lesson is the sibling of the inherited-number class and of
`reference_quiet_measurement_is_not_a_negative_result`: **an error from the tool describes the tool's
ability to report, not the world.** A write probe whose result you did not see is a write you must
assume landed and go check — at the database, which is the only place that knows.

Also on the record: two unintended write attempts reached production during coordinate-driven UI
clicks (one refused by enum validation, one the probe above). Both are XAVIA-family rows, both are
cleaned up and verified, and both are the reason I stopped driving the write by screen coordinates —
the tool's coordinate space is scaled against CSS pixels (1512 vs 1728 here) and the drawer re-flows
the grid mid-gesture, so each attempt is a live write aimed by arithmetic.

## AG.1 — the studio sheet's AG Grid audit (measured on GALE-JACKET, master scope, before any build)

Environment for every number below: local web `localhost:3000` → **local API `127.0.0.1:8091`** (asserted from
the page, not inferred), viewport **1440×723**, AG **36.1.0** Enterprise, product
`cmokmy3a40078pm0p1fvnu523`, market DE / locale de, 21 rows (parent + 20 variations), 100 built columns.
Permissions read `anon` under the local API, so every greyed family verb is expected, not a defect
([[reference_local_web_hits_local_api_8091]]). **No cell was ever committed** — every edit opened for
measurement was cancelled, because a local API still writes the prod database.

### Ranked by what it costs an operator

**1. 🔴 One double-click opens the cell editor AND the record drawer, and the drawer then eats the cell.**
Ruling #169's item (2), and the worst thing on the sheet. Measured: double-click `item_name` row 0 →
`getEditingCells()` = `['item_name']` **and** the URL gains `?rec=cmokmy3a40078pm0p1fvnu523`. The drawer
docks, the sheet narrows 1440 → ~930px, `item_name` goes **behind the drawer**, and the
`agLargeTextCellEditor` popup ends up floating over the drawer's photo gallery — detached from its cell,
over a panel that is separately offering an editable field for the same record. Escape closes the editor
and **leaves the drawer open**.
Cause is structural, not a bug in either lane: AG 36.1 dispatches `_onCellDoubleClicked` (which starts
editing, `main.esm.mjs:28806`) and `onRowDblClick` → `rowDoubleClicked` (`:31929`) from the **same**
`dblclick`, with no mutual exclusion; `MasterSheet.tsx` binds `onRowDoubleClicked={openRecord}`. Double-click
is the spreadsheet gesture for *edit*, and **95 of 100 columns on this sheet are editable**
(45 text · 23 select · 18 number · 9 long-text). It is a collision between PES.2's sheet and PES.4's drawer
on one gesture, and neither owns the other's half.
**Recommend:** give the drawer its own affordance (identity-cell chevron or the row menu, which already
exists) and return double-click to editing. Alternatives — `singleClickEdit: true`, or firing `openRecord`
only from non-editable cells — both keep two meanings on one gesture.

**2. 🔴 The select/dropdown editor cannot be opened at all.** Ruling #169's item (5), and it is not a
polish problem: on the master sheet these editors **do not work**. 23 columns use `SelectCellEditor`
(`country_of_origin` carries **268** options, `ghs_chemical_h_code` 100).
F2 mounts the editor and focuses the DS `Listbox` trigger, but the list stays closed (`aria-expanded="false"`);
clicking that trigger **destroys the editor**. Traced with focus listeners + a `MutationObserver` on body,
ms timestamps:
```
510010  focusout  BUTTON.nds-listbox-btn → relatedTarget INPUT   (the panel's search box)
510011  focusin   INPUT.
510012  focusout  INPUT. → relatedTarget null
510012  listbox-added   parent: BODY                              ← portals OUTSIDE the grid
510012  cellEditingStopped                                        ← AG tears the editor down
```
The panel portals to `document.body` (correctly) and autofocuses its search input (268 > `SEARCH_THRESHOLD`
7); AG sees focus leave the cell, `stopEditingWhenCellsLoseFocus: true` stops editing, and the editor
unmounts the panel with it — 2ms, no paint. A real pointer click gives the identical outcome, so this does
not rest on the synthetic one. DS.1 verified the primitive half at source: `Listbox.tsx:140` renders
`<input autoFocus>` unconditionally with no opt-out, while `MultiSelect`/`Combobox` have no autofocus at all
(their DS1-9).
Separately, the editor's own auto-open (`trigger.click()` in a mount effect, `SelectCellEditor.tsx:35-40`)
does not survive React StrictMode's double invocation — a toggle called from an effect is not idempotent by
construction. **That half is dev-only and unverified in prod; the focus teardown above is not.**
**Recommend:** replace the Listbox-in-a-cell with AG's **`agRichSelectCellEditor`** (`RichSelectModule` is
present in the licensed package, currently unregistered) themed through the existing token-bound Theming
API. It is built for this: inside AG's focus model, with search, keyboard and a virtualised list — which is
what 268 options need. DS.1's `aria-activedescendant` rework of the primitive fixes it too and helps every
other host; the two are not exclusive and sequencing is mine.

**3. 🔴 Changing a view silently throws away the operator's sort and their pinned columns.**
Measured, one gesture apart:

| after | sort | operator's pin | width |
|---|---|---|---|
| set `name:asc` (header click) + pin `productType` left (header menu) + width 420 | `name:asc@0` | `productType:left` | 420 |
| **switch view Overview → Content** | **gone** | **gone** | kept |
| **Customise → Save** | kept | **gone** | kept |
| **view chip on / off** | **gone** | **gone** | kept |

Cause: `columns/columnPrefs.ts` `prefsToColumnState` emits an explicit `sort: null` **and** `pinned: null`
for every column, and `MasterSheet`'s `applyPreset` / `applyVisibleColumns` build their `PreferencesValue`
with `sortBy: ''` hard-coded. Customise survives only because `openCustomise` happens to capture the live
sort back through `columnStateToPrefs`. Multi-sort works (`name:desc@1` + `productType:asc@0`) but the bridge
can only ever express one sorted column, so Customise collapses a multi-sort to a single one.
**Recommend:** a view decides visibility and order; it should not emit `sort`/`pinned` at all. Carry both
through the bridge, and give the operator a real "Reset columns" (see 8).

**4. Enter never opens an editor — there are only three edit gestures and one of them is compromised.**
`enterNavigatesVertically: true` (+ `…AfterEdit`), so Enter moves down and **never starts an edit** —
confirmed in AG's own source (`main.esm.mjs:29500`) and measured (`Enter` → `productType@3` → `productType@4`,
`editing: 0` throughout). So editing starts only by: **typing** (measured: seeds the editor with the typed
character, destroying the existing value), **F2** (preserves the value, undiscoverable), or **double-click**
(which also opens the drawer, item 1). The footer strip's "Type to edit · F2 · Enter ↓ · Tab →" is accurate;
the problem is that the only non-destructive, non-colliding gesture is the one nobody guesses.

**5. There is no export.** The GDS ships `export/gridCsv.ts` (`toCsv`, `downloadCsv`, `csvFileName`, RFC 4180,
UTF-8 BOM) and `CsvExportModule` is registered — the sheet offers no control at all. Swept the whole page:
zero buttons or links matching `export|download|csv|excel`. The Enterprise pass's finding on /products/next
(export was viewport-only) does not apply here because nothing exports.

**6. `ScrollApiModule` is not registered, so nothing can scroll a cell into view.** `api.ensureColumnVisible`
raises AG #200. No app code calls it today, so this is a blocker rather than a live defect — but the
"Missing required (42)" chip's stated job is to *take the operator to those cells* (it only filters today),
and PES.4's `?cell=` deep link needs the same call. `ScrollApiModule` is present in the licensed package.
Flagged to UX.1, who had specced §5.4 against it; now corrected there.

**7. Pinning an attribute column renders its column-group header twice.** Pinned `productType` left via the
header menu → **"IDENTITY" drew twice**, once over the pinned block and once over the centre. `columns.tsx`
sets `marryChildren: true` on every group and its comment asserts "no group here crosses the boundary" —
true at load, false the moment an operator pins. The same `marryChildren` is why `applyPreset` must pass
`applyOrder: false`, which makes **UX.1's §9.2 column-ordering rule unimplementable**. Removing the 30px
group strip (agreed with UX.1, §2.1a settled at 56px of chrome) fixes both; grouping survives where it earns
its place — the Customise dialog builds its own grouped list from `c.group`.

**8. "Reset columns" was deleted, not never built.** `NexusGrid`'s `getMainMenuItems` strips AG's
`columnChooser` **and** `resetColumns`, then re-adds only what `columnDialog` supplies; `MasterSheet` passes
`{ customise }` alone. So after any rearrangement there is no way back to the default view's columns.

**9. Minor, measured.** A multi-sort whose primary column is hidden leaves an orphan "2" badge on a visible
header with no "1" anywhere. The header menu offers AG's default *Expand/Collapse All Row Groups* on every
attribute column — noise on a 21-row, two-level family tree.

### What works, and should not be re-litigated
Range selection (measured 12 cells across 3 columns × 4 rows), the fill handle (`.ag-fill-handle` present),
Tab / Shift+Tab / arrow navigation, `undoRedoCellEditing` wired at depth 200, header-matched paste
(`sheetPasteProcessor`, with its null-means-leave-alone rule), the per-cell `SheetWriter` path, the one
Customise dialog, and named views (`Save current as new view…` is offered). Column **width** survives every
view change.

### Honest limits of this audit
- **Real key delivery to a backgrounded tab failed silently** — a `keydown` logger recorded **zero** events
  from the extension's key action while clicks kept working. Tab / Shift+Tab / arrows / Enter / type-to-edit
  above were therefore exercised against **AG's own handlers via dispatched `KeyboardEvent`**, not OS-level
  keys, and should be re-confirmed on a foreground tab. An earlier reading of mine ("focus lands on a
  floating filter after F2") was **my own bad click** — the screenshot space is 1.0847× CSS here — and is withdrawn.
- **`stopEditingWhenCellsLoseFocus` cannot be tested at runtime.** Flipping it with `setGridOption` and
  seeing the teardown persist reads as a refutation and is not one: AG marks it `@initial`, so the getter
  updates while the init-time value keeps driving behaviour. The focus trace is the evidence; that
  experiment is discarded.
- **Fill-drag and clipboard paste were not exercised end to end** — both would have written to the prod
  database. Presence is verified; round-trip is not.
- The select editor's **auto-open** failure is measured in dev only (StrictMode); its **focus teardown** is
  independent of StrictMode.
- `flaggedColumnKeys is not defined` from the app's error boundary was a **half-applied HMR bundle** while
  PES.2 edited these files live — the symbol is correctly defined and imported. Not a defect; reload cleared it.

**PES.7 — P6 + P7 COMPLETE (2026-09-01 ~23:58).** Analytics · Ads and Activity, both written fresh
on the DS, types transcribed from live responses.

🔴 **The finding that shaped both:** a **parent row has no figures of its own**. Measured across the
full set of 20 children — parent `byChannel: []` at 30/60/90 days and **0 ads for every identifier
it has** (incl. its own ASIN B0F7J163XJ), while children hold **427 units across 17 of 20** and
**93–107 ads / 70–76 campaigns each**. `totalUnits` is the sum of an empty list, so "0 units · £0
revenue" and "No ads are running against this product" are the opposite of the truth, stated
confidently. Both halves now name where the figures live and say explicitly that this is **not a
measurement of zero**. Aggregating children would be feature invention, so it is not done.

Related: the ad rows reference ASIN **B0BMSH19GY**, which belongs to one CHILD, not the parent — so
the query sends every identifier the product has. (The old AdsTab already did; no bug there.)

Other rules, each tested: **ACOS `null` ≠ 0%** (measured 759¢ spent, 0 sales → reads "No sales", and
sorts as +Infinity so it can't sort as the best row); `daysOfInventory: null` = "Not calculable";
`stockoutRisk: UNKNOWN` never folds into LOW; a £0.00 price stays visible; an all-zero sparkline
draws along the **bottom**. **Activity: only `BULK_OP_APPLIED` carries a delta** (all 157 events
scanned) — so only those 9 rows get an expander, because expanding a flat-file row would open empty
and imply the detail was lost; `null` renders as "cleared"; groups state their own size; no raw enum
reaches the screen.

**Three defects, all mine, caught by guards/hub and fixed:** inline `defaultColDef` ×2
(`check-grid-option-identity` — hoisted to module scope); **`--nds-danger-border` does not exist**
(PES.3's sweep — resolved to transparent, drew no border, silently; swept all three of my
stylesheets, no others); and a 74-row grid at `autoHeight` measuring **3675px** (given a height).
Also `width:auto` inside a flex-column card still stretched to 1584px until `align-self:flex-start`.

**Frame change, disclosed:** removed `StudioTabHost`'s now-callerless local `Placeholder` helper —
all five slots are real components and `noUnusedLocals` failed the build. Comment left saying why.

**Green:** 752 tests (`_studio`), web tsc 0 for my files, **16 guards 0**. No writes. Nothing
committed. Remaining: P8 parity audit + §5 audit.

### PES.1 — v2 §11 items BUILT (rulings #182, #185)

All four of my spec items, verified on screen at 1728×906 on GALE-JACKET master.

| | v1 | v2 | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| AppTopBar | 56 | **0** | gone; `--nds-chrome-top` unset so `.h10-shell` takes the full 906 |
| Product header | 48 | 48 → **32** | collapses on grid scroll |

| Note band | 31 | **0** | removed from the frame (§6.6) |

**Collapse verified end-to-end on a REAL wheel scroll** (a programmatic `scrollTop` + synthetic event
did not fire it — worth knowing): scrollTop 77 → header 32px, collapsed class on, **and the grid grew
583 → 599 (+16), R 92 → 76 (−16)** exactly as the invariant predicts. Scrolling back expands it and
the SKU/ASIN/pills return. Contents animate; **the height snaps** — `GridSheet` re-measures through a
body `ResizeObserver`, so animating 48→32 would re-virtualise AG every frame.

**Arming rule** (`R − C ≥ T`, `R` against EXPANDED geometry) is implemented as specified, with
`collapseIsArmed()` exported pure for test. 🔴 A comment beside it names the **row-height coupling**
(#185): at 28px rows the v2 budget leaves R = 0 and the header never collapses on any family — so
anyone who "optimises" density back to 28px kills this feature, and it presents as a collapse bug.
The next person finds the answer instead of hunting the threshold logic.

**AppTopBar removal is a THIRD AppShell level, not `NO_CHROME_PREFIXES`.** That list is a privacy
boundary for surfaces shown to people with no account, and its own note forbids moving prefixes
between the two. The studio has a session and renders the rail; it just declines one band. New
`NO_TOPBAR_PATTERNS`, and dropping `.nds-chrome-host` with it is what gives the shell the full
viewport rather than 56px less.

**Superseded files removed:** `StudioScopeBar.tsx` and `StudioTabs.tsx`. `STUDIO_TAB_ID_BASE` briefly
existed in two files during the change; `StudioTabHost` now imports the one in `StudioBar`.

**Not done, and why:** §3.5's chip edge-fade and active-chip-scroll-into-view live inside the DS
`ScopeBar`'s internals, and DS.1 now owns DS components — filed rather than forked. Tier B's icon
tabs carry `aria-label` via an `sr-only` label but **no tooltip**: `TabItem` has no `title`, and
adding one is DS.1's call now.

⚠ `check-grid-kit-ratchet` FAILS at 195/193 — **not mine**: PES.7's new `ancillary/ActivityTab.tsx`
and `ancillary/AnalyticsAdsTab.tsx` both contain a counting raw `<table>` (verified with the guard's

#### PES.3-24 — #173 on the channel scope: 15,664px → 1,660px, and a fix that silently did nothing

The default-view rule reached master and never reached this scope. Measured before: 102 columns at the server's own widths =
**15,664px, 11.4 screens** at a 1728px viewport.

🔴 **CORRECTION (2026-09-02): my "after" figure of 1,660px was the WRONG PROPERTY.** I read
`.ag-body-horizontal-scroll-viewport.scrollWidth`, which tracks the scrollable region and here
reports the same value as `clientWidth` — so it looked like "the content fits exactly" when it was
simply the viewport measuring itself. The honest measure is the sum of the rendered column widths:
**1,954px** — identical at innerWidth 1728 (1.13 screens) and at UX.1's 1372px grid area (1.36
screens), so the columns are fixed-width. It did NOT fit one screen, and I had said it did.

🔴 **SECOND CORRECTION (2026-09-02, after #233 landed): 1,954 was over AMAZON's columns.** With the
scope contamination fixed, eBay·IT serves its OWN 35-column set and the default view resolves to
**9 columns totalling 1,404px** — `__identity · brand · name · productType · status · basePrice ·
totalStock` plus the group and actions chrome. That is **0.81 screens at 1728px**, and 1.02 at a
1372px grid area: it fits, marginally, and the honest headline is **15,664px over 102 borrowed
columns → 1,404px over 9 of eBay's own**. Both earlier numbers are retired; this one is measured
with the right property on the right column set.

⚠ **THIRD reading (2026-09-02, after PES.5's every-column-yields-a-cell change, #458): 14 columns,
1,934px, 1.12 screens** at innerWidth 1728. Not a regression — the opposite. #173's rule selects
"every field REQUIRED for this product type" and "anything readiness flagged", and those are facts
about CELLS; with 76 of 97 columns previously carrying no cell, the rule could not see them. Completing
the payload let `fabric_type` and `gpsr_safety_attestation` qualify, which is the rule working on
complete data for the first time. **The 1,404px figure is superseded, and the reason is worth keeping:
a derived view is only as complete as what it derives from — the number moved because the input was
fixed, not because the rule changed.** Columns landed: identity · brand · name · productType · status ·
product_description · item_name · country_of_origin · bullet_point ·
supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation. Identity → spine → required-for-this-product-type → flagged,
exactly PES.2's rule.

**Imported, not forked.** `defaultViewColumns` is channel-agnostic (columns + context in, keys out),
so re-deriving it here would give the two scopes different answers to "what should an operator land
on" — the drift the anti-fork directive exists to stop.

🔴 **The trap, worth passing to any lane applying #173.** My first attempt gated the landing effect
on `apiRef.current` alone. **A ref is invisible to the effect system**, so the effect ran once with a
null api, returned, and never fired again — and the sheet measured **exactly 15,664px**, byte-identical
to having written no rule at all. A fix that silently does nothing measures the same as no fix. Gate
on a `gridReady` state, as master does.

#### PES.3-25 — 🔴 the channel CAS is still unusable: an accepted write bumps the version TWICE

`SheetListing.version` landed and the product CAS was excluded, so the FIRST write is now correct
(v15 + correct version → ok; deliberately stale v1 → 409). Then the rehearsal rule earned itself a
third time.

**An accepted channel write increments the listing version twice** — once by the CAS guard's
`channelListing.update`, once by `writeChannelOverrideMerge`'s own `"version" = "version" + 1` —
while the response reports one:

```
listing v15 → write → response "version": 16 → DB actually 17
listing v17 → write → response "version": 18 → DB actually 19
write 2 using the response's 18 → 409 CONFLICT
```

So **the second consecutive write always fails**. On an autosaving sheet the second cell an operator
edits is the normal case, not an edge: this would have shipped as "the sheet stops saving after your
first change, and blames you for a conflict that never happened".

**The recovery number is wrong too:** the 409's `currentVersion` is the PRODUCT's (the handler still
reads `prisma.product.findUnique`), so my message rendered "Someone else changed this listing (v1)"
while the listing was at 19. A client cannot recover from that even if it tried.

**→ PES.5, two fixes:** bump the listing version ONCE on an accepted write; and return the LISTING's
version as `currentVersion` on a channel conflict.

**RESTORED 2026-09-02 (#201)** once PES.5 fixed both halves. Re-verified by the same method, and the
chaining is the part that matters — three consecutive writes reusing the row the previous one
updated, **no refetch between them**:

```
start listing v22
write 1 → ok, row.listing.version 23
write 2 → ok, row.listing.version 24        ← the write that always 409'd before
write 3 → ok, row.listing.version 25
STALE (v2) → conflict: "Someone else changed this listing (now v25). Reloading."
```

Each write +1, response == DB. Read back in raw SQL: eBay·IT at v25 holding the value, the four
Amazon listings and the product untouched. Cleaned up, verified absent.

**And the client now reads `versionOf` rather than inferring it.** A listing version is written back
onto `row.listing` so the next edit chains, and is deliberately NOT returned as the write result's
`version`, which the sheet writer applies to the PRODUCT row it tracks. Applying one counter's number
to the other row is what made the old message say "v1" about a listing sitting at 19; the refusal now
names which row it is talking about, or says nothing about a version at all.

**Also applied: #182.** `onRowDoubleClicked` is gone entirely — double-click edits, the record opens
only through the explicit `open-record` verb.

#### PES.3-26 — #214: the add-a-coordinate path EXISTS and is two clicks — but the sheet lied about it

**The path is real.** `deriveScopeOptions` builds the scope bar from the **Marketplace table**, not
from the product's listings, so every channel × market that exists is reachable whether or not this
product is listed there. Measured on GALE-JACKET at a coordinate the family has **zero** rows on
(eBay·DE — DB confirms only AMAZON DE/ES/FR/IT and EBAY·IT exist):

- **2 clicks:** channel chip (eBay) → market dropdown (DE · Germany).
- The sheet renders fully: 21 rows, the 12-column default view, `+ Add listing alias` present.
- A cell edit there upserts the listing **born DRAFT + `isPublished: false`** (§14, verified in the
  endpoint). No wizard needed, and nothing publishable is produced by typing.

So the list wizard's replacement exists. **But it was not honest about what it was offering.**

🔴 **My bug, and it is the one that matters for this ruling.** The band rendered **"DRAFT"** on a
coordinate with no listing, because `AliasBandCell` did `alias?.listingStatus ?? 'DRAFT'`. The server
is explicit — `listing: null`, `listingStatus: null`, `isPublished: null`,
**`readiness.state: 'unlisted'`** — so the contract said "nothing here" and the UI said "a draft
listing". An operator could not tell *"this listing exists and is unpublished"* from *"there is no
listing here at all"*, and the second is the one where typing **creates** something. For the surface
replacing a "List on eBay · DE" wizard, that is the single thing it must not hide.

Fixed: the pill reads **NOT LISTED** with a neutral tone — the absence of a listing is not a listing
state, and must never wear the tone of a live one. The default `?? 'DRAFT'` is gone.

**Nothing for PES.5 here** — the contract already carried every field needed (`listing: null`,
`listingStatus: null`, `state: 'unlisted'`). This was a client defaulting over an honest answer,
which is the cheaper failure to make and the harder one to notice.

⚠ Still open on this path: `Preflight ★ (20)` and `Warnings (42)` render on a coordinate with no
listing — a preflight describing a listing that does not exist. Not fixed here; flagged.

#### PES.3-29 — 🔴 #233's fix removed the create path: every unlisted coordinate now refuses

**Supersedes PES.3-26.** I reported the two-click add-a-coordinate path as proven at 00:45. After the
01:08 restart it is gone, and D9's wizard removal depends on it.

**Measured now:** every eBay market except IT returns `scope_not_available`; every Amazon market the
family is not already listed on (BE, IE, NL, PL, SE, UK, TR) does the same. **The studio can only
reach coordinates the product is already on** — so "create a listing here" is unreachable, and the
scope bar still offers markets the sheet then refuses (`deriveScopeOptions` reads the Marketplace
table; the server reads listing presence).

**Mechanism, proven by calling the service rather than reading it.** `coordinatesFor`
(`sheet-columns.service.ts:393-395`) has two distinct options: `only` **narrows**, `channels`
**forces past the `present` filter**, where `present` is the set of channel:market pairs the product
already has listings on. `#233`'s fix passes `onlyChannels: [wantChannel]` — narrowing only — so an
unlisted pair is dropped by `present` and the sheet throws:

```
onlyChannels: ['EBAY'], market DE            → coordinates = []        (throws)
onlyChannels: ['EBAY'] + includeEmptyChannels → coordinates = ['EBAY']  (35 columns)
```

**→ PES.5: one flag on the studio-sheet call site** (`includeEmptyChannels: true`, or
`channels: [wantChannel]` alongside `onlyChannels`). Both already exist. Worth a regression test that
an unlisted coordinate still serves, because #233's fix and the create path pull in opposite
directions on the same call.

Incidentally confirms #233 landed correctly: eBay·DE returns **35** columns with the flag, not
Amazon's 102.

**Consequence for my own work:** PES.3-26's two clicks no longer hold, and **PES.3-30's §6.4 work is
currently dead code** — no coordinate returns `readiness.state: 'unlisted'` any more, so the
"Not listed" line, the removed counts and "Check before listing" cannot fire. All three are written
and unit-clean; none can be verified on screen until the flag lands.

#### PES.3-30 — §6.4 built, and the count deliberately left out

On `readiness.state === 'unlisted'`: the chip row is replaced by one line from
`readinessMeta('unlisted', 'row')` — **"Not listed"** plus its own hint — `Warnings (N)` and the
readiness figure are gone, and the preflight **survives as an action without a count**
("Check before listing"), because validating the payload that would be sent is the only safety check
before a create.

🔴 **The ruled label was "Not listed · N fields required to list" and I have shipped it WITHOUT the
N**, because the ruling told me to establish what my count is first and the answer is that no honest
N exists yet. Measured on eBay·DE:

- `warnings: 42` = **21 rows × the same 2 fields** (`dsa_responsible_party_address`,
  `gpsr_safety_attestation`), every one severity `warn` — a row×field product, not a field count.
- `errors: 0` and **`rowsMissingRequired: 0`** — nothing is missing that anything requires.

#### PES.3-31 — the wire-null guard, and the bug it found in my own mirror on the way

`scripts/check-wire-null-defaults.mjs` (#237). Type-checked, scoped to the studio, ratcheted at
**baseline 20**, `--check` exits 1 on a rise. Proven both ways: a fixture carrying
`alias.listingStatus ?? 'DRAFT'` takes it to 21 and `--check` to exit 1; removing it returns 20 / 0.

**Two dead ends first, both worth recording so nobody repeats them.** Name-based matching cannot
express this class: repo-wide it found **88,914** sites, and narrowed to studio contracts plus render
paths still **500** — of which a hand-checked sample was ~0% true positives (`presets.find()?.label`,
`c.width ?? 100`, `e?.message`). `label`, `width`, `status` and `message` are universal names; only
the checker can say that THIS `listingStatus` is `SheetListing.listingStatus`.

🔴 **And the checker silently defeated it.** With my ad-hoc compiler options the guard reported **0**
and looked finished. It resolved the declaration at exactly the right line — source text
`listingStatus: string | null` — and returned the type as **`string`**, because I had not passed
`strict`, and without `strictNullChecks` TypeScript **erases `null` from a union**. The guard against
"a default collapsed an absence into a value" was itself beaten by a tool collapsing an absence into
a value. Only the acceptance test caught it: a green that cannot fail is not a green.

**A real bug found on the way.** The fixture ALSO failed to trip the guard at first, and the reason
was mine: `AliasGroup.listingStatus` was declared `string` and `isPublished` `boolean`, while the
server sends **both as `null`** on an unlisted coordinate (measured on eBay·DE). So `?? 'DRAFT'`
type-checked as unreachable defensive code when it was the live path, and no type-driven guard could
ever have seen it — the type said it could not happen. Both are now nullable.
`reference_wire_parse_boundary_rules` in the other direction: never TIGHTEN a mirror past what the
wire sends.

**🔴 What it cannot do, stated so the number is not over-read: it finds the SHAPE, not the sin.**
`listing?.quantity ?? '—'` and `readOnlyReason ?? 'No listing on this coordinate.'` are the same
shape as `?? 'DRAFT'` and are **correct** — they name the absence. `totalAvailable ?? 0` is the same
shape again and renders "0 in stock" for "we do not know". Only a human separates them, so this
ratchets rather than blocks, and it is **not wired into pre-push**.

**→ PES.7, two of the 20 look like the real class** and are theirs:
`ancillary/AnalyticsAdsTab.tsx:277` `inventory?.totalAvailable ?? 0` and `:241`
`analytics?.sales.stockoutDays ?? 0` — an unknown availability rendered as zero stock is the
`clampPct` defect with a different noun.

## PES.6 — ruling #258 fixed, and the worse bug it uncovered, `nexus-commerce-33`

**As reported (BE.1 was right):** `exprDependencies` returned `{attributes:[],rules:[]}` on a parse
failure — indistinguishable from a formula that genuinely depends on nothing (`"New"`, `1 + 1`).
It now returns **null**, matching what `evaluateExpr` already did with its `error`.
`channel-mapping.routes.ts:134` passes the null through instead of faking an empty list; **:393**
(the expressions listing, previously unguarded) now returns `dependencies: null` **plus a
`parseError {message, pos}`**, and `BusinessRulesDrawer` prints *"This rule no longer parses — …
N fields using it resolve to nothing."* Test added covering both directions.

🔴 **Chasing it exposed something worse, and mine.** Proving the fix returned **no expressions at
all**. Cause: I had added expression-body syntax checking to `validateMapping`, and `parseMapping`
**discards the WHOLE mapping** when validation returns anything. So a single malformed formula
silently zeroed an entire marketplace — every field on AMAZON·IT would have read as `unmapped`,
its 13 rules invisible, with no error anywhere. Only reachable by a write that bypasses the
validating route (a rule authored before the check existed, or edited straight in the DB) — but
silent and total when reached, and I introduced the trigger on 2026-09-01.

Fix: `validateMapping(input, { checkExpressions })` — **true on the WRITE path** (a formula that
cannot parse is still refused before it can reach publish), **false in `parseMapping`**. A broken
body now degrades to "that formula is broken", never to "this marketplace has no mapping". Two
regression tests pin both halves.

Verified by planting a broken and a dependency-free rule side by side in AMAZON·IT's real
`schemaMapping`, reading them back through the route, and restoring the original exactly
(expressions before 0 → after 0). Gates: **51 files / 552 tests pass**, api + web typecheck clean
in my paths.

**PES.7 — #259 + A4 done, verified on screen (2026-09-02).** Details in inventory §32/§32.1.

`ready`, Available rendered `0` *and* Cover, Stockout risk, Quality and Reviews rendered **empty
`<dd>`s** — optional chaining made all six typecheck while producing a blank or a lie, and
`analytics?.quality.latestScore === null` is `false` when `analytics` itself is null. Fixed at the
row, not the line: the whole card row is gated, with `readAvailable()` keeping a **measured** 0
(out of stock is a fact) and refusing an **absent** one. **A4** (`stockoutDays ?? 0`) was the fifth
figure — the only one still read off the raw payload — and now travels in the reading with its
siblings. **A6 withdrawn by FE.1 as unreachable; confirmed and left alone.**

**Verified on screen, both paths:** real payload → Available 13, Stockout days **0** (a measured
zero, correctly shown), 0 empty `<dd>`s. Intercepted `{}` → no "Available 0", 0 empty `<dd>`s, and
*"The server returned no figures for this product… That is an absence of data, not a reading of

whole type unaided.

**P2-4 — centralised, union left open.** Closing it would lose the degrade-don't-drop property, so
`isPublished()` in `types.ts` is the single comparison; all three sites use it, and no raw
`=== 'PUBLISHED'` remains outside the definition.

**A third cast, found while removing those two:** `CrossChannelPlanner` typed the whole
publish-readiness response as a single `PublishReadiness` — that type is ONE channel's gate — and
cast it to a record to index it. `usePublishGate` had a separate private envelope that was correct:

`PublishReadinessByChannel`, indexed by known key, no cast; an unknown channel returns `null`
("not reported on"), deliberately distinct from a closed gate. Verified on screen — the planner
still reads "Every gate is closed on this deployment" and "Rehearse 2 targets".

#### PES.3-32 — long text edits in a box on the channel sheet too (#293)

SR.1 measured `item_name` (127 chars) on the same row and build: master opened a popup `textarea` at

showing the last ~23. The surface whose whole purpose is tuning a market's copy had the worse editor

sheet's own `editable` callback. Landing last it would have overridden the per-cell server answer and
made a `writable: false` alias row editable — trading a cosmetic defect for a correctness one.

**Verified on screen, same row and field as SR.1** (`GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-M`, `item_name`,
Amazon·IT): **`TEXTAREA`, popup, 460×126, all 127 characters, `maxlength=200`** — matching master
exactly. The 200 is Amazon's own declared cap (`item_name: maxLength 200`), not an invention;
`product_description` declares none and correctly gets no attribute.

#### PES.3-33 — `gateNote`'s shared default made "unknown" indistinguishable from "live" (#319)

FE.1 is right, and the fault is one my own file argues against two functions higher up.
`gateNote` warned for `gated` / `dry-run` / `sandbox` and returned `null` for everything else — so
`live` (silence correct: publishing is real) and an unrecognised mode (silence dangerous: the console
cannot vouch for what a retry would do) came out of the same branch. `modeForChannel` already refuses
to guess `'live'` for a channel the server did not describe; falling through to silence here undid
that reasoning one step later.

Now: `case 'live': return null` explicitly, and a default that WARNS — with two distinct sentences,
because collapsing them would repeat the very mistake being fixed:
- an unrecognised mode names it — *"reports an unrecognised publish mode (canary) … treat the queue
  below as unexplained until someone checks the gate"*;
- an undescribed channel says that instead — *"not described by this server response, so nothing here
  can say whether a retry would reach the channel"*.

**P4-3 — one shared `PublishMode`.** Mine was closed with four members (a new server mode would not
type-check); PES.7's `publishPlan.ts:23` was open with three and no `sandbox` (so `sandbox` fell to a
default that said nothing). Each type's weakness was masked by the other file's behaviour. Now
`'gated' | 'dry-run' | 'sandbox' | 'live' | (string & {})`. **Order was load-bearing (P2-4):** the
default had to warn *before* the union opened, or opening it would have created the silent-unknown
hole rather than closing it.

🔴 **And opening `null`'s meaning created a new one I had to close.** `gateNote(null, …)` now warns,
but the console's `readiness` state starts `null` while the request is in flight — so every operator
would have seen "we cannot vouch" flash on every load. **"Not yet asked" is not "asked and not
answered", and one `null` cannot carry both**: added `readinessSettled`, and the note is computed
only once the request has resolved either way. Verified on screen by sampling the DOM 20 times
across the load — zero frames carried the warning, and eBay·IT's real banner is unchanged.

### §6.3 chip triangle — LANDED, and the block was already lifted

Gated on `viewChipIsAlarm(chip)`; **4/4 mutations killed**. `MasterSheet.tsx` / `viewChips.ts` /

**The blocking condition was already met and nobody had noticed.** My own comment said two lanes
wanted this to travel with §6.3's move of the warning component, so the glyph would become a
property of the chip's **KIND** rather than of whichever component draws the bar. But

`missing-required` is `warning`, the channel's three are `danger`/`warning`/`danger`, and
`ai-drafts` deliberately sets none. The kind was always there; the renderer was ignoring it. So this
is the fix, not a third interim state, and it needed nothing from DS.1.

A warning glyph on a non-warning is a **false positive**, which costs more than a missing one: it
teaches operators the alarm means nothing, and then the real alarms mean nothing either. `:904`'s
triangle on the caps Pill is a real warning and stays.

### 🔴 A mutation run that reports ALL-PASS is an instrument check, not a verdict on the tests

My first pass on `viewChipIsAlarm` reported **4/4 passing** — i.e. nothing killed — and the obvious
reading is "these tests are worthless, go strengthen them". They were fine. `sed`'s `|` delimiter
collided with the `||` in the predicate; every run printed `sed: bad flag in substitute command`
**directly above** the passing line, and **all four mutations measured the unmutated file**.

All-pass has exactly two explanations — weak tests, or a mutation that never landed — and the
summary line is identical for both. **Check the instrument first; never go edit the tests.** And do
not drive mutations with `sed` when the target contains `|`, `&` or `/`: use a python `replace` with
`assert old in s`, which gives the anchor check as well.

#### PES.3-34 — Compare fed on the channel sheet (#325), and the two defects that surfaced

`compareTargets={[]}` was hardcoded, so the pane was permanently idle on every channel scope. Now
built from the frame's marketplace options: **master · this coordinate · the same channel's other
markets · the same market's other channels**, deduped. Bounded on purpose — a full cross product is
~19 entries, most of them a channel AND a market away from the one on screen, which is the same
"a list nobody reads" the default-view rule exists to avoid.

Verified on screen (Amazon·IT): the pane went from idle to listing Master + Amazon IT/BE/DE/ES/FR/IE/
NL/PL/SE. **Two defects it immediately exposed, neither in the target list itself:**

🔴 **1 — "this record" was on the wrong entry.** `RecordDrawer.tsx:511` picks the marker with
`compareTargets.find((t) => t.kind === scope.kind)` — by KIND, not by coordinate. Harmless while
master had one `master` target and channel scopes had none; the moment the list carries several
`channel` targets it labels whichever sorts first. Measured: on **Amazon·IT it marked Amazon·BE**.
Worked around by including the current coordinate FIRST, which makes the marker correct; **matching
by coordinate rather than kind is the real fix and is PES.4's line.**

🔴 **2 — every target read "No listing on this coordinate", including the record's own.** One word:
`useCompare.ts:55` sends **`marketplace=`**, and the route reads **`market=`** and 400s without it
(`product-studio.routes.ts:116`). Proven by curl on the same coordinate:

```
?scope=channel&channel=AMAZON&marketplace=IT  → HTTP 400   ← what readScope sends
?scope=channel&channel=AMAZON&market=IT       → HTTP 200
?scope=master                                 → HTTP 400   ← master target, no market at all
```

So **every** compare read has always failed, and `readScope` turns 400 into `null`, which the pane
renders as the legitimate-sounding "no listing on this coordinate". A wrong parameter name wearing
the costume of a real answer — the pane could not have looked more working while being entirely
blind. It was invisible until now only because no host had ever passed it a target. → PES.4.

#### PES.3-36 — #327 measured under the freeze (no code touched), and item 12 is bigger than it looks

Read-only work while #342's freeze holds. Findings, so the fixes are decided before the tree reopens.

🔴 **(12) is not "two counts that read as one" — every number in my summary line is a SAMPLE
presented as a TOTAL.** `sync-queue.service.ts:128` caps rows at `limit ?? 50` (max 200) while
`counts` is the true figure. Measured on the exact coordinate SR.1 used:

```
AMAZON·IT   counts.dead = 269   rows returned = 50   distinct products in page = 18
AMAZON·DE   counts.dead =  21   rows returned = 21   (whole set — no cap hit)
```

So the pane's **"50 queued writes across 1 cause · 18 products"** is 50 of 269, 18 products among a
50-row sample, and "1 cause" is one cause *in that sample* — there may be others in the unseen 219.
Beside a chip reading `Dead (269)` it looks like a breakdown of the same number. It is my own
repeatedly-filed mistake, in my own file: **a set claim measured over a subset**
(`reference_claims_must_match_their_measurement`).

Planned fix: headline from `page.counts[filter]`, never from `rows.length`; group counts stated as
within the sample whenever `rows.length < counts[filter]`; and drop the distinct-product figure or
scope it explicitly, because a product count over a sample cannot be made honest by wording alone.

**(12b) the date.** `causeSince` renders `toLocaleDateString('en-GB')` → `09/06/2026`, which an
American reader takes as 6 September. Write the month: `9 Jun 2026`.

**(17) both offer verbs on an ACTIVE row is CORRECT registry behaviour, and the ruling still wants
it changed.** Measured: all 21 Amazon·IT rows have `listing.offerActive: true`, so `pauseOffer` is
enabled and `activateOffer` is **disabled with "Already active on …"** — #114's rule that a disabled
verb teaches. The ruling asks for one label following state, which loses that sentence unless the
mixed case carries it. Planned: one `offer-toggle` whose label follows state (all active → "Pause
offer on X"; all paused → "Activate offer on X"), **disabled with a count when the selection is
mixed** ("3 active, 2 paused — pause or activate them separately"), which says more than the pair
did, and disabled on a row with no listing, because pausing an offer that does not exist is not an
action.

**(10) and (11)** are render-side and small: never show a truncated or colon-ended sentence from the
preflight (guard the render, PES.5 fixes the message itself), and bring `Not listed` next to the
`1 listing · 20 SKUs` line rather than ~200px away.

#### PES.3-37 — #327 built; the server rollup (#357) replaced my honest-wording stopgap

**Item 12 — every number now comes from the server, not the page.** `summarise` takes
`page.causes[]` + `page.causesTotal`; the distinct-product figure is **gone** rather than qualified
(a count over a sample cannot be rescued by wording); the row list, still capped at 200, says so once
beneath the summary instead of per group. Verified on screen both ways:

```
AMAZON·IT (capped)   "269 dead writes across 1 cause · none need you"
                     "Showing the 200 most recent of 269 — the cause totals above cover all of them."
                     chip: Dead (269)          ← agrees, where it used to read 50
AMAZON·IT (uncapped) "171 queued writes across 1 cause"   no page note, correctly
```

**Why the rollup mattered more than my wording.** I had planned "grouped into N causes" over the
page. PES.5's `causes[]` is authoritative: measured on `normal-knee-slider-yellow`, 1,239 rows and
**3** causes — `unknown` 1,167 · `throttled` 52 (37 actionable) · `rejected` 20 — where the 200-row
page holds **2**, one cause sorted entirely below the boundary. My honest wording would have said
"grouped into 2 causes" and been true about the page while leaving an operator to conclude "only
rejections here". Incomplete is survivable; **misleading-while-accurate is not**, and only a
server-side group-by could close it.

⚠ Contract note: the rollup groups by **`reason`** (the classifier's five values), not by this
file's normalised message. The keys are `reason` / `count` / `actionableCount` / `mostRecent` /
`sampleSummary` — `reason`, not `cause`, as #357's summary had it. Both axes are kept and they are
not interchangeable: the server says how many KINDS of problem exist, the client which distinct
failures are visible in the page.

**Item 12b** — `9 Jun 2026`, never `09/06/2026`. **Item 10** — `tidyServerMessage` drops dangling
`:`/`,`/`—` and closes the sentence, so `…This platform has: ` can never render. **Item 11** — the
state joins the count line (`Not listed · 1 listing · 20 SKUs on …`) instead of sitting 200px away.

**Item 17 — one `offer-toggle`.** Its label follows the SHEET's state, and 🔴 that is a registry
limit, not a choice: `GridAction.label` is a fixed `string` and `available()` returns an
availability, so no verb can word itself from the rows an operator ticked. A selection-following
label needs `label: string | ((rows) => string)` in `registry.ts` → **PES.2**. What the collapse
does buy is the sentence the PAIR could never say: a mixed selection is now refused with
*"3 active and 2 paused in this selection — pause or activate them separately"*, where before each
half went available because "not all rows agree" fell through to enabled. A row with no listing is
refused too — pausing an offer that does not exist would create a DRAFT row as a side effect.

🔴 **Fourth JSX-in-a-test trap tonight:** `tidyServerMessage` started in `AliasPublishControl.tsx`
and made the whole suite unparseable. Pure logic goes in a `.ts` file from the start.

#### PES.3-38 — 🔴 `mappedShared` is unreachable: the substrate reads a field the wire never sends

#365 asked me to widen my provenance allowed-set and assert the invariant rather than widen it bare.
Both readings a minute apart were **green** (12/12 at 03:13:39 and 03:14:57) — PES.2's §9.6 landing
had completed. But green was luck: my set omitted `mapped`/`mappedShared` and passed only because
**no cell on eBay·IT is resolver-derived**. Widened, with the iff, so a leak where `own` or
`inherited` was meant still fails.

Asserting the invariant is what exposed the real defect. `classifyProvenance` decides `mappedShared`
from a **per-cell** `cell.mappedProductLevel` (`provenance.ts:100` declares it, `:146` reads it), and
the server sends no such field. Measured on Amazon·IT:

```
cells with non-null `mapped`      15 of 21     ← the resolver did derive them
cells carrying mappedProductLevel  0 of 21     ← the field is absent entirely
meta.mapping.productLevelOnly      true        ← the fact it is meant to carry
```

So **every cell that should read `mappedShared` reads `mapped`, right now, on live data.** Not dead
code — a wrong classification. And it is precisely the case the rule exists for: §9.6b says
`mappedShared` outranks `mapped` *because editing one row changes N*, and `productLevelOnly: true`
IS "editing one row changes N". The substrate's own comment (`:98`) names the right source —
`meta.mapping.productLevelOnly`, "a fact about the RUN, not about the cell" — and then reads a cell
field instead.

**RESOLVED on my side (#379).** The hub ruled the boundary the other way and was right: the fact is
run-level, the wire already sends it as `meta.mapping.productLevelOnly`, and `mappedProductLevel` is
already part of the substrate's `ProvenanceLike` input — so the CONSUMER bridges the two and no
contract changes. `withMappingRun(cell, productLevelOnly)` attaches it at both call sites
(`ChannelSheet.tsx` class rules and `CascadeCell.tsx`), and returns the cell **untouched** when the
run was not product-grain, so the hot path allocates nothing.

**Counted, not spot-checked — Amazon·IT, all 441 cells:**

```
flag withheld:  mapped 63 · mappedShared  0
flag supplied:  mapped  0 · mappedShared 63     (own 138, inherited 239, pinned 1 unchanged)
```

⚠ **Reconciling the 63 with the "15 of 21" in the ruling, because the difference is the corrected
invariant in action:** 315 of 441 cells carry a `mapped` OBJECT, but only **63** have
`status === 'mapped'` — the other **252 are `'unmapped'`**, meaning the engine ran and matched
nothing. On the row the hub sampled: 15 cells with an object, **3** actually mapped. Had the
invariant been "non-null" as #365 first worded it, this fix would have moved 315 cells into
`mappedShared` and claimed a derivation for 252 that were never derived. I have **not** asserted the
`mappedShared` branch in my test — asserting a branch that cannot fire would encode the defect as
expected behaviour. The line goes in when a host can supply the flag.

**Method note:** the test was green, twice, a minute apart, on a substrate change that had landed —
and it was still wrong. The membership check alone could not see it; only pairing it with the iff
turned "the set contains this value" into "this value means what it says".

**Correction to #365's wording, which I had already avoided by reading the source.** The invariant is
`cell.mapped?.status === 'mapped'`, **not** "the `mapped` object is non-null": `MappedCell.status` is
`'mapped' | 'unmapped'`, and `'unmapped'` means the engine RAN and matched nothing — not a derived
value, and it must not wear the mark. A non-null test would go green against a build leaking the mark
onto every unmapped cell, which is the leak this guard exists for. My assertion reads
`c.mapped?.status === 'mapped'` because I opened `provenance.ts:145` rather than working from the
ruling's paraphrase.

⚠ **This entry is the record of record for the `mappedShared` finding.** A cross-session message
carrying it was dropped at the hub's inbox and not delivered; it is not re-sent here to avoid a
retry loop, and PES.2 needs the substrate change (`classifyProvenance(cell, scope,
{ productLevelOnly })`) regardless of whether that message ever arrived. Their §9.6 sign-off of
"tsc 0, 2346 tests" passes **with the branch unreachable**.

### §9.6 — the derived-value marks (#351/#355)

`CellProvenance` widened from six members to eight (`mapped`, `mappedShared`); `ProvenanceLike` gains
two optional fields; one tooltip wording; two **distinct glyphs** (Σ and Share2 — not a tint of one,
because the two differ in what happens when you edit). 14 tests, **5/5 mutations killed**.

🔴 **The compiler found a modelling error I would have shipped.** I first wrote `mapped?: boolean`,
and it refused against the real contract, where `StudioCellValue.mapped` is `MappedCell | null`. The
collision forced the right question and the answer changed the behaviour: **`status: 'unmapped'`
means the engine RAN and matched nothing** — not a derived value, and it must not wear the mark.
The classifier now requires `status === 'mapped'`. The hub's #365 was about to have PES.3 encode
*"mapped iff the object is non-null"* as a test, which would have locked the leak in; they were
told before writing it.

`sheet/master/types.ts` narrowed `mapped?: unknown` → `{ status?: string } | null`: `unknown` cannot
be read without a cast, and a local mirror of a server type must **add** fields, never relax them.

### #362 — both halves, and the measurement that separates them

Chip tone `warning` → `neutral` at **two** sites, not the one the ruling named — the counted branch
*and* the `count: null` pending branch, which would have worn the alarm for the whole load.

§9.3b: `name`/`status` moved after the required block. **§9.1 measured 5/7 → 7/7 at 1728 and

`country_of_origin`. §9.3a's three columns at 110 instead of 160 saves 150 → **1,299**, the ruling's

**Three of my own tests went red and I moved the TESTS, not the code** — they asserted "identity
still leads", which is what §9.3b deliberately reverses. The good instance of the shape that has bitten
this programme repeatedly: sound tests asking the previous question. Each assertion was replaced with
the rule *and* its rationale, so the next reader sees why `name` is not identity on a family sheet.

**`name`'s width: measured 380, now 220** (`SPEC_WIDTHS`, an allow-list of exactly one key). Nothing
server-side sets a width, so there was nowhere else to fix it. A test asserts the **110s are NOT in

should be told so the map can shrink to nothing.

### #363 — the callable `label`

`label: string | ((rows: T[]) => string)` + `actionLabel()`. 7 tests, 3/3 mutations killed.

🔴 **My grep found 2 consumers; the type change found 6.** Widening the union turned "find every
render site" from a search into a compile error — the argument for a union over a parallel
`labelFor?` field. And `renderers/overlays.tsx:62` reads `action.label` and must **not** change: a
different `action` (an overlay button), where a blanket replace would have "fixed" it into a call on
a string.

It takes the **rows**, not a count — only the verb knows whether "Pause 3 offers" or "Pause 2 of 3"
is honest for a mixed selection — and hands over a **copy**, so a label cannot mutate the selection
it describes.

#### PES.3-39 — the offer verb now words itself from the selection (#363/#371)

The limit I filed at PES.3-37 is lifted: `GridAction.label` accepts `string | ((rows) => string)` and
`actionLabel(action, rows)` resolves it. The verb's wording now follows what is **ticked**, not the
sheet's overall state, and `deps.offerState` — the approximation that existed only because a label
could not move — is deleted.

One `plan(rows)` decides what the verb would do, and the label, the availability, the confirmation
and the run all read it, so none of them can describe a different action from the one on the menu
item. Wording:

```
3 active            → "Pause 3 offers on eBay · IT"
2 paused            → "Activate 2 offers on eBay · IT"
2 paused + 1 active → "Activate 2 of 3 offers on eBay · IT"    ← the sentence a fixed string cannot say
no listing          → "Pause offer on eBay · IT"
```

🔴 **The mixed case needed a judgement, and my first answer was the wrong one.** `plan` originally
activated only when every row was paused, so 2-paused-plus-1-active produced **"Pause 1 of 3"** —
strictly true (the two paused rows are no-ops) and almost certainly not the intent. The tie-break is
**whichever action changes more rows**, which is also what makes the even-split refusal coherent: an
even split is precisely where "changes more" has no answer, and that is the only case still refused.
A mixed selection is otherwise NAMED rather than blocked, because the label can now say exactly which
rows it touches — the refusal was standing in for wording that did not exist yet.

Six tests cover it, including that the label and the availability agree on the same rows.
