## PES.2 — the cap merge, the toolbar band, §9.1 closed at 7/7, and D2's cause

**Repo tsc 0 · 2431 tests / 178 files · all gates green.** Nothing committed.

### #373/#380/#382 — length caps: my diagnosis was right and my first cure was wrong

`maxBytes` was a unit FLAG and never the cap, so `product_description` (`maxLength: null,
maxBytes: 20000`) counted bytes against `null`, took the uncapped early return and **never warned**,
while its header tooltip promised "Max 20000 bytes". *The column whose limit was stated loudest was
the one with no validation behind it.*

🔴 **Then I fixed it wrongly, quietly.** "A declared byte cap IS the cap" — pick a unit, count in
it. **Neither cap always binds.** PES.5 measured all 91 cached schemas: `maxLength` and
`maxUtf8ByteLength` are **independent** Amazon properties (1,061 fields declare both, 14 distinct
ratios). `style`/`pattern` is 2200 characters / 2000 bytes, so **2001 characters of pure ASCII**
breaks the byte cap while sitting inside the character cap — multibyte has nothing to do with it.
Any rule that picks a unit up front is wrong for some column.

**And I had already seen it.** I flagged the dual-cap gap in my own report and filed it as *a
question for PES.5* rather than as a defect. **A constraint the wire declares and the client ignores
is not a question.** That framing is the error worth keeping, not the arithmetic.

`evaluateLengthCaps` now evaluates every declared cap in its own unit and the worst binds, ranked by
`n / cap` — the only comparison meaningful across two units. Ranking by ratio and "worst verdict,
then ratio" are the **same ordering** (both `over` and `near` are ratio thresholds), so there is one
comparison and nothing to drift. **19 tests, 6/6 mutations killed — two of them reproduce my own two
wrong versions.** PES.5's four fixtures are in the suite.

### #388/#390 — the toolbar token was decorative

`--nds-toolbar-h` was applied as `min-height`, so the bar sized to its tallest child: **41 on
GALE-JACKET, 47 on GLOVES**, same build, same viewport. The tall child was the `⚠ caps` Pill, which
renders only for a family whose product types have a stale or missing schema — **the chrome's height
was a function of the catalogue**, which no single-product measurement can catch.

The 34px was **emergent, not declared**: `.nds-pill` is `inline-block` with an inline `<svg>`, so the
icon sits on the baseline and drags the descender space with it. Scoped the pill to the toolbar's
slot height rather than patching `primitives.css` — `.nds-pill` is oversized wherever it carries an
icon, which is a DS-wide question and not this band's to decide.

**After: toolbar 40 and rows 675 on BOTH products.** UX.1's ±1 tolerances on both bands can go —
they existed only because of this defect, and I would rather the fix not hide behind them.

### §9.1 — 7 of 7 at 1440, the prediction exact

Identity 389 + the required block 910 = **1,299 of 1,372 — 73px spare**, which is #371's predicted
number to the pixel. Widths read from `/studio/columns`, not from a client map: `item_name`,
`bullet_point`, `product_description` at **110**, `name` at **220**. `SPEC_WIDTHS` is deleted, and
the both-scope 220 was confirmed **from the contract** rather than from the map being gone.

One number needs its context: the full set totals **1629**, 257px past the viewport. That is `name`
+ `status` beyond the fold **by design** (§9.3b). The two numbers describe different sets.

### D2 (#356) — the sheet never resized

Measured before hunting anything: with the dock closed and open, `viewport 1660 → 1660`,
`root 1660 → 1660`, `sheet 1662 → 1662`, `cells 294 → 294`, `columns 28 → 28`, slide-over present.
**Nothing changes.** §5.1 holds, so the 189-cell repaint was never a response to a resize.

Two props were: `onCellKeyDown` and `getContextMenuItems`, both carrying `record` — a context value
whose identity changes on every dock open and close. Both are **invoked on demand**, so neither has
reason to re-identify; both now read the latest through a ref.

🔴 **My own banked note nearly ended the investigation.** "A new `getContextMenuItems` identity fires
0 column-model events" is true and measured with a positive control — and I had it filed as
"memoise for tidiness, not correctness". **A column-model rebuild and a React repaint are different
costs, and measuring the absence of one says nothing about the other.** A banked negative result is
scoped to the mechanism it measured.

**Not verified: that the repaint is gone** — that needs FE.1's profiler. Verified instead that the
fix changes no behaviour: Enter still opens the dock, geometry unchanged, and the right-click menu
still builds from the registry (which re-confirms #327's allowlist: no `export`).

## PES.2 — #404 (measured, not guessed), §14.1's shared toolbar, #397's fifth cap, #400's correction

**Repo tsc 0 · 2431 tests / 178 files · all gates green.** Nothing committed.

### 🔴 #404 — the repaint was a DEFAULT PARAMETER, and I was wrong twice first

`MasterSheet.tsx` read `export function MasterSheet({ …, variationAxes = [] })`. **A default parameter
is evaluated on every call**, so the component took a brand-new array on **every render** — the prop
is never passed — which fed `viewCtx` → `columnDefs` → AG re-rendering every mounted cell.

So `columnDefs` re-identified **from stable parts on every render**, not on dock open; dock open was
merely a render someone was watching. That is exactly FE.1's reading: a new array whose `[0]` is the
same object, length unchanged.

**The method matters more than the bug.**
1. I **reasoned from the dependency list** that `columnDefs` was stable on dock open. It was not —
   the same reasoning-as-measurement move I had apologised for on the pill an hour earlier.
2. I fixed two props that genuinely re-identify (`onCellKeyDown`, `getContextMenuItems`). Both fixes
   are correct and stay. **Neither was the cause.**
3. Only an in-page probe found it: bisect the memo's five deps → `viewCtx`; drill one level →
   `variationAxes`. Not `lockedColumns`, not FE.1's named `openRecordId`.

Confirmed after: `OPEN → changed: none`, `CLOSE → (no render)`.

**Excluded from the finding:** my probe also flagged `flagged` as changed — that is
`flaggedColumnKeys(…)` returning a fresh array per call, i.e. the probe measuring itself. Swept for
the same trap: no other component in `_studio/**` or `design-system/grid/**` defaults a prop to a
fresh literal.

**Probe removed by anchored replacement, not by restoring my pre-probe backup** — AG.1's collision
tonight was precisely that shape, and a whole-file restore would have discarded their work silently.

### §14.1 — one toolbar, and `absent` is the load-bearing part

The divergence was structural: the channel scope hand-rolled `<div class="nds-grid-prefsbar">` and
**never mounted `GridToolbar` at all**, which is how it lost search, Overview ▾, Customise, Export
and Reload without anyone deciding to remove them.

`_studio/sheet/SheetToolbar.tsx` now owns the standard controls — they are not props, so a scope
cannot drop one by omitting anything. Scope verbs go in `leading` / `trailing`, which can only add.
🔴 **`absent: { control, reason }` is the only way to omit a standard control, both fields required.**
Silence is what made the drift possible, so silence is unavailable.

Verified: toolbar 40, rows 675, same controls in the same order on both products — the extraction
changed no behaviour. Two things nearly changed silently and did not: the chips' alarm glyph
(restored), and a second `isViewChipVisible` filter (`useViewChips()` already filters; a second one
would look harmless while quietly becoming where the rule lives).

### #397 — and the reason the lab kept the fifth invented cap

`_sheet/MasterSheet.tsx:184`'s `?? 2000` was the fourth. The sweep then found a **fifth** at
`grid-lab/GdsSheetScenario.tsx:143`, on a line also still carrying the retired renderer shape.
**Zero live invented caps remain.**

**Why the lab kept one after everywhere else lost it: `SheetAttr` had no `maxBytes` at all.** The
place built to demonstrate the substrate could not represent a byte cap, so it exercised half of the
length behaviour. Fixture type widened; `bullet2` now carries the live `product_description` shape
and reads **`61 of 2000 bytes (Amazon · IT)`** on `?tab=gds`.

*Third time tonight the same rule paid: a fix to an invented default is not done until you have
grepped for the DEFAULT, not the call site.* I edited that file for the arity change and did not
grep it.

### 🔴 #400 — a correction of mine

I reported that `.nds-pill` was 34px because an inline `<svg>` sat on the baseline and dragged the
descender space. **That was reasoning, not a measurement.** DS.2 measured it: the app's reset
declares `svg { display: block }`, so the icon took a line of its own. **The tell was in my own
data** — a block child adds height and no width, and the pill measured 43.75px wide with and without
the icon. My override is removed; the base is fixed; the `caps` pill passes the `md` that `Pill`
documents (`sm` looked right only because, with an icon, it used to render taller than `md`).

#### PES.3-40 — §14.1: the channel scope now uses the shared toolbar (#410)

The hand-rolled `<div className="nds-grid-prefsbar nds-channel-toolbar">` is gone. It rendered its
own chips and status line and simply **had no search, Customise, Export or Reload** — SR.1's "a
different application" — because a bar assembled per scope can omit a control by forgetting it.

**Measured on Amazon·IT after the swap: toolbar 40px, grid 732px, both 1660px wide.** Controls, left
to right: `20 rows · 1 listing · 20 SKUs on Amazon · IT` · **search** · Missing required (42) ·
Warnings (42) · Mapping errors (63) · **Preflight ★ (20)** · **+ Add listing alias** · Customise ·
Export · Reload.

Wired rather than declared absent, because "not built yet" is an implementation reason and the
contract asks for a reason about the SCOPE:
- **search** — narrows on SKU, name and any cell VALUE; a band row survives when any of its variants
  matches, or the filter would strand children under no group.
- **Customise** — the DS `PreferencesModal`, the same component master opens, never a channel-local
  fork; `defaultVisible` is #173's short view, so "reset" returns to what the sheet lands on.
- **Export** — `exportGridCsv`, marked `narrowed` when the search or a chip has filtered, so the file
  cannot claim to be complete when it is not.
- **Reload** — already existed.

**One `absent` entry, for Views**, whose reason is a scope fact: a channel scope's columns are
dictated by the channel's schema for this market and #173's view is derived from it, so there is
nothing to save under a name.

🔴 **Two defects found by being `absent`'s first consumer — → PES.2.**

1. **The note has no layout.** It renders inline after Reload with no space allocated: my first
   reason laid out as **82 × 312px inside a 40px bar**; shortening it 5× to "No saved views here"
   still gives **45 × 96px**, wrapping to `saved / views` at the right edge. No string fits that
   slot — it needs a width and an ellipsis, with the full sentence in the `title` it already sets.
2. **`views` can still be dropped silently.** `SheetToolbar.tsx:102` renders it only when
   `p.views && p.presets` are supplied, so omitting the DATA omits the control with no `absent`
   entry and no reason — the "a scope cannot drop one by omission" guarantee does not hold for the
   data-driven controls. I kept the `absent` entry anyway: ugly-and-accounted-for beats invisible.

## PES.2 — the host pass, §9.5a, #426, B1 — and a retraction that mattered

**Repo tsc 0 (my files) · 2481 tests / 181 files · all gates green.** Nothing committed.
mtimes from `stat`: `MasterSheet.tsx` 04:48:57 · `useGridState.ts` 04:49:16 · `editors/sheet.ts`
04:42:27 · `components/Toast.tsx` 04:43:33 · `grid.css` 04:38:06.

### 🔴 RETRACTION — my D2 geometry was measured with the dock never open

I reported *"viewport 1660 → 1660, cells 294 → 294 — nothing changes"* across five readings. **The
dock never opened in any of them.** Two faults that only worked together:

- the probe clicked the row's **first** cell (the selection checkbox column); the dock opens from the
  **identity** cell, so the keypress did nothing;
- the "is it open?" check matched an element that is **always in the DOM**, so it returned `true` in
  every state.

**A positive control that is positive unconditionally will confirm any hypothesis, including one
about an event that did not occur.** A gate whose "yes" cannot be distinguished from its
"not measured" is not a gate.

Re-measured with the dock genuinely open and my staged inset neutralised: `root 1660 → 1660,
cells 336 → 336, cols 32 → 32`. **The conclusion survives; the evidence for it did not** — and
another lane had already corrected their own document to match mine. *The next person inherits the
method, not the verdict.* The D2 fix is unaffected: it rests on the dep-bisection and FE.1's profile.

### §5.4 — the ruled pad cannot work, measured; the outcome is reachable another way

A trailing `::after` widens the scroll container by exactly 520 (2439 → 2959) and **max `scrollLeft`
stays 779** — on a real wheel and on `scrollLeft =` alike. AG clamps to
`totalColumnWidth − viewportWidth`, and the container's DOM width is not an input to either term.
AG.1 then enumerated the API: three horizontal-scroll members, two of them readers, no spacer, and
every theming `*Padding` interior to the cell. **No third door.**

A **transient inset** — applied only while the panel is open, in the region the panel already covers
— gives the outcome: max scroll 779 → 1299, last column's right edge 1727 → **1207** against a panel
edge of 1208. Staged on the tree with a revert block, not landed: the cost is 30 → 24 rendered
columns twice per dock interaction, and that is UX.1's call on FE.1's numbers.

### The host pass (#421/#424/#427) — three lanes shipped their half and the link still failed

🔴 **`distance <= 0` → `=== 0`.** A negative distance IS the answer under `'reveal'`; `<= 0`
discarded it before `revealScroll` saw it, so **the plumbing above was inert while looking correct**.
Plus the left edges (without them the substrate returns 0 for every off-left cell), the intent
threaded through `revealNow`/`onRevealCell`, and **the intent stashed with the deferred replay** —
the `?rec=&cell=` path is both the one that needs `'reveal'` and the one that always defers.

### §9.5a / #425 — a side effect must not overrule a ruling

`stripScroll` withdraws `scroll.left` from persistence and keeps `scroll.top`. A restored 1,227px
lands the operator past identity, past required-and-incomplete and past the spine on every load —
**undoing §9.2's ordering with an accident of where somebody stopped scrolling.** Applied on the way
in *and* out, so an older stored value cannot outlive the rule. 5 tests, 3/3 mutations killed,
including one that over-corrects by dropping the vertical half.

The validator said `— the channel cap` unconditionally while `capFrom` sat on the reading. Now it
names the source, or says **`source not stated`** rather than borrowing an authority we do not have.
My own comment forty lines up warns about this exact hazard; the phrase survived beneath it. DS.1's
grep found it.

### B1 — `useToast()` stopped taking down surfaces

It threw when the DS provider was absent, so a route died the moment a sibling lane added the first
DS component that reports an outcome. It now renders through the same markup and complains once to
the developer — **not** a silent no-op, because an outcome the operator never sees is the failure
this design system exists to prevent.

Also caught, by a guard rather than by me: I wrote `cursor: help`, banned permanently by the Owner.

#### PES.3-41 — 🔴 D14 reproduced: `color` is not refused, it is NEVER OFFERED

The Owner's "I'm unable to write a lot of attributes still, such as color". Reproduced, and the
cause is not any of the three banked suspects.

**The write works.** `attr_color` with `target: 'channel'` on GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-M / Amazon·IT:

```
PATCH → updated: 1, errors: null
DB    → overrideData {"color": "Nero"} · listing v87 → v88 · master untouched (color still null)
        cleaned, key verified absent
```

**The sheet never asks.** The payload declares the column and sends no cell for it:

```
Amazon·IT   97 columns declared · 21 cells on every row · 76 columns have NO cell on ANY row
master     102 columns declared · 21 cells          · `color` absent there too
missing include: color, description, manufacturer, product_description, bullet_point, the GPSR pair
```

`values['color']` is `undefined`, so `valueGetter` renders empty, `isCellEditable(undefined)` is
**false** (`rows.ts:75` — `!!cell && …`), and there is no cell to carry a `writeBlockedReason`. The
answer to "accepted, refused with which message, or a silent no-op" is a **fourth category: never
attemptable**. Nothing is refused because nothing is ever sent — there is no cell to type into, and
the empty one cannot explain itself.

**Against FFD10's acceptance — "writable, or the cell says why not" — this is neither**, for 78% of
the declared columns, on BOTH scopes. It is not channel-specific and not a routing bug: routing was
the previous defect (§14), and it is fixed; this is one layer earlier.

**→ PES.5, and it is a contract question, not a client fix.** A column declared with no cell is the
sheet promising a field it cannot service. Either the row carries a cell for every declared column
(empty, with its own `writable`/`writeVerb`), or the column set is narrowed to what the row can
answer for. The client must NOT synthesise the missing cell: `writeField` is knowable from the
column, but `writable` and `writeVerb` are per-cell server answers, and inventing them is exactly
the `?? 'DRAFT'` class one level up — a plausible default standing in for a fact only the server has.

**PES.7 — the "hundreds of variations" caveat, closed where it could be (2026-09-02).** Detail in
§35. I flagged this untested when D11 landed; measured now, read-only, while D11 waits.

**It holds structurally: nothing in these surfaces iterates variations.** The grids are per AXIS
VALUE — 20 variations render **3 rows**, measured on screen, so 300 variations with 12 colours
render 13, on top of NexusGrid virtualisation. `picturelessCoordinates` is axis-values × slots, not
variations. Every growable list render is sliced (12/8/12/8/24/3). The only `variants` reference in
the lane is `.length` for a count.

**Preflight measured:** 4,691 bytes for 20 ASINs → **235 B/ASIN → ~69 KB at 300**, 0.4s. Not a
scale problem.

**Still untested and stated as such:** `apply-to-children` fans out server-side across every child;
its cost at 300 is not client-measurable, and exercising it means a destructive cascade this lane
has refused all session. Open question for that route's owner, not a claim of mine.

### PES.2 — §9.2 amendment: the unnamed tail is ordered by group

`orderColumnKeys` sorts `rank → group → schema index`. The ~75 columns the rule does not name used
to trail in raw schema order — the contract's cache order, meaningful to nobody — so an operator
scrolling the tail met `weave_type` beside `merchant_shipping_group` beside `skip_offer`. Grouped,
the tail is navigable and it agrees with the Customise dialog, which already sections by group.

Group order is the **contract's** (first appearance), not alphabetical: the server has already
decided what comes first. There is a test for that (`Zulu` before `Alpha`), because alphabetical is
the tidy-up someone makes in good faith.

**§9.1 measured after: `7/7` at both widths, required block `1299px`, `73px` spare at 1440 and
`361px` at 1728 — identical to before.** Not luck: ranked columns carry distinct ranks, so the group
tie-break is only ever reached by unnamed ones. A test asserts every required column still precedes
the whole tail. **4/4 mutations killed**, including one that lets the group key outrank the rule.

🔴 **One of my own tests could not have caught this change.** `it('leaves columns the rule does not
name in their schema order')` passed before AND after, because every unnamed column in that fixture
shares one group. Retitled to claim only what it tests, and joined by a fixture with **interleaved**
groups that comes out in runs only if the grouping works. **A fixture that cannot express the
distinction is a test that agrees with whatever you do** — the third instance tonight of a check
that cannot fail, after the unconditionally-positive dock control and the DOM check blind to
virtualised columns.

### PES.2 — D15.12 premise verified in source (queued, not built)

A pasted or fill-dragged value reaches the server **with no validation anywhere on the path**:

- `writeGate` has no concept of validity — its verdict is `{ write, reason }` with reasons
  `no-column | grid-data | self-inflicted | unchanged`. It answers only *"is this an operator's
  edit?"*
- `sheetWriter.ts` contains **zero** references to validation.
- `validation` in `columns.tsx` is display-only: `sheetClassRules` (the tint) at `:195` and a
  tooltip at `:204`. Nothing else reads it.

So a value that could not be TYPED — over a channel's byte cap, off a closed list — is committed by
a paste or a fill drag.

**Reconciling this with `writeGate`'s own header**, which argues for a deny-list because *"an edit
that shows on screen but never reaches the server is precisely the dishonesty a sheet exists to
prevent"*: the two are not in tension. **The gate's rule is against SILENTLY dropping an edit.** A
refusal that renders, states its reason, and keeps the pasted text on screen as unsaved is that same
honesty arriving by another route — the failure both rules prevent is an operator believing
something saved when it did not.

**Therefore the validator runs AROUND `writeGate`, never inside it.** The gate is pure, tested, and
answers one question; folding validation in would give it two answers under one name, and its rules
became assertable precisely because it has only the one.

Blocked on AG.1's XAVIA paste reading (`source: 'paste'` end to end) and D18's editor.

## PES.6 — wave-4 D16 endpoints other lanes build on, `nexus-commerce-33`

`routes/cell-formula.routes.ts` (mtime 2026-09-02T06:24:37), all under `/api`:

| endpoint | what it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /pim/formulas/preview` | the cell editor's live line. Resolves the row once, then `simulateFieldForCandidate` (pure, zero-DB). Writes nothing. Strips a leading `=`. Returns `{ok, value, dependsOn, rules, unresolved, error, errorPos}` |
| `GET /pim/formulas/functions` | the 35-function catalogue for autocomplete |
| `GET /pim/formulas/product/:productId` | that product's cell formulas |
| `POST /pim/formulas/batch` | formulas for ≤250 products, keyed productId → fieldKey |
| `PUT /pim/formulas/product/:productId` | set a cell formula: validate → evaluate → write the VALUE to the value layer → store formula + deps → cascade to dependents |
| `DELETE /pim/formulas/product/:productId?fieldKey=…` | pin a literal: audit row (`formula.pinned`), formula row deleted, **value kept** |
| `POST /pim/formulas/restore` `{auditLogId}` | (H) re-create from the audit row and re-evaluate — `restoreVia: 'formula'` routes here |
| `GET/PUT/DELETE /pim/formulas/master` + `/master/revisions` | master field rules |
| `GET /pim/formulas/master/evaluate/:productId` | read-time master rule values |

**Three behaviours the front-end should not re-derive:**
1. A formula that resolves to nothing **while warning about why** is an ERROR (`"The formula produced no value — division by zero."`), not an empty success. Division by zero, an unknown attribute and a skipped transform are all warnings in the engine, so without this the cell empties with `formulaError` unset.
2. An errored formula **clears the stored value** (§1.6(G)). `formula` present + `formulaError` present + `value` **null** is the real, common state.
3. `=` is stripped server-side as well as in the browser, and a *stored* expr beginning with `=` is refused — it is a real equality operator.

⚠ `AuditLog` is immutable by DB trigger. Anything exercising the pin path leaves permanent rows; that is by design, but budget for it and never put an audit delete in a cleanup block (it aborts everything after it).

### PES.2 — `optionLabel` hoisted to `_studio/sheet/` (#501)

`optionLabel(value, optionLabels?)` — one way to show a coded value, consumed by the grid's select
branch and by IO.1's import diff. **On a diff, identical values must look identical:** if the sheet
renders `PK` as "Pakistan" and the diff renders `PK`, every coded cell reads as a change.

Four rules, all of which a copy would lose, all tested (**4/4 mutations killed**):
- 🔴 an unmapped code falls back to the **CODE**, never blank — blanking presents a cell that has
  data as empty, and on a diff that reads as a value being REMOVED;
- 🔴 **`0` is a value, not an absence** — a `!value` guard blanks it, and `0` is a real code on more
  than one Amazon enum;
- `''` is never looked up — a schema entry for the empty string would put a label in an empty cell;
- non-string codes are coerced, since Amazon serves numeric-looking codes as numbers.

AG.1 asked for a dev-only `GridApi` hook on the lab sheet so probes can drive AG's real paste path
(`api.pasteFromClipboard()`; a synthetic paste event never changes a cell, because AG reads the

*A request to add a guarded thing is a good moment to check whether the unguarded version is already
there — not finding the feature you were asked for is weak evidence that nothing like it exists.*

14 guard scripts build a file list from `git ls-files` and then read those files. **Exactly one throws

### DS.1 — #583: the hand-kept dark pin is now mechanised, and it was missing FIVE not one

**mtimes:** `scripts/check-dark-pin-parity.mjs` **07:54:53** (new, DS.1) · `shared-shell.css`
**07:54:07** · `.githooks/pre-push` **07:55:40**.

**Guard, not generator.** The pin lives in a hand-written page sheet scoped to
`body:has(.h10-shell)` — a page concern, not a token concern. Having the token generator write into
`shared-shell.css` would put generated output inside a sheet whose cascade position is load-bearing
(`reference_ds_input_blocked_by_h10_cd_field`, `reference_css_source_order_beats_specificity`). A
guard is additive, self-testable and changes no cascade.

**🔴 The diff found 5, not 1.** `--nds-chrome-bg` (the one reported) plus **three provenance inks** —
`--nds-prov-ai-fg`, `--nds-prov-formula-fg`, `--nds-prov-inherited-fg` — and `--nds-grid-ai-draft-bg`.
The provenance inks are the marks that say where a cell's value came from: the surface that most
needs to stay legible when everything else is refusing. Four are now pinned to their `:root` values.

**`--nds-grid-ai-draft-bg` is deliberately NOT pinned** — its `.dark` value is byte-identical to its
`:root` value, so a pin would be a no-op. **The guard's rule is "the dark value DIFFERS", not "a dark
entry exists."** A presence-based check would have demanded a pointless entry, and noise in this list
is exactly why five real misses sat in it unnoticed. A guard that pads the haystack works against the
thing it guards.

```
CONTROL (--nds-chrome-bg unpinned, the #583 state)   exit 1
  ❌ 1 token changes under .dark and is NOT pinned
     --nds-chrome-bg   :root #18263b   .dark #1e3050

RESTORED                                             exit 0
  96 redefined under .dark · 95 pinned · 42 identical to :root · 0 missing
```

Control at both layers: a `--self-test` case over literals (6/6, including that a commented-out dark
override is not an override, and a token pinned only inside a comment is not pinned), and the live
run above against the real tree with a scratch shell sheet. No repo file was edited to force the red.

**Incidental measurement worth someone's attention: 42 of the 96 `.dark` entries are identical to
their `:root` value** — 44% of the dark block changes nothing. Not a defect and not mine to fix, but
if the generator is emitting them unconditionally, the block is nearly half noise, and this whole
incident was a miss hiding in noise.

**Wired into pre-push at `:242`,** after `tokens:check` so parity is measured against freshly
generated CSS rather than stale. It is green on the tree, so it blocks nothing today. That wiring was
my call from the ruling's own words — a guard that "fails on a missing entry" must be somewhere it
can fail — and it is one line to reverse if you would rather it stayed out.

## UX.1 — a probe's safety is not a loan from the page (2026-09-02, measured)

Two defects in `scripts/check-layout-v2.mjs`, found by checking a question rather than answering it.
Neither was a wrong number, which is why every check that asked "is this figure right?" missed both.
Filed here because SC.1 hit the same class the same hour, independently, in a different instrument.

**1. Safety inherited from the product, never re-measured.** `checkPopovers` clicked EVERY button
wider than 20px in the header and scope bar to discover which ones opened a panel — including the
four studio tabs (`Tabs onChange={setTab}`), so popovers had been measured on whatever tab it
navigated to. It was safe only because `PublishMenu`'s items are all `disabled: true` while publish
is unwired, against a dev server that writes to the **production database**. When PES.5 wires
publish, the unchanged line clicks a live trigger — and the failure reports itself as a clean
measurement, because a direct-action button opens no panel and lands in the ABSTAIN branch reading
"no popover opened". Separately `checkSelectClamp` opened a live cell editor and left teardown to
close it; AG's `destroy()` calls `stopEditing()` with COMMIT semantics, so "just navigate away" is a
write. Now gated on a declared `aria-haspopup` (the DS sets it on Menu/Listbox/DateField); anything
else is reported unclicked, and the editor is closed with an explicit Escape.

**2. A stale shared selector gives a false failure and a false pass from ONE defect.** The popover
check matched a global panel selector and the previous panel had not closed, so it re-measured that
one. The tell: **three different triggers reporting one identical geometry** (983–1264 w281 at 1280)
— three triggers cannot anchor to one position. `Market` was scored against `Publish`'s panel, a
false FAILURE I was close to filing with DS.2 as a real anchoring bug; `Content locale` passed only
because its trigger shares that panel's right edge, a false PASS. **The false pass is the dangerous
half, because nobody investigates it.** §13's "popovers 9/9 anchored" was therefore unearned until
today; it now holds with distinct panels (Market 1013–1213 w200 against trigger 1013–1135), and §13
records that it was unearned rather than quietly keeping the number.

**What found them.** SC.1 asked whether any §9 figure of mine depends on a write landing. The answer
is no — §9 is read-side geometry throughout, nothing asserts a value round-tripping — but I nearly
answered it from a grep for `startEditingCell|PATCH|POST|fill(` that returned two hits, both the word
"POST-OPEN" in a comment. **A scoped grep's clean result proves the scope, not the claim.** SC.1's
instance the same hour: `writeBlockedReason` read off the **column** when it exists only on the
**cell**, where `undefined == null` made "no reason given" and "I looked in the wrong object" print
the same string on three coordinates.

**The rule, for the ledger:** ask of a probe not what it MEASURES but what it DOES, and re-ask when
the page grows a control. Both defects were invariants holding by coincidence — publish being inert,
a panel usually closing — that nobody had written down as coincidences.

**Also corrected: a count quoted in the other's units.** §13 said "2 failures from 48" beside a
runner printing 7. Neither is wrong — 2 counts distinct defects, 7 counts failing assertions across
6 states, because §5.3 fails once per width and drags §9.1's drawer-open reading with it three more
times. §13 now states both and why they differ. A defect count is the useful number for a lane; an
assertion count is the honest number against the runner's own output.

### 🔴 Item 1 HELD — `--nds-chrome-bg: var(--nds-rail-bg)` would close a CYCLE

Not landed, and I would not land it without an explicit override, because the two declarations define
each other:

- `shared-shell.css:606` declares `--nds-rail-bg: var(--nds-chrome-bg)`, and its selector list at
  `:598-605` **includes `body:has(.h10-shell)` itself** — the very element the pin block targets —
  and it sits LATER in source order with equal specificity, so it wins there.
- The proposed pin would declare `--nds-chrome-bg: var(--nds-rail-bg)` on that same element.

On `body:has(.h10-shell)` that is `rail-bg → chrome-bg → rail-bg`. Custom properties in a cyclic
dependency are invalid at computed-value time, so **both** would drop, taking the rail ground, the
topbar ground and the chrome ground with them — in both themes.

**The premise is right and the direction is backwards.** `--nds-rail-bg` does hold `#18263b` on a
pinned page — but only *because* `:606` derives it FROM `--nds-chrome-bg`. That is also why DS.2's
`--nds-topbar-bg: var(--nds-rail-bg)` works: topbar is downstream of rail, which is downstream of
chrome. `--nds-chrome-bg` is the ROOT of that chain; there is nothing upstream to point it at.
`--nds-rail-surface` is not a candidate either — it is `#f1f3f5`, a light grey.

So the literal at `:561` is not an unconverted leftover; it is the one value the chain starts from,
and the file's 30 → 31 is the honest cost of that. The alternatives are to mint a Tier-3 chrome base
token (ruled out at #601) or to re-baseline this file by 1 with the reason stated.

**Offered:** DS.2 has the working instrument and measured form B for the topbar. The decisive test is
injecting `--nds-chrome-bg: var(--nds-rail-bg)` on `body:has(.h10-shell)` and reading the rail,
topbar and chrome triple — a cycle shows as the grounds dropping, not as a wrong colour.

### DS.1 — #605 done: re-baseline with a durable reason, and the pin-drift check

**mtimes:** `scripts/css-hex-baseline.json` **08:23:56** · `check-css-hex-ratchet.mjs` **08:23:56** ·
`check-dark-pin-parity.mjs` **08:25:01**.

**Re-baseline.** `app/_shared/shared-shell.css` 30 → 31, total 3203 → 3204. The ratchet's `files` map
holds plain numbers, so the reason went into a new sibling `reasons` map keyed by the same path, and
the `note` now says a raise without one is a regression.

**🔴 And a second change the ruling implies but does not say: `--baseline` would have DELETED the
reason.** The writer emits a fixed object (`note, updatedAt, total, files`), so the next person to
run `--baseline` for any unrelated file would have silently dropped the sentence and left a raised
number with no argument behind it. It now carries `reasons` forward, pruned to files still present.
A justification that a routine mechanical step erases is the same class as the pin-block comment that
could not enforce itself (DS1-35).

**Pin-drift check.** A pin is a COPY of a value that lives in the token file, and copies drift —
invisible to a presence check, because the entry is there and neither value looks wrong alone. The
guard now resolves each pin in its own cascade context and demands it equal the token's `:root` light
value.

```
LIVE     338 :root · 96 .dark · 96 pinned · 247 identical · 2 unresolvable
         · 0 missing · 0 drifted · 13 superseded by a later block          exit 0
CONTROL  (--nds-chrome-bg pin corrupted to #999999 in a scratch shell copy) exit 1
  --nds-chrome-bg   pin `#999999` resolves to #999999, but :root light is #18263b
  --nds-topbar-bg   pin `var(--nds-rail-bg)` resolves to #999999, but :root light is #18263b
```

The control catching **two** is the cascade working, not a double-report: corrupting the chain's root
breaks the alias downstream of it, which is precisely the coupling that made #601's ruling wrong.

**The model reads every block on the element, not just the pin list.** `:606` re-declares
`--nds-rail-bg: var(--nds-chrome-bg)` on a selector list containing `body:has(.h10-shell)`, later and
at equal specificity. A model reading only the pin block would resolve `--nds-topbar-bg` through the
pin's own rail-bg (`#f1f3f5`) and report drift on a correct line. **Reading one block and calling it
the cascade is exactly how #601 went wrong**, so the guard is built not to repeat it.

Self-test **14 cases**, including the four new ones: a wrong literal is drift; the right literal is
not; a `var()` alias that resolves correctly is not; and a token re-declared by a later block is
*superseded*, not drift.

**Both abstains are now NAMED, not counted** — `not compared: --nds-font-sans, --nds-font-mono` and
`pinned but overridden by a later block, so not drift-checked:` the 13 `--nds-rail-*` tokens the
chrome block deliberately owns. DS1-33 applied to my own gate twice over.

### DS.1 — #623: `tailwindType` metric, census and baseline

**mtimes:** `scripts/ds-conformance-guard.mjs` **08:42:04** · `scripts/ds-conformance-baseline.json`
**08:45** (re-captured, see below). Disclosed edit; the file is unclaimed, third DS.1 edit.

**🔴 The ruling's proposed regex was wrong on both halves, and I read `tailwind.config.ts` rather
than adopting it.** There is **no `font-heading` and no `font-label`** in this config — the families
are `sans | display | mono`. And the size scale includes **`body` and `body-lg`**, which the ruling
omits. A metric matching class names that do not exist would have censused zero and looked clean:
the same defect as #617's remedy naming a class nobody wrote, one ruling later.

Landed regex, keys from the config:
`text-(body-lg|body|2xl|3xl|4xl|xs|sm|base|md|lg|xl)` and `font-(display|sans|mono)`, with
`(?<![\w-])` / `(?![\w-])` rather than `\b` — `\b` would match `h10-text-sm`, because the `-` before
`text` is a word boundary. `body-lg` is ordered before `body` so the longer key wins.

**CENSUS — 12,068 across 38 sections** (44 baseline sections; 6 sit at 0). Largest:
products 3757 · fulfillment 2892 · marketing 881 · settings 787 · catalog 525 · bulk-operations 485 ·
listings 460 · orders 426 · dashboard 401 · sync-logs 238 · pricing 221 · insights 181 ·
customers 150 · design 127 · _shared 136.

**🔴 The hole is confirmed empirically, in the census itself.** At #591 the guard reported
`design: fontSize 0 → 38` (`formula-lab/page.tsx` ×24, `chrome/page.tsx` ×14). The `design` section's
`fontSize` is now **0** — and `tailwindType` shows the classes those inline styles became. The count
fell; the adoption did not move. That is the substitution the ruling describes, visible as two numbers
in one table.

**Baselined at CURRENT counts, `tailwindType` ONLY.** `--baseline` rewrites every metric from current
counts, and after #591 those include the untracked files — running it would have silently accepted
every violation this guard exists to hold. So the key was added per-section by hand and the other six
metrics are byte-identical.

**The baseline had to be re-captured once, and that is worth stating:** the first write put `design`
at 145 at 08:41; by 08:45 it was 127. `chrome/page.tsx` — the file that motivated this whole ruling —
had been converted in between, and it no longer appears in the manifest at all. So the baseline does
**not** grandfather it. It also invalidated my first control: `design` had 18 of headroom, so adding a
scratch file changed nothing and the ratchet looked inert. **A baseline captured against a live tree
is a moving target, and a control run against a stale one proves nothing.**

```
CONTROL  a new file with className="text-sm" under design/
  ❌ design: tailwindType 127 → 128 — new Tailwind type-scale class(s) added.
     Tailwind type classes are the legacy kit by another name — the inline fontSize count
     falls and DS adoption does not move. Use font-size: var(--nds-font-size-*) …
RESTORED  0 tailwindType failures
```

Self-test **16 cases** (was 5). Ten are the metric itself, and the ones that matter are the negatives:
`text-ellipsis`, `text-left/center/nowrap`, `font-heading`/`font-label`, `h10-text-sm`/`nds-text-lg`,
and `text-red-500` (rawColor's job) must all count **0**; `text-body-lg` must count **1**, not two.

**Reported by SECTION, not by file** — that is this guard's existing shape; the failure line points at
`--manifest <section>` for the file list, as the other six metrics do.

### DS.1 — #631: the utilities are named, and the list is no longer restated

**mtime:** `scripts/ds-conformance-guard.mjs` **08:51:02**.

Verified first: **14 `.nds-type-*` classes exist** in `design-system/styles/primitives.css`
(mtime 08:37:55) and their names match the token names exactly, so "of the same name" is true rather
than assumed.

**🔴 But my own remedy list was already stale, 40 minutes after I wrote it.** It named 11 steps from
`tokens.css:393-403`; the table now holds **14** — `nano`, `micro-plus` and `md-minus` arrived with
DS.2's utilities. That is the hub's just-banked lesson landing on the line that was written to fix
exactly this defect one ruling earlier.

**So the list is no longer restated: `typeScale()` reads it from `tokens.css` at runtime**, names and
line range together, and both remedies build their sentence from it. The message now reads
`nano|micro|micro-plus|xs|xs-plus|sm|sm-plus|base|base-plus|md-minus|md|lg|xl|2xl — tokens.css:393-406`
and updates itself when the table does. *A list of members is a set claim; read it, never restate it.*

**Self-test 18 cases, and the prohibition is flipped to a requirement.** `fontSize` must now contain
`nds-type-`, and must name the LAST step the token table holds — so adding a token without extending
the utilities fails here.

**Two controls on the precondition, because a precondition that cannot fail is decoration:**

```
normal cwd     PASS precondition: .nds-type-* exists (14 found)
               PASS every --nds-font-size-* step has a utility of the same name (14/14)   exit 0
cwd without design-system/styles
               FAIL precondition (0 found)
               FAIL parity — the token scale read as EMPTY, so this would have passed vacuously
                                                                                          exit 1
```

**The second FAIL is a hole I put there and then found.** With an empty scale, "every step has a
utility" is **vacuously true** and printed `PASS (0/0)` — a check that cannot fail on the input it
exists for, sitting directly beneath a check that had just failed. `scale.length > 0` is now part of
the condition, and the failure line says *why* rather than showing an empty ratio.

**Also hardened:** an unreadable token file used to degrade into a remedy naming an EMPTY set, which
reads as "there are no steps". It now points at the file instead and lets the self-test fail.

**PES.7 — `accept="image/*"` restored on DS.2's fix (2026-09-02).** Verified their change at source
before relying on it: the matcher is extracted to `design-system/lib/accept-match.ts` (08:57:11) and
keeps the slash when stripping the star (`image/*` → prefix `image/`), so it cannot match
`imagex/png`. `FileDropzone.tsx` 08:57:45.

Both inputs are back to `accept="image/*"` and the extension list is gone — `IMAGE_ACCEPT` deleted
from `types.ts`, no references remain. **mtimes:** `MasterGallery.tsx`, `BulkApplyModal.tsx` and
`types.ts` all **2026-09-02 09:00:34**.

**The negative, in situ, twice — with the network instrumented so "no request" is measured:**

| dropped on the master-images zone | result | requests |
|---|---|---|
| `contract.pdf` (`application/pdf`) | refused — *"Unsupported file — accepts image/\*."* | **0** |
| `looks-like.png` (`application/pdf`) | refused — same message | **0** |

Tiles 24 → 24 both times; `onFiles` never fired, so nothing reached `uploadFiles`. A `fetch`+`XHR`
spy recorded every outbound call and captured **none** during either drop.

The second case is the sharper one: a file whose **name** ends `.png` but whose **type** is
`application/pdf`. `image/*` matches on type, so a correct matcher must still refuse it — and it
did. That rules out the fix having been implemented as a filename check.

⚠ **What this evidence does NOT show, stated plainly:** a refusal is equally consistent with "the
wildcard is interpreted correctly" and with "the matcher still refuses everything", which was the
original bug. Discriminating requires an ACCEPT, and in `FileDropzone` acceptance *is* dispatch —
`onFiles` fires in the same pass — so on this surface it is an upload to the ASIN-global master set.
That half belongs to DS.2's pure-function test (`.png` against `image/*`, with the old-vs-new
control), which is where it costs nothing. My in-situ evidence covers the dangerous direction only:
the wildcard has not degraded into "accept anything".

**Green:** 323 image-lane tests / 20 files (+71 ancillary), web tsc clean for my files,
raw-primitives 0 of mine, hex 0 of mine. Nothing committed.

**🔴 Two things a successor must not lose:**
1. **#675's bound must not be widened.** The import path (`product-studio.routes.ts:500-531`) sums
   `body.updated` into `applied`. It sends NO token, so the equality pass never runs for it. Widen
   the bound past `expectedVersion !== undefined` and every already-correct cell returns
   `updated: 0`, and the import reports a partial failure that did not happen.
2. **A same-value write with a STALE token now returns 200 `unchanged`, not 409.** The equality pass
   runs long before the CAS. Anyone using a deliberately stale token to DETECT staleness must send a
   changed value, or they will be told "unchanged" and believe they are current. This is why #662's
   refusal recipe specifies a changed value.

**One property of #675 worth stating rather than leaving for someone to find.** The comparator is
`String(a ?? '') === String(b ?? '')`, so it treats `null`, `undefined` and `''` as one value. A
PATCH that genuinely clears a field from `null` to `''` (or back) is therefore counted `unchanged`
and skipped. I believe that is correct semantically — both render as an empty cell and both publish
as absent — but it IS a write the endpoint now declines to make, in the one direction that is not
conservative, and it was not in the hand-off's description of the check. Not changing it unasked;
flagging it so the hub can rule if it disagrees.

### DS.1 — #678: the hovercard is capped and the value wraps, measured on a real page

**mtimes:** `apps/web/src/design-system/styles/components.css` **13:47:59** ·
`apps/factory/src/design-system/styles/components.css` **13:47:59**.

Measured on `/marketing/ads/reporting?tab=library`, the **Hourly performance** entry — its `Caveat`
row is a real 179-character note from `catalogue.ts:152`, not a fixture.

| | BEFORE | AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| card width | **1147.3px** | **320px** |
| % of a 1728px viewport | **66.4%** | **18.5%** |
| `max-width` | `none` | `320px` (`--nds-popover-max-w`) |
| value | one unwrapped line | **5 line boxes** |
| content overflows card | — | `false` |
| key column | — | `nowrap`, one line each |

Same trigger, same value, both screenshotted.

**The cap and the wrapping are ONE change, not two.** `max-width` alone would have been worse than
the bug: `nowrap` inside a bounded box overflows it. That is also why `.r1` — the single-hint form —
had to wrap as well, which is beyond the literal ask and not optional: most HoverCard call sites pass
`text` rather than `rows` (`BrandMetricsPanel.tsx:333` passes a full sentence), and capping the card
while leaving `.r1` at `nowrap` would have turned an over-wide card into a clipped one.

`overflow-wrap: anywhere` rather than `break-word`, so a long unbroken token (an ASIN list, a URL)
also yields. The KEY column is explicitly `nowrap`: it is short by construction and a wrapped label
reads as two rows.

**Factory fork: same edit, `check-ds-fork-drift` green, NOT verified on screen** — the factory app is
a separate dev server and I did not start one. Source-identical, unmeasured; say so rather than imply
a second measurement.

**🔴 An instrument failure I chased and should record.** After the CSS landed, the hovercard stopped
opening for four consecutive attempts, including an exact replay of the sequence that had just
worked. The obvious reading was that my own change had broken the component. Two controls said
otherwise: injecting `max-width: none !important` did **not** bring the card back, and a listener
attached to the trigger recorded **zero** pointer events — *the browser was delivering nothing to the
page*. The hover tool had stopped reaching that tab. A fresh tab restored it immediately and the
measurement above is from that tab.

Worth keeping because the failure mode reads exactly like a real regression: the change goes in, the
feature stops working, and the timing is perfect. **Before believing your own edit broke something,
check that the instrument still works** — an A/B that neutralises the change, and a probe that asks
whether events arrive at all.

**Not touched, per the ruling, so nobody "fixes" them:** `.nds-taginput-menu` (field-width by
construction), `.nds-dp-pop` (structural), and the drawer's own max.

**5. 🔴 A correction to e2's diagnosis of its own instrument failure, and a trap for every lane.**
e2 filed "the hovercard stopped opening… a listener on the trigger recorded ZERO pointer events —
the browser was delivering nothing to the page." I hit the identical symptom; the cause is different
and measurable. **`computer` coordinates are SCREENSHOT space, not CSS pixels** — the screenshot is
1512 wide for a 1728 viewport, so every coordinate is scaled by **1.1428** on the way in.
`hover(250, 481)` (the trigger's CSS centre) landed at **CSS (286, 550)**, 36px right and 69px down,
on a `<td>`. A 12px icon is missed silently and the trigger records no events *because none arrive at
the trigger*. Proof in one call: a capturing document `mousemove` recorded `(286,550)` for
`hover(250,481)`, then `(250,481)` for `hover(219,421)` — and `.nds-hovercard:hover` then matched the
right trigger. **Convert: `shotX = cssX × 0.875`.** e2's observation was right and its controls were
sound; the inference had a second explanation, which a document-level listener separates from a
trigger-level one. This cost me four failed attempts before I stopped believing the page and
instrumented the pointer — the disproof was in my own printed coordinates the whole time.

Structurally it cannot bite either, which is why the component exists: `HoverCard` portals to
`document.body` at `position: fixed`, so a pane's `overflow` never participates. The only clamp is
the viewport one in `useLayoutEffect` (`left + width > vw − 8`), and a **320px card makes that clamp
fire LESS often than a 1147px one, never more** — cap and clamp compose as `min(content, 320)` then a
left-shift; they cannot fight. Other grid-mounted call sites, for the record:

**§9.1 required-column fit — GALE-JACKET, headless chromium, fresh context per arm (no persisted
view), backend read off the browser's own network log as `127.0.0.1:8091` on every arm, band measured
as root − pinned-left − pinned-right. No arm spans an API restart window.**

| coordinate | width | before 14:21 | + order (#687) 14:24 | + #690 14:33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master · IT | 1728 | 7/7 | 7/7 | 7/7 (361 spare) |
| master · IT | **1440** | **6/7** (87 short) | 6/7 | **7/7 (73 spare)** |
| master · IT | 1280 | 4/7 | 4/7 | 6/7 (87 short) |
| Amazon · IT | 1728 | 5/7 | 7/7 | 7/7 (410 spare) |

UX.1 reproduced all nine post-#690 cells independently at 14:36–14:44 on a different instrument and
selector set. My BEFORE channel numbers (5/7 · 3/7 · 2/7) reproduce theirs exactly.

**The three causes, in the order they were found, each measured rather than argued:**

1. **490px of non-required columns INSIDE the required block.** The channel imported
   `defaultViewColumns` (what is VISIBLE) and not `orderColumnKeys` (what ORDER renders), so it hid
   the right columns and drew the survivors in the CONTRACT's order — `name` 220 + `productType` 160
   + `status` 110 between `brand` and the other six. §9.3b fixed this exact arrangement on master;
   the channel never received it. One shared import, no copy.
2. 🔴 **`color.scope` is a MARKET fact, not a scope fact — and it made master·IT fail §9.1 too.**
   The contract returns `per_variant` on **IT** and `global` on **DE**, on BOTH scopes (four GETs,
   one variable at a time: master IT 102 cols per_variant · master DE 96 global · Amazon·IT 97
   per_variant · Amazon·DE 96 global). So rule 1 hoisted a 160px `color` in front of the seven
   required columns wherever the market says per_variant. **Every §9.1 master baseline in this
   programme — §9.3b's own "73px spare, 7/7", #679, the runner's fixture — was taken on DE**, the one
   coordinate where the hoist does not happen. master·IT read 6/7 at 1440 all along and nobody had
   looked. UX.1 first attributed the difference to the scope; their two payloads differed in scope
   AND market, so the pair could not separate them. Ruled at #690: axes now sit IMMEDIATELY AFTER the
   required block, in `views.ts`, for both scopes at once.
   **And the hoisted column was empty:** `color` is populated on **0 of 21 rows** on both scopes,
   while the values that do tell the rows apart live in `row.axisValues` (`{"Size":"XS","Color":"Nero"}`)
   — 160px of "—" in front of the work. Whether the `color` COLUMN should read `axisValues` is a
   contract question, unfiled, not mine.
3. **A 120px right-pinned `actions` column holding one 28px button.** Measured on screen: the cell
   renders a single `.nds-btn.sm.icon` (28px) in 9px/9px padding — 74px empty per row, and it is
   `.nds-btn` only because this scope passes `items` without `primary`. `actionsColumn` now sizes to
   its SHAPE (56 = 28 + 2×14 for `items`-only, 120 with a `primary`). Call sites enumerated BEFORE
   the change: four outside the DS, and only the `items`-only one moves — grid-lab `:145`/`:413` and
   `products/next/columns.tsx:252` all pass `primary` and keep 120. The verbs behind the ⋯
   (`offer-toggle`, `broadcast-to-listings`, `open-record`) are also on right-click, from the same
   `channelActions` declaration; master has NO ⋯ column at all and offers its verbs by right-click
   only. Recorded, not ruled: master staying without one is the hub's open item, and an un-narrowed ⋯
   added to master would cost it the 73px it has spare at 1440.

**What is NOT covered by the green suite, stated so nobody reads it as coverage.** 1,566 tests / 97
files pass across `_studio` + `design-system/grid`, and **nothing in them imports `ChannelSheet.tsx`
or `presets.ts`** — both are, or import, `.tsx`, and `apps/web`'s vitest is node-only. The two
ordering cases in `defaultView.vitest.test.ts` DID assert the opposite until today ("the axes lead");

## UX.1 — §9.1 had never been pointed at half its own subject (2026-09-02, `nexus-commerce-d1`)

**#679/#684/#690 closed at 1440 on every coordinate. The finding is not a number, it is that a
green check had been measuring one coordinate of a rule stated for all of them.**

§9.1 says *"every column REQUIRED for this row's product type must fit at 1440"* — scope-independent
by its own wording. For the life of the spec it ran on master OUTERWEAR. Pointed at a channel for the
first time it failed at every width **on a build nobody had changed**, and the fixture was hiding a
defect in the RULE as well as a missing arm: the check compared each column against the grid ROOT box
and subtracted no pinned section. Master pins nothing on the right, so the error was unobservable
there. **The arm that would have failed was the arm that was never run** — for the rule and for the
build. (`reference_a_fixture_pins_a_dimension`)

**Where #679's 505px actually went** (at 1440, root 1372 on both) — not the leading band, which the
channel spends 105px LESS on: 490px of non-required columns (`name` 220 + `productType` 160 +
`status` 110) sat INSIDE the required block, plus a 120px right-pinned `actions` column, minus the
cheaper left band. Cause read from source, not inferred: `orderColumnKeys` — §9.2/§9.3b's RENDER
order — had exactly two call sites, both `MasterSheet.tsx`; `ChannelSheet.tsx:84` imported only
`defaultViewColumns`. §9.3b measured this identical failure on master and fixed it there; the channel
never got the fix. **D11 was one missing shared import, not a budget to re-cut.**

**AFTER PES.3's #690** (axes behind the required block, `actions` 120 → 56) — nine of nine cells
match the hub's stated prediction, corroborated by four independent readings (three of my runs and
PES.3's own instrument, different selector set):

| coordinate | 1728 | 1440 | 1280 |
|---|---|---|---|
| master · DE/de | 7/7 (361 spare) | **7/7 (73 spare)** | 6/7 (+87) |
| master · IT/it | 7/7 (361 spare) | **7/7 (73 spare)** | 6/7 (+87) |
| Amazon · IT/it | 7/7 (410 spare) | **7/7 (122 spare)** | 6/7 (+38) |

**D11 is MET at 1440 on every coordinate**, and the asymmetry #679 opened with has reversed: at 1280
the CHANNEL is 49px better than master (284+56 beats 389+0). With the axes behind the block the
market no longer moves the verdict — master·IT is identical to master·DE at every width. What remains
at 1280 is the required block's own 910px against an 823/872px band: no chrome term is left to spend,
so it is a question about the seven declared widths and it is the hub's.

### What I got wrong, in the order I got it wrong

1. **#679's channel line was mine and is RETRACTED** (1728 7/7 · 1440 6/7 · 1280 4/7). One cause
   proven — the root-box rule, worth 120px on that scope — and it does not account for the whole gap.
   Residue recorded rather than explained away: channel `scrollWidth` read 2444 against 2599 at #679
   on an unmoved `ChannelSheet.tsx` mtime whose content cannot be diffed, because nothing is committed.
2. **I published a confound.** I called `color.scope` a master-vs-channel difference from two payloads
   differing in BOTH scope and market. PES.3 varied one at a time: it is the MARKET (`per_variant` at
   IT, `global` at DE, on both scopes). My pair could not have separated them and I concluded from it
   anyway. `master · IT/it` is now a permanent third coordinate, and the suite prints the controlled
   pair (market fixed) apart from the historical cross-variable pair, labelled so nobody reads a cause
   out of it as I did.
3. **A prediction that missed:** I said Amazon·IT 1280 would be 5/7; it measured 4/7. The shortfall
   (+262) was exact, the count was not — I missed `fabric_type` ending 42px past the band. **The
   shortfall and the fits count are different questions and getting one right is not evidence for the
   other.** PES.3 caught it independently first.
4. **I deleted a guard while moving code and did not see it go.** Moving §9.1 out of the page dropped
   its off-fixture abstain; on any non-fixture product it would have measured OUTERWEAR's seven
   against another product type's sheet — confidently, in both directions. Caught only because
   `FIXTURE` was left unreferenced. **Nothing in a diff shows an invariant that stopped existing.**
   Restored, and proven firing with `LAYOUT_PRODUCT=zzz`.

### Two defects in the instrument, both found by RUNNING it (`reference_the_quoted_exit_path_skipped_the_notice`)

- **The disturbance banner did not print on the FAILURE path.** `suspect()` was called on the
  nothing-measured and all-green exits only, so a run that was both disturbed and red printed its
  failure list in silence — the output that actually gets quoted. It would not have fired for the
  incident it was written for. Fixed, then proven on a real disturbance, not a self-test.
- **`const suspect` was scoped inside `if (measured === 0)`**, so the all-green exit threw
  `ReferenceError`. **The success path had never run to completion**, and nobody noticed because the
  suite had been red for days.

### What the runner carries now

One band-aware §9.1 (the in-page copy DELETED, not fixed beside it) · three coordinates × three
widths every run · the pinned bands, centre band, `scrollWidth` and full column SET printed beside
every verdict, because the default view admits data-dependent `flagged` keys and axes and several
lanes write this fixture — **a §9.1 reading is not a function of the build alone** · an arithmetic
closure control (`pinnedLeft + Σcentre + pinnedRight === scrollWidth`) that ABSTAINS rather than
under-report · **W-4**, deriving the required set per coordinate: master·DE 7, Amazon·IT 7, Amazon·DE
7, **eBay·IT 1** — §9.1 there is 1-of-1 and cannot fail, so W-4 asserts only where §9.1 measures and
prints the denominator elsewhere · wall-clock timestamps on every row (the hub voids by time window
and my rows carried only load) · the stamp SAMPLED BETWEEN VIEWPORTS, so a drift names the file and
the interval and a reader can keep the rows taken on one side of it · `presets.ts` (sets the `actions`
width — a term in every shortfall) and `flaggedColumns.ts` added to the stamp, having been off it.

Filed to the hub, not decided in-lane: §9.1's wording should read *required at this COORDINATE*; the
axis match is orthographic (`'colore'.includes('color')` at `views.ts:137`, while `size` matches
"Taglia" by no clause, so a family varying on two axes hoists one); rule 1 ignores `defaultVisible`;
and PES.3's observation that `color` is populated on 0 of 21 rows while the distinguishing values live
in `row.axisValues`.

### UX.1 addendum — #688 media-cell clipping, both arms on one build (15:05, `nexus-commerce-d1`)

PES.2 saved the fix at 15:02:06 before my hold reached them, so the before-state was off disk and the
hub's "signal at the before-state" could not be carried out. They offered to revert `grid.css`; I
declined — the same control is available with **no write at all**, by re-applying the pre-fix
declarations in the browser context only. One build (`grid.css` 15:02:06, 63,567 B, sha1 `62dc42db…`),
both arms, one instrument, nothing on disk.

**The reconstruction was validated, not trusted:** it reproduces PES.2's three recorded computed values
(`flex: 0 1 auto`, `min-width: auto`, width 80) and the two rect numbers PES.7 measured independently
before either of us (tile right 568, marks 571→593, 2 of 2 clipped).

| | BEFORE (reconstructed) | AFTER (live) |
|---|---|---|
| img width | 80 | **54** |
| marks span | 571 → 593 | 545 → **567** |
| past the CLIP rect | **+26** | **0 — flush** |
| clipped marks | 2 of 2 | **0 of 2** |
| hit-test at the glyph centre | `ag-cell` — glyph unreachable | the `svg` inside `.nds-media-marks` — glyph on top |

**Three corrections to the acceptance as framed.**
1. **"The 80px and 70px renditions" are neither renditions nor tile sizes.** Both media grids are
   `TILE_PX = 84` (`AmazonMatrix.tsx:64`, `EbayGrid.tsx:40`). 70px is the image width when a tile
   carries NO mark (82 − 6 gap − 6 empty strip); 80 was the floored pre-fix width; 54 is post-fix
   beside a 22px strip. **0 of 14 images here are portrait-aspect (all 168×168), so PES.7's "portrait
   already worked by accident" is UNVERIFIED and unverifiable on this surface** — an unavailable arm,
   not a passing one.
2. **+25 is +26, and the AFTER's "−1px inside" is ZERO.** Same pixels, different rect: `overflow:
   hidden` clips at the PADDING box (567), not the border box (568). Post-fix the marks land at 567
   against a clip rect of 567 — **flush, no slack**; any growth in the strip or the 6px gap re-clips
   on the first pixel. The same 1px made my own predicted image width (56) wrong against 54 — I
   subtracted from the border box, on a day spent insisting a required column is measured against the
   CONTENT band.
3. **PES.2's `.nds-media-empty` extension is a NO-OP — that box never had the bug.** 70px in both
   arms. Rather than leave it unexercised (no empty tile here carries a mark), both boxes were squeezed
   identically (`.nds-media-marks { min-width: 22px }`) under the pre-fix declarations: the **image
   refused to yield (80px, +26 over)**, the **empty box yielded on its own (54px, 0 over)**.
   `min-width: auto` is the intrinsic width on an `<img>` and min-content on a `<span>` flex container.
   "Same box, same row" was a reason to expect the behaviour, not evidence of it. Keep the line — it
   states one intent for both boxes — but it fixed nothing and should not be recorded as having.
   PES.2 asked to be told if so.

Also measured, and nobody had it: **the pre-fix row overflowed on 14 of 30 tiles, not 2** (overhangs
0 / 10 / 26px; the 10px is the twelve unmarked image tiles). Nothing visible was lost there — the
shape of the defect, not a second one.

NOT measured, plainly: any surface but the Amazon·IT matrix; the eBay bucket grid (same `TILE_PX`,
untested); any portrait asset; and whether the zero margin is acceptable — the hub's call.

**#701 follow-up — the invariant, and where it ENDS (15:1x).** The hub ruled the zero slack acceptable
because the image absorbs growth (`flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0`), which retracts my "re-clips on the
first pixel" — true of a fixed-width image, carried over to one that yields. Their arm passed exactly
as predicted; I ran two more, because an arm that can only pass is the thing this lane spent the day
arguing against. ⟦`grid.css` 15:10:04 sha1 `ad4a8e62…`, browser-only overrides, predictions written
before the run, all four exact⟧

| override | image | marks | past the clip rect | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 54 | 22 | 0 | ✅ |
| marks `min-width: 30px` | 46 | 30 | 0 | ✅ the hub's arm |
| marks `min-width: 76px` | **0** | 76 | 0 | ✅ **the boundary** |
| marks `min-width: 90px` | 0 | 90 | **+14** | ❌ 2/2 clipped |
| `gap: 20px` | 40 | 22 | 0 | ✅ |

**The invariant holds while `marks + gap ≤ 82`** (the content box) — at gap 6, a 76px strip. Beyond it
the image is exhausted and the next pixel is past the clip rect. Roughly three and a half glyphs of
headroom, so nothing near today's usage threatens it; but "the yield rule protects the mark" is
unconditional as written and conditional in fact, and the bound belongs in the ruling rather than in
whoever adds the third mark.

🔴 **"The strip clips" and "the glyph is lost" are DIFFERENT EVENTS, and both framings blurred them.**
At the 90px arm the strip overhangs 14px and the hit-test at the glyph centre still returns the `svg`
inside `.nds-media-marks` — the first glyph sits at the strip's left edge, inside the clip, and
survives. In the real BEFORE the glyph was unreachable (`elementFromPoint` → `ag-cell`). Overhang is a
fact about the STRIP; whether a given mark is lost depends on where it sits inside it. PES.7's original
finding was about the glyph, which is the stronger claim, and the acceptance should say which it means.

stated pattern — vitest here is `environment: 'node'`, so a hook cannot be rendered and the branches
belong outside it. **No behaviour of the frame changed except the count itself.**

### What was measured, not inferred

| item | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| #662 reason-first tooltip order | ✅ on screen | `"…their version.\n\n19 of 700 characters (Amazon · IT)"`, `white-space: pre-line`, `.nds-vh` === paragraph 1 |
| #663 Reload asks / cancel / confirm | ✅ both branches on screen | cancel: six properties byte-identical; confirm: value, marks, notes, counter all cleared |

| item (5) outbound sync on a `brand` write | ⚠ **NOT ANSWERED** | 0 rows — but 0 for ANY product in the window, newest queue row 2h older. The zero is vacuous |

### Six things worth not re-paying

1. **A gate can have a mode that cannot fail.** `check-raw-primitives-ratchet.mjs` is
   `process.argv[2] ?? '--census'`: run bare it prints a census and exits 0 without consulting the
   baseline. I reported three ratchets green from that mode and the hub did the same independently.
   `--check` said `MasterSheet.tsx: 0 → 1`. **Run the gate the way pre-push runs it.**
2. **A CSS collision can be decided by WEIGHT, not order.** `.nds-btn.xs` (0,2,0) beat
   `.nds-grid-sheet-help` (0,1,0) on padding; the declared `width: 18px` then lost a second time to
   flex `min-width: auto`, which floors an item at content + padding + border. The banked lesson is
   "source order beats specificity" and reaching for it first was wrong here.
3. **HMR can leave TWO elements matching one selector**, and `querySelector` hands you the stale one.
   Symptom: a computed value that contradicts the pixels, and an injected override at higher
   specificity that changes nothing. The tell is the impossible control, not the reading.
   `document.querySelectorAll(sel).length` is the one-line check.
4. **`requestAnimationFrame` never fires in this hidden Chrome window** — an `await` on a double-rAF
   hung the tab for 45 s and returned a CDP timeout. `setTimeout` everywhere until item 32.
5. **`overflow: hidden` clips at the PADDING box.** Reading the overhang against the border box gave
   +25 where it was +26, and made a flush edge look like a pixel of slack (UX.1).
6. **"Same box, same row" is a reason to expect behaviour, not evidence of it.** I extended #688 to
   `.nds-media-empty` on that analogy; measured, it never had the bug — `min-width: auto` is the
   intrinsic width on an `<img>` and min-content on a `<span>`. The line is kept as intent and
   **fixed nothing**. It went in because I treated an analogy as a measurement.

### PES.7 (`nexus-commerce-ac`) — #708 / P12 LANDED: image writes are filed by subject, 15:48

**The defect, precisely.** `useImageWorkspace.write()` called `reporter.pending(id)` with a fresh
`img-N` and **no subject**, and `ledgerPending`/`ledgerResolved` fall back to the write id when the
subject is absent (`saveState.ts:52,59`). Every attempt was therefore filed under a key nothing could
match again: a refused alt-text edit stayed in `failed` forever, and re-saving the SAME picture
successfully ADDED a key rather than clearing one. The images header counted a history of attempts,
unclearable by any gesture on the page. Same shape PES.2 fixed on the sheet at #699; images had no
row concept, which is why it was missed.

**The subject vocabulary I chose (delegated to me by #708 — overrule it and I will re-point it).**
Three kinds, built in `imageWrites.ts` rather than spelled at 21 call sites so a typo is a compile
error and not a subject that silently never matches its retry:
- `asset:<rowId>` — one existing picture or video (alt text, delete, hero, derived crop).
- `upload:<name>` — work with no row id yet: a file by name, `dam:<assetId>`, `ai:<prompt slice>`. A
  retry of the same file is the same subject, which is what lets a successful re-upload clear the
  first attempt's refusal.
- `surface:<name>` — a write about a SET (bulk save, reorder, publish, restore), keyed **per surface,
  never per endpoint**: `amazon-matrix`, `ebay-grid`, `amazon-bulk-apply`, `publish-settings-restore`
  all POST to `bulkSave`, and one landing must not clear another's refusal. Cross-channel publish is
  `surface:publish:<target.key>`.

**Scope, counted rather than described:** 21 call sites given a subject, **18 mirrored prop
signatures** updated (every consumer restates `write<T>(run…)` as its own prop type — a local mirror
of the hook's type, which is why the compiler, not a grep, is what proves none was missed), 16
imports added. Each replacement asserted `count == 1` before the file was written. `grep` for
`write(() =>` and for `write<T>(run:` in `images/**` now returns nothing.

**Evidence.**
- **8 tests** in `imageWrites.vitest.test.ts`, driving `reportedWrite` — the same function the hook
  calls — against the REAL `../saveState` ledger, because `apps/web` vitest is `environment: 'node'`
  and the hook cannot be rendered. Refusal → success on one asset ends at **0 unsaved**.
- **Mutation, because a green suite proves the suite.** Dropping `subject` from the two reporter
  calls (exactly the pre-#708 code) turns **4 of 8 red**, and the CONTROL test — which reproduces the
  defect deliberately — stays green, as it must. File restored byte-identical (sha compared).
- Full `apps/web` suite **195 files / 2781 tests pass**; images tree 21 files / 331 tests.
- **Typecheck**: `scripts/typecheck-scoped.mjs` over all 22 files — clean in 2.7 s (it caught one
  real error first, an unused import, now fixed). The runner warns it cannot see CONSUMERS of an
  exported signature, so I enumerated them instead of assuming: `useImageWorkspace`/
  `ImageWorkspaceApi` is imported by exactly one file, `ImagesTab.tsx`, which was in the scope, and
  nothing outside `images/` passes a `write=` prop.
- **DS guards**: all four exit 0. Not vacuously — the whole `_studio/images` tree is UNTRACKED, so I
  checked the enumerator rather than trusting the pass: `check-raw-primitives-ratchet.mjs:55-56` runs

not by touching the stylesheets** (`design-system/tools/token-guard.mjs`, 15:48:31; the three sheets
still carry mtimes 13:47:59 / 08:37:55 / 08:37:55 and **all three explanatory comments survive**,
which was the whole point).

The "raw hex" it found was **`#617` — the hub ruling number inside a trailing comment.**
`commentMask` classified a WHOLE LINE as comment or code; a comment that opens MID-LINE after a
declaration (`font-size: 14.5px; /* … hub #617 left it literal */`) starts with code, so the line
read as code. **This is the third instance of a banked lesson** (`reference_scanner_false_positive_worse`:
"Strip comments before scanning code. Twice now") and the second of the guard's own documented
failure mode — *the guard pressures the author to delete the explanation*, and here the explanation
is the one naming the ruling that blessed the literal.

**The fix strips comment SPANS, not lines** — `codeOnly(lines, lineComments)` blanks each comment
span to spaces (line count, line numbers and columns preserved); all four checks (hex / ramp /
Tailwind / platform-alias) now scan that instead of the raw line. Strings stay CODE on purpose —
`color: '#ff0000'` in a `.tsx` IS a violation — and are tracked only so the `//` of an https URL
cannot blank a line's tail, which is exactly the false negative DS.1-b warned me not to trade for.
`//` counts as a comment in TS/TSX only; in CSS a hex after one still fails.

**It also closed a false NEGATIVE nobody had reported:** a block comment CLOSING mid-line
(`/* note */ color: #123456;`) marked the whole line comment under the old mask and **hid real code
after it**. The bug report was a false positive; the same defect was silently swallowing violations
in the other direction.

**`--self-test`, eight cases, both directions** (DS.1-b asked for exactly this): a ruling number in a
trailing comment is NOT a hex · a real hex in code still fails · a real hex fails even with a comment
on the same line · a hex inside a multi-line block is ignored · code after a mid-line close still
fails · a `//` line comment in TS is not scanned · a URL in a TS string does not blank the line ·
`//` is not a comment in CSS. **8/8 green.**

**🔴 And the control that makes that green mean something:** I ran the same eight cases against the
OLD `commentMask` (scratch script, verbatim copy) — **2 of 8 FAIL**: case 1, the reported false
positive, and case 5, the unreported false negative. *A guard that cannot fail is not a guard, and a
self-test that passes on the broken implementation is a restatement, not a check.* Run as the gate
runs it (`node apps/web/src/design-system/tools/token-guard.mjs`, no flags, `.githooks/pre-push:282`):
**exit 0**, push no longer blocked on this.

### PES.7 (`nexus-commerce-ac`) — #708 THE PIXEL, and a correction to my own #649 claim, 15:56

**#708 verified on screen.** Amazon·IT images tab, viewport 1728×906. A fetch interceptor installed
IN THE PAGE matched `/live-channel-images/refresh` and returned a synthetic `Response` **without
calling the original fetch**, so nothing on that path left the browser and no data was written.
Two clicks of "Check Amazon", two intercepted calls:
- forced **409** → header: **"1 change not saved"**, `title` carrying the refusal's own words
  ("Forced 409 — PES.7 #708 probe…"), and the panel's refusal banner on screen.
- forced **200** on the retry → header: **"Saved 15:54"**, `title` "1 change saved this session",
  refusal banner gone. **0 unsaved.** Screenshots taken of both states.
`window.fetch` restored (`[native code]` confirmed), tab closed. What I did NOT do: instrument the
server to prove nothing arrived — the evidence is that the interceptor returns before `orig` on the
matching path and that 2 clicks produced exactly 2 matches.

**🔴 CORRECTION to my 14:2x #649 filing, and it is an over-claim in the same direction as the one it
was itself correcting.** I reported that the media provenance mark "is not painted at all" on the
Amazon matrix, from a measurement showing the two real `pinned` marks laid out at x 574–585 with
their tile ending at 568 (`overflow:hidden` → clipped), and I sent that to PES.2 as the reason its
one-liner mattered more. **Measured again today at 15:53 on the SAME tile at the SAME viewport
(1728×906, tile l=484 r=568): the mark is at 548–559 — INSIDE, `insideTile: true`, 9px of margin —
and the pencil is plainly visible in the screenshot.** What differs is the image: 80px wide when the
mark was clipped, 54px wide when it fits. The tile is `flex` with `gap:6` in an 84px box and the
marks span is `flex:0 0 auto`, so whether the mark has room depends on whether the `img` shrank —
and that resolved differently between two page loads of the same route at the same size.

~~So the honest statement is neither "invisible" nor "fine": the provenance mark on a media tile is
clipped or not depending on how the image's flex sizing resolves on that load, and both outcomes
occur on the same tile at the same viewport.~~ **STRUCK 16:00 — wrong, and wrong in a way my own lane
rules name.** Hub #689: the two readings are on two BUILDS, not two loads. PES.2 landed **#688 at
15:02:06** in `grid.css` — `.nds-media-img { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0 }` — which is exactly why the
image now shrinks to 54px and the 22px marks strip fits. Verified here, not accepted: the rule is
present at `grid.css:618`, and the file's mtime has moved off the **13:30:12** I recorded on my own
read path at 14:0x (it now reads 15:57:26, so PES.2 has touched it again since my 15:53 measurement —
that measurement is of a build between 15:02:06 and 15:57:26, not of the current bytes).

So: my 14:2x reading (img 80px, mark at 574–585, clipped) is TRUE of the pre-#688 build, and my 15:53
reading (img 54px, mark at 548–559, pencil visible) is TRUE of the fixed one. Nothing to retract in
either measurement and no A/B to run. What was wrong was the INFERENCE — I compared two numbers
across two builds and called the difference nondeterminism, when the lane rule I was given says every
number carries its BUILD and a "done" is checked by content. One `stat` on the file I had already
recorded at 13:30:12 would have settled it before I filed a correction, told two lanes, and banked a
memory. The `:582` border one-liner is unaffected and still stands.
