### 🔴 PES.5 — the audit log cannot ENUMERATE writes; a CAS chain can (evidence for #764)

Third message to the hub dropped in delivery tonight, so this goes here. **New content**, not a
repeat of the entry above.

UX.1 put it to the hub that #764's `4 → 7` reconstruction — three audit rows matched to three
version increments — is "consistent, not proof", because a formula save increments `Product.version`
and writes no audit row, so an unaudited write could hide among them. **The principle is correct and
worth banking. The specific conclusion is not, and the reconstruction survives.**

**The identification never rested on the audit rows.** It rests on the CAS token chain, measured:

> `4/SUCCESS → 5/SUCCESS → 6/SUCCESS`

A CAS write succeeds only when the row is at exactly the version it carries. Write 2 carried **5**
and SUCCEEDED, so nothing bumped between writes 1 and 2; write 3 carried **6** and succeeded, so
nothing bumped between 2 and 3. Three contiguous successful tokens with the row ending at 7 leave no
room for a fourth increment. An unaudited formula save interleaved there would have carried a stale
token and returned **409**, not SUCCESS.

**The bounded statement:**
- The **audit log cannot enumerate** writes — an absence in it is not evidence of no write.
- A **contiguous, all-SUCCESS CAS chain CAN enumerate**, within its own window, because any
  unrecorded write breaks it.
- The window here is only `4 → 7`. Writes outside are unconstrained — which is exactly why UX.1's
  17:53:44Z formula save is invisible: it sits BEFORE the chain and is what put the row at 4.

**Verified for UX.1's demonstration case:** the audit log holds nothing on that entity between
17:50:00Z and 17:54:10Z, so their claimed, stack-traced formula PUT genuinely left no row.

**For the pending ruling:** a new `formula.set` audit row wants the CAS token as well as the `ip`.
With `ip` alone a save becomes attributable but stays invisible to any reconstruction; with the token
it becomes enumerable too. Neither instrument alone reaches the answer.

### 🔴 THE ONE THING TO READ FIRST — AG 36 React editors

`ag-grid-react@36`'s `CellEditorComponentProxy` **owns the edited value**. An editor must call
`props.onValueChange(v)`; a `getValue` on an imperative handle is **never called**, and neither
`getValue` nor `isPopup` is in the optional-method copy-list `useGridCellEditor` honours
(`isCancelBeforeStart · isCancelAfterEnd · focusIn · focusOut · afterGuiAttached ·
getValidationErrors · getValidationElement`). Consequences already paid for:
- `SelectPanelEditor` had **never committed through AG** — proven with a witnessed RED (a real select
  change issued no request at all) and fixed with one `onValueChange` call.
- `isPopup` must live in the ColDef as `cellEditorPopup: true`.
- AG also owns **Enter, Tab and Escape** inside a popup editor; no React handler can take them.
  Three mechanisms were tried and measured failing. Design around them.

🔴 **THE FINDING: the sheet contract and the formula writer disagree, and they are asked DIFFERENT
QUESTIONS.** Full round trip captured on `batteries_included`:

```
→ POST /pim/formulas/preview   {fieldKey:"batteries_included", expr:"\"banana\"", scope:"channel", channel:"AMAZON", marketplace:"IT", market:"IT"}
← 200  {ok:true, value:"banana", error:null}          ← evaluated happily; NOT checked against the 2 allowed options
→ PUT  /pim/formulas/product/cmokmy0jf…2yy  {fieldKey:"batteries_included", …}
← 400  {"error":"\"batteries_included\" is not a channel field a formula can write."}
```

The contract computes `formulaWritable` from the ROUTED name —
`studio-sheet.service.ts:1378 isChannelWritable(r.writeField)` with `writeField:
attr_batteries_included` → **true**. The writer gates on the RAW key the client sends —
`cell-formula.service.ts:346 isChannelWritable(coord.fieldKey)` with `fieldKey:
batteries_included` → **false**. The `#758` comment says "one gate per scope, each asked of the
writer that enforces it"; the gate is the same function asked with two different arguments, which is
[[reference_a_comment_asserts_property_code_lacks]] in its purest form.

**Scale, measured not guessed:** every `attr_*`-routed column is affected — on Amazon·IT that is the
20 selects and 10 numbers of the 73 the UI now offers. The columns the writer WOULD accept by raw key
(`amazon_title`, `amazon_description`, `amazon_variationTheme`) are master-routed and therefore
`formulaWritable: false`, so the editor never opens on them. **The set the UI offers and the set the
writer accepts are very nearly disjoint on this scope.** Master is unaffected: there the column key
IS the gated name.

Server-side, so not mine to fix. Recommendation to the Owner: the writer should apply the same
routing the contract used before gating, and keep STORING under the column key — storing under the
routed name would break `exprFor(rowId, col.key)` and every formula cell would open empty.

~~**Honesty of the refusal** … the server's sentence appears NOWHERE on the page.~~

🔴 **RETRACTED — the sentence IS on the page, verbatim, and my instrument could not see it.** Three
successive probes each failed differently and each produced a confident "absent": a leaf-node DOM
walk cannot see a sentence split across children; `body.innerText` does not include `title`
attributes, which is exactly where `describeSaveState` puts it (`saveState.ts:203`, "The server's own
sentence, verbatim"); and a regex written for one error message cannot match a different one. Asking
for the server's EXACT sentence, captured from the response, found it at once:
`<span class="…saveState" title="unexpected \"99\" (at character 9)">`. The header's count and the
kept cell text were honest all along, and so was the reason. PES.2's contract says the reason rides with the kept text.
Mine to fix once the gate disagreement is settled, since the reason to show is currently the wrong
one.

**Files changed (3, all tooling):** `apps/web/src/design-system/tools/token-guard.mjs` ·

**1. 🔴 The finding P14 did not have: BOTH copies said `const ROOT = 'apps/web/src/design-system'`.**
The factory copy did not merely lag (Aug-25, 4,358 B) — **it scanned WEB.** So factory's design
system has never been checked by this guard in any version, and its "172 violations" were web's
tree read with the old buggy logic. Wiring the copy up as it stood would have produced a confident
green about a tree it never opened. *A scanner aimed one app away is the vacuous pass that looks
most like coverage.*

**Fixed by deriving the anchors from the file's own location** (`import.meta.url`), which also makes
the two copies **byte-identical** — the hardcoded path was the only thing that had ever differed, and
removing it is what lets fork-drift hold them. Two things came with it, neither optional:
- `REPO` (for `git ls-files`) is anchored to the file too, **not `process.cwd()`**. With an absolute
  ROOT and a cwd-derived tracking set, the walk succeeds while every lookup misses and every file is
  skipped — ✓ over a tree it never read. **Control: mis-anchor `REPO` → exit 1**, and the guard now
  runs identically from `/tmp` (166 files), which it could not do before.
- The corpus size is printed on both branches and **`scanned === 0` is a FAILURE**. There is no
  legitimate state in which this tool has nothing to look at.

**2. FACTORY'S DS MEASURED FOR THE FIRST TIME: 332 violations / 105 files — and 328 of them are NOT
work.** They are one check (D, platform aliases) whose premise is **web-specific**: it exists because
web defines those names as **RGB channel triplets** (`--surface-card: 255 255 255`), so `var()`-ing
one raw yields an invalid declaration that is DROPPED. **Factory defines all 20 as real colours**
(`--surface-card: var(--nds-surface)`, …) — they resolve. Converting them would churn 328 working
declarations. **Do not route that as a task.** The durable fix, if the check is ever pointed at both
apps, is to test the PROPERTY (does this alias resolve to a channel triplet?) rather than the NAME.

**3. The 4 real ones are an unprotected FORK DRIFT in a live component.**
`styles/primitives.css:590` — factory's `.nds-tooltip--light > .tip` still carries `#ffffff` /
`#1e293b` / `#e2e8f0`; **web tokenised the same block** to `--nds-tooltip-light-bg` / `-fg` /
`-border`. `styles/primitives.css` is **FROZEN in `ds-fork-baseline.json`**, so nothing could see it
— the exact shape of `reference_ds_fork_guard_blind_to_stylesheets`. Live in both apps
(factory `primitives/ToolbarButton.tsx:150`).

**`-bg` and `-border` are UNDEFINED in factory.** A naive hex → `var()` swap leaves two invalid

hand-edit is erased by the next regen**), then swap the stylesheet. 48's new

**→ DS.2** (factory token files are theirs). Values to match web: `-bg: var(--nds-white)`,

**P16 — `ListboxPanel` takes an external active index; existing consumers untouched.** New optional
props, all no-ops when absent: `activeIndex` (controlled highlight), `onActiveIndexChange`,
`onMatchesChange` (the flat ranked+grouped list — the ONLY honest index space, because the panel
re-ranks what it is given and a caller counting its own array counts a different one), `idPrefix`
(option ids so a caller holding focus elsewhere can point `aria-activedescendant` at the row; without
it a screen reader follows focus, which never moves).

## PES.2 (`nexus-commerce-9f`) — #752 SOLVED: the reveal was reading a layout 46 ms before it settled (2026-09-03)

**HEAD `80f6cfb84`, nothing committed. 2951/2951 tests, tsc clean (whole `apps/web`), four DS gates `--check` exit 0.**
Files: `_studio/drawer/revealHost.ts` `061fa8de…` (new) · `_studio/sheet/master/MasterSheet.tsx` `cfac797e…` · `_studio/drawer/index.ts` `f9587426…`

### 1 · The hoist the Owner asked for

`revealColumn` is out of `MasterSheet.tsx` and into `_studio/drawer/revealHost.ts`, beside `revealStash`
— one host rule, exported from the drawer barrel. `revealCell.ts` (pure, node-testable) is unchanged;
only the DOM-touching half moved. **`ChannelSheet.tsx` still holds its own inline copy** — that is
PES.3's file and the adoption is a one-line call change, sent to them separately.

It carries a **dev-only trace** in a ring buffer at `window.__ndsRevealTrace` as well as the console,
because a probe that reads `console` must install itself before the load it wants to watch, and on a
cold deep link that is the one thing it cannot do.

### 2 · 🔴 The #752 premise was FALSE, and every lane including me built on it

The narrowed question was *"why is `panelOverlap` 0 on a cold `?rec=&cell=` load when the panel is
present with `data-resting-left`"*. **`panelOverlap` is not 0. It is 519, and it always was.**
Measured, cold load, 1280, master·DE·it, `?cell=bullet_point`:

`readiness: 'at'` · `panelLeft: 760` · `panelOverlap: 519` · `viewportRight: 1279`

Every input to the rule was correct. There was no unmounted panel and no missing measurement.
I had also derived a second candidate from `panelOverlap`'s source (`max(0, gridRight − panelLeft)`
is 0 whenever `gridRight ≤ panelLeft`) — **also wrong.** Both hypotheses were about the panel, and
the panel was never the subject.

### 3 · What it actually was, on one tape

The identity band mounts at `BAND_WIDTH_FLOOR` (240) and derives its real width from content.
Sampling the pinned block and the target column together, one cold load:

| t | pinned block | `bullet_point` |
|---|---|---|
| 698 ms | 43 + **240** = 283 | 510 → **620** |
| 744 ms | 43 + **404** = 447 | 674 → **784** |

The stashed reveal replayed **inside that 46 ms window**. It read `cellRight: 620` against a panel at
760, correctly concluded "clear by 140", returned `distance: 0` — and **retired the stash as served**.
The cell settles at 784. The panel starts at 760. **Covered by 24px**, which is UX.1's unexplained
figure to the pixel.

The far-column arm is the same number: the shortfall is 404 − 240 = **164**, and
164 − `REVEAL_MARGIN`(16) = **148** — the "writes 136 and stops 148 short" logged beside it.
One quantity explains both arms.

**It was a STALE measurement, not a missing one.** From the outcome the two are identical: a grid
that did not move. That is why a day of instruments aimed at the panel could not separate them —
they all measured the outcome, and the outcome is what both hypotheses agree on.

### 4 · The fix, and a wrong first version worth recording

`revealColumn` takes a **required** `bandReady`; false ⇒ `pending`, stash survives — the same answer
the panel already gets one branch up, for the second thing that arrives late.

🔴 **My first fix did not work and the trace caught it.** I replayed synchronously right after
`setColumnWidths` — and measured the replay *still* reading `viewportLeft: 350`, 124 ms later.
Asking for a width is not the width changing: `setBandWidth` lands through a React render of
`autoGroupColumnDef`, and the pinned column's id is **`ag-Grid-AutoColumn`, not `product`**, so the
`setColumnWidths(['product'])` call is not what moves it either. The replay now rides
`onDisplayedColumnsChanged` / `onColumnResized` — AG saying the columns **have** moved.

Stated cost: a band that can never be derived would now strand the reveal forever, where it used to
serve wrongly. `remeasureSoon` therefore **releases** the gate when its retry budget is exhausted.

### 5 · Verified on screen, both arms, cold load at 1280 (prediction written before the run)

| `?cell=` | distance | wrote | settled right edge | panel | clearance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bullet_point` | 40 | 40 | 744 | 760 | **16** |
| `supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation` | 300 | 300 | 744 | 760 | **16** |

Both land exactly one `REVEAL_MARGIN` clear; `unreachableBy: 0`; `viewportEl` `.ag-grid-viewport.ag-layout-normal`.
Before: 784 (covered 24) and 136-written/148-short. Screenshots taken.

### 6 · 🔴 Correction to a constraint I put in the ledger and made other lanes carry

**`resize_window` DOES work.** I recorded it as broken in this environment and asked UX.1 to take
every 1280 reading for me. It fails only against a **background** tab; taking a screenshot first
activates the tab and it then resizes correctly (`innerWidth: 1280`, verified). This is the
hidden-tab trap wearing a different coat, and I mis-attributed it to the tool. UX.1 does not need to
carry my width runs.

Two probe caveats from these runs, neither a page defect: a "buffer stable for 2 s" predicate broke
**before** the grid had laid out (`maxScroll: 0`) and showed 1 of 2 entries; and
`.ag-body-horizontal-scroll-viewport` read `scrollLeft: 0` long after the settled scroll of 300 —
the cell rects, not that element, are what confirm a scroll.

### 9 · A defect the blocked-branch attempt found instead (fixed)

Trying to exercise `formulaWritable: false` on `condition_type`, **no editor opened for `=`, for a
plain `N`, or for Enter** — and the cell's class list carried `nds-cell-is-editable` throughout.
The wire says `editable: false`, so AG is right to refuse; the CLASS was the lie.

applies AND the cell's own flag). The class rule was testing only the middle one. An "equivalent"
predicate re-derived one line from the real one, diverging exactly where it mattered.

Both rules now use `cellIsEditable`. Verified on screen, both arms:
`amazonAsin` / `ebayItemId` / `parentAsin` (`editable: false`) → **locked**, 3/3;
`ean` / `gtin` / `model_name` / `part_number` (`editable: true`) → **editable**, 4/4.
(`upc` was virtualised out of the body — not a mismatch, not a reading.)

### #775/PES.4 — the drawer seam landed with a DECLARATIVE refusal, and the A/B that proves it (PES.3)

Build: `ChannelSheet.tsx` 07:10:15, 102,840 B, sha1 `71a68b937df7f5b56e17a1e9b79757337651881f`.
`tsc --noEmit` exit 0; all four DS guards exit 0.

Landed three lines, not two: `formulas={formulas}`, `onFormulaSaved={() => reload()}`, and PES.4's new
`writesRefused`. **The third is why the first two are safe.** This scope's dock refuses writes on
purpose — the sheet owns the cascade and the writer — and `FormulaField` references `onWrite` zero
times by design, so without a declarative signal the drawer would have offered a live formula write
three lines under its own refusal. PES.4 confirmed from their source that `RecordField`'s `editable`
derives only from cell and column facts; and my "make the field read `onWrite`" suggestion was not
implementable — a host that refuses WHOLESALE can only be discovered by CALLING `onWrite`, and
calling it is the write.

⚠ ONE constant (`DRAWER_READ_ONLY`), read by both `onWrite`'s message and `writesRefused` — not the
same sentence typed twice, which would drift the first time either was reworded and leave the drawer
explaining a refusal in words the refusal does not use.

**A/B on this scope, because the first control was worthless.**

| arm | build | ƒ controls in the drawer | buttons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | `writesRefused` present | **0** | 33 |
| B (control) | flag removed | **6 × "Write a formula"** | 39 |

Six controls, six buttons of difference. The control build was restored byte-identical afterwards
(sha1 back to `71a68b93…`), and `tsc` re-run clean.

🔴 **Two false negatives before that, both mine, both the same shape.** My first control was master
scope — which has not landed the seam, so "no ƒ there either" measured nothing. My second was worse:
I CONSTRUCTED the deep-link row id as `':<productId>'` when `aliasKeyOf(null)` returns **`'primary'`**,
so every drawer probe I had run was reading a panel saying *"That record is not on the current page
of the sheet"* — an EMPTY drawer, in both arms, which is why removing the flag changed nothing and
briefly looked like the flag was inert. **Constructing an id from source instead of reading it from
the running app is the same class of error as constructing a control from an assumption.** The probe
now refuses to report on an unresolved drawer at all.

**#752 re-run on the real path** (the earlier trace had the same malformed id — the panel was open
and measured, so the finding never depended on it, but it is re-taken rather than argued): identical
tape, `band-not-derived` → `scrolled` wrote 40, cell at rest **clear by 16**.

**NOT measured, and blocked:** PES.4's deliberate exception — a STORED formula still DISPLAYS under
the flag, read-only. I agree with it (hiding the rule behind a computed value is the hazard
`formulaAvailability`'s "always available" arm exists to prevent), but I cannot witness it on this
scope until PES.5's fix lands: no channel column can hold a stored formula today, `brand` included —
it is `formulaWritable` because it routes to master, and the writer still refuses the raw key.

### #775 — locked cells now LOOK locked on the channel scope (PES.3)

Found by PES.2's cross-check request, from the OPPOSITE direction to their own defect: master had the
class and derived it from the wrong predicate (`applies()` rather than `cellIsEditable`); **this scope
had no class at all** — every field column rendered `nds-ag-cell` and nothing else.

**Measured on the wire before the fix, Amazon·IT, GALE-JACKET: 236 of 2,037 cells (12%) across 16
columns are not editable** — `sku`, `condition_type`, `amazonAsin`, `parentAsin`, `buyBoxPrice`,
`competitorPrice`, `shippingTemplate`, the variation axes — and all of them rendered exactly like a
cell an operator can type into. The server even supplies the sentence ("Read-only on this channel —
the marketplace does not accept a value for this field."), which reached the tooltip and nothing
else. A sheet that shows 236 cells as writable and then swallows the keystroke breaks the honest-UI
rule in the quietest way there is.

Fix: two `cellClassRules` entries derived from `isCellEditable` — **the same predicate AG's own
`editable` prop uses two dozen lines above**, not a second rule that agrees today. Re-deriving it
would have reproduced PES.2's bug rather than avoided it.

**Verified on screen** (scan across the full `scrollWidth`, computed colours):

| | columns | computed colour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| locked | `color` (9), `size` (9) — the variation axes on rows with no single value | `rgb(98, 108, 123)` |
| editable | `brand` 42, `bullet_point` 42, `item_name` 84, `country_of_origin` 42, … | `rgb(28, 37, 48)` |

The two differ, so the DS's `--nds-grid-locked-fg` (`grid.css:511`) is reaching the cells that earned
it. `sku`/`amazonAsin`/`buyBoxPrice` are NOT in the default view, so this run witnessed the axis case
only — the other 14 columns are asserted from the wire flags and the shared predicate, not seen.

**#775 — the `=` keystroke arm, verified with a control (PES.3).** PES.4 stated that a read-only
scope never opens the formula panel at all; checked rather than accepted, since it is a claim about
my scope. Drawer resolution witnessed first (the empty-drawer trap that broke my earlier A/B):

| arm | action | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| drawer, `writesRefused` set | `=` into a focused drawer field | **0** formula editors anywhere; field text unchanged |
| CONTROL, same page, same key | `=` into a sheet cell | **1** formula editor |

So the suppression covers the keystroke path as well as the ƒ button, and the instrument can detect

### #775 — the allowed-option rule is implemented TWICE, and the two disagree (PES.3 → PES.5)

Found by noticing that a refusal sentence I measured at 04:40:50Z did not match one at 05:33:39Z for
the same rule on the same field. Both live in `cell-formula.service.ts`:

| | **A** — `optionRefusal` (`:121`), called at `:509`/`:741` | **B** — inside `evaluateAgainstContext` (`:364`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| matching | EXACT only (`options.includes`) | exact **or case-insensitive**, on a `.trim()`ed value |
| shown values | raw option codes, 8 then `… (N in all)` | localised **labels** via `optionLabels`, 6 then `(+N more)` |
| returns | `{error, allowedOptions, actualValue}` — **the agreed refusal contract** | `{value: null, error}` — neither field |
| sentence | `"maybe" is not an allowed value for Are batteries included? — choose one of: true, false` | `"banana" is not an accepted value. This field takes: No · Sì.` |

**Measured, two data points, same field `batteries_included`:** my channel·IT write hit **B**; a
master·DE write at 05:33:39Z hit **A**. They are mutually exclusive by construction — A is guarded
`outcome.error ? null : optionRefusal(...)`, so if B refuses, A never runs.

🔴 **The divergence is behavioural, not cosmetic.** `"TRUE"` or `" true"` is ACCEPTED by B and
REFUSED by A. So the same input can be valid or invalid depending on which path evaluates it — and
only A returns the `allowedOptions`/`actualValue` the drawer and sheet were promised, so a refusal
through B cannot render the contract PES.2/PES.4 built against.

**Recommendation (not a ruling — PES.5's file):** one check. A's shape carries the agreed contract, so
it is the natural survivor; but B's leniency is a real question rather than a bug to delete — if
case-insensitive, trimmed matching is wanted, A should adopt it, and if it is not, B has been
silently accepting values the store should refuse. Either way it must be decided once.

**NOT verified:** the selector that chooses between the two paths. I have two measured data points
(channel→B, master→A) and the code structure; I did not confirm that scope is what selects, and it
may be the field SOURCE (mapped field vs sheet column) rather than the scope.

**Also recorded: activity continues after every disclosure.** The 05:33:39Z row is
`batteries_included = "maybe"` on 4XL, master·DE, `refused: true`, followed by a pin at 05:33:48Z.

### 🔴 ENVIRONMENT — the restarted web server points at the DEPLOYED PRODUCTION API (PES.3, 07:45)

Found because my success arm timed out waiting for `.ag-row` after the 07:38 restart. Not my code, and
not a probe fault:

**Measured.** Every API call from a studio page load goes to
`https://nexusapi-production-b7bb.up.railway.app/api/...` — all **401** — and the page renders
"Couldn't open this product". 0 rows, 0 grid roots. My first diagnostic stripped the host from those
URLs and so could not see it; capturing the FULL url is what found it.

**Cause** — `apps/web/src/lib/backend-url.ts:11-13`:
```ts
const raw = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'https://nexusapi-production-b7bb.up.railway.app'
```
**The fallback IS production.** A dev web server started without `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` silently talks
to the deployed API. Discriminator: the Railway API returns **401** unauthenticated while the local
one returns **200**, and my pre-restart probes rendered 21 rows — so the old process had the variable
and the new one does not. (`ps eww` shows 0 vars for pid 65293, so this is inferred from behaviour,
not read from the process.)

🔴 **The hazard is larger than the outage.** A local dev browser was pointed at production. The 401 is
accidentally protective — but had any lane held a session on that API, **UI writes from a dev browser
would have gone to the deployed production API over the network.** Every rehearsal-write protocol in
this programme assumes the local API; that assumption was silently false for ~10 minutes.

**A design point for the Owner, not a ruling:** a fallback that defaults to PRODUCTION means "no
configuration" resolves to "the real system". The safe direction is the opposite — fail loudly, or
default to localhost in development — because the failure mode here is silent, and it is silent in
exactly the direction that can do damage. `getBackendUrl` is not my file.

⚠ **A retraction this forces.** My "publish mode is `gated`" derivation used pid **4859**'s
environment (47 vars visible, none of them the publish flags). That process is gone and `ps eww`
returns 0 vars for its replacement 65327, so the process half of that derivation is no longer
verifiable. The `.env`-file half stands. Recorded as reduced, not as still-measured
([[reference_a_banked_rule_can_go_false]]).

**Also relevant to every "route is fine" check:** `/products/:id/edit/studio` returned **200 in 0.39s**
throughout. The route compiled perfectly; it was talking to the wrong backend. A 200 on the route is
not evidence the page works.

ColDef is built before any editor exists. On the base `def`, so all six branches inherit it.

### 21 · The save verdict extracted and pinned against a MEASURED refusal

UX.1 confirmed both 4XL rows as register entries 6–7 and handed over the shape that matters:

> **the refusal arrives as HTTP 200 with `ok: false`** — value not written, formula KEPT with its
> error, cell showing the reason with a warn class.

My hook already read the body rather than the status, so nothing was broken — but the rule lived
**inline in a `useCallback`**, where this repo's vitest cannot reach it. Same shape as
`completionToAccept` before §18: correct, and untestable. Extracted to `formulaSaveOutcome(body)` in
`formulaEditing.ts` and pinned against the payload UX.1 measured on a live case rather than one I
invented:

```
200 {"ok":false, lastError:'"maybe" is not an allowed value for Are batteries included?
                            — choose one of: true, false'}
```

**Mutation-verified on the discriminating line.** `body?.ok === false` is deliberately not `!body?.ok`:
a payload that OMITS the flag is not a refusal, and the loose form would report every older response
as refused. Mutating it fails 2 of 5 (`expected {ok:false} to deeply equal {ok:true}`); restored
byte-identically. Full suite now **2981** across 205 files.

🔴 **The general rule, from a live case rather than a doctrine:** a probe that reads the STATUS
records this refusal as a success, and the cell would stamp "saved" over a value that was never
written. Status AND body — and this is the second time tonight a 200 was true about the wrong thing
(PES.4's DELETE returned `{"pinned":true}` and HTTP 200 while their own autosave put the formula
straight back).

**UX.1's own correction is worth keeping too:** their published expression list
(`upper($brand)`, `1+1`, `"false"`) was accurate when published and stale within the hour, because
entries 6–7 came after it. **A published member list is a snapshot, not a standing fact** — the same
shape as a hardcoded token list going stale, and the reason asking beat inferring.

They have also closed the blind spot my Railway incident exposed: a new **W-5 backend-origin** check
collects every `/api/` origin the page dials and fails the run on a mismatch, carrying the explicit
restart command in its failure text. Their first version compared origin STRINGS and reded on a clean
run — the page dials `localhost:8091`, their constant is `127.0.0.1:8091`, one listener with two
names — so it now compares resolved host:port with loopback aliases unified, proven green **and** red.
An identifier's form is not an identity, caught inside the guard written to catch a different form of
exactly that.

### 5 · 🔴 For the Owner — one design point I did NOT decide

Design rule 1 also says "fall back to a queue for large fan-outs (**> 50 dependants**)". I did not
build it, because the file's own reasoning argues the opposite and I will not silently pick a side:
`reevaluateDependents` is documented as synchronous *because* "a product has ≤ ~100 fields, and a
job would break 'the value you see is the value that was stored'". A queue also cannot be verified
here — local dev has no Redis, so a queue-backed path is inert and would look identical to a
working one. Half-building it is the "flag that is accepted but ignored" shape. **Which holds — the
50-dependant queue fallback, or synchronous always?**

Also NOT built (not mine, and not claimed): the client repaint the design costs at half a day of
PES.2 — a recalculated cell currently needs a re-read to repaint. And the reader half of the
re-entrancy guard has no UNIT test; it is covered by the live rehearsal above, where an unhonoured
header would have recursed instead of answering in 55 ms.

### 6 · 🟢 OWNER RULING, 2026-09-03 — recalculation is SYNCHRONOUS, ALWAYS

The design draft's rule 1 recommended a queue fallback above 50 dependants. **Refused.** No
threshold, no cap, no deferral: every dependant re-evaluates in the request that wrote the source,
whatever the fan-out. Nothing had to be removed — I had not built the fallback — but the ruling is
now written into all three places that could drift apart:

- **The code.** A 🔴 block on `reevaluateDependents` states the ruling and why re-introducing a
  threshold would be wrong (the walk's own premise; and a queue path is INERT here with no Redis,
  so a fallback would look identical to a working one while dropping the tail of the fan-out).
- **The design doc** (`docs/2026-09-02-formula-recalculation-design.md`, sha1 `eceaa715`): rule 1's
  queue clause struck through with the ruling quoted beneath it, and the stale
  `**Status:** design only. Nothing built.` header corrected to what is actually built. A doc that
  keeps recommending what was refused is the "doc describing code that never shipped" trap.
- **A test that fails if anyone re-adds one:** *"NO CAP: 60 dependants (past the refused 50
  threshold) all recalculate in ONE call"*. 60 sits clearly past 50 so an off-by-one cap cannot
  pass, and it asserts every row produced a VALUE — a cap that "succeeded" by recording 60 errors
  would otherwise read as a pass. **Mutation M7** (re-adding `if (out.length >= 50) continue`)
  fails exactly that test by name; restored byte-identically.

Final: `cell-formula.service.ts` sha1 `31c195c77aa576fc17b1dc2aa0b38ade84881e43`,
`cell-formula-recalc.vitest.test.ts` sha1 `6e72f297be3fb075c72049f584cb980cb8699e9c` (13 tests).

— the pending log is the pool's pg/SSL warning noise, so the race surfaces against whichever file
is running when the worker closes.

**Consequence for the push gate:** anyone quoting `vitest run`'s exit status for `apps/api` will
read a red that has no failing test behind it. Quote the `Tests N passed (N)` line, or fix the race
first. Two consecutive runs reproduced it; one earlier run did not, so it is timing-dependent, not
constant.

**Three findings, in order of seriousness.**

   `nds-cell-is-*` classes present is `locked · mapped · editable · pinned · select · formula`.

consumed by `useCellFormulas`, which `MasterSheet.tsx:96` and `ChannelSheet.tsx:70` both import —
one implementation, so the in-editor verdict almost certainly does appear on the channel at the
moment of saving. I did not exercise it, because that needs typing into a live production cell and
the reading above did not require it. **The gap is persistence, not scope:** a refusal is visible
only to the operator who caused it, in the instant they caused it. Reload, or arrive at a row
someone else refused, and the cell claims it is calculated.

### 14 · 🔴 TWO SESSIONS EACH EXCLUDING THE OTHER'S LOAD — the agreement would have been the artefact

The open-gesture gate disagreed between the hub and me. We each concluded, independently and
correctly, that concurrent load was a candidate cause, and we each started a "quiet" run to
eliminate it. **The runs overlapped.**

```
pid 92986  <- 92984 <- 94745 (this session)   node scripts/check-editor-open.mjs --strict   14:17:45
pid   297  <-   286 <- 82837 (the hub)        node scripts/check-editor-open.mjs --strict   14:19:28
9 chromium/playwright processes alive
```

Two Playwright gates driving the same page against the same API on :8091, each declared quiet, each
being the other's load. **Both possible outcomes were traps:** two greens would have mutually
confirmed a clean gate neither of us had measured quietly; two reds would have mutually confirmed a
regression that was only our contention. Two independent-looking measurements agreeing *because of
one shared cause they both created*. The agreement would have been the artefact — and agreement is
exactly what we would each have treated as confirmation.

Caught from the PROCESS TABLE, not from either log: no log records what else was running while it
was written. A run's own output cannot show you its contention.

**Resolved by serialising, at the cost of my run.** I killed mine mid-flight (theirs was
contaminated from its own start — mine had been running 1m43s when theirs began, so theirs needed
restarting too), verified the machine clean — zero `check-editor-open`, zero chromium/playwright,
**no orphans from my kill**, which is the part that would silently have polluted the next run — and
held off the API until the hub's solo run reports.

**The correction that eliminates a whole class of explanation:** the hub attributed the divergence
to "the machine and the load". It cannot be the machine. Both sessions are processes on ONE Mac
sharing ONE API and ONE filesystem. On a single-machine multi-session programme "my machine versus
yours" is never available, and two sessions can only eliminate load by taking turns.

Bucket (b) — master `select/locked` and `select/fxblocked`, green on the hub's `cc6f7623` run and
red on both of mine — is therefore a LOAD question, not a script-version question. Two serialised
runs on `8e930612` decide it, each carrying its own build-stamp sha1 and its exit read from
`GATE_EXIT`, never from the wrapper.

### 15 · 🔴 Bucket (c) was a TRUE POSITIVE — and I had a ready explanation that would have buried it

b0 disclosed a helper declared in the temporal dead zone below the channel sheet's column memo:
the whole Amazon·IT scope threw before initialisation and rendered **no rows at all**, roughly
13:47 → 14:10. A dead sheet for anyone on the channel in that window. `ChannelSheet.tsx` mtime
**14:14:16** confirms the fix landed when the hub says it did.

My gate run reported exactly that — `AMAZON·IT text/fresh` and `text/batch: NOT MEASURED — no rows
rendered`, output last written 14:17:09, the run spanning most of the dead window. **The gate was
right. It detected a real regression.**

**And I had already offered the explanation that would have thrown it away.** I wrote that my own
preview curls ran concurrently and that "no rows rendered is exactly the shape a slow page load
takes" — a true, plausible, self-blaming account of a finding that was actually a live defect
breaking a whole scope for twenty minutes. Self-blame reads as rigour, which is what makes it
dangerous: nobody challenges the investigator who says *the noise was probably mine*. What saved it
was recording the finding as UNKNOWN and running the experiment, rather than closing it with the
explanation I found most humbling.

**Instrument limit, stated rather than glossed:** I cannot prove the minute-level overlap from my
own log. The gate prints no per-assertion timestamps, so a finding cannot be correlated with a time
window from the log alone — only the file's last-write time and the scope ordering place it. Same
family as §14's lesson: a run's log records neither what else was running nor when each assertion
ran. Both would be one line of output to fix.

**Where the three buckets now stand.** (a) FIXED, b0's `bringOnScreen()` — confirmed passing.
(c) SOLVED, a real TDZ defect, fixed 14:14, my reading a true positive. (b) master `select/locked`
and `select/fxblocked` — STILL OPEN with two live candidate causes I cannot separate: contention,
or b0's pre-fix un-scrolled-snapshot artefact, which explains equally well why they read identical
across two script versions. The hub's solo run on `8e930612`, started 14:23 after the TDZ fix with

### 17 · A log with no clock still has a SEQUENCE — the shape settled both open buckets

*(Renumbered from 16: b0 had already taken §16 for the refused-cell fixture register and I
appended without checking. Their number is the one other sessions will cite, so mine moved.)*

The hub asked for my red run's start time to test whether b0's dead-sheet regression could be
bucket (c)'s cause. The start time (**14:05:15**, run ending **14:17:09**) does place it inside the
window — but the ORDER of the assertions turned out to be far stronger evidence, and it also moved
bucket (b), which no timestamp could have done.

**(c) — the failures are a PREFIX.** AMAZON·IT contract block, in execution order:

```
text/fresh      NOT MEASURED — no rows rendered   ← arm 1
text/batch      NOT MEASURED — no rows rendered   ← arm 2
text/flush      ✅                                 ← arm 3
longtext ✅✅✅  number ✅✅✅  select ✅✅✅  select/locked ✅  select/fxblocked ✅
```

Exactly the first two arms fail, then **twelve consecutive passes**. Contention produces SCATTERED
failures; a sheet that is dead and then comes alive produces exactly a prefix, and the transition
sits between arm 2 and arm 3 — where a fix saved at `14:14:16` plus an HMR recompile lands in a run
ending `14:17:09`. (Note the stated window "13:47 → 14:10" cannot be right: the fix file's mtime is
14:14:16, so the sheet was dead until ~14:14, not 14:10.)

**(b) — the SAME RUN refutes the load hypothesis.** In that one run:

```
master     … twelve arms ✅ … then  select/locked ❌  select/fxblocked ❌  "could not bring a select column on screen"
AMAZON·IT  …                  then  select/locked ✅  select/fxblocked ✅
```

The identical two arms fail on master and pass on AMAZON·IT — LATER in the same run, under the same
or worse contention (b0's unannounced run was still going). **Load cannot explain a failure that
reverses itself for the same two arms minutes later in the same process.** So bucket (b) is
probably neither contention nor "never fixed" as I first framed it: it looks like `bringOnScreen()`
works on the channel scope and does not reach `condition_type` on master. Specific, testable, and
b0's — with those two log lines attached. My third revision of this framing, each one away from the
tidier story.

🔴 **The method, banked:** both conclusions came from the ORDER and SHAPE of the assertions, not
from any clock. The per-assertion timestamp queued to b0 would have answered (c) directly — and
would still not have answered (b), which needed the master-versus-channel contrast within one run.
**When a log has no clock, its sequence is still evidence:** which arms failed, in what order, and
what passed immediately afterwards. Ask what pattern each competing cause PREDICTS — scattered
versus prefix, persistent versus self-reversing — and the log often discriminates without a single
timestamp.

### 21 · Duplicate attributes — MEASURED, routed to AM.1 + Owner, not fixed here (b0, 2026-09-05 00:26 CEST)

**Owner:** *"I see multiple attributes for the same thing. I see item name along with another column
for the name, so it contradicts, sort of. We must make sure that there are no duplications at all."*

**Measured on the live contracts (all columns, all three scopes, by write cell):**
- **Amazon·IT — duplicate by construction:** `name` and `item_name` BOTH write
  `channelListing/amazon_title`; `description` and `product_description` BOTH write
  `channelListing/amazon_description`. Two columns, one cell; values identical on 21/21 rows. The
  channel label ("Nome dell'articolo"), the 200-char cap, `requiredBy`, `applicableProductTypes` all
  sit on `item_name`; `name` carries none of them.
- **master·DE — two storages for one concept:** `name` → `Product.name`, `item_name` →
  `attr_item_name` (the bag); `description` → localizedContent, `product_description` → the bag.
  On the fixture `name` = `item_name` on 19/21 rows; the two XXS rows differ by a variant suffix
  ("… (XS, Nero)") that `Product.name` carries and the Amazon title does not. Descriptions: both
  empty on 21/21.
- **eBay·IT:** no pair (`name` → `ebay_title`, `description` → `ebay_description`, no `item_name`).
- EAN / GTIN / UPC are three identifier schemes, not one concept — not duplicates.

**Mechanism:** `sheet-columns.service.ts#buildSheetColumns` dedups by `normaliseKey(key)` only;
`name` and `item_name` normalise apart, so the core field and Amazon's flat-file attribute for the
same thing both survive, and the channel path then points both at the same `amazon_title` cell.

**Recommendation (for the Owner, inside 5c's AM.1 design — the resolver and registry are PES.5's):**
one TITLE and one DESCRIPTION column per scope, keyed `name` / `description`, writing that scope's
cell (master → `Product.name`, Amazon → `amazon_title`, eBay → `ebay_title`) and carrying the scope's
channel metadata (label, cap, required, product types) merged from the attribute; `item_name` /
`product_description` cease to be separate columns. The dedup belongs in the contract builder so the
sheet, drawer, import diff and readiness agree. On master this retires `attr_item_name` /
`attr_product_description` as master attributes — a DATA decision with a migration (the Amazon
title already lives on the Amazon scope's own cell, identical on 21/21 fixture rows), and the
variant-suffix divergence on the two XXS rows has to be ruled (keep the suffix on `Product.name`;
the axes are already the band's second line). **Nothing edited in the API; nothing committed.**

**Confirmed by `nexus-commerce-5c` (AM.1, in build on the API side):** one concept, one column, keyed by the
MASTER key; a channel field links via `masterKey` in the channel adapter and the column carries the channel's
metadata; on a channel scope it writes the channel store, on master the master store; the `attr_item_name` /
`attr_product_description` / `attr_bullet_point` / `attr_generic_keyword` bag keys retire from writes. Same
rule joins Amazon `material` and eBay `aspect_Material`. b0 stops here; the two drifted XXS rows are handed to
5c for their entry.

### 23 · Write-shape probe — the list editor sends an ARRAY of codes; the request was ABORTED at the network layer, nothing written (b0, 2026-09-05 02:13 CEST)

Master·DE, child `cmokmy0jf0003pm0ppnu1b2yy` (GALE-JACKET-BLACK-MEN-3XL), column
`supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation`, cell reading "Nicht zutreffend" (inherited). Double-click → `popup:multi`;
ticked one more option ("Andere"); count line "2 selected · Enter saves · Esc cancels"; Enter. The browser
issued exactly one non-GET request, captured and aborted by the probe's route handler before it left the
page:

```
PATCH /api/products/bulk
{"changes":[{"id":"cmokmy0jf0003pm0ppnu1b2yy","field":"attr_supplier_declared_dg_hz_regulation","value":["not_applicable","other"]}],
 "marketplaceContexts":[{"marketplace":"DE","locale":"de"}],"expectedVersion":16}
```

An array of CODES (not labels, not a joined string), the row's `expectedVersion`, the coordinate — the shape
5c's `coerceForShape` accepts. The cell then read both chips plus "Connection lost — refresh to see
whether this saved." with `nds-cell-is-unknown`: the transport-failure honesty path, not a false "saved".
**No request reached :8091; the fixture is untouched** (the aborted request is the only write-class call
in the run). A real rehearsal on a compliance field (dangerous-goods regulation) of a LIVE Amazon listing
is not something this lane will do on its own judgement — the outbound sync could carry it to the
marketplace; if the Owner wants an end-to-end write rehearsed, `keywords` (free text, empty on the fixture)
is the candidate, announced first and restored by value.

**Found by the probe design, fixed:** the free-text list editor's DRAFT — AG's popup owns Enter and commits
before the DS `TagInput` can turn the typed text into a chip, so the last value would vanish. The draft is
now mirrored and reported as the final item (de-duplicated), so Enter means "add and save".

#### VP.4 · §1.4 VERDICT — `Variation order` DOES order what buyers pick from. It folds into the dock's drag order — but it must keep writing through its OWN endpoint, and it carries three capabilities the dock does not yet have. (2026-09-11, measured in code)

**The question §1.4 asks:** does `PresentationTab mode="order"` order the variations/specifics buyers
pick from, or something else?

**Answer: it orders exactly that, on two dimensions.** Measured, `file:line`:
- `_studio/PresentationTab.tsx:26` → `VariationOrderTab` = `PresentationPage mode="order"`, which at
  `:140–141` mounts `OrderEditor` (`app/products/ebay-flat-file/Presentation/OrderEditor.tsx`)
  embedded, keyed on `productId · marketplace · accountId · aliasKey`.
- `OrderEditor.tsx:106` — **axis order**: `OrderedList label="Buyer-facing axis order"` under the
  sentence *"Which option buyers choose first."*
- `OrderEditor.tsx:113–115` — **per-axis value order**: one `OrderedList` per axis, *"The sequence of
  {axis} options."*
- Server: `ebay-presentation-order.service.ts:98–126` (`changePresentationOrder`) writes
  `_variationAxes` (the axis sequence) and `_axisValueOrder` (per axis) into the listing's
  `platformAttributes`; `ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:617` caps `_variationAxes` at `.slice(0, 5)` — the
  same 5-specifics limit §4.5 states for eBay.

So §1.4's first branch fires: **it folds into the mapping dock's drag order.** §4.4.1's "Drag to set
the order buyers pick in" IS `_variationAxes`, and §4.4.2's Values section is where
`_axisValueOrder` belongs.

**🔴 Three things the fold must not drop, and one it must not break.**

1. **It writes through its OWN endpoint, not VP.2's projection PATCH.**
   `GET/PUT /api/ebay/cockpit/presentation-order` (`ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:124–125`). Its CAS is a
   PAIR — `expectedVersion` (the `ChannelListing.version`) **and** `expectedToken`, a
   `mappingToken()` hash over products, listings, memberships, categories, schemas, images, themes,
   value maps and size scales (`ebay-presentation-order.service.ts:43–79`). It saves inside a
   `Serializable` transaction with a `platformAttributes: { equals: … }` compare-and-set and writes
   a `bulkOperation` audit row (`:134–142`). A second writer on `platformAttributes._variationAxes`
   through VP.2's `PATCH /studio/projection` would be two writers on one fact with two different
   CAS schemes — and the cockpit route already refuses that shape explicitly at
   `ebay-cockpit.routes.ts:596`: *"Use the destination-specific presentation order editor with the
   current listing version and input token"*, `409`, with the URL in the body.
   → **Recommendation to the Owner and VP.2:** the dock's drag order calls
   `PUT /api/ebay/cockpit/presentation-order` with that endpoint's own `expectedVersion` +
   `expectedToken`; VP.2's projection PATCH owns mapping + split and never touches `_variationAxes`
   or `_axisValueOrder`. One fact, one writer. VP.2's §5.4 GET should relay the order READ so the
   dock paints without a second round trip.
2. **The order INHERITS from a shared rule, and the editor can restore inheritance.**
   `view.source` is a shared presentation rule with a name and version, linked to
   `/channels/ebay/variation-order-rules` (`OrderEditor.tsx:94–96`); `explicitAxes` /
   `explicitValues` say which parts this listing has overridden; `Restore inherited ordering`
   (`reset`) and the two per-part `Restore inherited …` buttons delete the stored keys so the rule
   takes over again (`ebay-presentation-order.service.ts:101,104,119`). That is the SAME
   inherit/pin cascade §4.3 gives mapped values — so the dock's drag rows want the same
   `SourceIndicator` vocabulary (link = following the shared rule, pin = this listing's own order),
   not a bare list.
3. **It is ALIAS-scoped and per-destination.** `aliasKey` is part of the destination
   (`ebay-presentation-order.service.ts:13–38`), and membership is bound to the selected root
   listing's ItemID. §4.4.3's listing split therefore changes WHICH order document the dock is
   editing. While split creation is held (PES.5-ii), the dock edits the single destination's order;
   the moment a second alias exists, the dock needs a listing selector or it will silently edit one
   alias's order while showing another's counts.
4. **What must not break: publication is SEPARATE and stays so.** `readPresentationOrder` returns
   `publication: 'separate'`, and saving stamps an `ORDER_RECEIPT` but pushes nothing
   (`ebay-presentation-order.service.ts:137`); publishing runs through `PublicationReview` /
   `ebay-presentation-publication.service.ts`. A `Save mapping` in the dock that also ordered would
   still not publish — correct — but the dock must not absorb the **Review publication** button
   without a home. My recommendation: it stays on `Description themes`, which is where the rest of
   the eBay presentation work already lives and where the publication review already mounts.

**Net, for VP.1:** `Variation order` can leave the nav. Nothing is dropped IF (a) the dock's
Variation specifics section drags `_variationAxes` and its Values section drags `_axisValueOrder`,
both through `PUT /api/ebay/cockpit/presentation-order`; (b) the dock renders the shared-rule source
and a restore-inherited control; (c) `Review publication` stays reachable from Description themes.
If the Owner would rather not move the value-order dimension into the dock in this wave, the honest
fallback is §1.4's second branch for that half only: keep it reachable from Description themes and
say so on screen. **This lane builds (a) and (b) into the dock; it does not delete anything —
`PresentationTab.tsx:26` is VP.1's line to remove, on this verdict.**

Measured on GALE-JACKET (local Docker DB). A child's variation-axis value exists in up to three places:

| 2 | `categoryAttributes.{color,size}` — the sheet's `axis: true` columns, `writeField: attr_color` | **0 / 20** (every cell reads `null`) | the studio SHEET reads and writes exactly this |
| 3 | `Product.variantAttributes.{Color,Size}` | **2 / 20**, and both of those carry the corrupt `variantAttributes: "[object Object]"` key | `studio-sheet.service.ts:608 readAxisValues` — the sheet's `axisValues` and `family.axes` coverage |

**Consequences, all visible today, none introduced by this lane:**
- The master sheet reports `family.axes[].rowsWithValue: 2 of 20` for both Colore and Taglia, and every child's
  `axisValues` is `{}` except two — while all 20 genuinely have a colour and a size. The sheet is reading
  store 3; the data lives in store 1.
- The two children that DO have store 3 (`…-BLACK-MEN-XXS`, `…-YELLOW-MEN-XXS`) have had their store 1 values
  **destroyed** by whatever wrote the `[object Object]` key: their `variations` is now `{"variantAttributes":
  "[object Object]"}` and nothing else. Their store 3 also says `Size: "XS"` while their SKU says `XXS`.
- Typing a value into the sheet's Colore cell writes store 2, which the eBay push never reads. A value an
  operator can see on the sheet is therefore not the value eBay receives.

**What VP.2 does about it, and what it does NOT do.** The family read presents the UNION with a stated
precedence — sheet cell (store 2) → `variations` (store 1) → `variantAttributes` (store 3) — filtering the
`[object Object]` key exactly as `readAxisValues` already does, and reports every disagreement in
`coverage.axisValueConflicts` rather than silently picking a winner. That makes the Variants page correct on
20 of 20 rows instead of 2. **VP.2 does not change any WRITE path**: spec §3.3 says the axis cell uses the
sheet's existing editor, which is PES.2's, and the fix — one writer that lands all three stores together so
the sheet, this page and the eBay push cannot disagree — is a ruling, not a lane's improvisation.
**Owner: this needs a decision.** Until it is made, the Variants page will show values the master sheet's own
Colore/Taglia columns show as empty, and that difference is real, not a rendering bug.

     and `syncSharedTradingQuantity` (:1555) do **not** — Shopify is gated instead by `getShopifyPublishMode()`,
     an environment gate, not a per-row one. So the pause is what stops the row entering the queue; it is not a
     second belt at dispatch on three of the five paths. Said plainly rather than claimed uniformly.

**Known limitation, stated rather than discovered later:** `expectedVersion` on the include/exclude route is
the PARENT listing's version, and a child-row write does not bump it. So it guards against a concurrent
MAPPING or split change, not against two operators toggling the same child — where each write is idempotent in
its own direction and last-write-wins. Cheap to tighten if the Owner wants the stronger guarantee.

#### VP.1 -> EVERY LANE: SEVEN files in this repo are invisible to grep right now, hiding 33 exports. And `file --mime-encoding` is the WRONG test for it. (2026-09-11 18:5x, measured)

VP.3 fixed the two NUL bytes I found in `family/coverage.ts`, found four more in
`GenerateCombinationsDialog.tsx`, and passed on the cause: a literal NUL lands when the intended source
text is the two characters `backslash-zero` and the file is written through the file-writing TOOL rather
than a shell heredoc. **That cause is not confined to the variants lanes.** I swept `_studio/**`,
`design-system/**`, `apps/api/src/{services,routes}/**` and `docs/**`:

| file | grep sees | actually has | blinded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `services/error-grouping.service.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 3 exports | **YES** |
| `services/ebay-inventory-readback.service.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 11 exports | **YES** |
| `services/advertising/ads-contest-flags.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 4 exports | **YES** |
| `services/advertising/ads-contest-flags.vitest.test.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | - | **YES** |
| `services/agent-fleet/sweep-report.service.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 3 exports | **YES** |
| `services/pim/value-map.service.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 10 exports | **YES** |
| `design-system/grid/workspace/drafts.ts` | 0 lines, rc=1 | 2 exports | **YES** |
| `services/ebay-variation-order-apply.service.ts` | 254 lines, 8 exports | 8 exports | no |
| `services/advertising/ads-console-import.service.ts` | 485 lines, 10 exports | 10 exports | no |

Every blinded file is the same shape - a composite map key or a join separator, `` `${a}<NUL>${b}` ``,
written raw. `grep '^export'` returns **0** on each while the exports are plainly there.

**The check VP.3 and I both reached for is WRONG.** `file -b --mime-encoding` reports `binary` for NINE
files; grep is blinded on only SEVEN. The last two rows carry a `0x01` SOH and no NUL, and grep reads them
perfectly. **`binary` over-reports; the blinding byte is specifically NUL.** Use a NUL count, or the
behavioural form `grep -c "" <file>; echo $?` - EMPTY with rc=1 is the tell.

**What it costs, and why it is not a tidiness note.** Any repo-wide grep silently drops these seven from
its denominator, with no notice and the same exit code it uses for "no match". A census, an "is there
another caller?" sweep, or a "this symbol is unused" conclusion taken by grep in recent weeks may have
been taken over a short denominator - `reference_a_list_of_members_is_a_set_claim` and
`reference_control_must_target_the_branch` both apply, and the dangerous green is the one produced by
having nothing to look at.

**A live demonstration, recorded because it is the sharpest evidence of the cause.** Writing THIS ledger
entry, my first attempt embedded a literal NUL where I meant to type the escape, and the shell tool
refused the command for "control characters that would be hidden in the approval dialog". VP.3 reported
the same thing happening inside their own report about it. The byte arrives when you are writing ABOUT
the byte; that is how reproducible this path is.

**Not fixed here - none of these is VP.1's.** `services/pim/value-map.service.ts` is VP.2's neighbourhood,
`design-system/grid/workspace/drafts.ts` is VP.5's/the engine's, and the ads and agent-fleet files belong
to the ads lanes. The fix is two characters in each: spell the separator `'\u0000'` as an escape, which
keeps the collision-proof property and keeps the file text. **VP.1's own files were all checked and are
`utf-8`** - they were written through shell heredocs and python, consistent with VP.3's diagnosis.

**VP.2 · nexus-commerce-15 · 2026-09-11 · 🔴 THE GREP-BLINDING MECHANISM IS NOT WHAT ANY OF US SAID. Measured, and it corrects my own entry above as well as VP.1's banked note.**

VP.4 reported my held-cell sentence was false on three markets; chasing that put me back on the grep question,
and the two sweeps I ran DISAGREED with each other — a shell loop said 7 files were blinded, a Python
`subprocess` loop said all 8 were readable. Same files, same minute. Settling that is the finding.

**`grep` in a Claude Code shell is a shell FUNCTION, not `/usr/bin/grep`.** `type -a grep` resolves it to
`~/.claude/shell-snapshots/…`, which execs **`ugrep … -I …`**. `-I` is *ignore binary files*. That is the
entire mechanism. Python's `subprocess` bypasses the function and gets the system grep, which is why the two
sweeps disagreed.

| command, same file (1 NUL at byte 1099 of 2773) | result |
|---|---|
| `grep -c "" <f>` — the shell function, i.e. `ugrep -I` | empty, **rc=1** |
| `/usr/bin/grep -c "" <f>` | **60**, rc=0 |
| `command grep -c "" <f>` | **60**, rc=0 |
| `grep -ac "export" <f>` — `-a` overrides `-I` | **4**, rc=0 |

**`/usr/bin/grep` reads ALL EIGHT NUL-carrying files in the live tree** — rc=0, real counts, up to 12,785
lines. So BSD grep was never the blinder, and `-a` works because it overrides `-I`, not because it defeats a
binary heuristic in BSD grep.

**Three corrections follow, two of them to things I wrote.**
1. **My "10 NUL-carrying files, three inside my proof's trees" was a BYTE COUNT, and byte count is not the
   test.** VP.1 got there first and they are right: `routes/advertising.routes.ts` holds SEVEN NULs and is read
   fine, while a file with ONE is blinded. The behavioural sweep gives **7 blinded** in the live tree.
2. **VP.1's mechanism ("BSD grep refuses to read it as text") is wrong, and so is the position theory** ("the
   difference is where the byte sits"). It is ugrep's own binary heuristic under `-I`. Their *test* —
   `grep -c "" <file>; echo $?` — is the one thing that survives, and it survives because it is behavioural:
   it tests THIS SHELL's grep rather than a property of the file.
3. **Fixing the file is optional, not required.** My `value-map.service.ts` edit still stands on its own merits
   (it makes the file readable by the wrapper every lane actually uses, byte-identically) but it is not a
   correctness fix, and no lane should feel obliged to chase the other seven.
**My no-push-path proof is unaffected either way** — the re-run used `grep -a`, which overrides `-I`, so it
read every file including all eight. The conclusion and the numbers stand.
The banked memory has been corrected in place, mechanism and test, with the note that its previous advice
(mine and VP.1's both) was wrong.

**A refinement to the guidance I gave three lanes, measured just now.** I told VP.2, VP.4 and VP.5 that
`/usr/bin/grep` closes both blinding flags. It closes `--ignore-files`, and it does NOT lie - but on a
NUL-carrying file it prints `Binary file <path> matches` instead of the content. So:

| | prints content from a NUL file? | honours .gitignore? |
|---|---|---|
| `grep` (wrapper) | no - silent, rc=1 | YES, skips |
| `grep -a` | yes | YES, skips |
| `/usr/bin/grep` | no - ANNOUNCES the match | no |
| **`/usr/bin/grep -a`** | **yes** | **no** |

**`/usr/bin/grep -a` is the robust form**; anything less leaves one hole open.

**Why my §6 zeros survive this anyway, checked rather than assumed.** Runs 3 and 4 piped
`/usr/bin/grep -rn ... | grep -c .`, so a match inside a NUL file arrives as the `Binary file ... matches`
LINE and is COUNTED - it inflates the total, it does not vanish. Verified with a positive control:
searching `detectVariantAxes`, a symbol that lives inside the blinded `variantAxes.ts`, returns 1 through
that exact pipeline. So the failure mode is SAFE FOR A ZERO CLAIM: a hidden hit raises the count above
zero rather than hiding under it. **The eleven §6 zeros stand.**

| AIREON | 40 | `Colore[0]` `Taglia[0]`, both **`declared`** | 0 / 0 | 40 of 40 | **"0 of 0 combinations exist · 0 missing"** ❌ |
| MISANO `3K-HP05-BH9I` | 15 | none | 0 / 0 | **15 of 15** | **"0 of 0 combinations exist · 0 missing"** ❌ |

**Defect 1 — a degenerate coverage sentence that reads as health.** "0 of 0 combinations exist · 0 missing" is
literally true and operationally useless: on AIREON it describes a family of FORTY children whose two declared
axes have nothing stored under them, and it renders identically to a family that is genuinely complete. The
signal exists one field away (`axes[].source === 'declared'`) but the sentence does not carry it.
**Queued fix:** `coverage.state` — `'ok'` when every axis has values and the counts mean something;
`'no-axes'` when the family declares none; `'no-values'` when axes are declared and nothing is stored, so
combinations CANNOT be computed. `0` then stops being a number the band presents as a result. The §9 copy for
the two degenerate cases is VP.3's to choose; the server's job is to say which case it is, and today it does not.

**Defect 2 — `childrenMissingAxisValues` is wrong when a family has NO axes.** MISANO declares none, and I
report all 15 children as "missing axis values". There is nothing to miss. VP.3's chip would print 15 on a
family where the concept does not apply. Cause is mine and exact: the guard reads
`if (axes.length === 0 || tuple.some((v) => !v))`, and that first clause is the bug.
**Queued fix:** when `axes.length === 0`, `childrenMissingAxisValues` is `[]` — `axes: []` already says the
family has no axes, and saying it twice in a way that reads as a fault is worse than not saying it.

**🔴 AND FOR THE OWNER — AIREON makes the store question bigger than GALE-JACKET showed.** Measured:
40 children · declared axes `["Colore","Taglia"]` · `Product.variationTheme` `"Colore,Taglia"` ·
**0 of 40 children carry an axis value in `categoryAttributes.variations`** · **0 of 40 in
`Product.variantAttributes`** · and the family is **LIVE on eBay·IT with ItemID `257646289420`**. Its SKUs
carry the values (`AIREON-JACKET-CREMA-E-VINO-MEN-3XL` — a multi-segment colour), and its parent listing has
no `_variationAxes` and no `_axisValueOrder`. So this is a family selling as a multi-variation listing on eBay
while our local record holds **no axis data at all**. The GALE-JACKET finding was "three stores disagree";
AIREON is "the stores are empty and the channel is live anyway". Whatever is ruled about one writer has to
answer for this shape too, and the Variants page will show 40 variants with no axis values and no combinations
until it does.

posts done; the six file hashes stamped above are unchanged.

**VP.2 · nexus-commerce-15 · 2026-09-11 · 🔴 The AIREON defect is WORSE than I filed it: the contradiction is inside MY PAYLOAD, and the house already has the right fix. Still queued — no `apps/*` write.**

VP.3 reported their band and chip contradicting each other in one 40px bar on AIREON. Measuring my own
response shows the contradiction is not theirs — **it ships in a single object of mine**:

| family | children | axes / values | `coverage.missing` | `coverage.childrenMissingAxisValues` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GALE-JACKET | 20 | 2 / `[2,9]` | 0 | 0 |
| **AIREON** | **40** | 2 / **`[0,0]`** | **0** | **40** |
| MISANO | 15 | 0 / `[]` | 0 | **15** |

One payload asserting "**0 missing**" and "**40 children missing axis values**" at the same time. The two fields
have different meanings — `missing` counts absent TUPLES from the Cartesian product, the other counts children
with an incomplete tuple — but when the product is EMPTY that pair is incoherent, and no consumer should have
to know my internals to see that. VP.3's chip escapes it only because they count from rows and early-return on
no axes, which they measured rather than assumed; **anything that consumes `coverage` directly gets the
contradiction.** So this is mine whether or not it reaches their surface.

**The fix I queued first (a `state` field) was not enough, and this codebase already rules the right one.**
`StudioSheet.counts.mapped` is `number | null` with the comment *"`null` when the mapping enrichment did not
run — never 0 for that"* (D14.3). Zero is a real answer; not-counted is a different fact; they must not share
a value. My coverage breaks that rule three times.

**REVISED queued fix — a contract change, flagged as one:**
- `combinations`, `existing` and `missing` become **nullable**. `null` = the Cartesian product could not be
  computed, so nothing was counted. They are numbers only when every axis has at least one value.
- `coverage.state`: `'ok'` · `'no-axes'` (the family declares none) · `'no-values'` (axes declared, nothing
  stored under them). The band gets a sentence; the server never presents a 0 it did not count.
- `childrenMissingAxisValues` is `[]` when `axes.length === 0` — there is nothing to miss, and `axes: []`
  already says so.
This makes the contradiction impossible by construction rather than merely visible: you cannot report
"0 missing" beside "40 missing values" if you did not count and said so.

**Consumer impact, checked before proposing it:** VP.3 counts from rows and does not consume these fields, so
nil for the family surface; VP.4 reads the projection contract, which has no `coverage`. Both told. Contract
`docs/vp2-contracts.md` §2 updates with the change when the hold lifts.

**VP.2 · nexus-commerce-15 · 2026-09-11 · 🔴🔴 A FABRICATED 100% ON A READINESS PILL, found by applying VP.3's prose-vs-compiler lesson to my own definitions. Queued behind the hold; no `apps/*` write.**

VP.3's observation is the one that found these: *a convention that lives in PROSE gets obeyed at call SITES and
lost at DEFINITION sites* — they obeyed the null-means-not-counted rule where `number | null` forced them to and
broke it in a type they wrote themselves. I took that as an instruction to audit my own definitions rather than
to agree, and two defects of the same class fell out. Measured on GALE-JACKET, read-only:

| coordinate | `meta.schemaMissing` | columns | what I relay |
|---|---|---|---|
| eBay·IT | `[]` | 51 | `readiness.pct 71`, `targetOptions 3` — honest |
| Etsy·GLOBAL | **`["ETSY:*"]`** | 57 | `readiness.pct 4`, **`targetOptions 0`** |
| **Amazon·PL** | **`["OUTERWEAR"]`** | **4** | **`readiness.pct 100`** |

**Defect A — I relay a 100% for a coordinate whose schema could not be read.** Amazon·PL's product-type schema
is unreadable (`cached Amazon schema unreadable: OUTERWEAR Access to requested resource is denied`), only FOUR
columns survive, completeness computes `2/2 = 100`, and my family/projection reads hand that to the pill as
`readiness: { pct: 100, state: 'errors' }`. **A variant is reported COMPLETE on a market where nothing could be
checked.** That is the most confident possible wrong answer and it is precisely what the programme's honesty
rule exists to stop — `pct: null` plus a note, never a number, when it cannot be computed.

**Defect B — `targetOptions: []` is ambiguous between three different facts.** "This channel genuinely offers no
variant-eligible properties", "the channel takes free names" (Shopify, and `freeform: true` does say so), and
"the schema could not be read" (Etsy·GLOBAL, `schemaMissing: ["ETSY:*"]`) all serialise identically. The dock
would render an empty Listbox meaning "none exist" when the truth is "we could not look". Same shape as the
`targetOptions` bug VP.4's probe caught earlier today, one layer further out.

**Root cause, and it is mine alone: the substrate already publishes the not-counted signal and my read ignores
it.** `StudioSheet.meta.schemaMissing` is exactly this fact, produced by the column build, and neither
`getFamilyRead` nor `getProjectionRead` consults it. My types were already `pct: number | null` — the shape was
right and nothing forced me to fill it correctly, which is VP.3's point landing on my own file.

**Queued fixes** (with the coverage ones above):
- `readiness` is `null` — with a reason naming the missing schema — for any coordinate whose `schemaMissing`
  is non-empty. Never a percentage derived from the handful of columns that survived.
- `targetOptions` gains a state: `'ok'` · `'freeform'` · `'unavailable'` (+ the schema that is missing), so an
  empty list is never three different facts wearing one shape.
- Both reads relay `schemaMissing` so a consumer can say which coordinates were not measurable at all.

VP.1's discriminator is the decisive one: **signed in, with no 401 anywhere, the condition is still false** — so fixing the gate's authentication would not have made those four measurable, and the permission story was wrong.
**And the failed-request evidence I leaned on was worthless for this:** every surface logs exactly one, including the three variants surfaces that pass. A signal present on green and red alike discriminates nothing. I had it in front of me and read it as a cause.
**Fixed:** readiness now waits until the visible control count outside the rail, top bar and AG root has STOPPED CHANGING across consecutive samples and is non-zero — readiness by behaviour, not by a named container that can rot the same way. **Run time also fell from 4m29s to 35s**, because four surfaces had been burning a 60s timeout each.

|---|---|

is `AuthProvider` calling `/api/auth/me`. That is exactly what VP.5 concluded from their own evidence: a signal
present on both arms discriminates nothing.

for everything. I had that memory in context. I reasoned past it.

   OUTERWEAR·IT marks **28 values deprecated and EVERY `_NAME` spelling is among them** (`COLOR_NAME`,
   `SIZE_NAME`, `COLOR_NAME/SIZE_NAME`, `SIZE_NAME/COLOR_NAME`, `STYLE_NAME`, …) while `COLOR/SIZE` and
   `SIZE/COLOR` are not. So the ambiguous pair resolves by Amazon's own lifecycle marker: `tieBreak: 'only-live'`
   fires first, and `'bare-form'` remains only for a product type whose deprecation list does not separate them.
   The deprecated twin is still OFFERED, so the editor lists it under `Deprecated` — warn, never hide.
   (Also measured: Amazon's own `enumNames` for the bare form are machine-cased — `COLORE/DIMENSIONI` on IT,
   `FARBE/GRÖSSE` on DE — which is why the label comes from the bound attributes' titles: `Colore / Taglia`,
   `Farbe / Größe`. `limits.axes` = 4 on OUTERWEAR, derived from the widest segment count in the enum itself.)

🔴 **The most serious thing I found — and it was mine.** `ChannelListing.variationExcluded` is **not in the Prisma
schema**; it exists only because a migration added it. So on a database built from the schema alone — the "real
disposable PostgreSQL" `content-write.vitest.test.ts` creates — the raw exclusion query fails `42703`, and a failed
statement **aborts the caller's transaction** (`25P02 current transaction is aborted`). ONE unguarded read turned into
**12 failing tests** whose error pointed at `readinessIndex.deleteMany`, a line with nothing to do with variations.
A `try/catch` does not help: by the time JavaScript sees it the transaction is already poisoned. `variation-excluded.ts`
now probes `information_schema.columns` first (a catalogue read that cannot fail, memoised per process) and reports
the exclusion set as UNKNOWN when the column is absent — so the cell says `collisions: null` ("not computed") rather
than "0 collisions". With the probe: `content-write.vitest.test.ts` **18/18**, all 12 failures gone.

  if the schema declares it — plus a fourth (a property whose own name canonicalises to the segment's key).
  Measurement: with it, **every segment of all 50 themes binds on both IT and DE** and all four of the doc's examples

  where the design says the English label. Rule added: when `canonicalVariantAxis` CHANGED the stored key, the stored
  key is a localized alias and the canonical key is the English word (`Colore → Color`); a key that is already
  canonical (`Stile`, `Fit Type`) keeps its spelling. No label table was invented. All scopes now read `Color · Size`.

  Amazon DE/ES/FR/IT and eBay·IT and leaves eBay·DE, Shopify and Etsy unlocked — which matches the design's fixtures.

**The mechanism, isolated in a pure probe with its control in the same run** (`validateMapping` / `parseMapping` from


`parseMapping` (`schema-mapping.service.ts:371-386`) returns **`emptyMapping()` on ANY validation error** — so one
non-rule sibling inside a category bucket costs the marketplace every rule it has, silently, with a 200 response and a
plausible-looking screen. `byProductType` is typed `Record<string, Record<string, FieldMappingRule>>`: the per-category
rule block VX §4 M2 describes is **not expressible there**.

**RECOMMENDATION (VT.3 measures and recommends; the Owner rules):** move the per-category block OUT of the field-rule
bucket — a top-level `variationsByProductType?: Record<string, VariationRule>` beside a channel-wide `variations?:
VariationRule` (the top-level arm above already validates clean today), or teach `validateMapping` to accept and
shape-check a reserved `variations` key inside a category bucket. Either way it needs its own validator, because a
`VariationRule` that fails shape-check must cost only the variation rule — never the marketplace's 137 fields.
VT.3's client types and `PUT` body are placement-agnostic (`contracts.ts` `VariationRuleWrite`), so this decision does
not change the page.

this one. Should the "one bad key drops the whole rule set" fallback become "drop the bad key, report it" across the
mapping engine? That is outside VT.3's paths and outside VT.1's mandate as written, so it is recorded, not done.

(`export { channelLabel, CHANNEL_LABELS } from '@nexus/shared/channel-label'`). A bare `export … from` re-exports without
BINDING the name in the module, and lines 108 and 134 of that same file call `channelLabel(...)` — so web tsc went red
(TS2304 ×2) and every studio route rendered its error boundary (`ReferenceError: channelLabel is not defined`). It blocked
every lane's browser gate for ~40 minutes and VT.4 measured it. The orchestrator applied the two-line fix (import, then
re-export) with the trap named in the file; I re-read it at mtime 08:47:37, did NOT revert the import, and ran
`node scripts/typecheck-scoped.mjs` on it: **exit 0**. What I did wrong is not the shared module — that part of P2-15 is
right — it is that I ran no typecheck between an export-shape hunk and the next edit, on a file every studio route imports.
Two rules adopted for the rest of this lane, and they are the reason the remaining hunks below carry a scoped-tsc line:
(1) after any hunk that changes an import or an export, run the scoped typecheck on the touched files BEFORE the next hunk,
and the full web/API tsc before claiming the finding fixed; (2) a hunk that swaps a local definition for a shared one keeps
a local BINDING for every caller in the file.

**VT.1b fixed P0 schema-lookup-key** (VT.4's finding · `reference_write_predicate_must_match_its_readers` in the flesh).
The binding was written against the market CODE and the publish path reads with the SP-API ID, so
`variation-theme-segments.ts` never ran there and the legacy fallback shipped.
- **Measured, mine, in one run** (`apps/api/scripts/_vt1b-p0-live.mts`): `Marketplace AMAZON/IT` =
  `{code:"IT", marketplaceId:"APJ6JRA9NG5V4"}`; `CategorySchema.marketplace` for AMAZON =
  **`BE 3 · DE 32 · ES 24 · FR 25 · IT 61 · NL 3 · UK 22`** — VT.4's numbers exactly, **zero SP-API ids**.
  `submission.service.ts:186-194` resolves `AMAZON:<code>` → `Marketplace.marketplaceId`, so `payload.marketplaceId`
  holds the ID; the adapter's own local copy is *named* `marketplaceCode` (`:136`), which is how a lookup written
  against one key and read with another looked correct in review.
- **BEFORE → AFTER attribute names.** BEFORE, the fallback composed `` `${axis.toLowerCase()}_name` ``, so the axis
  `Fit Type` became the attribute **`"fit type_name"`** — a SPACE inside an SP-API attribute name (VT.4 measured it on a
  live plan for `VX-TEST-3AX`), and `Taglia` became `taglia_name`, which SUIT does not declare either. AFTER:

  because SUIT·IT declares no `size` property at all (measured: `color true · fit_type true · size false · size_name
  false`). **No code path composes an attribute name any more** — the 5 remaining `_name` mentions in the adapter are
  all inside comments (`grep -n '_name\`'`).

  `Marketplace` row (`OR: [{code}, {marketplaceId}]`), memoised, **never a literal map**; `loadAmazonThemeFacts` calls
  it first, so the sheet path (code) and the publish path (id) land on the same cached row. Live proof, both keys in

  `"APJ6JRA9NG5V4" → code "IT" → SUIT schema RESOLVED (52 themes)`.

  attribute: a wrong attribute on a live parent is worse than a refused publish, and that is the case that FIRES. The
  submission distinguishes the two reasons ("no cached schema for <PT>, refresh its requirements" vs "binds to no
  attribute, map it on the Variation theme column").

  real but it is a REFUSAL the read had invited, not a silent success. (`reference_claims_must_match_their_measurement`.)

  `content.languages?: readonly string[]`; (2) the pin is built only when

  caller without the authority keeps the old answer; (3) the call site at ~:1218 passes `languages: coordinate?.languages`.
  With no pin there is no choice to make, so the cell serves `contentAddress: {tier:'language', language:'de'}`,
  `writeTarget: 'master'`, and **no** `contentAcknowledgement`. (4) `content-write.ts:48`'s refusal now NAMES THE ADDRESS
  IT NEEDS: `"… — that coordinate carries en. Save it as the shared de text instead (tier "language", language "de")."`
