as one defect ("the transfer APPLY … refuses the second row"). They are **two unrelated causes**: the CAS defect is real
and lived in `catalog-transfer-http`'s 2, while **5 of the 6 `catalog-product-transfer` reds were workbook-shape drift**
from LX.19 and never touched the apply at all.

**The CAS defect — three layers, each measured before it was changed.**
1. **The listing snapshot.** `master-content.service.ts:137` bumps a followed listing's `version` and sets
   `lastSyncStatus:'PENDING'` / `lastSyncedAt:null`; Prisma stamps `updatedAt`. A workbook carrying a shared `name` AND a
   channel `title` therefore applied target 1 and refused target 2 with "Listing changed since preview", job `PARTIAL`.
   **The whole difference, printed by an `LXF2_DIFF` probe at the throw site:** `version` **8 → 9** · `updatedAt`
   `2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z → 2026-09-13T07:57:53.190Z` · `lastSyncStatus` `undefined → 'PENDING'` · `lastSyncedAt`
   `undefined → null`. **Nothing else.** → `listingConflictSnapshot()` (ONE function, both sides of the comparison) drops
   those four; the write keeps its compare-and-set on the **freshly read** `version` + `updatedAt`, and any difference in a
   stored value still refuses.
2. **The pin rows.** The same cascade writes a `ChannelListingTranslation` carrying only `follows` for every language that
   follows the shared text. With the harness's `translations` include repaired (below) that reappeared as a snapshot
   difference — `translations: [] → [{language:'it', follows:['title'], version:1}]` — and the job read PARTIAL again. →
   the comparison keeps only pins that CARRY CONTENT (`name`/`description`/`bulletPoints`/`keywords`/`attributes`), and
   compares their content plus `language` and the sorted `follows` set, never ids or versions.
3. **The workbook's declared version.** `catalog-transfer-plan.ts:207` re-checks the exported `version` column at APPLY
   time, so the same cascade made targets 2 and 3 answer "The exported version no longer matches this record". →
   `buildTransferPlan(…, options?: { revalidateDeclaredVersion })`, **false on the two apply paths only**
   (`catalog-transfer-jobs.ts:226`, `catalog-transfer.service.ts:264`). The PREVIEW keeps the check — the arm that proves
   it is the test's own re-upload of the stale workbook, which still reads **INVALID** in the same run. The malformed-workbook
   arm (two different declared versions for one record) still fires on every path.

**Two harness defects that were hiding production behaviour** (`catalog-transfer-test/store.ts`, LX's own file):
- `findUnique` special-cased **two** compound uniques by NAME (`workspace_*`, `channel_code`) and threw on the third:
  `content-write.ts`'s closing `channelListingTranslation.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { channelListingId_language: … } })`
  answered `Not found` for a row it had created five lines earlier, and the job's only word was "Not found". The rule is
  now DERIVED — a key the row does not carry whose value names only keys it does carry is a compound unique.
- `translations` answered `row.translations ?? []`, a field **no writer ever sets**, so it was permanently `[]`. Consequence:
  `content-write.ts`'s `prior = listing.translations.find(…)` never saw the cascade's pin row, took its `create` branch, and
  left **two `ChannelListingTranslation` rows for one `(channelListingId, language)`** — `fixture-6 {follows:['title']}` and
  `fixture-130 {name:'HTTP title'}`, both `p0-account-a`/`it`, in one apply. The production unique index makes that pair
  impossible, so the harness was exercising the wrong branch. It now reads the real relation for both owners.

**5 `catalog-product-transfer` reds were LX.19 workbook drift, not the apply.** Measured on a real export: the editor
workbook has had **TWO header rows** since LX.19 — row 1 the human labels (`Title`, `Material`), row 2 the machine keys in
the `key@channel:market:locale` grammar (`item_name@amazon:IT:it`), data from **row 3** — and locale-bearing text moved to

wrote row 2, so `sheet` came back `undefined`, `col('item_name')` was `-1`, and exceljs threw "-1 is out of bounds". Fixed

writes the SOURCE tier, `de` the LANGUAGE tier, and the cell's provenance word is `it · pin`, not `Listing override`.

VT.4b gate finished the catalogue screens exit 0 + the footer pass exit 0 + the census exit 1 — 10:23 local.
**Four browser attempts, and the first three found defects in MY code or MY instrument. Each is recorded, because a
reading I did not keep is a reading nobody can check:**
1. attempt 1 — `page.waitForFunction(fn, {timeout})` puts the options in the ARG slot, so the default 30 s applied and a
   slow first compile read as "the grid is not there". Fixed to `(fn, null, {timeout})`.
2. attempt 2 — **a real defect of mine**: every `/products` route rendered the error boundary,
   `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` at `useMemo[variationMapping]`. Cause: a SAVED
   layout is JSON written before the `variationMapping` key existed, and `restorePageState` did
   `setFilters(pg.filters ?? EMPTY_FILTERS)` — a plain assignment, so the key was `undefined`. Fixed by MERGING over
   `EMPTY_FILTERS`, which protects any future context key, not just this one.
3. attempt 3 — **the second real defect**: the grid POST carried `variationMapping: []` on all four visits (captured), so

LX.F2 fixed P2-21 (R-LX-17): the durable sortable projection. **`title@de` 101.7 ms → 10.4 ms and
`description@de` 86.0 ms → 7.8 ms per 50-row page at 360 products**, warm, measured through the real
`orderCatalogLanguage()` against the local catalogue before and after.

- **BEFORE, measured (`apps/api/scripts/_lxf2-p221.mts`, 360 products, `deletedAt: null`, page 0/50, after a warm-up
  run):** `title@de` **101.7 ms**, `description@de` **86.0 ms**. The cost was 100-row batches of
  `catalogLanguageValues`, each pulling the product, its `translations` and its parent's, then running the resolver over
  all of them to order fifty rows — linear in the FILTERED set, not in the page, so ≈0.85 s at 3,000 products and
  ≈2.8 s at 10,000.
- **AFTER, same script shape (`_lxf2-p221c.mts`):** `title@de` asc **10.4 ms** · desc **8.0 ms** ·
  `description@de` asc **7.8 ms** · desc **7.8 ms**. One `ORDER BY` on the index; what remains is the candidate id scan
  the filter needs anyway.
- **Schema (LOCAL ONLY).** `ReadinessIndex.sortTitle` + `sortDescription`, both nullable TEXT, plus two PARTIAL indexes.
  `current_database()` asserted **`nexus_development`** and GALE-JACKET `Product.version` **59** immediately before the
  apply; `npx prisma db execute --url <local> --file …` → `Script executed successfully.`; read back from
  `information_schema.columns` (both `text`, both `is_nullable YES`) and `pg_indexes` (`ReadinessIndex_sortTitle_idx`,
  `ReadinessIndex_sortDescription_idx` present beside VT.1b's `variationSource` index). 884 rows, **0** carrying a value
  at apply time = not computed. The folder is `docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-f2/`, deliberately NOT
  `packages/database/prisma/migrations/` (PES.0 ruling #12). `npx prisma generate` announced in this file before it ran.
- **PROD SQL, VERBATIM, for the Owner** (additive · nullable · no backfill · no existing index touched):
  ```sql
  ALTER TABLE "ReadinessIndex" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "sortTitle" TEXT;
  ALTER TABLE "ReadinessIndex" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "sortDescription" TEXT;
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "ReadinessIndex_sortTitle_idx"
    ON "ReadinessIndex" ("workspaceId", "language", "sortTitle") WHERE "sortTitle" IS NOT NULL;
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "ReadinessIndex_sortDescription_idx"
    ON "ReadinessIndex" ("workspaceId", "language", "sortDescription") WHERE "sortDescription" IS NOT NULL;
  ```
- **The producer is the SAME resolver, not a second answer.** `readiness-index.service.ts` now loads the family's
  content once (`translations` + `parent.translations`, one extra `select` on a query it already made) and calls
  `resolveContent()` — **the very function `catalog-language.ts`'s own page projection calls** — for `title` and
  `description` per (product, language). Deriving the key from the sheet cell instead would have been a second answer to
  "what does this cell say" (`reference_two_column_builders_drift`). 5 hunks, listed: the family read, the
  `sortProjection()` helper, the absent-destination rows, the real rows, the import.
- **PARITY PROVEN ON THE FIXTURE, not asserted.** `reconcileFamilyReadiness('cmtzci5kf0000njr9f8yhrsxm')` (announced
  above before it ran) wrote **170 rows in 2,770 ms** for the family (34 before), read back after **8.5 s**, and for
  **9 of 9 languages** the stored `sortTitle` and `sortDescription` are byte-equal to what `catalogLanguageValues()`
  projects for the same (product, language) — `titleMatches: true` and `descMatches: true` on every row, no exception.
- **Design decisions stated, not hidden.** (1) These columns are a SORT KEY and **never a content read** — the comment on
  the model says so and nothing reads them as a value. (2) `sortDescription` is cut to **512 characters**: a sort key's
  business, and two rows tie only when their first 512 characters match. (3) `COLLATE "C"`: Postgres cannot apply the
  requested language's collation per row, and a stable byte order that is the same for every language beats a collation
  that silently differs from the previous page's. (4) **NULL sorts LAST in BOTH directions** (`NULLS LAST` on ASC *and*
  DESC) — a row written before the column existed must never be ordered as if it held an empty string, which is R-LX-9's
  rule one column over.
- **Tests:** `catalog-language.vitest.test.ts` 5 → **6 passed (6)** — the new arm asserts **exactly one** `$queryRaw`
  call (the property the finding was about), the `ORDER BY r."sortTitle" COLLATE "C" ASC NULLS LAST, p.id ASC` and
  `… DESC NULLS LAST …` text for both fields, the limit/offset pair, and a **POSITIVE CONTROL** that the readiness sort
  still emits its severity `CASE` and no sort column at all (so the arm targets the text branch, not the function).
  Regression: `catalog-language` + `content-readiness` + `readiness-account` + `variation-mapping-filter`
  **4 files / 20 passed (20)**. `apps/api` tsc **exit 0**.
- 🔴 **QUESTION FOR THE OWNER — this makes the text sort DEPEND on the index, and that is a coverage change.** Before, a
  `title@de` sort resolved live and therefore ordered every product. Now it orders the products whose readiness has been
  produced and puts the rest last in id order. Measured right now on local: **884 index rows, 170 carrying a sort key**

🔴 **FINDING 1 (P1) — an order-only change on Amazon/Shopify/Etsy answers 200, bumps the version, and stores nothing.**
Cause, one line each side, both read: `writeProjectionMapping` builds `flat: Record<axisKey, target>` and **drops
`entry.order`** (`variationMapping` is a flat map, it has no order); `readStoredMapping`'s non-eBay branch re-derives
`order` from the FAMILY axis index. eBay is the only channel with a real order store (`_variationAxes`, behind its own CAS
token). This is `reference_api_accepts_a_flag_it_ignores`, and a version bump for a no-op also burns every other
operator's CAS token. **Fixed in this pass, the honest half:** `ProjectionRead.order.reason` is now STATED per channel

coordinate is a DRAFT (`locked: null`), so `variationThemeWrite` correctly decides to SEND; the coordinate goes live
between that read and the PATCH; VT.1b's route answers **409 `axes_locked`** with the lock's own sentence. Before this
the operator's only signal was a refused cell carrying the raw code `axes_locked` — design §3.5's rule ("a SET change on a
live coordinate is a plan") enforced on the LOCAL read and abandoned on the SERVER's. Now the server's 409 opens the SAME
dry-run Modal with the SERVER's reason (it is the one that knows the listing went live), the cell reads `ok` with that
sentence (nothing was written either way, so red would claim a failure), and `conflict` stays true so the row refetches
and comes back carrying the lock. 🔴 If no plan host is listening, `askForThemeChangePlan` returns false and the cell
keeps the sentence as a REFUSAL — degraded, never silent.

**The fix — two rules, because the two routes know different things (4 + 1 + 5 hunks, no file rewritten).**
1. `/translations/:language` is told only the language, so the SURFACE addresses it. `ProductDrawer`'s four calls now
   send `contentAddress: sharedContentAddress(code|language)`; `markReviewed` and `remove` gained a JSON body (they
   sent none at all, and `contentAddress(undefined)` is a 400 on a DELETE exactly as on a PUT).
2. `/ai/bulk-generate` is told the MARKETPLACE and **already derived the language from it** for the write it performs
   (`languageForMarketplace(marketplace,'AMAZON')`, the `writeToMaster` branch). Demanding the same fact a second time
   from five client pages would be a second answer to "which language does this marketplace write in"
   (`reference_two_column_builders_drift`) — a page whose copy drifted by one row would write German text under an
   Italian address. So the SERVER derives it (`products-ai.routes.ts`), and an address a caller *does* send is
   **compared, not ignored** (`reference_api_accepts_a_flag_it_ignores`): a mismatch is a 400 naming both.
3. ONE derivation for the shape, in `packages/shared/content-language.ts`:
   `sharedContentAddress(language, primaryLanguage?)` — the primary language's shared text is the `source` tier, every
   other language the `language` tier; a caller that does not know the primary omits it and gets the `language` tier,
   which the server then refuses BY NAME rather than writing to the wrong home. `packages/shared` rebuilt (`tsc`,
   exit 0) because the web resolves `@nexus/shared/*` through `dist/`.
4. `TranslationsLens.tsx`'s `MARKETPLACE_FOR_LOCALE` literal is **deleted**. The market now comes from the workspace's
   own `GET /api/marketplaces/grouped` through the studio's existing `flattenGrouped` / `primaryLanguageFrom` readers
   (one memoised fetch, the `FamilyFooter` precedent), restricted to `channel === 'AMAZON'` because that is the channel
   the route resolves against, and the verb **refuses with a sentence** (`No active marketplace sells in DE — nothing
   was sent.`) rather than falling back to `'IT'` and writing Italian-addressed German.

LX.FIN item 3 — **R-LX-23 DONE: the `error-grouping` fingerprints are recomputed on LOCAL with every group count
identical, and the prod one-shot is written verbatim for the Owner.** The rehearsal earned its own refusal first:
**it projected 74 groups down to 50 and the control stopped the write.**

🔴 **AN ETIQUETTE BREACH OF MINE, RECORDED RATHER THAN BURIED.** I wrote the announcement for this LOCAL data
write in the SAME shell command as the script heredoc, and that command was **rejected** by the harness (the heredoc
carried a raw control byte), so the announcement never landed — and I then ran the rehearsal and the apply without
one in the file. The write itself is the one described below: LOCAL only, 73 rows, one derived column, the whole
before-state captured to `docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-fin/error-grouping-fingerprints-before.json` before the first read,
restorable by value with `--restore`. Nothing outside `SyncLogErrorGroup.fingerprint` was touched and no product,
listing or fixture row was involved. The rule I broke is "announce before you write", and the lesson is narrower than
it looks: **an announcement chained to the work in one command is not an announcement, because the command can fail as
a unit.** Announce in its own call.

**The defect the control caught, before it could reach anything.** `fingerprintError` takes an `ErrorOccurrence`, whose
message field is `message`; the stored row calls it **`sampleMessage`**. The first version passed the row straight in,
so every "new" hash was computed over `<no-message>` and 74 rows projected to **50 distinct fingerprints** — a
silent MERGE of 24 groups, which would have reported success. The script refuses to write unless the projected distinct
count equals the current one, so it exited instead (`groupCountsIdentical: false`). One line fixed it. The
transformation HAD run; it ran on the wrong input, and only a before/after INVARIANT could tell
(`reference_a_mutation_that_does_not_mutate`, from the other side).

**The faithfulness control, which is the whole safety argument.** A hash cannot be converted, only recomputed. So the
script recomputes each row's hash from the row's own stored components with the **OLD** delimiter (U+0000) first and
compares it against the STORED value; only a row that reproduces is rewritten. The normaliser is the service's own
`normaliseMessage`, **exported by this lane for exactly this**, with the reason at the site — a backfill with its
own normaliser would be measuring a different function from the one that wrote the value.

| reading | LOCAL `nexus_development`, GALE-JACKET `Product.version` 59 |
|---|---|
| rows | **74** |
| distinct fingerprints BEFORE | **74** |
| occurrences BEFORE (`sum("count")`) | **2,284** |
| status BEFORE | **74 ACTIVE / 0 RESOLVED** |
| already on the new delimiter | **0** |
| reproduced under the OLD delimiter -> rewritten | **73** |
| **not** reproduced -> left untouched | **1** — `cmt14dsy20001s4a38var7ybg`, AMAZON `ads POST /reporting/reports`, stored `d9ed22a81f37b70f…` vs recomputed-old `3c9a4817e186689e…`. Its `sampleMessage` has been refreshed since the group was created (the writer replaces it on every occurrence) or truncated at 1,000 characters, so the hash cannot be reconstructed — and inventing one would move a group with nobody able to see it happen. |
| projected distinct fingerprints | **74** -> `groupCountsIdentical: true` |
| **AFTER**, read back **2026-09-13T09:42:38.194Z (8.5 s)** | **74** rows · **74** distinct · **2,284** occurrences · **74 ACTIVE** — every count identical |
| `everyRewrittenRowMatchesTheLiveWriter` | **true** — each rewritten row now equals what the LIVE `fingerprintError` produces for the next occurrence of the same error, which is the only property that stops a duplicate group opening |
| rows still not matching the writer | **1** (the unreproducible row above, by design) |

**FOR THE OWNER — the prod one-shot, verbatim.** There is no SQL for this: the value is a SHA-256 over five parts,
one of which is the JS normaliser's output, so it cannot be computed in SQL. The script is
`docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-fin/20260913_lxfin_error_grouping_fingerprint_backfill.mts`; it writes ONLY the
`fingerprint` column, only on rows that pass the faithfulness check, and refuses if the group count would move.

```
# 1. Rehearse — writes nothing, prints the report:
railway run --service "/api" env -u REDIS_URL npx tsx docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-fin/20260913_lxfin_error_grouping_fingerprint_backfill.mts

# 2. Only if the report says `groupCountsIdentical: true`:
railway run --service "/api" env -u REDIS_URL npx tsx docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-fin/20260913_lxfin_error_grouping_fingerprint_backfill.mts --apply
```
```sql
-- 3. Verify: every number must be unchanged from the pre-run reading.
SELECT count(*) AS rows, count(DISTINCT fingerprint) AS groups, sum("count") AS occurrences,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE "resolutionStatus" = 'RESOLVED') AS resolved
  FROM "SyncLogErrorGroup";
```

🔴 **ORDER MATTERS:** run it BEFORE the deploy that ships the new delimiter, or immediately after and before the
next sync error arrives. Between the two a recurring error opens a duplicate group, and the backfill does not merge it
back.
🔴 **The number that decides whether to run it at all is production's own `resolved` count** (query 3). LOCAL had
**0** RESOLVED, so skipping it there would have cost one duplicate group per recurring error, once. Every RESOLVED group
on prod is a suppression that stops.

- GALE **eBay·IT**, live, `orderChangeAllowed: true` → an **order-only** change is a **request**, every other kind is a

## D · DEPLOY PREREQUISITES — verbatim, for the Owner

**1. `ReadinessIndex.variationSource` (VT.1b).** Applied to LOCAL only; the folder is deliberately outside
`prisma/migrations/` per ruling #12. Additive, nullable, no backfill, no lock beyond a catalog update:

```sql
ALTER TABLE "ReadinessIndex" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "variationSource" TEXT;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "ReadinessIndex_variationSource_idx" ON "ReadinessIndex" ("variationSource") WHERE "variationSource" IS NOT NULL;
```

**2. The one-shot readiness backfill (R-LX-9).** Production holds **0** `ReadinessIndex` rows, and after R-LX-9 an empty
index reads `Not computed` rather than `absent` — which is correct and means **every** variation-mapping surface is inert
on prod until the index is built: the catalogue filter narrows to nothing, `FamilyFooter` prints `Not computed`, and the
three readiness kinds (`theme-unset`, `collision`, `attribute-unbound`) never fire. The producer is one hunk in the one
materialiser (`readiness-index.service.ts`), so it covers the write path and the reconcile job by construction; the
backfill is the existing `reconcileFamilyReadiness(rootId)` run once per family root, and `jobs/readiness-reconcile.job.ts`
is the scheduled path that keeps it current. **This is a prerequisite, not an option** — without it the `variationSource`
column above exists and is NULL on every row, which the code correctly reads as "not computed", so the deploy would land a
filter that answers 0 for every word.

**3. Nothing else. VT.F adds NO schema change, NO migration and NO backfill.** Everything in this pass is code, tests,
declarations and one CSS deletion. The only database writes I made were on the LOCAL fixture, and the fixture is deleted.

(a) the `env.ts` CWD hazard (P0 above) — every `npx vitest run --root apps/api …` from the repo root resolves
`DATABASE_URL` to **Neon prod**; (b) the Neon credential in the repo-root `.env` is the one whose rotation is open

## ASSUMED: / QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: — VT.F's own, each with its measurement

- `ASSUMED:` **the R-VT-4 width belongs in the SERVER producer as well as the engine default.** `variationThemeColumn()`
  serves `width`, and the client honours it (`col.width ?? 160`), so changing only the engine default would have been a
  silent no-op — `reference_token_scale_defined_twice`. Both now say 160, and `check-editor-open` asserts the SERVED width
  absolutely, per scope. If the Owner wants the width to be the engine's alone, the server field should be dropped rather
  than left disagreeing.
- `ASSUMED:` **`targetOptionsState` gains a FOURTH word, `no-theme`.** Three words could not tell "no cached schema" from
  "a cached schema that declares no theme", and R-VT-7 says an empty list carries its own state word. It is additive on
  both sides and an older server's `undefined` is read as `unavailable`, never as `ok`.
- `ASSUMED:` **the dock's theme PATCH omits `theme` unless the draft touched it.** The route reads an explicit `null` as
  "clear the theme", so sending one on every reorder would wipe an override. Pinned by a test that asserts the KEY is
  absent (`'theme' in draft === false`), not merely undefined.
- `ASSUMED:` **`addableAxes` includes a DROPPED axis.** A dropped axis is exactly one an operator may want back, and the
  alternative (delivered-or-nothing) would make `+ Add` unable to undo a drop. Pinned by its own arm.
- `ASSUMED:` **`Colore → special_size_type` on the fixture's Taglia axis** was a fixture-only binding to make A2's 200 arm
  runnable — SUIT·IT declares no `size`. It never touched a live coordinate and the fixture is deleted.

**PROD SQL, VERBATIM, for the Owner** (file:
`docs/audits/2026-09-13-lx-fin/20260913_lxfin_seller_reference_labels.sql`; additive, one new table, no ALTER, no
backfill, no data dependency — an empty table behaves exactly as today, and `DROP TABLE "SellerReferenceLabel";` is a
complete rollback):

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "SellerReferenceLabel" (
  "workspaceId"  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT NULLIF(current_setting('nexus.workspace_id', true), ''),
  "id"           TEXT NOT NULL,
  "channel"      TEXT NOT NULL,
  "connectionId" TEXT NOT NULL,
  "marketplace"  TEXT NOT NULL,
  "productType"  TEXT NOT NULL,
  "fieldKey"     TEXT NOT NULL,
  "labels"       JSONB NOT NULL,
  "fetchedAt"    TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  CONSTRAINT "SellerReferenceLabel_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "SellerReferenceLabel_channel_connection_market_type_field_uq"
  ON "SellerReferenceLabel" ("workspaceId", "channel", "connectionId", "marketplace", "productType", "fieldKey");

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "SellerReferenceLabel_workspaceId_idx"
  ON "SellerReferenceLabel" ("workspaceId");
```
🔴 The unique key carries **`connectionId`** because seller templates belong to the SELLER. Naming account B's
templates from account A's definition is the defect `isPrimaryChannelConnection` already refuses in this service; a
cache keyed without the connection would reintroduce it silently and durably.

**Service — 4 hunks in `apps/api/src/services/categories/reference-labels.service.ts`, no file rewritten.** The live arm
(a gesture, or a write's name->ID resolution) `upsert`s what it learned; the `cachedSchemasOnly()` arm reads the row
instead of returning `{}`; the stamp gains **`sellerTemplateSource`** (`live` / `memory` / `database` / `none` /
`not-requested`) and **`sellerTemplatesFetchedAt`** — the ROW's date, never the request time — and both module readings
are RESET at the top of `amazonReferenceLabels` so a stamp can never report the previous request's source
(`reference_stale_measurement_looks_like_a_missing_one`). The route already spreads `result`, so both are on the wire
(`categories.routes.ts:66`).

Three properties on purpose: it **starts no provider work** (the cached arm returns before `seller-schema.service.js`
is even imported); it **never widens an option list** (allowed VALUES still come from the definition / cached
`CategorySchema` — this answers only "what does this id read as", and a stale label on a withdrawn template is a wrong
NAME, never a writable value); and a read or write failure is **swallowed**, because a label cache that can fail the
page it rode in on is worse than the raw id it replaces.

🔴 **A FRESHNESS REGRESSION I WROTE AND THEN REMOVED, with the test that keeps it out.** My first version wrote
the database answer into the in-process provider cache. That measurably changes a DIFFERENT path: `live=1` (the
reference editor opening its option list) skips `withCachedSchemas` but still takes a memory HIT, so a cold page load
that seeded memory from the database would make the operator's next "show me the live list" serve a stored answer for up
to **5 minutes** — a shipping template created a minute ago invisible in the one place it matters. The database answer is
now returned WITHOUT touching the provider cache (one indexed row read per cold request), and there is a named test arm
for it.

```sql
  CONSTRAINT "SellerReferenceLabel_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "SellerReferenceLabel_channel_connection_market_type_field_uq"
  ON "SellerReferenceLabel" ("workspaceId", "channel", "connectionId", "marketplace", "productType", "fieldKey");

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "SellerReferenceLabel_workspaceId_idx"
  ON "SellerReferenceLabel" ("workspaceId");
```
🔴 **AND ONE THING I GOT WRONG AND CAUGHT WHILE WRITING THIS RECORD — the grants.** Migration
`20260912_lx5_readiness_index` ends with `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON "ReadinessIndex" TO
nexus_workspace_runtime;` because `packages/database/workspace-adapter.js:11` does `SET LOCAL ROLE
nexus_workspace_runtime` on every routed query. **My SQL above has no grant and no RLS policy**, so on production the
runtime role would be REFUSED on this table and the label cache would silently fall back to today's behaviour (the read
is in a `try/catch`, so no request would fail — which is exactly why it would go unnoticed). On LOCAL the table is
reachable because my probe used a superuser URL, so the tests and the readings above are unaffected; the defect is in
the SQL handed to the Owner, not in the code. **Append this before the prod apply, and add the same two statements to
the eventual migration folder:**

```sql
DO $$ BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'nexus_workspace_runtime') THEN
    GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON "SellerReferenceLabel" TO nexus_workspace_runtime;
  END IF;
END $$;
ALTER TABLE "SellerReferenceLabel" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY nexus_workspace_isolation ON "SellerReferenceLabel" FOR ALL TO nexus_workspace_runtime
  USING ("workspaceId" = NULLIF(current_setting('nexus.workspace_id', true), ''));
```
🔴 The policy above is the SHAPE of `20260911_category_taxonomies`' but **not** its full predicate (that one also
joins `Workspace`/`WorkspaceMembership` to check the actor). I have deliberately NOT invented the full predicate for a
derived label cache: **the Owner should apply the project's standard isolation policy for a derived table**, and if that
is the fuller predicate, use the fuller one. I did not apply either to local, because the tests and readings above must
not be taken through a policy nobody has ruled on.

- It is the same `runReadinessReconcile()` the nightly 02:17 UTC cron calls; it replaces only derived rows

  serialised it, so `readStoredMapping`, the Shopify axis order and the Shopify/Etsy cell all keep FAMILY order for a
  flat value. My own test caught the opposite behaviour in my first version.

  null, SQL NULL, `{}` and `{axes:[]}` alike as "empty"). Four spellings of nothing, one word for them.

  root now FAILS instead of quietly being redirected to the local database. The alternative (pin and carry on) would have
  been friendlier and would have left the author believing their command was right. The ruling asked for the refusal; I
  note the trade rather than hide it.
- 🔴 **QUESTION FOR THE OWNER (1) — a 400 from a cell commit does not show the server's SENTENCE.** Measured on screen:
  the sheet footer said `1 refused · 1 cell blocked` and a status line said `1 change not saved`, but the route's actual
  words (*"Map each shared axis once to a nonempty channel specific."*) appeared only in the browser console, and the
  cell kept the unsaved value. The honest half is there (nothing claimed to be saved); the missing half is WHY. That is
  the SheetWriter's refusal path for **every** column, not this one, so it is a design decision and not a lane's.

  guard to vitest, as the ruling says. The three durable options remain VT.F's: (a) load `apps/api/.env` explicitly in
  `env.ts` regardless of CWD; (b) refuse to start when `current_database()` is not the one the CWD's `.env` names;
  (c) remove `DATABASE_URL` from the repo-root `.env`. My recommendation is **(c)**: the root `.env` is the only reason a
  repo-root process resolves production, and nothing in the repo needs `DATABASE_URL` there — but removing a credential
  line from a shared env file is the Owner's call, not a lane's.

  BOTH `our_price` and `discounted_price` (proved by the dry-run payload test in phase 3, never live); and a sale without BOTH
  dates cannot be pushed → the door refuses a windowless sale value by name. `fulfillment_channel_code` enum = `AMAZON_EU |
  DEFAULT` on every cached market incl. UK.

  `MX-TEST-20260913` (DRAFT, `syncPaused:true`, `isPublished:false`) under the XAVIA root `xavia-knee-slider`
  (`cmokmy2ym006fpm0pa4raljl7`) before the first write rehearsal, announced here, deleted at the end.
- **Design choices measured, not assumed:** (i) VP.2's `getFamilyRead` costs 840 ms warm / 2.8 s cold on GALE and 770 ms of it is
  its per-channel projection reads, which the Matrix does not need — so the Matrix read composes the SAME exported helpers
  (`resolveFamilyRoot`, `FAMILY_MEMBER_SELECT`, `buildFamilyAxes`, `axisValuesOf`, `completeAxisValueOrder`,
  `readExcludedListingIds`) for the rows, their axis-value order and `needs-value`, without the sheet. (ii) `variationExcluded`
  (VP.2, 09-11) is live in this database and UNDECLARED in `schema.prisma` — that file's own rule ("a database ahead of the
  schema is inert; a schema ahead of a database is an outage") — so `salePriceStart`/`salePriceEnd` follow the same precedent:
  migration folder + LOCAL apply, raw-SQL access through two typed helpers, `schema.prisma` untouched (my claim's "EDIT
  schema.prisma" is WITHDRAWN for that reason; the declaration folds in once prod carries the column). (iii) The page's
  `applyVerbRun` sends `params: { verb }` + the carried `preview` on commit, so the server cannot re-run a VALUE verb from `params`
  alone — it re-verifies EVERY carried change by re-running the shared preview per target with params rebuilt from `change.to`
  (set-price/adjust/copy → `set-price {value: to}`, pin → `{value: to}`, buffer → `{value: to}`, fulfilment → `{method: to}`), and
  refuses a change the fresh preview does not reproduce. (iv) A new pure module `services/pim/matrix-cells.ts` (added to my claim)
  holds the listing-state table, the queue fold, the writable rules and the coordinate order so they are pinned without a database.
